topics.description: American painter and illustrator best known for his Saturday Evening Post covers, the Four Freedoms series, Triple Self-Portrait, and The Problem We All Live With.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: A boy, his father, and their dog wait on a bench for a train that will take the boy to university in this artist’s painting Breaking Home Ties. In another painting by this artist, three half-dressed boys race past a sign that reads, “No Swimming.” In one painting, this artist peers into a mirror while smoking a pipe so he can draw a portrait of himself on an easel. This artist depicted a Thanksgiving dinner in the (*) “from Want” section of one work. This artist showed Ruby Bridges walking in front of a wall with a racial slur scrawled on it while going to school in The Problem We All Live With. For 10 points, name this American artist who created the Four Freedoms series for the Saturday Evening Post.

parts.label: L
parts.question: For 10 points each, answer the following about unusual self-portraits.

parts.label: A
parts.question: This man depicted himself with the title features in his Self-Portrait with Seven Fingers. He depicted a burning synagogue in his depiction of the Crucifixion, and his most famous work, I and the Village, was inspired by a village in Belarus.

parts.label: B
parts.question: This man depicted himself thrice in his Triple Self-Portrait. He also painted for the Saturday Evening Post, and depicted Ruby Bridges walking to school escorted by National Guardsmen in The Problem We All Live With.

parts.label: C
parts.question: Rockwell also created a series of paintings depicting this many freedoms. In another unusual self-portrait, Belgian surrealist René Magritte painted himself with this many arms, two more than the usual number.

topics.description: A white marble mausoleum in Agra commissioned by Mughal emperor Shah Jahan for his wife Mumtaz Mahal and renowned as a masterpiece of Mughal architecture.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: The earliest depiction of the dodo bird in color was made by this dynasty's artist Ustad Mansur  (OO-stahd mahn-SOOR). The painting Prince with a Falcon depicts a popular hobby of this dynasty  in a form used up to 1400 times in some of its manuscripts, miniature painting. Over 410 fountains  were included in the Shalimar Gardens during this dynasty, whose architect (*) Ustad Lahauri (OO-stad lah-hah-OR-ee) designed a tomb for Mumtaz (MOOM-tahz). For 10 points, name this dynasty whose  emperor Shah Jahan (jah-HAHN) commissioned the Taj Mahal during its rule as the last Muslim dynasty  to control most of India.
parts.answer: Mughal dynasty [or Mughals; or Mughal empire]

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: One ruler of this empire named Auraungzeb re-established the jizya tax to encourage conversion to the religion it followed. This empire was founded by Babur and reached its zenith under Akbar. One ruler of this empire built a large white marble (*) mausoleum in the city of Agra for his wife Mumtaz. For ten points, Shah Jahan, commissioner of the Taj Mahal, ruled what Indian Islamic empire?

topics.description: Michelangelo’s monumental fresco cycle depicting biblical scenes, prophets, sibyls, and ignudi on the ceiling of the Sistine Chapel in Vatican City.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: This man sculpted a horned Moses along with a dying and a rebellious slave for the tomb of Pope Julius II. A marble sculpture by this man located in the Palazzo Vecchio (VEK-yo) is depicted in contrapposto and depicts a nude David. He also depicted himself as the flayed skin of St. Bartholomew in his mural The (*) Last Judgement. For ten points, name this Italian Renaissance artist who painted the ceiling of the Sistine Chapel.
parts.answer: Michelangelo [or Michelangelo di Lodovico Buonarroti Simoni]

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: In one painting, this artist used a male model to depict a muscular woman turning away from the viewer to lift up a large book. In that painting by this artist, scenes like The Separation of Light from Darkness and The Drunkenness of Noah are flanked by nude figures called ignudi and the prophets and sibyls who foresaw the coming of Christ. This artist depicted his own face on the flayed (*) skin of Saint Bartholomew in his version of the Last Judgement. In a fresco by this artist, God reaches out his fingertip to the outstretched hand of Adam. For 10 points, name this Renaissance artist who painted the ceiling of the Sistine Chapel and sculpted a marble David.
parts.answer: Michelangelo [or Michelangelo di Lodovico Buonarroti Simonini]

topics.description: An 1899 painting by Winslow Homer depicting a Black man stranded in a small boat amid rough, shark-infested ocean waters.

parts.label: L
parts.question: The Bahamian story of McCabe’s curse inspired this painting while its artist was vacationing in the Caribbean after his father's death. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [M] Name this Winslow Homer painting of a Black man stranded on a small boat in the middle of the ocean.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] Homer’s painting The Gulf Stream depicts several of these animals. A painting by John Singleton Copley depicts one of these animals attacking Brook Watson off of the coast of Havana Harbor.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [H] The sharks in Homer’s The Gulf Stream inspired damned souls biting the title ship in this artist’s The Barque of Dante. During his Orientalist phase, this artist painted three women sitting in an ornate room around a hookah pipe.

parts.label: L
parts.question: In addition to painting landscapes, J.M.W. Turner was known for painting these vessels, such as one being “tugged to her last berth,” The Fighting Temeraire. For ten points each,

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name these subjects of nautical paintings.
parts.answer: ships (accept boats; accept specific types, like steamships, warships, sailboats, etc.)

parts.label: B
parts.question: In a massive oil canvas on display at the Louvre, Théodore Géricault depicted one of these decidedly less seaworthy objects carrying the survivors of the wrecked Medusa.
parts.answer: rafts (accept The Raft of the Medusa; accept Le Radeau de la Méduse)

parts.label: C
parts.question: A Black fisherman braces himself in a small boat in choppy, shark-infested waters in this 1899 painting by Winslow Homer.

topics.description: Dorothea Lange's iconic 1936 documentary photograph of Florence Owens Thompson and her children, made during the Great Depression.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: In this state, a woman told a photographer that she sold her car tires and lived on frozen  vegetables. Eadweard Muybridge's (Edward MOY-brij's) series Sallie Gardner at a Gallop was made  in this state. Florence Owens Thompson is the subject of a photo taken in this state, where the moon appears over a (*) rock face in another photograph. Sites such as Manzanar (MAN-zuh-nar) in  this state were photographed by Ansel Adams and Dorothea Lange (LANG), who documented Japanese  internment camps. Migrant Mother was taken in, for 10 points, what state, where Moon and Half Dome shows Yosemite (yoh-SEM-it-ee)?

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: In a photo by this artist, two men walk past a billboard of a man in a recliner chair. Paul Taylor produced captions for this artist’s book An American Exodus, which includes a photo of a long New Mexico road. After Ansel Adams, this artist visited Manzanar to take gritty photos of children taking the Pledge of Allegiance. An old man leans against a wood fence in this photographer’s White Angel Breadline. While working for the Farm Security Administration, this artist photographed pea picker Florence Owens Thompson gazing into the distance as her children cling to her. For 10 points, name this photographer of Migrant Mother.

topics.description: Yoko Ono is a Japanese-born avant-garde, performance, and multimedia artist and musician associated with Fluxus and known for works including Cut Piece and collaborations with John Lennon.

parts.label: L
parts.question: This member of the Fluxus movement encouraged audience members to cut off her clothes in the  performance Cut Piece. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [10] Name this Japanese-born performance artist who was photographed with her husband by Annie  Leibovitz on the day she became a widow.
parts.answer: Yoko Ono [or Ono Yoko; accept, but do not otherwise reveal, Yoko Ono Lennon]

parts.label: B
parts.question: [10] Yoko Ono met this future husband as he vandalized one of her installations in 1966. This man sang  lead on the songs "Strawberry Fields Forever" and "Imagine."

parts.label: C
parts.question: [10] Oko and Lennon protested the Vietnam War using these events in hotel rooms, named in analogy to  a tactic of the civil rights movement.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Answer the following about the works of female performance artists, for 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [E] Marina Abramovic's last performance with her partner Ulay, titled Lovers, involved walking from opposite ends of this structure. This 13,000-mile-long structure is not actually visible from space.
parts.answer: Great Wall of China [or Wànlǐ chángchéng]

parts.label: B
parts.question: [M] This performance artist allowed participants to cut off parts of her clothing in Cut Piece. This author of Grapefruit helped write the lyrics to her husband’s song “Imagine.”

parts.label: C
parts.question: [H] While more famous for her Infinity Mirror Room pieces, this artist often painted nude New Yorkers with polka dots. In Walking Piece, this artist walks through New York City in a brightly-colored kimono.

topics.description: The 1875 incidental music by Edvard Grieg for Henrik Ibsen’s play Peer Gynt, including “Morning Mood” and “In the Hall of the Mountain King.”

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: An ascending theme in this work is first stated in B minor, where it ends with the notes [read slowly] “A G E C E long G.” A flute plays [read slowly] “B, G-sharp, F-sharp, E” and ascends to B in one piece of this work, while another featuring the triangle depicts “Anitra’s Dance.” An E major piece in 6/8 time from this work depicts the sun rising over a desert and is called (*) “Morning Mood.” Increasingly fast and loud cellos, bassoons, and double basses represent trolls chasing the protagonist of this work in its piece “In the Hall of the Mountain King.” For 10 points, name this collection of incidental music to a Henrik Ibsen play composed by Edvard Grieg.
parts.answer: ANSWER: Peer Gynt [accept the Peer Gynt Suites; accept the incidental music to Peer Gynt; prompt on “Morning Mood” or “In the Hall of the Mountain King” before mention]

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: A collection by this composer features the same melody in its opening “Arieta” and closing “Remembrances.” That collection of 66 short piano pieces by this composer also includes one titled for a “Wedding Day” at this composer’s hometown. The Lyric Pieces are by this composer, who also wrote a cello and bass pizzicato melody that gradually increases in both speed and volume. The piece (*) “Morning Mood” begins a suite by this composer that ends with the title character being chased by a horde of trolls. For 10 points, name this Norwegian composer who included “In the Hall of the Mountain King” in his incidental music to Peer Gynt.

topics.description: Johannes Brahms was a German Romantic composer known for works including A German Requiem, Hungarian Dances, symphonies, and the lullaby Wiegenlied.

parts.label: L
parts.question: This composer critiqued music under the pseudonyms Florestan and Eusebius and was editor-in-chief for the New Journal For Music for ten years. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [H] Name this composer, who included those pseudonyms as characters in his piece Carnaval. Symphonies by this composer include the “Spring” and “Rhenish” ones.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] In 1840, Schumann married Clara Wieck, a composer and player of this instrument, which contains 88 black and white keys.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [M] The Schumanns engaged in the “War of the Romantics”, during which they sided with this other German composer, who composed A German Requiem and a famous lullaby.

parts.label: L
parts.question: After its 1876 premiere in Vienna, this composer’s First Symphony was dubbed “Beethoven’s Tenth.” For ten points each,

parts.label: A
parts.question: [H] Name this composer. Other works by this composer include Hungarian Dances and A German Requiem.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] Brahms wrote one of these pieces titled Wiegenlied for Bertha Faber’s son. These pieces are sung to children to put them to sleep.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [M] Brahms’s Opus 39 is a set of 16 of these dances. The Beautiful Blue Danube is a dance in this Austrian style, usually in 3/4 time.

topics.description: American minimalist and contemporary classical composer whose operas include Nixon in China and Doctor Atomic.

parts.label: L
parts.question: In one aria, this operatic character sings that “when [he] shook hands with Zhou (joh) En-lai… the world was listening.” For ten points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [M] Name this character who sings that “news, news, news… has a kind of mystery” after getting off of the plane “Spirit of ‘76.” This character meets Chairman Mao in an opera about his presidential visit to China.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [H] Nixon in China is an opera by this composer, who also wrote Short Ride in a Fast Machine, Doctor Atomic, and Death of Klinghof er. This composer shares his name with an early President of the United States.
parts.answer: John Coolidge Adams [do not accept or prompt on “John Luther Adams”]

parts.label: C
parts.question: [E] Adams wrote the opera A Flowering Tree based on a folk tale from this country. Another minimalist composer, Phillip Glass, loosely based his opera Satyagraha on the life of a figure from this country, Mohandas Gandhi.

parts.label: L
parts.question: A pianist from this country premiered Must the Devil Have All the Good Tunes? in one of her signature eye-catching outfits. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [H] Name this country also home to a pianist known for his manic mannerisms while playing, who was inspired by the Tom and Jerry episode The Cat Concerto to take up piano.
parts.answer: China [or People’s Republic of China or Zhongguo or Zhonghua Renmin Gongheguo; do not accept or prompt on “Republic of China”]

parts.label: B
parts.question: [M] This composer of Must the Devil Have All the Good Tunes? gave it the marking “Gritty, funky, but in Strict Tempo; Twitchy, Bot-like.” This composer’s operas include Nixon in China and Doctor Atomic.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [E] This city’s Philharmonic, directed by the Venezuelan composer Gustavo Dudamel, premiered Must the Devil Have All the Good Tunes? at the Walt Disney Concert Hall.
parts.answer: Los Angeles [or L.A.; accept the Los Angeles Philharmonic]

topics.description: Angkor Wat is a monumental Khmer temple complex in Cambodia, built by Suryavarman II, originally dedicated to Vishnu, and later used as a Buddhist temple.

parts.label: L
parts.question: This ethnic group names an empire, whose ruler Suryavarman II built a complex meant to resemble Mount Meru. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [H] Name this majority ethnic group of a certain Southeast Asian country. Pol Pot ruled over a Communist government named after this ethnic group and “Rouge”.
parts.answer: Khmer [accept Khmer Empire or Khmer Rouge]

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] The Khmer are native to this country. This country’s Khmer Rouge was toppled from its capital of Phnom Penh after an invasion from its eastern neighbor, Vietnam.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [M] This was the aforementioned complex built by the Khmer emperor Suryavarman II. This large Hindu temple complex appears on Cambodia’s flag.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: A Dead Kennedys song is titled for a "Holiday in" this country. An empire in this country developed a martial art called "lion-pounding", or bokator. The use of "killing fields" was among the atrocities committed by Pol Pot, the head of this country's (*) Khmer Rouge regime. The massive Angkor Wat temple is located in, for 10 points, what Southeast Asian country with capital at Phnom Penh?
parts.answer: Kingdom of Cambodia [or le Royaume du Cambodge, or Prĕəh Riəciənaacak Kampuciə; accept Democratic Kampuchea or Kâmpŭchéa Prâcheathippadey; accept Srok Khmae; accept “Holiday in Cambodia”]

topics.description: The fourth and final opera in Richard Wagner’s Ring Cycle, ending with the destruction of Valhalla.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: The annual Bayreuth (by-ROYT) Festival celebrates the works of this composer. This composer’s opera Lohengrin contains the “Bridal Chorus”, and another of his works ends with Brunnhilde riding into a funeral pyre that burns (*) Valhalla. That work, Gotterdamerung, ends this composer’s Ring Cycle. For ten points, name this German composer of the “Ride of the Valkyries.”

parts.label: L
parts.question: After Siegfried slays one of these creatures, tasting its blood gives him the ability to understand birdsong. For ten points each,

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this type of mythical creature. In a series of 19th century German operas, Fafnir turned from a giant into this creature to guard a horde of gold.

parts.label: B
parts.question: Siegfried kills the dragon Fafnir in the third of the four operas in this cycle by Richard Wagner [ree-kart VAHG-ner], which begins with Das Rheingold.
parts.answer: Ring Cycle (accept Ring of the Nibelung cycle)

parts.label: C
parts.question: This final opera in the Ring cycle typically takes five or more hours to perform, and ends with Valhalla itself burning to the ground.

topics.description: A colossal neoclassical statue in New York Harbor, gifted by France to the United States and depicting Liberty holding a tablet and torch.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: Railway terminals that this architect designed across the world include the Budapest Nyugati Station. After the previous engineer died, Auguste Bartholdi asked this architect to finish the metal framework of the Statue of Liberty. A spindly steel monument named for this architect was built for the 1889 (*) World’s Fair and is located on the Champ de Mars. For ten points, give this namesake of an iconic Parisian Tour, or tower.

parts.label: L
parts.question: During the immigration boom of the late 19th and early 20th centuries, unrest in Europe led millions to go through this island to get to the United States. For ten points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [M] Name this island located halfway between New York and New Jersey, home to the main historical immigration point for the East Coast.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] Immigrants entering at Ellis Island would often see this structure while entering. A gift from France, this large green statue depicts a woman holding a tablet and a torch.
parts.answer: Statue of Liberty [or Liberty Enlightening the World, or La Liberté éclairant le monde]

parts.label: C
parts.question: [H] This other island was known as the “Ellis Island of the West.” Located in California’s San Francisco Bay, it saw most of its immigrants from China and Japan.

topics.description: Belgian-born French-Romani jazz guitarist and composer who pioneered jazz manouche and wrote standards including “Minor Swing” and “Nuages.”

parts.label: L
parts.question: The Squirrel Nut Zippers participated in a 1990s revival of this style. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [10] Name this jazz style “electrified” in a genre pioneered by Caravan Palace, in which eighth notes are  not played straight. It evolved out of the “big band” era.
parts.answer: ANSWER: swing [or swing revival; or neo-swing; or retro swing; or electro swing; or swing house]

parts.label: B
parts.question: [10] “New Jack Swing” was popularized in the Ghostbusters II theme “On Our Own” by a singer with  this surname, shared with the funk pioneer who recorded “I Got You” and “Papa's Got a Brand New  Bag.”
parts.answer: ANSWER: Brown [or Bobby Brown; or Robert Barisford Brown; or James Brown]

parts.label: C
parts.question: [10] “Minor Swing” and “Nuages” (NOO-aaj) were written by this jazz manouche (man-oosh) pioneer  and guitarist, who worked mostly in France.

parts.label: L
parts.question: This musician lost the use of two fingers on his left hand after he accidentally knocked over a candle, badly burning himself. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [H] Name this French-Romani jazz guitarist. He composed the standards “Minor Swing” and “Nuages” with his Quintette du Hot Club de France.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [M] Reinhardt’s album Djangology features a recording of the “I Got Rhythm,” a standard by this American composer. This composer fused jazz with classical music in pieces like An American in Paris.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [E] Django Reinhardt also recorded a number of pieces with Duke Ellington, who played this keyboard instrument. Thelonius Monk and Herbie Hancock also played this instrument with 88 black and white keys.

topics.description: American regionalist painter best known for American Gothic and Daughters of Revolution.

parts.label: L
parts.question: This painting depicts James Monroe holding up an American flag. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this Emmanuel Leutze (LOYT-zuh) painting depicting the first president of the United States sailing a boat across a river during the Revolutionary War.
parts.answer: Washington Crossing the Delaware [do not accept or prompt on “George Washington Crossing the Delaware”]

parts.label: B
parts.question: This American regionalist artist painted Daughters of Revolution, a work that depicts three people who may be Ben Franklin, Thomas Jefferson and George Washington in drag standing in front of Leutze's Washington Crossing the Delaware.

parts.label: C
parts.question: Grant Wood also created this painting, depicting a farmer standing next to his daughter and holding a pitchfork in front of a house in Eldon, Iowa.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: One of this painting’s central figures wears a rick-racked collar and a cameo brooch and looks uncertainly to her left in front of the Dibble House in Iowa. This painting’s models were a (*) dentist and the artist’s sister, Nan, who insisted that this painting did not depict a man and his wife. For ten points, name this painting by Grant Wood in which a somber-looking woman and a man holding a pitchfork stand side-by-side, looking at the viewer.

topics.description: The ancient Roman amphitheater in Rome, commissioned under the Flavian emperors and used for gladiatorial contests, animal hunts, staged naval battles, and other public spectacles.

parts.label: L
parts.question: This emperor’s last words were “dear me, I think I’m becoming a god.” For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this emperor, who put down the Great Jewish Revolt alongside his son, Titus. This man emerged  victorious after the Year of the Four Emperors.

parts.label: B
parts.question: Vespasian constructed this Roman amphitheater, which hosted many mock naval battles and gladiator fights.

parts.label: C
parts.question: Vespasian fell asleep during one of this emperor’s recitals and was exiled for a year. This emperor did not  actually fiddle while Rome burned.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: The hypogeum beneath this structure contained tunnels to transport exotic animals for venatores to hunt. In this structure, the pollice verso thumb gesture signaled the fate of defeated competitors. Vespasian began building this structure, alternatively called the (*) Flavian Amphitheater. Mock naval battles and gladiatorial fights were performed in, for 10 points, what large Roman arena?

topics.description: Chicago is the John Kander and Fred Ebb musical, choreographed and directed by Bob Fosse, about murderers Roxie Hart and Velma Kelly seeking fame and acquittal in Jazz Age Illinois.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Name the following musicals with famous dance sequences, for ten points each.

parts.label: A
parts.question: This Rodgers and Hammerstein musical essentially invented the dream ballet, a sequence in which the dance advances the plot and no singing takes place, in its Act 1 finale in which Laurey realizes she loves Curly, not Jud. This musical ends with Laurey and her new husband leaving for their honeymoon in the surrey with the fringe on top.

parts.label: B
parts.question: Gillian Lynne choreographed the Jellicle Ball in this Andrew Lloyd Webber musical, whose singing roles include Skimbleshanks.

parts.label: C
parts.question: Bob Fosse’s signature jazz hands are used throughout this musical, in which Roxie Hart and Velma Kelly try to get acquitted of murder in Illinois during the Jazz Age.

parts.label: L
parts.question: A director with this last name collaborated with performer Gene Kelly on films like An American in Paris and Brigadoon. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [H] Give this last name of that director, Vincente. A performer with this last name, Liza, rose to prominence by playing Sally Bowles in Bob Fosse’s musical film Cabaret.
parts.answer: Minnelli [accept Liza Minnelli or Vincente Minnelli]

parts.label: B
parts.question: [M] Liza Minnelli worked with Fosse again when she subbed in for Gwen Verdon on the original production of this musical, which opens with the song “All That Jazz.” The 1996 revival of this musical is now the second longest-running show on Broadway.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [E] Liza Minnelli is one of the few performers to have won an EGOT, meaning she has won an Emmy, a Grammy, an Oscar, and one of these awards. These awards recognize performances live on Broadway.
parts.answer: Tony Awards [or Antoinette Perry Award for Excellence in Broadway Theater]

topics.description: A musical by Lin-Manuel Miranda dramatizing the life of Founding Father Alexander Hamilton through hip-hop, R&B, and other contemporary musical styles.

parts.label: L
parts.question: For 10 points each, answer the following about musicals that feature U.S. Presidents:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [M] In this musical, residents of a shantytown offer a toast to Herbert Hoover in the number “We’d Like to Thank You (Herbert Hoover).” Later, this musical’s title character meets FDR and reprises a song about a time when “the sun will come out.”

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] Characters perform a rap-battle to win George Washington’s support in this musical’s “Cabinet Battle #1,” which quotes a song by Grandmaster Flash. This Lin-Manuel Miranda musical is titled for a Founding Father.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [H] John Wilkes Booth sings, “Move your little finger and you can change the world” in this musical’s “Gun Song,” which precedes a ballad about killing President McKinley. Other characters in this Stephen Sondheim musical include Charles Guiteau and Lee Harvey Oswald.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Answer the following about recent winners of the Tony award for Best Musical, for 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: This Lin-Manuel Miranda musical retelling the stories of the Founding Fathers with a nonwhite cast won a whopping 11 Awards at the 2016 Tonys, including Best Musical. It recounts the life and death of the title "Bastard orphan".

parts.label: B
parts.question: Hadestown, the most recent best musical winner, is a jazzy retelling of the tale of this Greek mythological figure, who has to rescue his wife Eurydice from the underworld.

parts.label: C
parts.question: 2018's winner was this musical following the experience of the Alexandria Police Orchestra’s trip to a remote Israeli town for a day after a clerk misunderstands their accent and sells them bus tickets to the wrong destination.

topics.description: Gioachino Rossini's grand opera about the Swiss hero William Tell and his resistance to the Austrian governor Gessler.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: In one opera by this composer, the title character sings his name several times in the aria “Largo al Factotum”. One opera by this composer sees a soldier shoot an apple off of Jemmy’s head. That opera’s overture contains a galloping “March of the Swiss Soldiers”. Count Almaviva and Rosina are married while (*) Figaro looks on in one opera by this composer. For 10 points, what Italian wrote music for operas such as The Barber of Seville and William Tell?

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: In an opera by this composer, Clorinda and Tisbe's father hides Angelina, who falls in love  with Prince Ramiro. This composer wrote an opera in which the female lead sings the aria “Deh!  tu reggi in tal momento” (DEH TOO rej-ee in TAL moh-MAIN-toh) from a scaffold. This composer of  La Cenerentola (lah CHAY-nay-REN-toh-lah) wrote an opera that includes a (*) galop called the  “March of the Swiss Soldiers” and centers on Gessler forcing the protagonist to shoot an arrow through  an apple on Jemmy's head. For 10 points, name this Italian composer of Cinderella, The Thieving  Magpie, and William Tell.

topics.description: Austrian composer and violinist renowned for popularizing the Viennese waltz, including The Blue Danube and Tales from the Vienna Woods.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: One work by a composer with this last name is played by string instruments without bows and is called the Pizzicato Polka. The movie 2001: A Space Odyssey featured music by two composers of this last name, including one with a rising C-G-C motif titled Also Sprach Zarathustra and another titled The (*) Blue Danube Waltz. For ten points, give the last name of the Austrian composer Johann and the German composer Richard.
parts.answer: Strauss [accept Richard Strauss or Johann Strauss II “the Younger”; do not accept or prompt on Johann Strauss I]

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: Musical works in this style include Tales from the Vienna Woods and a “Grand” and “Brilliant” one by Chopin [shoh-PAN]. The polka evolved from this slower dance style, but while the polka is in duple meter, this dance for turning partners is in triple meter. This ballroom dance, and its accompanying music, is characterized by an “OOM-pah-pah” rhythm. Johann Strauss wrote many of, for ten points, what kind of dance music exemplified by the “Blue Danube” one?
parts.answer: waltzes (prompt on “dance” or “dance music” before “dance” is read)

topics.description: An early-20th-century avant-garde artistic and literary movement associated with antiwar attitudes, absurdity, chance, collage, and anti-art techniques.

parts.label: L
parts.question: The sound poem “Gadji beri bimba” was written by one member of this art movement, Hugo Ball. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [M] Name this art movement. Another member of this movement created a series of readymades that included a urinal signed “R. Mutt” that was rejected from an exhibition with a no-rejection policy.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] That urinal, Fountain, was created by Marcel Duchamp, who also drew a mustache and a beard on this painting in his readymade L.H.O.O.Q. This painting by Leonardo da Vinci depicts a woman with an enigmatic smile.
parts.answer: Mona Lisa [or La Gioconda or La Joconde]

parts.label: C
parts.question: [H] Duchamp was photographed cross-dressing as his alter-ego Rose Sélavy by this other Dada artist. This artist also showed Kiki de Montparnasse holding a mask while resting her head on a table in the photograph Noire et Blanche.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Answer the following about flarf poetry, for 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [M] Writing flarf poetry involves using search engines as phrase generators and assembling the results into poems, similar to this movement’s use of the cut-up technique. This movement, whose members included Hugo Ball and Tristan Tzara, allegedly took its name from a French term for “hobbyhorse.”

parts.label: B
parts.question: [H] Flarf poet K. Silem Mohammad wrote a poem titled for “[these animals] [coming] hither in great numbers.” A Charles Baudelaire poem titled for these animals opens “Andromache, I think of you!”

parts.label: C
parts.question: [E] In a flarf poem, Sharon Mesmer claimed that her “soul still radiates luminous intensity” despite a “stupid” job at one of these places. Mesmer studied under Allen Ginsberg while at one of these institutions of higher learning.
parts.answer: ANSWER: a university [or a college; accept “Stupid University Job”]

topics.description: The practice and art of creating decorative, representational, or geometric forms by folding paper, traditionally without cutting or gluing.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: Friedrich Fröbel, who invented kindergarten, names a star made of this material used to teach children geometry. Refugees from the ship Golden Venture popularized using interlocking triangular modular forms of this material, prototypically to make swans. Imitations of gold and silver (*) yuanbao ingots made of this material are used at funerals. The tradition of making 1000 of one item from this material to grant a wish originates from the story of Sadako Sasaki, a Hiroshima survivor. “Valleys” and “mountains” are types of steps for manipulating this material, which is used to make iconic cranes. For 10 points, name this material which is folded in the art of origami.
parts.answer: paper [or origami paper or kami or zhi]

parts.label: L
parts.question: The Huzita-Hatori axioms govern operations that can be done when creating this art form. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [E] Name this Japanese art form made by folding paper.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [M] In the technique of renzuru, a sheet of paper is folded and cut into a group of these animals. The Hiroshima victim Sadako Sasaki partook in a tradition of folding one thousand of these animals to grant a wish from the gods.
parts.answer: paper crane [or red-crowned crane; or orizuru]

parts.label: C
parts.question: [H] This most famous origami artist contributed the technique of wet-folding. Along with Randlett, he also names a system of diagramming folding steps.

topics.topic: Beethoven’s Symphony No. 5 in C minor, Op. 67
topics.description: Ludwig van Beethoven’s celebrated Fifth Symphony, recognized for its opening short-short-short-long motif and 1808 premiere.

parts.label: L
parts.question: The superstitious composer Gustav Mahler steadfastly refused to give his Song of the Earth its rightful status as a numbered symphony because, having seen what happened to men like Anton Bruckner and Franz Schubert, he was afraid of this number. For ten points each,

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this number, the subject of a supposed “curse” on the composers of symphonies.
parts.answer: nine (accept ninth; accept additional information like ninth symphony)

parts.label: B
parts.question: The “curse of the ninth” is said to have started with this German composer, who was totally deaf when he conducted the premier of his Choral ninth symphony.

parts.label: C
parts.question: Before he succumbed to the curse of the ninth, Beethoven gave a massive concert in December 1808 where he premiered his Pastoral Symphony and this piece. This symphony doesn’t have a nickname, but it does feature Beethoven’s famous “short-short-short-long” motif.
parts.answer: Fifth Symphony (accept Symphony Number 5 in C minor)

parts.label: L
parts.question: Name some symphonies written by Ludwig van Beethoven, for ten points each.

parts.label: A
parts.question: This middle symphony by Beethoven has a “fate knocking at the door” motif with a dramatic “short-short-short-long” pattern.
parts.answer: Symphony Number Five in C minor (accept Beethoven’s fifth symphony)

parts.label: B
parts.question: Beethoven originally meant to dedicate this symphony to Napoleon. After Napoleon declared himself emperor of France, Beethoven scratched out the dedication and renamed it “Heroic” or “Eroica.”
parts.answer: Symphony Number Three in E-flat major (accept Beethoven’s third symphony; accept Eroica Symphony or Sinfonia Eroica before it is read)

parts.label: C
parts.question: Although most Beethoven symphonies have four movements, this symphony has five. Each movement represents a different time of day by depicting a “Merry gathering of country folk” and a “Scene by the brook.”
parts.answer: Symphony Number Six in F Major (accept Beethoven’s sixth symphony; accept Pastoral Symphony or Pastorale)

topics.description: Sandro Botticelli was a Florentine Early Renaissance painter known for mythological works including Primavera and The Birth of Venus.
aliases: Alessandro di Mariano di Vanni Filipepi

parts.label: L
parts.question: In a painting of this season, Flora reaches into a pocket of flowers in her dress while, next to her, a blue Zephyrus grabs Chloris. For ten points each,

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this season represented allegorically in a painting set in an orange grove. In the painting, the three Graces dance in a circle to welcome this season of rebirth.
parts.answer: spring (accept Primavera; accept Allegory of Spring)

parts.label: B
parts.question: The Allegory of Spring, or Primavera, was painted by this Renaissance artist from Florence. This artist made several mythological paintings for his patrons, the Medici family.
parts.answer: Sandro Botticelli (accept Alessandro di Mariano di Vanni Filipepi)

parts.label: C
parts.question: Flora, Chloris and Zephyrus also appear in this other mythological Botticelli painting, which depicts the title Roman goddess being blown to shore while standing on a seashell in this painting
parts.answer: The Birth of Venus (accept Nascita di Venere; do not accept or prompt on “Venus” alone; do not accept or prompt on “Aphrodite”)

parts.label: L
parts.question: Zephyrus blows the central figure of this painting towards the shore. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [H] Name this painting depicting the creation of the title goddess, who rides a seashell.
parts.answer: The Birth of Venus [or Nascita di Venere]

parts.label: B
parts.question: [M] This Italian artist painted The Birth of Venus as well as various mythological figures frolicking in an orange grove in Primavera.
parts.answer: Sandro Botticelli [or Alessandro di Mariano di Vanni Filipepi]

parts.label: C
parts.question: [E] Botticelli’s Mystical Nativity is set shortly after the birth of this religious figure, and features the Virgin Mary and Joseph.

topics.description: A rounded or polygonal architectural roof or structure that spans and encloses space, including onion domes, Brunelleschi’s dome on Florence Cathedral, and the Pantheon’s dome.

parts.label: L
parts.question: The Florence Cathedral was built despite the fact that, at the time, there was no known way to produce one of these structures large enough to finish it. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [10] Name this type of architectural element. Many Russian churches contain numerous examples of their "onion" types.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [10] This architect designed the dome on top of the Florence Cathedral after it had spent almost a hundred years unfinished.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [10] Another Italian Renaissance-era dome tops the St. Peter's Basilica, the most important church in this smallest country in the world. It is the home of the Pope and the headquarters of the Catholic Church.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Andrea Mantegna used foreshortening, a form of this technique, in The Lamentation over the Dead Christ. For  10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this technique, which artists use to depict three-dimensional space on a flat canvas. Further objects are  shown as smaller in this technique, in which parallel lines are drawn such that they converge at a vanishing point.

parts.label: B
parts.question: This Italian artist used a mirror in order to rediscover linear perspective. This artist lost a contest against  Lorenzo Ghiberti for the commission for the doors to the Florence Baptistry.

parts.label: C
parts.question: Brunelleschi designed an octagonal brick one of these features for the Florentine Cathedral. One of these  features in the Pantheon features an oculus.

topics.description: A visual-art genre depicting arranged inanimate objects such as food, flowers, vessels, books, and skulls.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: This artistic genre was the lowest on the French Academy's hierarchy of painting. Francisco  Zurbarán (zoor-boo-RAHN) pioneered a Spanish subgenre of this kind of art called bodegónes (boh-day-HOH-nays). This artistic genre was the main output of Dutch artists Rachel Ruysch (rah-SHEL  rowsh) and Clara Peeters. Several paintings in this genre depict (*) skulls stacked on top of each  other. Paul Cezanne (say-ZAHN) often included apples in examples of this genre. For 10 points, name  this genre of painting that depicts inanimate objects.

parts.label: L
parts.question: These objects are typically featured in Memento mori paintings. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name these human remains that frequently symbolize death in art. This skeletal structure protects the brain and supports the face.

parts.label: B
parts.question: This American artist painted skulls of horses, cows, and deer. After living in New York, she moved to New Mexico and painted many depictions of its landscape.

parts.label: C
parts.question: Skulls were sometimes featured in paintings of this genre. More popular subjects in this genre include flowers and baskets of fruit.

topics.description: A large circular window with radiating tracery, often filled with stained glass, characteristic of Gothic churches and cathedrals.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: Rangoli carpets made of these objects are popular during the Onam festival. Earth, humanity, and heaven are unified by these objects in ikebana. Victorian society developed a “language” of these objects to express unspoken feelings such as virtue and chastity. Crescent, cascading, and nosegay are three ways to arrange these objects, which are bound by doilies. These objects name wheel-like (*) windows that appear in Gothic churches. Boutonnieres and corsages containing these objects are worn at weddings, where brides traditionally carry a bouquet of them. For 10 points, name these objects that include daffodils and carnations.
parts.answer: ANSWER: flowers [accept specific types of flowers such as roses; accept daffodils and carnations before they are read; accept hana; accept pookolam; prompt on bouquet before mention with "A bouquet of what?"]

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: A kind of this material similar to milk, called lattimo, was made by producers on the Venetian island of Murano. Dale Chihuly is an artist best known for working with this material, which makes up the shade of Tiffany lamps. This material can be shaped by blowing into a hollow clay rod. This material is used in circular “rose” apertures on the walls of many Gothic cathedrals. For 10 points, name this material, which is “stained” in many church windows.

topics.description: The artistic and documentary practice of creating images by recording light with a camera or other imaging device.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: The book The Decisive Moment is a collection of works of art in this medium by Henri Cartier-Bresson, who pioneered its “street” variety. An early process for creating art in this medium was created by Louis Daguerre, and required very long (*) exposure times. Artists who create work in this medium may utilize a darkroom to develop film. For 10 points, name this artistic medium whose practitioners use cameras to capture images.

parts.label: L
parts.question: A man jumps into a puddle over a ladder in an example of this artistic discipline called Behind Gare  Saint-Lazare (GAR saan laa-ZAR). For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [10] The creator of Behind Gare St. Lazare, Henri Cartier-Bresson (ahn-REE KAR-tee-BRAY-sahn) advanced the theory of “the decisive moment” governing what field of art?
parts.answer: photography [or taking photographs; prompt on taking pictures; prompt on using film]

parts.label: B
parts.question: [10] The cover for Cartier-Bresson's book Images on the Sly was created by this Fauvist (FOE-vist) artist  whose paintings include The Joy of Life.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [10] Cartier-Bresson photographed this man an hour before his assassination. Margaret Bourke-White  photographed this political activist near a spinning wheel symbolizing the swadeshi (swah-DEE-shee) initiative.
parts.answer: Mohandas Gandhi [Mohandas Karamchand Gandhi; or Mahatma Gandhi]

topics.description: An American composer, conductor, pianist, and educator known for composing West Side Story and leading the New York Philharmonic.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: One character in this musical describes "knobs on the doors" and "wall-to-wall floors" as attractions of moving from Puerto Rico to New York in the song "America". This musical's song "I Feel Pretty" is sung by Maria, who holds her lover (*) Tony as he dies. For 10 points, name this musical inspired by Romeo and Juliet about a gang war between the Jets and the Sharks, composed by Leonard Bernstein.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: A repeated motif in this musical begins with a tritone that represents Bernardo’s sister. A song in this musical alternates between three-four and six-eight time to describe a place where “industry booms” but there are “twelve in a room.” In this musical, (*) “America” is sung by the Sharks, members of a Puerto Rican gang that opposes the white Jets. For ten points, name this Leonard Bernstein musical in which Tony and Maria’s doomed love retells the story of Romeo and Juliet in 1950s New York.

topics.description: German late-Romantic and 20th-century composer known for tone poems, operas such as Der Rosenkavalier and Elektra, and Also sprach Zarathustra.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: One work by a composer with this last name is played by string instruments without bows and is called the Pizzicato Polka. The movie 2001: A Space Odyssey featured music by two composers of this last name, including one with a rising C-G-C motif titled Also Sprach Zarathustra and another titled The (*) Blue Danube Waltz. For ten points, give the last name of the Austrian composer Johann and the German composer Richard.
parts.answer: Strauss [accept Richard Strauss or Johann Strauss II “the Younger”; do not accept or prompt on Johann Strauss I]

parts.label: L
parts.question: The Marschallin (MAR-shaa-lin) and Sophie have a love triangle with a mezzo-soprano (MET-soh-suh-prah-noh) in a “breeches role” in this opera. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this comic opera in which Octavian gives Sophie a silver flower.
parts.answer: Der Rosenkavalier (dair ROH-zen-KAA-vuh-leer) [or The Knight of the Rose]

parts.label: B
parts.question: This other opera by the composer of Der Rosenkavalier and librettist Hugo von Hofmannsthal  (HOO-goh vahn HAHF-manz-stahl) is named for a character who joyously dances herself to death. She is  the sister of Orestes (or-EST-eez) who, in the opera, avenges her father Agamemnon (ag-uh-MEM-non).

parts.label: C
parts.question: This composer wrote both Der Rosenkavalier and Elektra. He shares his surname with the “Waltz  King” who composed The Blue Danube.

topics.description: Art that emphasizes color, form, line, composition, and ideas rather than directly representing recognizable subjects from reality.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Dutch painter Piet Mondrian [PEET MON-dree-yon] created Broadway Boogie-Woogie with these colors among thick black lines and white squares. For ten points each,

parts.label: A
parts.question: Give the term that refers to the pigments red, yellow, and blue.

parts.label: B
parts.question: Mondrian’s late works, like Broadway Boogie-Woogie, are the geometric form of this type of work, contrasted with realistic art. Mondrian represented ideas instead of images of reality.
parts.answer: abstract art (accept word forms like abstraction; accept geometric abstract art)

parts.label: C
parts.question: In the 1960s, Mondrian’s work was adapted by Yves Saint Laurent [EEV sawn lah-RAWN] into this art form. The adaptation transformed Mondrian’s geometric designs into A-line works in this art form.
parts.answer: fashion (accept clothes; accept descriptions like wearable art; accept dresses)

parts.label: L
parts.question: A series of color field paintings by Barnett Newman is titled “Who’s Afraid of [these three colors]?” For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name these three primary colors.
parts.answer: red, yellow, and blue [accept answers in any order as long as all three are present]

parts.label: B
parts.question: With Theo van Doesburg, this painter founded De Stijl, an art movement which used only black, white, and the primary colors. Yellow squares represent taxis in this painter’s Broadway Boogie-Woogie.

parts.label: C
parts.question: The painter of Yellow, Red, Blue, Wassily Kandinsky, was a pioneer of this type of art. Jackson Pollock was part of a movement known as “[this word] expressionism.”

topics.description: El Greco was a Greek-born Spanish Mannerist painter known for expressive religious works, portraits, and landscapes including The View of Toledo.

parts.label: L
parts.question: For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [M] Name this artist who painted The Disrobing of Christ. This mannerist artist depicted the Alcázar Citadel on the right as a storm gathers in the background in his View of Toledo.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] El Greco was one of many artists to depict this woman’s assumption into heaven. El Greco also depicted the archangel Gabriel appearing to this mother of Jesus in his Annunciation.
parts.answer: Virgin Mary [or Madonna, or the Virgin; accept The Assumption of the Virgin or The Assumption of Mary]

parts.label: C
parts.question: [H] This painting by El Greco shows St. John raising his hands towards heaven to the left of the canvas while angels cover naked figures in robes in the background. Picasso studied this painting while creating Les Demoiselles d’Avignon.
parts.answer: The Opening of the Fifth Seal [or The Fifth Seal of Apocalypse or The Vision of Saint John or Profane Love; do NOT accept or prompt on “Sacred and Profane Love,” which is by Titian]

parts.label: L
parts.question: This artist depicted Saint Stephen and Saint Augustine entombing Don Gonzalo Ruiz in his painting The Burial of the Count of Orgaz. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this artist who also painted a famous landscape of his hometown, titled View of Toledo. He is commonly known by a name indicating his country of birth.

parts.label: B
parts.question: Although he was born in Greece, El Greco lived in this country. Diego Velasquez was a court painter of this country's king Philip IV, who ruled both it and its neighboring country, Portugal.

parts.label: C
parts.question: This is the most famous painting by Velasquez. It shows the young Spanish princess Margaret Theresa in Velasquez's studio surrounded by an entourage including two maids as well as Velasquez himself painting on a huge easel.
parts.answer: Las Meninas [or The Ladies in Waiting, or The Maids of Honor]

topics.description: Diego Rivera's 1932–1933 cycle of fresco murals depicting industrial labor and technology at the Detroit Institute of Arts.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: Chris Burden was nailed shirtless to one of these objects in his performance art piece Trans-Fixed. Works made from these objects are found at an Art Reserve in Nebraska, where Jim Reinders created a replica of Stonehenge using them. The Aztec gods are invoked in a 27-panel mural series depicting laborers creating these objects by Diego Rivera. One of these objects is declared to be “more beautiful than the Victory of Samothrace” in the (*) Futurist Manifesto. 1960s hippies often had brightly-painted examples of these objects with their logos replaced by a peace sign. For 10 points, name these objects manufactured by companies like Volkswagen.
parts.answer: automobiles [or cars; or minibuses; accept Carhenge; accept specific brands of cars]

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: An artwork of this type was destroyed on the orders of Nelson Rockefeller because it depicted Vladimir Lenin, and was called Man at the Crossroads. A work of this type that shows Plato and Aristotle walking together is Raphael’s The (*) School of Athens. A set of these artworks depicting Industry were created by Diego Rivera to line a room in the Detroit Institute of Art. These artworks that are called “frescoes” when they are painted on wet plaster. For ten points, name this type of painting done on a wall.
parts.answer: murals (accept frescoes before it is read; prompt on “painting” before “painted” is read; do not accept or prompt on “graffiti”)

topics.description: Auguste Rodin was a French sculptor known for works including The Thinker, The Burghers of Calais, and The Kiss.

parts.label: L
parts.question: A sculpture featuring one of these animals in St. Petersburg’s Senate Square depicts Peter the Great. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [E] What animals are featured being ridden by humans in equestrian statues?

parts.label: B
parts.question: [H] That aforementioned sculpture was created by Étienne Falconet out of this material. Artists who sculpt in this material may use plaster molds and the “lost wax” method to “cast” it.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [M] Along with Falconet, this other French artist often sculpted in bronze. This artist’s bronzes include The Burghers of Calais and The Thinker.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: A cast of this sculpture in Meudon sits over its creator’s grave. This bronze sculpture was intended to sit under The Three Shades at the top of the (*) Gates of Hell, and was originally named The Poet, since it depicts Dante Alighieri contemplating the sinners he wrote about in the Inferno. For ten points, name this Auguste Rodin [ow-GOOST roh-DAN] sculpture in which a seated man leans forward pensively with his chin on his hand.
parts.answer: The Thinker (accept Le penseur; accept The Poet or Le poete ` before “Poet” is read)

topics.description: Anish Kapoor’s monumental polished-stainless-steel public sculpture in Chicago’s Millennium Park, popularly known as The Bean.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Answer the following about sculptor Anish Kapoor. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: Anish Kapoor is perhaps most famous for this sculpture in Chicago’s Millennium Park, nicknamed “the Bean.”

parts.label: B
parts.question: Cloud Gate is a popular selfie spot because it is made of the reflective “stainless” variety of this iron alloy.

parts.label: C
parts.question: Anish Kapoor has faced backlash from many artists for buying the exclusive artistic rights to a coating of this  color, which was made using VANTA nanotubes.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Lorado Taft taught sculpture at this city’s Art Institute, a museum whose entrance is flanked by two bronze lions. For ten points each,

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this major US city where the Pritzker Pavilion and Crown Fountain can be found in Millennium Park. Burnham Park and Jackson Park are also along this city’s Lake Michigan shoreline.

parts.label: B
parts.question: Millennium Park’s most photographed artwork is this Anish Kapoor sculpture of polished stainless steel. You can give either its official name or its very popular nickname.

parts.label: C
parts.question: South of Millennium Park and the Art Institute is one of the world’s largest examples of these artistic water features, a memorial for Clarence Buckingham.

topics.description: Objects made by shaping clay or other ceramic materials and hardening them through firing, including earthenware, stoneware, and porcelain.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: The lustre (“luster”) variety of these works were developed in the Islamic world as a substitute for gold gilding. Works of this type from the Chenghua era depicting chickens feature vivid red and greens achieved through the doucai (“doh-tsai”) technique. Imperfections in these works are highlighted with metallic powder in the kintsugi (“KEEN-tsoo-ghee”) method. Mass production of these works can be achieved with the slipcasting. Works of this type produced at (*) Jingdezhen (“jing-duh-juhn”) used cobalt glaze to achieve a distinctive blue and white coloring. The term “throwing” refers to the shaping of these works by hand on a rapidly spinning wheel. For 10 points, name these works made of materials like clay and porcelain.
parts.answer: pottery [accept ceramics or wares; accept porcelain before mention; prompt on vases or cups or bowls or plates by asking “what more general type of artworks do they exemplify?”]

parts.label: L
parts.question: A certain city’s boule oversaw the process for dealing this kind of punishment, which required 6000 votes to be carried out. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [M] Name this kind of punishment,which was dealt to people who were ostracized in ancient Athens.
parts.answer: exiled [or banished or expelled; accept ostracized before mentioned]

parts.label: B
parts.question: [H] This man’s father, Xanthippus, was recalled from exile during the Second Persian invasion of Greece. This leader during Athen’s Golden Age delivered a notable funeral oration during the Peloponnesian War.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [E] Voting on ostracisms was done using shards of this material. This material is fired in kilns to make artworks like pots and vases.

topics.description: A musical performance technique involving a regular or rapid slight fluctuation in pitch, produced instrumentally or vocally.

parts.label: L
parts.question: You're trying to emulate a violin. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [H] You might use this flexible electronic instrument championed by Wendy Carlos that creates waveforms and uses filters and envelopes to change its characteristics.
parts.answer: synthesizer [accept specific types of synthesizers such as analog synthesizer or Moog synthesizer]

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] Like violins, most synthesizers are able to produce sounds with varying levels of this property. This property related to frequency determines how "low" or "high" a sound is.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [M] You might use low-frequency oscillations to emulate this effect on a synthesizer. Violinists create this pulsating change in pitch by wobbling their fingers from side to side.

parts.label: L
parts.question: For 10 points each, answer the following about the Japanese popular music genre enka:

parts.label: A
parts.question: Because the genre is popular with older generations of Japanese and represents a romanticized view of traditions, many female enka singers wear this traditional Japanese garment secured by an obi sash.

parts.label: B
parts.question: A key characteristic of enka is the vocal technique of kobushi, which is often compared to this technique in Western music. For string instruments, this technique involves “wobbling” the finger on the fingerboard.
parts.answer: vibrato [do NOT accept or prompt on “tremolo”]

parts.label: C
parts.question: The yona nuki scale used by many enka songs omits the fourth and seventh of the Western scale, making it effectively one of these scales common in East Asian music that can be played on a piano’s black keys.

topics.description: A Rodgers and Hammerstein musical set in Oklahoma Territory and centered on Laurey's courtship by Curly and Jud.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Name the following musicals with famous dance sequences, for ten points each.

parts.label: A
parts.question: This Rodgers and Hammerstein musical essentially invented the dream ballet, a sequence in which the dance advances the plot and no singing takes place, in its Act 1 finale in which Laurey realizes she loves Curly, not Jud. This musical ends with Laurey and her new husband leaving for their honeymoon in the surrey with the fringe on top.

parts.label: B
parts.question: Gillian Lynne choreographed the Jellicle Ball in this Andrew Lloyd Webber musical, whose singing roles include Skimbleshanks.

parts.label: C
parts.question: Bob Fosse’s signature jazz hands are used throughout this musical, in which Roxie Hart and Velma Kelly try to get acquitted of murder in Illinois during the Jazz Age.

parts.label: L
parts.question: This composer wrote the music for musicals like A Connecticut Yankee and Babes in Arms. For ten points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [M] Name this composer who had a longtime partnership with lyricist Lorenz Hart. This composer collaborated on musicals like Carousel and South Pacific as part of a duo with Oscar Hammerstein.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [H] This Rodgers and Hammerstein musical features a rendition of Uncle Tom’s Cabin and the song “Getting to Know You.” This musical follows the story of a British teacher hired to tutor Thailand’s royal children.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [E] This musical, the first written by Rodgers and Hammerstein together, tells of Laurey’s courtship by rivals Curly and Jud. This musical is set in the title territory, which is now a state just north of Texas.

topics.description: A large-scale classical composition for orchestra, typically organized into multiple contrasting movements.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: Musical works of this type that are nicknamed Palindrome and Surprise are two of the one-hundred-four of these works written by their “father,” Joseph Haydn. Mahler wrote his “Song of the Earth” to avoid the “curse of the (*) ninth” associated with these works, and Brahms’s first one is nicknamed “Beethoven’s Tenth.” Four movements make up the modern form of, for ten points, what long musical works for full orchestra?
parts.answer: symphony (accept symphonies; accept New World Symphony or Symphony From the New World; accept Palindrome Symphony; accept Surprise Symphony; accept symphonies by Dvorak before “Palindrome” is read)

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: A supposed “curse” affected composers who wrote at least nine of these pieces. Gustav Mahler added a chorus and vocal soloists to the typical ensemble for one of these pieces, which was later nicknamed the one “of a Thousand”. Beethoven’s (*) fifth one of these employs a “short-short-short-long” motif, while his ninth features a chorus singing “Ode to Joy”. For 10 points, name this type of classical composition for a large orchestra.
parts.answer: symphony [accept Symphony of a Thousand or Beethoven’s Fifth Symphony or Beethoven’s Ninth Symphony]

topics.description: A crystalline carbonate stone, typically formed by metamorphism, valued for its polishability and widely used in sculpture, architecture, and monuments.

parts.label: L
parts.question: A black-and-white landscape by Lǐ Sōng depicts one of these features named for being west of Hangzhou (“hong-joe”). For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [H] Name these features. A Chinese gardening practice in which one of these features is paired with three hills informed the design of one of these features at the Summer Palace named Kūnmíng (“kwen-ming”).
parts.answer: lake [or hú; accept West Lake or Kunming Lake or Xī Hú or Kūnmíng Hú]

parts.label: B
parts.question: [M] The Empress Dowager Cíxī (“tsuh-shee”) commissioned a boat made of this material that still “floats” on Kūnmíng Lake. The Old Summer Palace contained a European-style mansion made of this material, which was worked by Antonio Canova and other Neoclassical sculptors.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [E] Kūnmíng Lake is crossed by a seventeen-arch one of these structures bedecked with marble lions. Marco Polo is the namesake of one of these structures in Beijing that crosses the Yǒngdìng River.
parts.answer: bridge [or qiáo; accept Seventeen-Arch Bridge or Marco Polo Bridge or Shíqīkǒng Qiáo or Lúgōu Qiáo]

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: Alexandros of Antioch used this substance to depict a half-nude goddess who may have been hand-spinning or holding an apple, although his work was originally attributed to Praxiteles [prack-SIH-tah-leez], who was a master of this material. This material was used to create (*) Hermes and the Infant Dionysus and a sculpture of Aphrodite whose arms have broken off, called the Venus de Milo. For ten points, name this material used to create Michelangelo’s David, a type of white stone.

topics.description: A traditional Australian Aboriginal wind instrument, typically a long hollow tube, played by vibrating the lips to produce a sustained drone.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: An island separated from this country’s mainland by the Bass Strait is the only native home of a carnivore that has been endangered by DFTD. This country’s eucalyptus trees are commonly used to make a native instrument called the didgeridoo. The (*) Tasmanian devil is endemic to this country, which is also home to most of the world’s marsupial species. For 10 points, name this home country of koalas and kangaroos, whose largest city is Sydney.

parts.label: L
parts.question: This ethnic group plays an instrument called a bullroarer during rituals. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this general ethnic group, whose “songlines” represent paths marking routes during The Dreaming. The Yolngu (YAHL-noo), a smaller people within this group, sing Bunggul (BUN-gool) songs.
parts.answer: Australian Aborigines [or Indigenous Australians; prompt on Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islanders]

parts.label: B
parts.question: Djalu Gurruwiwi (JAH-loo goo-roo-WEE-wee) and Mark Atkins play this Australian wooden instrument whose players vibrate their lips to produce a drone.

parts.label: C
parts.question: Aborigine instruments called bilma or clappers are similar to these musical items that are used to strike cymbals.

topics.description: An American musical genre characterized by syncopated rhythms, especially in piano music, and exemplified by works such as Scott Joplin’s “Maple Leaf Rag” and “The Entertainer.”

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: A composer from this country wrote pieces such as “The Thunderer” and “El Capitan.” Piano works including “Maple Leaf Rag” and “The Entertainer” were part of this country’s genre of (*) Ragtime music. A composer from this country names a tuba-like instrument intended for use while marching. For 10 points, John Philip Sousa wrote marches such as “The Stars and Stripes Forever” for what country’s military?
parts.answer: United States of America [or U.S. or U.S.A. or America]

parts.label: L
parts.question: Standards originally composed by this musician include the “King Porter Stomp” and “Dead Man’s Blues.” For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [H] Name this leader of the Red Hot Peppers who claimed to have invented jazz in an interview with Alan Lomax. The title of a Broadway show about this musician’s “Last Jam” puns on his nickname.
parts.answer: ANSWER: Jelly Roll Morton [accept either underlined; or Ferdinand Joseph La Menthe]

parts.label: B
parts.question: [M] Jelly Roll’s jazz emerged in part from improvising on songs in this genre like the “Maple Leaf.” Player pianos often play a 1902 song in this genre called “The Entertainer.”

parts.label: C
parts.question: [E] During an interview with Lomax, Jelly Roll and this musician bickered over scat singing with this artist explaining his song “Heebie Jeebies.” This trumpeter who led the Hot Five sang “What a Wonderful World” in a gravelly voice.
parts.answer: ANSWER: Louis Armstrong [accept Satchmo; accept Pops]

topics.description: American documentary photographer known for Depression-era photographs including Migrant Mother and images of the Manzanar internment camp.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: In a photo by this artist, two men walk past a billboard of a man in a recliner chair. Paul Taylor produced captions for this artist’s book An American Exodus, which includes a photo of a long New Mexico road. After Ansel Adams, this artist visited Manzanar to take gritty photos of children taking the Pledge of Allegiance. An old man leans against a wood fence in this photographer’s White Angel Breadline. While working for the Farm Security Administration, this artist photographed pea picker Florence Owens Thompson gazing into the distance as her children cling to her. For 10 points, name this photographer of Migrant Mother.

parts.label: L
parts.question: This man photographed a “moonrise” above Hernandez, New Mexico illuminating the crosses in a cemetery. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [H] Name this photographer, a member of the group f-stop-64. With Fred Archer, this photographer formulated the Zone System to determine the correct exposure to use in any lighting condition.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] In his “Mural Project,” Ansel Adams was commissioned to take pictures of these federally protected natural areas. Adams photographed Half Dome and El Capitan in Yosemite, another one of these places.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [M] Like Adams, this photographer took many photos of the Manzanar internment camp. This photographer is most famous for featuring Florence Owens Thompson in Migrant Mother.

topics.description: An unfinished basilica in Barcelona designed chiefly by Antoni Gaudí, combining Gothic and Catalan Modernist elements.
aliases: Temple Expiatori de la Sagrada Família

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: In this country, a roof arched like the back of a dragon and a turret representing St. George’s lance appear on top of the “House of Bones.” Josep Jujol [zhu-SHEP zhu-ZHOL] collaborated with an architect from this country to design a house nicknamed “The Stone Quarry.” The entrance to a park in this country contains a mosaic (*) salamander. Columns rest on the backs of turtles as a part of the Nativity Façade at a church in this country that is scheduled to finish on the hundredth anniversary of its architect’s death in 2026. For 10 points, the Park Güell and the La Sagrada Familia were designed by Antonio Gaudí in what country's city of Barcelona?
parts.answer: Spain [or Kingdom of Spain or España or Reino de España]

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: A palace in this country contains the Court of the Myrtles, and was built during the Nasrid Dynasty. In this country, an eighteen-spired cathedral combining Gothic and Art Nouveau styles has been under construction since 1882, and was designed by (*) Antoni Gaud´ı. The Alhambra in Granada is within, for ten points, what European country, where the Sagrada Familia cathedral is being built in Barcelona?
parts.answer: Spain (accept Kingdom of Spain; accept Reino de Espana˜ )

topics.description: Tintoretto was a Venetian Mannerist painter known for dramatic, dynamic compositions including multiple depictions of The Last Supper, The Miracle of the Slave, and The Origin of the Milky Way.

parts.label: L
parts.question: In a painting of this scene, Judas clutches a bag of silver while the other disciples react to the revelation that Jesus will be betrayed by one of them. For ten points each,

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this biblical scene. In a painting of this scene by Leonardo da Vinci, Jesus spreads his hands over the table where he and his disciples eat a meal together.

parts.label: B
parts.question: Judas kneels across the table from the other disciples in this artist’s diagonally-aligned painting of The Last Supper. This Italian Mannerist also painted Paradiso and The Miracle of the Slave.

parts.label: C
parts.question: Judas is absent from Albrecht Durer’s depictions of The Last Supper, which he created by printing with blocks of this material. To make block prints, artists carve along the grain of this natural material.

parts.label: L
parts.question: An artist who painted in this style depicted Heracles nursing at Hera's breast, from which stars appear.  For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [10] Name this style of The Origin of the Milky Way. Parmigianino's (PAR-mij-uh-NEE-noh's) Madonna  with the Long Neck is in this exaggerated style which Michelangelo used for many of his later paintings.
parts.answer: ANSWER: Mannerism [prompt on Late Renaissance style]

parts.label: B
parts.question: [10] The Origin of the Milky Way is by this Venetian Mannerist, who depicted a diagonal table and 500  people in his final painting.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [10] Tintoretto used the diagonal table in a depiction of this scene. Leonardo's version of this scene  shows Jesus and the disciples all on the same side of a table during a meal.

topics.description: A large keyboard instrument that produces sound by directing air through ranks or sets of tuned pipes, commonly used in churches and concert settings.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: The concerto for this instrument nicknamed “The Cuckoo and the Nightingale” was composed by G.F. Handel. A toccata and fugue in D minor for this instrument were written by Johann Sebastian Bach. Players of this instrument use (*) stops to control its sound and may operate a pedalclavier with their feet. For 10 points, name this large keyboard instrument often found in churches, which produces sound by moving air through pipes.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Johannes Ringk recorded the only known copy of a piece for this instrument, in which pedalboard notes are marked with a “p” instead of being written on a separate musical staff. For ten points each,

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this enormous keyboard instrument that pushes air through arrays of metal pipes.

parts.label: B
parts.question: This composer supposedly walked 250 miles to Lubeck to hear Dietrich Buxtehude, a famous organ player. This composer also wrote the Brandenburg Concertos and numerous fugues [fyoogs].

parts.label: C
parts.question: Bach wrote many works for the organ. Johannes Ringk recorded the sheet music for Bach’s Prelude and Fugue in this minor key, which has one flat.

topics.description: Dmitri Shostakovich was a Russian and Soviet composer whose works include fifteen symphonies, concertos, string quartets, and the opera Lady Macbeth of the Mtsensk District.

parts.label: L
parts.question: This composer prominently used the DSCH motif through many of his works. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this man, who composed his Fifth Symphony as a “response to justified criticism” of his opera Lady Macbeth of the Mtsensk District.

parts.label: B
parts.question: Shostakovich quoted the DSCH motif in his concerto in E-flat major for this instrument. This stringed instrument is also played by Yo-Yo Ma.

parts.label: C
parts.question: Shostakovich used the DSCH motif in every movement of his 8th work in this genre. This genre typically consists of two violins, a viola, and a cello.

parts.label: L
parts.question: The first movement of this composer’s fifteenth and final symphony repeatedly quotes from Rossini’s William Tell overture. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [M] Name this composer. His fifteenth symphony includes his “D, E-flat, C, B” or “D-S-C-H” monogram, and its finale is reminiscent of the “invasion theme” he wrote in a previous symphony.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] The finale of Shostakovich’s fifteenth symphony quotes the fate motif from Die Walküre, an opera by this German composer of the Ring cycle.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [H] The finale of Shostakovich’s final composition, a sonata for viola and piano, paraphrases the repeated rising right-hand triplets G-sharp, C-sharp, E that begin this piece. A slow adagio sostenuto comprises the first movement of this Beethoven piece.
parts.answer: Moonlight Sonata [or Piano Sonata No. 14 or Fourteenth Piano Sonata or Opus 27 No. 2; prompt on partial answers]

topics.description: Maurice Ravel's 1928 orchestral composition characterized by a continuously repeated ostinato, especially the snare-drum pattern, and gradually intensifying orchestration.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: An instrument of this type plays a continuous ostinato for the entirety of Maurice Ravel's Boléro. The tabla is an Indian instrument of this type. A metal kind of this instrument popular in Caribbean music can play several different notes and is called its (*) "steel" type. Timpanis are large, tunable examples of, for 10 points, what percussion instruments with "bass" and "snare" types?
parts.answer: drums [accept specific types of drums; prompt on percussion until mention]

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: It’s not Rimsky-Korsakov, but this composer wrote his Scheherazade Overture during his time at the Paris Conservatoire. A six-movement suite by this composer uses an antique Baroque structure and has sections named for dances like the Forlane and Rigaudon. This composer wanted to exceed the difficulty of Balakirev’s Islamey with the final movement, (*) Scarbo, of a three-part solo piano suite. This composer commemorated seven friends who died in World War I with his Le Tombeau de Couperin. Another orchestral composition by this composer includes 169 repetitions of a snare drum ostinato. For 10 points, name this French Impressionist composer of Boléro.

topics.description: An acting approach associated with Konstantin Stanislavski that emphasizes psychologically inhabiting a character and drawing on the character's memories, motivations, and experiences.

parts.label: L
parts.question: This author thinks “It’s more real to me here than if I went up” while outside the Paris apartment of his former lover. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [H] Name this New York socialite who questions his recent engagement to May Welland after seeing Ellen Olenska during a performance of Faust in the novel The Age of Innocence.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] This author’s autobiography A Backwards Glance revealed that Newland Archer was inspired by her own time with “old money” in New York. She wrote the Age of Innocence and Ethan Frome.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [M] Daniel Day-Lewis walked with a cane on and off the set of Martin Scorcese’s adaptation of The Age of Innocence as part of this acting technique developed by Konstantin Stanislavski in which actors try to embody their characters’ memories and motivations by acting exactly like them.

parts.label: L
parts.question: It’s Morbin’ time! Answer the following about Morbius, the (sarcasm) INCREDIBLY WELL-RECEIVED film that has 138% positive reviews on Rotten Tomatoes, for ten points each.

parts.label: A
parts.question: Morbius is based on a Marvel character known as the “Living” one of these common monsters that suck blood from their victims to survive.

parts.label: B
parts.question: This actor basically killed the “Morbin’ time” meme by acknowledging it on Twitter. In addition to Morbius, this man made a nuisance of himself while playing Joker in Suicide Squad.

parts.label: C
