parts.question: Leto keeps making himself impossible to work with because of his approach to this acting style. This system of acting was created by Konstantin Stanislavski, and demands that actors stay in character both in and out of scenes.

topics.description: American jazz singer celebrated for her precise vocal technique, improvisational scat singing, and interpretations of the Great American Songbook.

parts.label: L
parts.question: The hit song “You're the Top” was composed by this man for the musical Anything Goes. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this composer whose songs include “Begin the Beguine” (beh-GEEN) and “Night and Day.”

parts.label: B
parts.question: This singer's first songbook featured many of Porter's songs including “I Get a Kick Out of You.” This “First Lady of Song” was known for her scat singing.

parts.label: C
parts.question: Many of Porter's songs including “Well, Did You Evah!” were written during this decade. Glenn Miller's “In the Mood” competed with “God Bless America” as the most popular song of this decade, in which Bessie Smith died.

parts.label: L
parts.question: This musician featured an extended scat section quoting from Charlie Parker’s “Ornithology” in the version of “How High the Moon” she recorded in Berlin. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [M] Name this jazz singer. This “First Lady of Song” reworked a nursery rhyme about a “brown and yellow basket” for her song “A Tisket, A Tasket.”

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] With this other jazz artist, Fitzgerald released three collaboration albums, including a set of excerpts from Porgy and Bess. This jazz trumpeter sang about “trees of green / Red roses too” in “What a Wonderful World.”

parts.label: C
parts.question: [H] At a concert in Berlin, Fitzgerald improvised new lyrics to this song referencing Louis Armstrong because she forgot the original ones. Armstrong’s own 1955 cover of this ballad excerpted from The Threepenny Opera helped establish it as a jazz standard.
parts.answer: “Mack the Knife” [accept “The Ballad of Mack the Knife” or “Die Moritat von Mackie Messer”]

topics.description: George Gershwin's 1924 composition for solo piano and jazz ensemble or orchestra, blending concert music with jazz and featuring an opening clarinet glissando.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Benny Goodman, the "King of Swing", played this woodwind instrument. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this single-reed woodwind instrument also played by Artie Shaw. Most professional players of this instrument must own two, one tuned to B-flat, the most common, and another tuned to A.

parts.label: B
parts.question: The clarinet plays the opening glissando of this George Gershwin piece composed for solo piano and jazz band.

parts.label: C
parts.question: The clarinet was largely replaced in jazz ensembles by this iconic jazz instrument, typically featuring a U-bend and a tilted bell and made out of brass. It was played by stars such as Charlie Parker and Cannonball Adderley.
parts.answer: saxophone [accept alto saxophone, since Parker and Adderley both were primarily alto players, but also generously accept tenor saxophone]

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: A song by this composer features a chord progression used in Dizzy Gillespie’s “Salt Peanuts.” A blues-inspired aria about when “the livin’ is easy” was created by this composer of “I Got Rhythm” for an opera set in Charleston’s Catfish Row. A train ride to Boston inspired this composer of “Summertime” to write a piece which begins with Ross Gorman’s improvised clarinet glissando. For 10 points, name this composer of Porgy and Bess and Rhapsody in Blue.

topics.description: German early Romantic composer known for orchestral works including The Hebrides, the Italian Symphony, the Scottish Symphony, and the Reformation Symphony.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Sixteenth notes played underneath the lyrical theme of this piece represent rolling waves. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [H] Name this concert overture and early tone poem. This piece was inspired by a composer’s trip to a sea cave in Scotland.
parts.answer: The Hebrides [or Hebrides Overture; accept Fingal’s Cave]

parts.label: B
parts.question: [M] The Hebrides is an orchestral piece by this German composer. Other travel-inspired pieces by this composer include his fourth symphony, nicknamed the Italian Symphony.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [E] The rumble of the waves depicted in The Hebrides is represented by the timpani, part of this family of instruments. Other orchestral instruments in this family include the cymbals and the triangle.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Although it was written in 1830, this symphony was not published until 1868, 21 years after its composer’s death, resulting in its achronological numbering. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [H] Name this symphony whose fourth movement centers on Martin Luther’s hymn “A mighty fortress is our God.” The name of this symphony was chosen by its composer’s sister Fanny.
parts.answer: Reformation Symphony [accept but do not reveal Felix Mendelsohn’s Symphony No. 5; prompt on Symphony No. 5]

parts.label: B
parts.question: [M] This early Romantic German composer wrote the Reformation Symphony for the tricentennial of the presentation of the Confession at the Diet of Augsburg. Two of his other symphonies are titled Italian and Scottish.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [E] The second section of Mendelsohn’s Festgesang, composed for the quadricential of Gutenberg’s invention of the printing press, was adapted as one of these Christmas tunes with lyrics “Hark! The Herald Angel Sings.”
parts.answer: Christmas carol [accept hymn; prompt on Christmas song]

topics.description: British cellist renowned for her performances and recording of Elgar’s Cello Concerto before multiple sclerosis ended her career.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: The same two chords begin both the first and second movements of a concerto for this instrument although the second time is pizzicato instead of arco. Camille Saint-Saëns (“kah-MEE san-SAWN”) used the unusual structure of one continuous movement in his first A minor concerto for this instrument. Multiple sclerosis ended the career of Jacqueline du Pre, who popularized Edward Elgar’s (*) E minor concerto for this instrument. This instrument represents the swan in the final movement of The Carnival of the Animals, which is often excerpted as an encore by Yo-Yo Ma, who plays this instrument. For 10 points, name this string instrument that is pitched lower than a viola but higher than a bass.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: A player of this instrument created the oratorio The Manger and formed a trio with Alfred Cortot and Jacques Thibaud. A player of this instrument founded the Silk Road Ensemble and played frequent solos for the film Crouching Tiger, Hidden Dragon. A player of this instrument married to Daniel Barenboim recorded Elger Concerto in E Minor before her career ended at age 28 due to (*) multiple sclerosis. Mstislav Rostropovich played the Davidov Stradivarius, one of these instruments that belonged to Jacquline du Pré and now belongs to a Chinese master who often plays Bach’s Suites in C Minor. For 10 points, Yo-Yo Ma plays what largest string instrument?

topics.description: A major art museum in Paris, housed in the former Louvre Palace and known for collections including the Mona Lisa and Venus de Milo.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: Two towers appear on the facade of this city's Reims (RENCE) Cathedral, an early example of High Gothic Architecture. An underground lobby in a museum in this city can be reached by entering an I. M. Pei-designed glass (*) pyramid. A medieval cathedral in this city is currently being rebuilt after a 2019 fire. For 10 points, name this city home to Notre Dame and the Louvre (LOOV), the capital of France.

parts.label: L
parts.question: This museum honors musicians like Aretha Franklin, the Beatles, and Tina Turner, a 2021 inductee. For ten points each,

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this museum dedicated to commemorating great musicians in a certain music genre. A glass pyramid makes up part of this museum in Cleveland, Ohio.
parts.answer: Rock and Roll Hall of Fame and Museum (accept RRHoF; accept Rock Hall; prompt on “Hall of Fame”)

parts.label: B
parts.question: Another glass pyramid designed by the same architect is in the courtyard of this French art museum that is home to the Mona Lisa and the Venus de Milo.

parts.label: C
parts.question: The glass pyramids at the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame and the Louvre were both designed by this Chinese-American architect who passed away in 2019.

topics.description: A musical key centered on C in the minor mode, with three flats and E-flat major as its relative major.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Yunchan (YOON-chan) Lim concluded the winning performance at the 2022 Cliburn Competition by  playing the third in a set of this kind of piece in D minor. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [10] Name this genre used for four compositions by Sergei Rachmaninoff (SUR-gay rahk-MAH-nin-off),  the second of which imitates tolling bells.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [10] The second of Rachmaninoff's piano concertos is in this key, whose relative major is E-flat major.
parts.answer: C minor [do not accept or prompt on “C”]

parts.label: C
parts.question: [10] The “Russian” version of this term refers to how Rachmaninoff played his piano concertos as a  soloist. This term refers to a sustained increase in volume.

parts.label: L
parts.question: This number symphony has been deemed cursed, as many composers have died after the completion of their symphony of this number, such as Antonín Dvořák (dih-vor-JAHK), Franz Schubert, and Gustav Mahler. For ten points each,

parts.label: A
parts.question: [H] Name this number, the most famous symphony of which uses text from Friedrich Schiller’s “Ode to Joy,” and is nicknamed the Choral Symphony for its use of voices.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] The Choral Symphony is by this composer, whose third symphony is known as the Eroica and his sixth is known as the Pastoral. His 5th symphony begins with a short-short-short-long rhythm that depicts fate knocking at the door.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [M] Beethoven’s 5th symphony is in this key’s minor, which has 3 flats in the order B E A, and is the relative minor to E-flat major. This key’s major has no sharps or flats.
parts.answer: C [accept C major or C minor]

topics.description: Gustav Mahler’s symphonic song cycle for two voices and orchestra, based largely on German translations of Chinese poetry and deliberately left unnumbered as a symphony.
aliases: The Song of the Earth, Das Lied von der Erde

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: Musical works of this type that are nicknamed Palindrome and Surprise are two of the one-hundred-four of these works written by their “father,” Joseph Haydn. Mahler wrote his “Song of the Earth” to avoid the “curse of the (*) ninth” associated with these works, and Brahms’s first one is nicknamed “Beethoven’s Tenth.” Four movements make up the modern form of, for ten points, what long musical works for full orchestra?
parts.answer: symphony (accept symphonies; accept New World Symphony or Symphony From the New World; accept Palindrome Symphony; accept Surprise Symphony; accept symphonies by Dvorak before “Palindrome” is read)

parts.label: L
parts.question: This composer dedicated a song cycle based on poems by Friedrich Rückert to his dead daughter, Maria. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [M] Name this Austrian composer of Songs on the Death of Children. He featured the tam-tam and the rute in his Tragic Symphony, which also contains three “hammer blows of fate.”

parts.label: B
parts.question: [H] The third “scherzo” movement of this Mahler piece heavily uses the pentatonic scale. This piece, which depicts the infinite beauty of nature, also includes a movement based on a poem called “The Solitary One in Autumn.”
parts.answer: Das Lied von der Erde [or The Song of the Earth]

parts.label: C
parts.question: [E] Mahler avoided naming The Song of the Earth as his symphony of this number to avoid a so-called "curse" of this number. Beethoven died after completing his symphony of this number, which includes a setting of Ode to Joy.
parts.answer: Ninth Symphony [or Symphony Number Nine; accept Beethoven’s Ninth; accept the Curse of the Ninth]

topics.description: A class of percussion instruments that produce sound through the vibration of a struck membrane or, in some related forms, a resonant surface.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Some stories describe the origins of this activity as the volcano goddess Pele performing it to celebrate finding land in spite of Namakaokahaʻi [“nah-mah-koh-KAH-ah-ee”]. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [M] Name this activity whose ku’i genre involves oli chants. Performers of this activity wear kī leaf dresses and lei.
parts.answer: hula dancing [prompt on dancing with “What type of dancing?”]

parts.label: B
parts.question: [H] Pele sends Hi’iaka [“hee-ah-ka”] on a journey to Kawai’i to find a husband after being awoken by these jula instruments. Griots of West Africa sing mythical stories while playing one of these instruments called the djembe.

parts.question: [H] This surrealist artist’s Time Transfixed includes a train exiting a fireplace. This Belgian artist’s work titled The Treachery of Images depicts a pipe, but says “This is not a pipe.” at the bottom.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [M] This impressionist artist practiced en plein air, the act of painting outdoors, by painting the Gare Saint-Lazare (gahr sahnt-lah-ZAR) Train Station. This French artist also painted Impression: Sunrise and a series of about 250 Water-Lilies.

parts.label: L
parts.question: A floating apple obscures the face of a man wearing a bowler hat in one painting from this movement. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [H] Name this art movement, a Belgian member of whom created artworks such as The Son of Man.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [M] Son of Man was created by this surrealist, who, in The Treachery of Images, declared “this is not a pipe”.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [E] Many Magritte paintings feature a background of this subject. Magritte’s depictions of this subject were usually blue and often featured clouds.

topics.description: Pablo Picasso's 1907 painting of five angular or mask-like female figures, a landmark in the development of Cubism and modern art.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: This artist captured the attention of Georges Braque with a painting of five angular figures inspired by women in a brothel and by African masks, Les (*) Demoiselles d’Avignon [[lay day-mwah-zels da-VEE-nyawn]. This artist created a black-and-white painting of the bombing of a Basque city during the Spanish Civil War, and during his Blue Period, he painted The Old Guitarist. For ten points, name this Spanish painter who painted Guernica and co-founded Cubism.
parts.answer: Pablo Picasso (accept Pablo Ruiz y Picasso)

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: An untitled steel statue by this artist is located in Chicago’s Daley Plaza. A large black-and-white painting by this artist is titled for a town destroyed in a 1937 war. Fruit lays on a table in front of five women wearing African-inspired (*) masks in this artist’s Les Demoiselles d’Avignon. This artist painted scenes such as The Old Guitarist and La Vie during his Blue Period. For 10 points, name this Spanish painter of Guernica, a co-founder of Cubism.

topics.description: A formal theatrical dance tradition involving codified choreography, music, and often pointe shoes, costumes, and scenery.

parts.label: L
parts.question: In one work by this composer, Prince Ivan defeats Kashchei (kuh-SHAY) with the help of the title animal. For ten points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [H] Name this composer who included an “Infernal Dance” in his The Firebird. Another work by this composer sparked a riot at its Paris premiere and is called The Rite of Spring.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] Stravinsky’s The Firebird and The Rite of Spring are works of this type. Stravinsky composed many works for this type of dance, often performed with specialized pointe shoes by tutu-wearing dancers.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [M] Stravinsky’s ballet Petrushka tells the story of the Wizard bringing to life three of these objects. In another work, one of these objects was brought to life after it was made by the woodcarver Geppetto.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: A video of the North State orchestra performing one of these works went viral because a woman in the audience screamed after a sudden fortissississimo. A “Dance of the Knights” features in Sergei Prokofiev’s adaptation of Romeo and Juliet as one of these works. Prokofiev collaborated with George Balanchine (“BAL-un-cheen”) on one of these works titled Prodigal Son for (*) Sergei Diaghilev, an impresario for these works. A high-pitched bassoon solo opens one of these works by Igor Stravinsky that caused a riot at its Paris premiere. For 10 points, The Firebird and The Rite of Spring are examples of what stage works involving tutu-wearing dancers?
parts.answer: ballets [prompt on suites by asking “from what larger works were the suites extracted from?”]

topics.description: Sandro Botticelli’s Renaissance allegorical painting depicting mythological figures in an orange grove and the arrival of spring.

parts.label: L
parts.question: In a painting of this season, Flora reaches into a pocket of flowers in her dress while, next to her, a blue Zephyrus grabs Chloris. For ten points each,

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this season represented allegorically in a painting set in an orange grove. In the painting, the three Graces dance in a circle to welcome this season of rebirth.
parts.answer: spring (accept Primavera; accept Allegory of Spring)

parts.label: B
parts.question: The Allegory of Spring, or Primavera, was painted by this Renaissance artist from Florence. This artist made several mythological paintings for his patrons, the Medici family.
parts.answer: Sandro Botticelli (accept Alessandro di Mariano di Vanni Filipepi)

parts.label: C
parts.question: Flora, Chloris and Zephyrus also appear in this other mythological Botticelli painting, which depicts the title Roman goddess being blown to shore while standing on a seashell in this painting
parts.answer: The Birth of Venus (accept Nascita di Venere; do not accept or prompt on “Venus” alone; do not accept or prompt on “Aphrodite”)

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: In a painting, this deity is blown toward an orange grove by the god Zephyr, where this deity is received by the Hora of Spring. This deity stands in an arch underneath her son, a child aiming a (*) bow and arrow, in the painting Primavera. This goddess uses her long, blonde hair to cover her naked body as she floats to shore on a seashell in a Botticelli painting titled The Birth of this goddess. For ten points, name this Greco-Roman goddess of love.
parts.answer: Venus (accept Aphrodite; accept The Birth of Venus; accept Nascita di Venere. In Primavera, Venus stands under Cupid.)

topics.description: A relief-printing technique in which an image is carved into a wooden block, ink is applied to the raised surface, and the image is transferred to paper or another material.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: The wildly inaccurate artwork Rhinoceros is a work made in this material by Albrecht Durer. Pieces of this material were used by the artist Hokusai [hoh-koo-sah-ee] to add overlapping sections of colored ink to Fine Wind, Clear Morning and The Great Wave off Kanagawa. This material is used in (*) ukiyo-e [oo-kee-yoh-ay], a technique that makes prints with blocks of this material that might be cut along or against the grain. For ten points, name this natural art supply harvested from the trunks of trees.

parts.label: L
parts.question: In a painting of this scene, Judas clutches a bag of silver while the other disciples react to the revelation that Jesus will be betrayed by one of them. For ten points each,

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this biblical scene. In a painting of this scene by Leonardo da Vinci, Jesus spreads his hands over the table where he and his disciples eat a meal together.

parts.label: B
parts.question: Judas kneels across the table from the other disciples in this artist’s diagonally-aligned painting of The Last Supper. This Italian Mannerist also painted Paradiso and The Miracle of the Slave.

parts.label: C
parts.question: Judas is absent from Albrecht Durer’s depictions of The Last Supper, which he created by printing with blocks of this material. To make block prints, artists carve along the grain of this natural material.

topics.description: Andrew Lloyd Webber's musical based on T. S. Eliot's Old Possum's Book of Practical Cats, featuring the Jellicle Ball and the song “Memory.”

parts.label: L
parts.question: Name the following musicals with famous dance sequences, for ten points each.

parts.label: A
parts.question: This Rodgers and Hammerstein musical essentially invented the dream ballet, a sequence in which the dance advances the plot and no singing takes place, in its Act 1 finale in which Laurey realizes she loves Curly, not Jud. This musical ends with Laurey and her new husband leaving for their honeymoon in the surrey with the fringe on top.

parts.label: B
parts.question: Gillian Lynne choreographed the Jellicle Ball in this Andrew Lloyd Webber musical, whose singing roles include Skimbleshanks.

parts.label: C
parts.question: Bob Fosse’s signature jazz hands are used throughout this musical, in which Roxie Hart and Velma Kelly try to get acquitted of murder in Illinois during the Jazz Age.

parts.label: L
parts.question: For ten points each, answer some questions about musicals by Andrew Lloyd Webber.

parts.label: A
parts.question: [E] This Lloyd Webber musical tells of the annual Jellicle Ball, where the title animals decide which one will be reborn after ascending to Heaviside Layer. T.S. Eliot’s poetry provided most of the lyrics to this feline musical.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [M] Webber also wrote this musical about the title character whose facial deformations force him to wear a mask. That character sings “The Music of the Night” after luring his love into his lair under an opera house.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [H] This other musical by Lloyd Webber concentrates on the life of the title political leader from Argentina, the second wife of Juan Peron. That title character sings from her balcony in the song “Don’t Cry for Me Argentina.”

topics.description: French composer associated with musical Impressionism, known for works including Boléro, Le Tombeau de Couperin, Gaspard de la nuit, Rapsodie espagnole, and Miroirs.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: It’s not Rimsky-Korsakov, but this composer wrote his Scheherazade Overture during his time at the Paris Conservatoire. A six-movement suite by this composer uses an antique Baroque structure and has sections named for dances like the Forlane and Rigaudon. This composer wanted to exceed the difficulty of Balakirev’s Islamey with the final movement, (*) Scarbo, of a three-part solo piano suite. This composer commemorated seven friends who died in World War I with his Le Tombeau de Couperin. Another orchestral composition by this composer includes 169 repetitions of a snare drum ostinato. For 10 points, name this French Impressionist composer of Boléro.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: It’s not Spain, but one composer from this country was accused of plagiarizing his Rapsodie espagnole,  which appears in his Miroirs suite. This country was home to the composer of a “habanera,” in which a  woman sings that “love is a rebellious bird.” In an opera by a composer from this country, the toreador (*) Escamillo feuds with Don Jose. For 10 points, name this country home to Maurive Ravel and the composer of  Carmen, George Bizet.
parts.answer: France [or the French Republic; or Republique Francaise]

topics.description: Dutch graphic artist known for mathematically inspired tessellations, impossible architectural scenes, and paradoxical prints such as Waterfall and Ascending and Descending.

parts.label: L
parts.question: This man depicted a skull in the title object in his painting Eye, and he depicted two hands drawing each other in his Drawing Hands. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this Dutch artist known for his tessellations and depictions of paradoxes such as waterfalls which flow into themselves.
parts.answer: M. C. Escher [or Maurits Cornelis Escher]

parts.label: B
parts.question: Escher's Hand with Reflecting Sphere is an unusual form of this type of artwork, in which the artist depicts themselves.

parts.label: C
parts.question: Escher also painted a paradoxically infinite one of these structures in Ascending and Descending. Marcel Duchamp produced a painting of a "Nude Descending" one of these structures.
parts.answer: a staircase [accept obvious equivalents like a stairwell or stairway or just stairs] <Young, Fine Arts>

parts.label: L
parts.question: Victor Vasarely is considered the leader of an art movement that focused on creating these things, which he used in works such as Zebra. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [H] Name these things, one of which was depicted by Bridget Riley in Movement in Squares. Another artist’s painting Waterfall was inspired by another one of these things, the Penrose steps.
parts.answer: optical illusions [or visual illusions; prompt on illusions]

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] This artist of Waterfall depicted impossible staircases in works such as Ascending and Descending and Relativity. This Dutch artist’s many tessellations include one in which a school of fish turns into a flock of birds.
parts.answer: M. C. Escher [or Maurits Cornelis Escher]

parts.label: C
parts.question: [M] Optical illusions may use this technique, which creates the illusion of depth in a two-dimensional painting. In works that use the linear form of this technique, parallel lines appear to converge at the vanishing point.

topics.description: Italian Renaissance architect and engineer best known for designing the dome of Florence Cathedral and contributing to the development of linear perspective.
aliases: Filippo di ser Brunellesco di Lippo Lapi

parts.label: L
parts.question: Andrea Mantegna used foreshortening, a form of this technique, in The Lamentation over the Dead Christ. For  10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this technique, which artists use to depict three-dimensional space on a flat canvas. Further objects are  shown as smaller in this technique, in which parallel lines are drawn such that they converge at a vanishing point.

parts.label: B
parts.question: This Italian artist used a mirror in order to rediscover linear perspective. This artist lost a contest against  Lorenzo Ghiberti for the commission for the doors to the Florence Baptistry.

parts.label: C
parts.question: Brunelleschi designed an octagonal brick one of these features for the Florentine Cathedral. One of these  features in the Pantheon features an oculus.

parts.label: L
parts.question: The Florence Cathedral was built despite the fact that, at the time, there was no known way to produce one of these structures large enough to finish it. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [10] Name this type of architectural element. Many Russian churches contain numerous examples of their "onion" types.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [10] This architect designed the dome on top of the Florence Cathedral after it had spent almost a hundred years unfinished.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [10] Another Italian Renaissance-era dome tops the St. Peter's Basilica, the most important church in this smallest country in the world. It is the home of the Pope and the headquarters of the Catholic Church.

topics.description: Auguste Rodin's bronze sculpture of a seated, contemplative male figure, originally conceived as part of The Gates of Hell.

parts.label: L
parts.question: This sculpture was first conceived as the centerpiece of a larger door frame. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [10] Name this sculpture whose subject is sitting with his hand supporting his chin in a contemplating pose.
parts.answer: The Thinker [or Le Penseur; accept The Poet]

parts.label: B
parts.question: [10] The Thinker was created by Auguste Rodin for The Gates of Hell, a sculpture based off of this Italian author's Inferno.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [10] Auguste Rodin also created this sculpture depicting six leaders of a French city that was besieged during the Hundred Years' War.
parts.answer: The Burghers of Calais [or Les Bourgeois de Calais]

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: A cast of this sculpture in Meudon sits over its creator’s grave. This bronze sculpture was intended to sit under The Three Shades at the top of the (*) Gates of Hell, and was originally named The Poet, since it depicts Dante Alighieri contemplating the sinners he wrote about in the Inferno. For ten points, name this Auguste Rodin [ow-GOOST roh-DAN] sculpture in which a seated man leans forward pensively with his chin on his hand.
parts.answer: The Thinker (accept Le penseur; accept The Poet or Le poete ` before “Poet” is read)

topics.description: Giuseppe Verdi's opera about the Ethiopian princess Aida and the Egyptian commander Radamès, who are sealed alive together in a vault at the conclusion.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: In one of this composer’s operas, Violetta asks Alfredo to love her forever before dying of tuberculosis; that opera is La Traviata. Another of this composer’s operas premiered using twelve live elephants for its “triumphal march.” In that same opera by this man, (*) Radames (ruh-DAH-miss) falls in love with the title character and is buried alive with her at its end. For ten points, name this composer of an opera set in Egypt about an Ethiopian princess, Aida.

parts.label: L
parts.question: This opera includes the aria "Ritorna vincitor", and its title character and her love interest are sealed inside a vault at its end. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [10] Name this opera whose title Ethiopian princess falls in love with Radamès, the Captain of the Guard.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [10] This Italian composer of Rigoletto and La traviata composed Aida.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [10] Aida is set in this African country during its Old Kingdom period. The premiere performance of Aida took place in this country's capital city of Cairo.
parts.answer: Arab Republic of Egypt [or Jumhūrīyat Miṣr al-ʻArabīyah, or Gomhoreyyet Maṣr el-ʿArabeyya]

topics.description: An institution that collects, preserves, exhibits, and interprets works of visual art, such as the Guggenheim museums referenced in the question.

parts.label: L
parts.question: For ten points each, answer some questions about American architects named Frank.

parts.label: A
parts.question: [H] Frank Lloyd Wright designed this building in southwestern Pennsylvania for the Kaufmann family. This building uses cantilevered floors to extend over a waterfall.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] Architect Frank Shaver Allen designed the Kenosha High School and Christ Episcopal Church in Joliet, a city in this state. Frank Lloyd Wright designed the Robie House in this state’s city of Chicago.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [M] Frank Gehry designed a building of this type in Bilbao for the Guggenheim Foundation. Frank Lloyd Wright also designed one of these buildings for the Guggenheims, which is down the street from another one called MoMa.
parts.answer: art museum [do not accept or prompt on answers containing “gallery”]

parts.label: L
parts.question: Leon Battista Alberti’s trabeated three-tiered design for the facade of one of these buildings progresses from rustication to ornamentation with each ascending floor. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [H] Name these buildings, one of which Alberti designed for the Rucellai (“ROO-chuh-lye”) family. A copy of Michelangelo’s David stands in one of these buildings nicknamed “vecchio” (“VEH-kee-oh”).
parts.answer: palaces [or palazzo or palazzi; accept Palazzo Rucellai; accept Palazzo Vecchio]

parts.label: B
parts.question: [M] Both the Palazzo Rucellai and Palazzo Vecchio stand in this city. Filippo Brunelleschi used a herringbone pattern to construct a dome in this city that, to this day, remains the world’s largest brick and mortar dome.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [E] Many palazzi like the Palazzo Pitti now function as these institutions. Other examples of these institutions include the Uffizi and the Louvre.

topics.description: A chapel in Vatican City's Apostolic Palace renowned for Michelangelo's frescoes, including The Creation of Adam and The Last Judgment.

parts.label: L
parts.question: This artist created The Genius of Victory for the tomb of Julius II [second], but it was not included in the finished tomb. For ten points each,

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this Italian Renaissance sculptor who did manage to include a scupture of a horned Moses as well as a Rebellious Slave and a Dying Slave for the same tomb.
parts.answer: Michelangelo (accept Michelangelo di Lodovico Buonarroti Simoni)

parts.label: B
parts.question: Julius II was the “warrior” one of these religious leaders. Michelangelo earned commissions from several of these leaders to produce art for the Vatican.
parts.answer: Pope (accept Bishop of Rome; accept Roman Pontiff; accept Pontifex Maximus)

parts.label: C
parts.question: Julius II commissioned Michelangelo to paint the walls and ceiling of this chapel in the Vatican’s Apostolic Palace. Michelangelo included an iconic image of God reaching toward Adam on this chapel’s ceiling.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: One painting in this building depicts souls in the process of being sent to either heaven or hell. In a painting in this building, God reaches out with one finger to give life to the first man. The Last Judgment and The (*) Creation of Adam are frescoes in this church. An artist hired to paint the inside of this church designed a scaffolding system to paint its ceiling. For 10 points, name this church in Vatican City with an interior painted by Michelangelo.

topics.description: The bony structure of the human head that protects the brain and is often depicted as a symbol of death or mortality in art.

parts.label: L
parts.question: These objects are typically featured in Memento mori paintings. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name these human remains that frequently symbolize death in art. This skeletal structure protects the brain and supports the face.

parts.label: B
parts.question: This American artist painted skulls of horses, cows, and deer. After living in New York, she moved to New Mexico and painted many depictions of its landscape.

parts.label: C
parts.question: Skulls were sometimes featured in paintings of this genre. More popular subjects in this genre include flowers and baskets of fruit.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Paintings of these things were thought by Alfred Steiglitz to represent various body parts. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name these things, which title paintings such as Black Iris III and Oriental Poppies.

parts.label: B
parts.question: Black Iris III and Oriental Poppies were some of the many paintings of flowers by this American artist. This painter was married to the photographer Alfred Steiglitz.

parts.label: C
parts.question: O’Keeffe also frequently depicted these body parts belonging to cows. An anamorphic one of these body parts appears in Hans Holbein the Younger’s The Ambassadors.

topics.description: A pigmented liquid or coating used as an art material and applied to surfaces such as canvas with brushes or other tools.

parts.label: L
parts.question: A 20th-century artist popularized a technique known as “drip” using this substance. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [E] Name this art material that comes in types such as oil and tempera and is applied using brushes.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [H] Drip painting achieved mainstream success during this 20th-century art movement led by artists like Jackson Pollock and Mark Rothko.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [M] Helen Frankenthaler, an Abstract expressionist, popularized the “soak stain” technique, which is similar to this common painting technique in which pigments are suspended in water.

parts.label: L
parts.question: The Betterton-Kroll process is used to extract bismuth from alloys containing this element. For ten points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [M] Name this element that was used in pipes until its toxicity was discovered. Today, it is still used in acid car batteries.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [H] Thomas Midgley used lead to decrease engine knock and to boost this gasoline rating. More premium gasoline generally has a higher value of this rating shown on gas pumps.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [E] Lead was once found in this substance, until it was discovered that it would crack and contaminate the environment. Watercolors are a type of art in which this substance is applied to canvas with brushes.

topics.description: A period and style of Western art music dating approximately from 1600 to 1750 and preceding the Classical period.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Name some things about the first name Johann and canons… no not the ones that go boom boom. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: Johann Sebastian Bach dedicated a set of 30 variations to this person. Every third movement of that piece named after this person is a canon.
parts.answer: Johann Gottlieb Goldberg [or the Goldberg Variations]

parts.label: B
parts.question: Johann Pachelbel’s most famous and stupid work is a Canon in [this key]. This major key signature has two sharps.

parts.label: C
parts.question: The music of Johann Pachelbel and Johann Sebastian Bach are labeled as part of this style. This style typically refers to music from 1600-1750 and preceded the “Classical” period.

parts.label: L
parts.question: A musical notation in which numerals and symbols appear above or below notes to indicate intervals  or chords is called the “figured” kind of this word. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [10] Give this word, which also refers to the clef in which cello and trombone music is commonly  written.
parts.answer: bass [or figured bass; or bass clef]

parts.label: B
parts.question: [10] Figured bass was commonly used during this musical era of the 17th and early 18th centuries,  which preceded the Classical era.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [10] The symbol “6” in figured bass commonly denotes the first type of a chord known by this word, in  which the third is the bass note and the root is a sixth above it.

topics.description: John Coltrane’s 1960 jazz album featuring compositions including “Giant Steps,” “Mr. P.C.,” and “Naima.”

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: This musician’s track “India” features a tanpura playing beneath Eric Dolphy’s clarinet solo. Paul Chambers plays an E-flat pedal tone on a slow ballad by this musician. A bassline by Jimmy Garrison leads into chants of one of this artist's album names at the end of the track “Acknowledgement.” This artist’s “Countdown” appears on an album alongside a track named for his first wife, (*) “Naima.” On an album’s first track, Tommy Flanagan struggled to keep up with rapid chord progressions known as this musician’s namesake “changes.” For 10 points, name this jazz saxophonist whose “sheets of sound” style appears in A Love Supreme and Giant Steps.

parts.label: L
parts.question: DownBeat magazine columnist Ira Gilter used the phrase “sheets of sound” to describe the unique, improvisational style of this artist. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [M] Name this jazz musician, who recorded the album A Love Supreme. A harmonic progression in major thirds is named for this man’s “changes.”
parts.answer: John Coltrane [or John William Coltrane; or Coltrane changes]

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] Coltrane was a player of the “alto” variety of this instrument. This instrument is also played by Charlie Parker and Kenny G.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [H] The difficulty of the “Coltrane changes” was shown when Tommy Flanagan, a piano player, struggled to improvise over them on this album. This album by Coltrane features the hits Mr. P.C. and Naima.

topics.description: An art form and technique in which small pieces of stone, glass, ceramic, or other materials are arranged to create decorative or pictorial designs.

parts.label: L
parts.question: The Italian city of Ravenna is home to many ancient Christian works in this art form, including ones at the Mausoleum of Galla Placidia and at the Basilica of San Vitale. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [H] Name this art form common in both Classical and Christian art. The House of the Faun was once the site of a work in this art form depicting the Battle of Issus.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] The Alexander Mosaic was discovered on the floor of the House of the Faun in this city. Many mosaics have been preserved in this city because, like Herculaneum, it was buried in ash by the 79 AD eruption of Mt. Vesuvius.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [M] Like Ravenna, this city is home to many Christian mosaics, including one depicting the ascended Christ in front of a starry blue sky. Those mosaics are found in this city’s Basilica of Saint Mark.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: In an artwork in this medium found in a church in Ravenna (rah-VEN-uh), Jesus sits on an orb. That same church contains one of these artworks depicting Justinian I (the first) with his court and army. The House of the Faun in Pompeii contains one of these artworks that shows a victory for Alexander at the Battle of Issus. Islamic examples of these artworks decorate the walls at the (*) Alhambra's (ahl-HAHM-brah's) Court of the Lions. These artworks are often made using tesserae (TESS-uh-rai), or cut pieces of glass. For 10 points, name these artworks composed of small pieces of tile that form an image.
parts.answer: mosaics [prompt on tiles; prompt on glass]

topics.description: A genre of traditional religious folk songs developed by African Americans, especially enslaved and formerly enslaved people in the United States.

parts.label: L
parts.question: The virtuoso Clair Omar Musser popularized this instrument in the U.S. with a traveling, all-female orchestra of over 100 people. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [M] Name this wooden keyboard percussion instrument from Guatemala most commonly heard as the default iOS ringtone instead of the xylophone.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [H] Ney Rosauro’s Three Preludes for Marimba were inspired by this composer’s Bachianas Brasileiras [bah-shee-AH-nuss brazh-zee-LAY-rus]. This Brazilian drew from street music to compose his Chôros [SHOW-roos].

parts.label: C
parts.question: [E] Minoru Miki composed one of these pieces for a marimba and three Japanese instruments. Antonín Dvořák’s [dih-vor-JAHK’s] New World Symphony inspired one of these traditionally-Black religious songs, “Going Home.”
parts.answer: spirituals [accept gospels; accept Marimba Spiritual; accept Black spirituals; accept African-American spirituals; accept Negro spirituals]

parts.label: L
parts.question: One work of this type describes the title object “coming for to carry me home.” For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [H] Name these religious songs created by African-Americans. Examples of these songs include “Go Down Moses” and “Swing Low, Sweet Chariot.”
parts.answer: spirituals [prompt on folk songs; prompt on hymns; prompt on gospels; prompt on blues]

parts.label: B
parts.question: [M] The melody of “Swing Low, Sweet Chariot” is played in a flute solo in the first movement of this piece. This symphony was composed by Antonín Dvořák after a trip to Spillville, Iowa.
parts.answer: “New World” Symphony [or Symphony “From the New World” or Symphony No. 9 in E minor]

parts.label: C

topics.description: Romanian modernist sculptor known for works including Bird in Space, Endless Column, The Beginning of the World, and The Table of Silence.

parts.question: An egg-like stone representing “perfect beauty” appears in a sculpture titled for “The Beginning of the [this thing].” For 10 points each:

parts.answer: world [accept the globe; accept Earth; accept The Beginning of the World]

parts.question: The Beginning of the World is a sculpture by this Romanian artist, who designed a monument for World War I soldiers called Endless Column. A series by this artist consists of sixteen slim pieces of marble and bronze.

parts.question: This supporter of Brâncuși owned the Bird in Space series when it was seized by customs officials. This photo-secessionist took the photo The Pond—Moonlight and founded the 291 gallery with Alfred Stieglitz.

parts.question: [E] Klimt was from this country. Joseph Maria Olbrich sculpted the Secession Building to exhibit artworks from this country’s Vienna Secession movement, which was co-founded by Klimt.

parts.question: [10] Monks belonging to the Digambara, or "sky-clad", sect of Jainism generally dress in this manner. Jews are required to dress in this manner before entering a ritual bath, and many paintings of the Garden of Eden use strategically-placed fig leaves to hide the fact that Adam and Eve dressed in this manner.
parts.answer: they did not wear clothes [accept obvious equivalents like nudity, etc.]

parts.label: L
parts.question: Several Indian religions have a concept called dharma; in this religion, dharma is a form of righteousness taught by the 24 tirthankaras. For ten points each,

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this Indian religion whose most recent tirthankara, Mahavira, lived over 2,500 years ago.

parts.label: B
parts.question: There are two main schools of Jainism: the “sky-clad” Digambara, whose monks have this dress code, and the “white-clad” Svetembara, who don’t. In Christianity, Adam and Eve follow this dress code before the fall of man.
parts.answer: nudity (accept nakedness; accept descriptions of not wearing clothes)

parts.label: C
parts.question: Many Indian religions include a form of this concept, in which one’s good or bad actions have a corresponding impact on one’s future. In Jainism, this concept attaches to one’s soul, either purifying it or tarnishing it.

topics.description: A formalized practice of one-on-one armed combat conducted under agreed rules to settle an insult, dispute, or matter of personal honor.

parts.label: L
parts.question: This phrase is uttered during the so-called “nunnery scene” of the Shakespeare play in which it appears. For ten points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: Give this phrase contrasting life and death that is said by a prince in a soliloquy just before Ophelia returns his love letters. It is followed by a musing of “Whether ‘tis nobler in the mind to suffer.”
parts.answer: “to be, or not to be, that is the question”

parts.label: B
parts.question: The phrase “to be, or not to be” appears in this play about a Prince of Denmark. The title character seeks revenge on his uncle Claudius, who killed his father to claim the throne, in this tragedy by Shakespeare.
parts.answer: Hamlet [accept The Tragedy of Hamlet, Prince of Denmark]

parts.label: C
parts.question: The courtier Osric delivers an invitation to one of these events to Hamlet. An event of this type between Laertes and Hamlet involving a poisoned sword ends with every character besides Horatio dying.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Grushnitsky falls off a cliff in the Caucasus during one of these events in Mikhail Lermontov’s A Hero of Our Time. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [E] Both Lensky from Eugene Onegin [oh-NAY-gin] and his creator Alexander Pushkin died during what type of event, in which two men pace apart from each other then shoot?
parts.answer: duels [accept word forms such as dueling]

parts.label: B
parts.question: [M] The nihilist doctor Bazarov treats Pavel’s leg after wounding him in a duel in this author’s novel Fathers and Sons. This author’s time with peasants inspired his collection A Sportsman’s Sketches.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [H] The protagonist of this Fyodor Dostoyevsky book believes he is dueling a policeman by bumping into him on the street in its section “Apropos [a-pruh-POH] of the Wet Snow,” and rants about the Crystal Palace and ideal living from the title location.
parts.answer: Notes from Underground [or Notes from the Underground or Letters from the Underworld]

topics.description: The use of cosmetic products such as foundation, lipstick, eyeliner, bronzer, and primer to alter or enhance a person’s appearance.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: Elizabeth I may have used ceruse, one of these products which caused severe lead poisoning with repeated use. One brand of these products called Fenty was launched by Rihanna and designed to be inclusive of people with darker (*) skin tones. Users of these products may use brushes or their fingers to apply foundation. For 10 points, what cosmetic products include lipstick and eyeliner?
parts.answer: makeup [accept foundation until mentioned; prompt on cosmetics or beauty products]

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: A brand of these products is named “Florence” after the great-grandmother of the creator, who is nicknamed “Mills.” A type of this product named “Kind Words” comes in varieties like Creative and Humble. Etude House, Kaja, and 3CE are Korean brands of these products. Types of these products like (*) bronzer can come in cream and liquid types. One might use a primer before using these products. “Pro Filt’R” is one of these products known for coming in over 50 different shades, and is created by Fenty. For 10 points, name these products exemplified by Rihanna’s iconic red “Stunna Lip Paint.”
parts.answer: makeup products [or beauty products; accept lipstick or foundation; prompt on skincare for the first and third lines only by asking “what other products does the brand create?”]

topics.description: Paper is a fibrous sheet material made from processed plant fibers and used for writing, printing, crafts, packaging, and other purposes.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: The first process for making this substance was developed by Cai Lun (tsai loon) during the Han dynasty. Cotton fibers can be used to make this substance stronger and more durable. In modern times the Kraft process creates (*) pulp, which is turned into this substance. Ancient civilizations pounded strips of wood into sheets to make a substance similar to this one, papyrus. For 10 points, name this fibrous substance that is often written on.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: Friedrich Fröbel, who invented kindergarten, names a star made of this material used to teach children geometry. Refugees from the ship Golden Venture popularized using interlocking triangular modular forms of this material, prototypically to make swans. Imitations of gold and silver (*) yuanbao ingots made of this material are used at funerals. The tradition of making 1000 of one item from this material to grant a wish originates from the story of Sadako Sasaki, a Hiroshima survivor. “Valleys” and “mountains” are types of steps for manipulating this material, which is used to make iconic cranes. For 10 points, name this material which is folded in the art of origami.
parts.answer: paper [or origami paper or kami or zhi]

topics.description: A massive sandstone monolith in Australia's Northern Territory that is sacred to the Anangu and other Indigenous Australians.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: The separation of these peoples’ children from their families was detailed in the Bringing them Home Report. National Sorry Day commemorates the mistreatment of these people’s “Stolen Generations.” These peoples’ myths feature a sandstone rock formation once named for (*) Henry Ayers, Uluru. For 10 points, name these people British explorers met in the Outback, the indigenous peoples of Australia.
parts.answer: Australian Aborigines [or Aboriginals; prompt on descriptions of indigenous peoples of Australia until mentioned]

parts.label: L
parts.question: Trains crossing this country's large "outback" include the Indian Pacific and the Ghan, the latter of which is named in honor of Afghan camel herders. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this large island country south of Asia. Its largest city, Sydney, is home to an iconic Jørn Utzon-designed opera house.

parts.label: B
parts.question: This capital and largest city of Western Australia lies where the Swan River meets the Indian Ocean. Attractions in this city include Kings Park and a botanical garden on Mount Eliza.

parts.label: C
parts.question: This massive sandstone monolith in Australia's Northern Territory holds spiritual significance to indigenous people, prompting a 2019 ban on climbing it. One of the outback's best known tourist attractions, it is located near the city of Alice Springs.

topics.description: A U.S. state in New England, known as the Green Mountain State, whose history includes the Vermont Republic and the Green Mountain Boys.

parts.label: L
parts.question: This state is represented in the Senate by Patrick Leahy and Bernie Sanders. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [10] Name this northeastern state nicknamed the "Green Mountain State" and located between New York and New Hampshire.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [10] This capital of Vermont is the least populous state capital in the U.S., with fewer than ten thousand inhabitants.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [10] This most populous city in Vermont lies on Lake Champlain. Bernie Sanders was elected mayor of this city in 1981.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: A government in what became this state entered secret relations with the U.K. in the  Haldimand Affair and was led by Moses Robinson and Thomas Chittenden. A holiday in this state  commemorates the 1777 defeat of John Burgoyne at the Battle of Bennington. Seth Warner was a  Revolutionary War officer from this state, whose (*) Catamount Tavern hosted a meeting that  planned to capture Fort Ticonderoga. For 10 points, name this fourteenth state of the Union, where a  militia called the Green Mountain Boys was founded by Ethan Allen.

topics.description: A landlocked Alpine country in Central Europe, formally known as the Swiss Confederation, with a federal cantonal system and four national languages.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: The World Economic Forum meets annually in this country’s city of Davos. Romansh is one of the official languages of this country, where the Winter Olympics were hosted twice in the ski resort town of St. Moritz. This country’s southern border is home to the (*) Matterhorn. This country is divided into cantons, some of which are named after its largest cities like Zurich and Geneva. For 10 points, name this Alpine nation known for its neutrality.

parts.label: L
parts.question: For 10 points each, answer the following about caged panthers in literature:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [E] In Franz Kafka’s story “A Hunger Artist,” the title character starves to death in his cage after taking this action for 40 days, after which he is replaced by a panther. This action involves not eating for a prolonged period of time.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [M] A panther “paces in cramped circles” “like a ritual dance around a center” in a poem by this poet. This poet asked “Who, if I cried out, would hear me among the angelic orders?” in the first of his Duino Elegies.
parts.answer: Rainer Maria Rilke [or René Karl Wilhelm Johann Josef Maria Rilke] [RYE-ner muh-REE-uh RIL-kuh]

parts.label: C
parts.question: [H] Claire Zachanassian arrives with a caged panther that escapes in The Visit, by Friedrich Dürrenmatt, who is from this country. A character who spends seven years in this country notices a humanist’s name contains seven in Italian.
parts.answer: Switzerland [or Swiss Confederation or Schweiz or Suisse or Svizzera or Svizra or Schweizerische Eidgenossenschaft or Confederation Suisse or Confederazione Svizzera or Confederaziun Svizra]

topics.description: Indiana is a Midwestern U.S. state known for Indianapolis sports and motorsports, Purdue University, and the University of Notre Dame.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: A World Hockey Association team in this state was where Wayne Gretzky began his career. In 1984, Robert Irsay secretly moved an NFL franchise to this state overnight, where they began playing at the RCA Dome. A shooting guard for an NBA team in this state is nicknamed the “Knick Killer” for his clutch three-pointers. Victors like Hélio Castroneves usually drink (*) milk after winning a Memorial Day weekend sporting event in this state’s city of Speedway. Players for this state’s NFL team, which is coached by Frank Reich, include Darius Leonard and Jonathan Taylor. For 10 points, name this state home to the NBA’s Pacers and the NFL’s Colts.
parts.answer: Indiana [accept Indiana Pacers; do not accept or prompt on franchise names alone, or answers that include “Indianapolis” or “Indy”]

parts.label: L
parts.question: These institutions are often found in namesake “towns,” exemplified by Ann Arbor and Berkeley. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name these academic institutions such as Rutgers and Ohio State, which are part of the Big 10.
parts.answer: colleges [accept university or universities or collegetownes]

parts.label: B
parts.question: Purdue University, another Big 10 school, is located in this state. Purdue has a rivalry with the University of Notre Dame, which is also located in this state.

parts.label: C
parts.question: In 2022, UCLA and this nearby university announced that they will leave the PAC-12 for the Big 10. This school’s athletic teams are known as the Trojans.

topics.description: A major European river rising in the Swiss Alps, flowing through or along Switzerland, Germany, France, and the Netherlands, and emptying into the North Sea.

parts.label: L
parts.question: The highest mountain in Western Europe, Mont Blanc, is in the western part of this range. For ten points each,

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this European mountain range. Mont Blanc lies on the border between Italy and France, before this range stretches to Switzerland.

parts.label: B
parts.question: This major European river has its source in the Swiss Alps; it then flows north, creates much of the border between France and Germany, and empties into the North Sea in the Netherlands.

parts.label: C
parts.question: This iconic, pyramid-shaped Alpine peak lies on the border between Switzerland and Italy. Hundreds of climbers have died on this peak, including four members of the first team to summit it in 1911.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Tacitus (TASS-it-us) wrote an ethnography about this region describing such groups as the Ingaevones  (ing-ai-VOH-nays). For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [10] Name this region to the north of the Roman Empire, also inhabited by the Marcomanni (MAR-kohMAH-nee) and Alemanni (AH-lay-MAH-nee). Romans were killed here during a battle in which Arminius  (ar-MIN-ee-us) betrayed Varus.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [10] After this 9 AD battle in Germania, at which Roman forces were destroyed by the Cherusci (chayROO-skee), Augustus supposedly said, “Quintilius (kwin-TIL-ee-us) Varus, give me back my legions!”
parts.answer: Battle of the Teutoburg (TOY-toh-burg) Forest [or Teutoburger Wald]

parts.label: C
parts.question: [10] Germania was often defined as being east of this river in present-day western Germany. A “land”  named for this river included Cologne.

topics.description: A landlocked country in the Horn of Africa, with Addis Ababa as its capital, whose history includes the Solomonic monarchy, resistance to Italian conquest, and the Derg period.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: This country’s residents used the hashtag #thisismydam to support the construction of its Grand Renaissance Dam. This country contains Lake Tana, which is the source of the Blue Nile. This country lost its Red Sea coastline after neighboring (*) Eritrea became independent from it, and it comprises the Horn of Africa, along with Djibouti and Somalia. For 10 points, name this country, home to the capital Addis Ababa.
parts.answer: Ethiopia [or Ityop’iya; or Federal Democratic Republic of Ethiopia; or YeEtiyop’iya]

parts.label: L
parts.question: Recently, 570,000 liters of fuel were stolen from the World Food Program by authorities in this region, where  approximately 5.2 million people suffer from severe hunger. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [H] Name this region, where hostilities between the TPLF and the government of Abiy Ahemed resumed after a 5  month long ceasefire in August 2022.
parts.answer: Tigray [or Tegray; or Tigrai; or Tigre]

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] Tigray is a region in this country, whose capital is Addis Ababa.
parts.answer: Ethiopia [or Ityop’iya; or Federal Democratic Republic of Ethiopia; or YeEtiyop’iya]

parts.label: C
parts.question: [M] Peace talks in Tigray led by this organization have proved to be unsuccessful. Addis Ababa is home to the  headquarters of this 55 member organization, which was formed by the Sirte Declaration.

topics.description: A U.S. state in the Southern Plains, admitted to the Union in 1907 from territory that included the former Indian Territory.

parts.label: L
parts.question: An aerial bomb that failed to explode helped Bill Blizzard avoid being convicted of treason for his role in this event. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [H] Name this 1921 clash between West Virginia coal miners and government authorities over unionization efforts. Nearly 100 people, mostly striking miners, were killed during this week-long conflict.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] Another 1921 aerial bombing occurred during a 1921 race massacre in this state, when private individuals and law enforcement officers firebombed people and businesses in the Greenwood district of this state’s city of Tulsa.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [M] The Battle of Blair Mountain and Tulsa Race Massacre both took place during the tenure of this president. This president promised a “return to normalcy” in his successful campaign over Democrat James M. Cox.
parts.answer: Warren G. Harding [or Warren Gamaliel Harding]

parts.label: L
parts.question: The Georgia Gold Rush provided additional impetus for this event, which was legally enabled by the Indian Removal Act of 1830. For ten points each,

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this decades-long event in which tens of thousands of Native Americans were forcibly and brutally relocated from southern states to “Indian Territory”.

parts.label: B
parts.question: While this seventh US President is often blamed for the Trail of Tears, modern scholars note that forced relocation of Native Americans was the general goal of the US government long before and long after his two terms in office.

parts.label: C
parts.question: Several decades later, the Indian Territory was admitted to the union as this US state, removing further sovereignty from its Native American population.

topics.description: The capital city of New York, located on the Hudson River and historically associated with the 1754 Albany Congress and the Erie Canal connection to Buffalo.

parts.label: L
parts.question: The Constitution and Declaration of Independence were both signed in this city, which was the de facto early capital of the United States. For ten points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [E] Name this city, whose Independence Hall was the site of many important events in early American history. This city is the most populous in Pennsylvania.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [M] This iconically cracked bell was long hung in the steeple of Independence Hall in Philadelphia, and is said to have been rung to commemorate the reading of the Declaration of Independence.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [H] Before the building of Washington DC, American congresses met elsewhere. This city in New York was the site of a 1754 convention about the French and Indian War that served as precursor to many later congresses.

parts.label: L
parts.question: This city is located between a namesake mountain range and the Medicine Bow Mountains. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [10] Name this city, the third most populous in its state after Casper and Cheyenne, which contains the  remains of Fort Sanders. A Moisés Kaufman play titled this city's “project” remembers an infamous  1998 hate crime here.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [10] Laramie is located in this state, also home to the tourist center of Jackson Hole.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [10] Laramie is located in a county that shares its name with this non-Wyoming city, which was  connected via a canal to Buffalo in 1825.

topics.description: A volcanic island chain extending from Alaska toward Russia and forming the southern boundary and northernmost portion of the Bering Sea and Pacific Ring of Fire.

parts.label: L
parts.question: In 2015, the official name of this mountain was changed from that of a former president.

parts.label: A
parts.question: For ten points, name this tallest mountain in the United States. Its now-current name means "the High One" and is of Athabaskan origin.

parts.label: B
parts.question: Denali is located in this largest U.S. state, which is separated from Russia by the Bering Strait.

parts.label: C
parts.question: This island chain extends from the southwest of Alaska towards Russia, forming the northernmost portion of the Pacific Ring of Fire. Vitus Bering is credited with discovering this island chain.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: This state’s Dutch Harbor is the busiest fishing port in America and a center for the crab industry. This state’s city of Nome is the finish line of the yearly Iditarod sled-dog race. The (*) Aleutian Islands, off the west coast of this state, form the southern end of the Bering Sea. For 10 points, name this state home to Fairbanks, Anchorage, and the capital of Juneau.

topics.description: A manmade ship canal across the Isthmus of Panama connecting the Atlantic and Pacific Oceans.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: Some pundits incorrectly argued that John McCain was ineligible to serve as President because he was born in a zone named for this structure. In 1977, Omar Torrijos and Jimmy Carter signed a treaty that promised the transfer of this structure in 1999. The ports of (*) Balboa and Colón lie on opposite ends of this structure, where the Gatun Dam and Gatun Locks were built. For ten points, name this manmade waterway across a Central American isthmus that links the Atlantic and Pacific Oceans.
parts.answer: Panama Canal (accept Panama Canal Zone; prompt on “Panama” alone; prompt on descriptive answers like “the isthmus of Panama”)

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: The nationalization of one of these structures by Gamal Nasser caused a namesake 1956 crisis. China’s Sui dynasty completed a “Grand” one of these structures. Yellow fever afflicted workers who built one of these structures across the (*) Isthmus of Darien. Egypt controls the Suez example of these structures. For 10 points, what kind of artificial waterway connects the Atlantic and Pacific Oceans in Panama?
parts.answer: canal [accept Suez Canal or Grand Canal or Panama Canal]

topics.description: Japan’s highest mountain, an active volcano on Honshu and a prominent subject of Japanese art.

parts.label: L
parts.question: In one letter, Vincent Van Gogh said, “these waves are claws, the boat is caught in them, you can feel it,” while describing a print by this artist. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [M] Name this artist. In that print by this artist, fishermen hang onto three boats as they get swept up by the title Great Wave.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] The Great Wave of Kanagawa is the first entry in a series of ukiyo-e prints by Hokusai depicting Thirty-six Views of this mountain. This volcano is the tallest mountain in Japan.
parts.answer: Mount Fuji [or Fujisan; accept Thirty-six Views of Mount Fuji]

parts.label: C
parts.question: [H] This print is the second entry in Thirty-six Views of Mount Fuji after The Great Wave of Kanagawa. This print is also known as Red Fuji because it depicts clouds around a distinctly red Mount Fuji.
parts.answer: Fine Wind, Clear Morning [or Fine Wind, Clear Weather or South Wind, Clear Sky or Gaifū kaisei]

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: In a close-up image of this natural feature, titled Shojin tozan, a group of pilgrims in a straw hats use a ladder to ascend this place. Fine Wind, Clear Morning is one of the (*) Thirty-Six Views of this natural feature created by the woodcut printer Hokusai, which also includes Thunderstorm Beneath the Summit. For ten points, name this mountain that appears in the background of The Great Wave off Kanagawa, a prominent mountain near Tokyo in Japan.

topics.description: A mountain range in western Russia extending toward northern Kazakhstan and traditionally forming part of the geographic boundary between Europe and Asia.

parts.label: L
parts.question: The largest example of this ecosystem extends from northeastern China and Mongolia to Eastern Europe; its temperate climate and terrain are credited with allowing the spread of technologies like the wheel and horse riding. For ten points each,

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this type of inland region that is typically marked by flat grassland plains, as there is not enough rainfall to promote forest growth but too much rainfall to allow desertification.
parts.answer: steppes (accept the Eurasian steppe; accept the great steppe)

parts.label: B
parts.question: The Eurasian steppe is crossed by this western Russian mountain range, which is typically cited as a boundary between Europe and Asia.

parts.label: C
parts.question: The Urals extend southward into this landlocked country, the largest former Soviet republic by area other than Russia. Much of this country’s northern land is dry steppe.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: This mountain range’s Mount Manaraga lies within the Yugyd Va (“you-gid VAH”) national park, which is part of the Virgin Komi Forests. A language family named for this mountain range includes the proposed Ugric branch. Small pelmeni dumplings, which are frozen outdoors for storage, originate in this mountain range. This mountain range is the western limit of the native range of the (*) sable. Streams on the eastern slopes of this range drain into the Kara Sea via the Ob River. The archipelago Novaya Zemlya extends the northern part of this range, which stretches south to Kazakhstan north of the Aral Sea. For 10 points, name this mountain range that separates Europe and Asia.
parts.answer: Ural Mountains [or Urals or Uralskie Gory; accept Uralic languages]

topics.description: A national park in California famed for Yosemite Valley, granite formations including El Capitan and Half Dome, and scenic landmarks such as Bridalveil Fall and Glacier Point.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: One of these places in Utah has multiple spires of rock called hoodoos. Climbers visit monoliths like Half Dome and El Capitan in another one of these places. A tri-state one of these places is home to multiple geysers including Old Faithful. Some of these places in California include (*) Joshua Tree and Yosemite. For 10 points, name these protected areas in the United States, the oldest one of which is Yellowstone.
parts.answer: American national parks [accept Arches National Park or Yosemite National Park or Joshua Tree National Park or Yellowstone National Park until mentioned; prompt on park alone; prompt on Arches or Yosemite or Joshua Tree or Yellowstone alone before mentioned with “What designation is given to this place?”] <Geography–Sareddy>

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: In this state, a thin layer of melting ice allows some stones to “sail” across the surface of Racetrack Playa. A national park in this state contains the Bridalveil Fall vista and was advocated for by John Muir’s (myurzz) Sierra Club. In that national park in this state, Glacier Point gives views of (*) El Capitan and Half Dome. For ten points, name this state which contains Death Valley and Yosemite (yoh-SEM-ih-tee).

topics.description: An island and East Asian polity historically known as Formosa, associated with Austronesian settlement, Dutch Fort Zeelandia, and governance by the Republic of China since 1949.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: This island’s indigenous Gaoshan people are descended from Austronesian settlers. On this island, the Kingdom of Tungning was established by the pirate Koxinga. Descendents of Hakka hill people make up about 20 percent of this island’s population. Fort Zeelandia was an early trading post on this island, whose colonial name comes from the (*) Portuguese for “beautiful island.” This island was held under martial law during the White Terror. After the Chinese Civil War, Chiang Kai-Shek and the rest of the Kuomintang fled to this island. For 10 points, Formosa was the former name of what island off the coast of southern China?
parts.answer: ANSWER: Taiwan [prompt on Formosa before mention]

parts.label: L
parts.question: Imelda Marcos, the wife of this country's leader Ferdinand Marcos, had more than 3,000 pairs of luxury shoes at the end of his reign. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [10] Rodrigo Duterte is the current leader of this country, whose capital is Manila. America took possession of it after the Spanish-American War.
parts.answer: Republic of the Philippines [or Republika ng Pilipinas]

parts.label: B
parts.question: [10] Once Marcos was exiled, he lived in this state, formerly known as the Sandwich Islands. They became an American possession after they were ruled by 5 kings named Kamehameha.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [10] Both Hawaii and the Philippines were settled by Austronesians, who are generally considered to have emigrated from this Asian island, where the Dutch East India Company established Fort Zeelandia. It was historically known as Formosa.

topics.description: A vast cold desert spanning southern Mongolia and northern China.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: One of these features “of Death” covers the provinces of Nimruz (NIM-rooz) and Helmand (HEL-mund). One of these features between the Amu Darya (AA-moo DAAR-yuh) and Syr Darya (SEER  DAAR-yuh) is the native habitat of Russian tortoises and is called the Kyzylkum (kuh-ZEEL-koom).  A so-called “death worm” is said to live in one of these features. The largest of these features  completely within China is west of (*) Lop Nur and includes Kashgar and Urumqi (oo-RUM-chee). The  Tian Shan mountains divide one of these features called the Taklamakan (TAHK-lim-uh-KAHN) from  another with snow-capped dunes. For 10 points, name these dry features such as the Gobi.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Answer the following about reforestation projects, for 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [E] This rainforest has naturally recovered land about the size of the United Kingdom amidst deforestation largely caused by cattle ranchers. This South American rainforest is the largest in the world.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [H] The Three-North Shelterbelt Program has been an effort to stop the expansion of this desert by planting trees. This desert is home to the endangered Przewalski [per-zhuh-VAL-skee] horse and the brown bear relative of the Mazaalai.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [M] The grassroots Green Belt Movement to stop the growth of the Sahara was founded by a person from this country, Wangari Maathai. This country home to the Kikuyu and Luo people is the northernmost country where the Maasai people migrate.
parts.answer: Kenya [or the Republic of Kenya; or Jamhuri ya Kenya]

topics.description: A southeastern U.S. state extending from the Atlantic coast and Outer Banks to the Appalachian Mountains, with Raleigh as its capital.

parts.label: L
parts.question: The Cape Hatteras National Seashore protects this chain, which has been called the “Graveyard of the Atlantic” for its tendency to wreck ships. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [H] Name this series of barrier islands which separates Pamlico Sound from the ocean. Towns like Buxton and Avon are holiday destinations on these islands.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] The Outer Banks are off the east coast of this state, while Roanoke Island lies between the Outer Banks and this state’s mainland. This state’s Research Triangle near Raleigh and Durham contains Duke University.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [M] This town also lies on the Outer Banks. This town is often credited as the site of the Wright brothers’ first flight, despite the actual flight occurring several miles south.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: This state contains the highest point in the U.S. east of the Mississippi, its Mount Mitchell. This state shares the Great Smoky Mountains National Park with its western neighbor, (*) Tennessee. This state's Duke University contests a fierce sporting rivalry with its public flagship school. For 10 points, name this southeastern US state with capital at Raleigh.

topics.description: A peninsula in southeastern Mexico between the Gulf of Mexico and the Caribbean Sea, containing sites including Cancún, Chichén Itzá, Tulum, and the Chicxulub impact crater.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: This peninsula's Loltun Caves contain paintings and is on the Ruta Puuc (ROO-tah pook) route  to Labna. A war in this region included the seizure of Valladolid (vai-yah-DOH-leed) before a  march to Mérida (MAY-ree-dah). Chetumal (CHAY-too-mahl) is the capital of a state on this  peninsula called (*) Quintana Roo. This region, whose town of Tulum features historical ruins, is the  site of the Chicxulub (CHAIK-chu-LOOB) Crater off its northwest coast. The Temple of Kukulcán (koo￾kool-KAHN) is a popular site in this peninsula's city of Chichen Itza (CHEE-chen EET-sah). For 10  points, name this peninsula that separates the Gulf of Mexico from the Caribbean Sea.

parts.label: L
parts.question: The Barringer one of these geographical features in Arizona is one of the best preserved ones in the U.S. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [E] Name these geographical features present at sites where asteroids and meteors strike the Earth’s surface.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [M] The Vredefort Crater, the largest certified impact crater in the world, is located southwest of Pretoria in this African country, which has three capitals.

parts.label: C
