parts.question: [H] The K-T extinction was caused by an asteroid that created the Chicxulub Crater beneath this peninsula. The popular tourist destination Cancún is located on this Mexican peninsula.

topics.description: China’s longest river, also known as the Chang Jiang, flowing eastward through central China to the East China Sea near Shanghai.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: This river’s native baiji was the first species of dolphin to have a human-caused extinction. Over 1 million  people were displaced by the construction of the Three Gorges Dam on this river, which is connected to  another river to its north by the (*) Grand Canal. This river is located south of the Yellow River and has its mouth  near Shanghai. For 10 points, name this longest river in China.

parts.label: L
parts.question: China harvests about a third of the world’s supply of this crop. For ten points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [E] Name this crop, farmed in paddies and terraces. During the Song Dynasty, a strain of this crop called Champa helped lead to a population boom.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [M] The ancient Liangzhu culture farmed rice around this Chinese river, whose drainage basin is home to approximately one third of China’s population. This river is spanned by the Three Gorges Dam.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [H] Due to rice being a staple crop, a poor rice season led to widespread famine in the 1850s during this Chinese dynasty. This last Chinese dynasty faced the Taiping Rebellion partly as a result of that famine.

topics.description: A major river of Italy that flows through Rome and empties into the Mediterranean Sea near Ostia.

parts.label: L
parts.question: In a dispute over where to build this city, its eventual founder claimed to have seen twelve auspicious birds to his brother's six. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this city in modern-day Italy, named for the brother of Remus. It eventually became the center of an empire whose gods included Jupiter, Mars, and Pluto.

parts.label: B
parts.question: Romulus and Remus were legendarily raised by one of these creatures, who were honored in the festival of Lupercalia.

parts.label: C
parts.question: After Romulus and Remus were abandoned on the banks of this river, its god saved them. This third-longest river in Italy flows through Rome.

parts.label: L
parts.question: According to legend, this city was founded by twin boys raised by a she-wolf, Lupercal, who had saved them from drowning in a river. For ten points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [E] Name this city mythically founded by Romulus and Remus.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [M] King Amulius allegedly sent Romulus and Remus to drown in this river. This river is the largest in Rome and meets the Mediterranean at the suburb of Ostia.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [H] According to legend, the first seven rulers of Rome held this title; Romulus was the first and Tarquin the Proud was the last.

topics.description: The historic neighborhood and district in central New Orleans, Louisiana, known for its French and Spanish architecture, Jackson Square, Bourbon Street, and cultural landmarks.

parts.label: L
parts.question: This neighborhood’s Cathedral-Basilica of Saint Louis is located near Jackson Square. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [H] Name this neighborhood south of Tremé. After the nearby red light district, Storyville, was closed in the 1920s, this neighborhood’s Bourbon Street became the center of its city’s nightlife.
parts.answer: the French Quarter [or the Quarter or Vieux Carré]

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] The French Quarter is part of this Louisiana city on the Mississippi River. The French Quarter was largely spared when this city was devastated by Hurricane Katrina.
parts.answer: New Orleans [or Nola or Nawlins; prompt on the Big Easy]

parts.label: C
parts.question: [M] Another remnant of Louisiana’s French heritage is its division into these regions, the equivalent of counties. In the Catholic Church, a diocese is divided into these regions, which are each presided over by a priest.
parts.answer: parishes [accept civil parish or eccesiastical parish or parish priest]

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: A sandwich originating in this city typically involves fried seafood served on top of a loaf of French bread and is called the Po' Boy. The beignet (ben-YAY) purveyor Cafe Du Monde is on this city's Bourbon Street. Jambalaya and gumbo are characteristic of this city’s (*) Creole and Cajun-influenced cuisine. The French Quarter is located in, for ten points, what city central to the Mississippi River Delta in Louisiana?

topics.description: An island off the northwestern coast of Hispaniola, now part of Haiti, that became a major base and haven for French buccaneers and other pirates.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Argh matey! We need somewhere to store all these bonuses! Name these famous pirate hotspots in the Caribbean, for 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [M] Many pirates residing at this Jamaican port were able to become legal English privateers under Governor Henry Morgan. This port was eventually destroyed by an earthquake in 1692.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [H] This island northwest of Hispaniola was occupied by French traders before the Brethren of the Coast took it over. Many pirates turned to log cutting on this island now owned by Haiti.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [E] The pirate Jean Laffite was based in this state’s Barataria Bay. The French Quarter in this state is home to America’s largest Mardi Gras celebration.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Anne Bonny and Mary Read were among the women who “pled the belly” to have their executions for this crime delayed. For ten points each,

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this crime whose “Golden Age” in the late 1600s and early 1700s included extensive buccaneering in the Caribbean Sea.

parts.label: B
parts.question: Captain Henry Morgan was one of several pirate leaders based in this island’s village of Port Royal. After an earthquake in 1692, Port Royal was largely abandoned, and Kingston became this island’s major port city.

parts.label: C
parts.question: This island, which is shaped somewhat like a turtle shell off the north shore of Haiti, was a pirate haven throughout the Golden Age.

topics.description: Anchorage is Alaska’s largest and most populous city, located in south-central Alaska and serving as the usual starting point of the Iditarod Trail Sled Dog Race.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Answer the following about the Iditarod, a large sled dog race. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this state, where the Iditarod takes place. This state’s capital is Juneau.

parts.label: B
parts.question: Although Juneau is Alaska’s capital, it is not on the Iditarod route. Instead, the race begins in this most  populous city in Alaska.

parts.label: C
parts.question: Sled dogs race for nearly one thousand miles before the Iditarod ends in this Western Alaska city on the Seward  Peninsula.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Give the following about the geography of the Iditarod [“eye”-dih-tah-rod], for ten points each.

parts.label: A
parts.question: The Iditarod is an annual sled dog race that takes place over hundreds of miles in this US state.

parts.label: B
parts.question: The Iditarod begins in this most populous Alaskan city which, due to its polar location and size, is home to the surprisingly busy Ted Stevens International Airport.

parts.label: C
parts.question: The Iditarod ends in this town on the southern tip of the Seward Peninsula.

topics.description: A group of three waterfalls on the Niagara River along the Canada–United States border, between New York and Ontario.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: Charles Stephens was the first to die at this location while trying to replicate Annie Edson Taylor’s 1901 stunt. In 2012, Nik Wallenda presented his passport after crossing this feature on a tightrope. The (*) Maid of the Mist tours this location, which includes three features called Bridal Veil, American, and International. It’s illegal and dangerous to try to “ride” a barrel down, for ten points, what waterfall system on the US-Canada border?
parts.answer: Niagara Falls (accept Niagara River; accept International Falls before “International” is read)

parts.label: L
parts.question: This city's suburb of Tonawanda was among the cities studied by Soviet cartographers to determine how American industry worked. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [10] Name this Western New York city on the northeast corner of Lake Erie. The Peace Bridge connects this city to Fort Erie, Ontario.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [10] This massive waterfall lies about 20 miles northwest of Buffalo, and gives its name to cities in both New York and Ontario. It is the largest waterfall in the U.S. by flow rate.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [10] Sports fans in Buffalo are known for their passionate support for the Buffalo Bills, who play in this professional league which also includes the New England Patriots and the Denver Broncos.
parts.answer: the NFL [or the National Football League]

topics.description: Austin is the capital city of Texas and the seat of Travis County in Central Texas.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: In this city, fifteen “moonlight towers” built in the nineteenth century still operate at night. This seat of Travis County has suburbs called San Marcos and Round Rock, and hosts the (*) South by Southwest festival. This city’s namesake was defeated in an 1836 presidential election by Sam Houston. For ten points, name this city that trails San Antonio and Dallas in population, the capital of Texas.

parts.label: L
parts.question: For 10 points each, name these Texas cities home to major universities:

parts.label: A
parts.question: This Texas city is home to the state's flagship university and hosts a Formula 1 Grand Prix. It has been the capital of Texas since 1837.

parts.label: B
parts.question: Texas Christian University is located in this North Texas city which makes up the state's largest metro area along with Dallas, which is located just east of it.
parts.answer: Fort Worth [accept Dallas-Fort Worth metro[politan] area]

parts.label: C
parts.question: Texas Tech is found in this Northwest Texas city which is also known as the birthplace of Buddy Holly and the home of the National College Baseball Hall of Fame. Interstate 27 runs north from this city to Amarillo.

topics.description: A New England state in the northeastern United States, including Boston and the site of significant events in colonial Massachusetts.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: This state’s incumbent governor defeated Jay Gonzalez with 67% of the vote in 2018, after earlier  succeeding Karyn Polito. Two planes of illegal immigrants were flown to this state by Florida governor Ron  DeSantis. Barack Obama bought a waterfront home on this state’s (*) island of Martha’s Vineyard. This state’s  governor is housing Florida’s migrants at Cape Cod. For 10 points, name this state, led by Charlie Baker from  Boston.

parts.label: L
parts.question: This conflict began after John Sassamon revealed a plot to attack colonial settlements. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [H] Name this conflict fought by the Narragansett and Wampanoag tribes against the New England Confederation. Over 600 Narragansett warriors were killed in the Great Swamp Fight during this conflict.
parts.answer: ANSWER: King Philip’s War [accept First Indian War or Metacomet’s War or Metacomet’s Rebellion or Pometacomet's Rebellion or Pometacomet's War]

parts.label: B
parts.question: [M] John Sassamon warned this colony’s governor Josiah Winslow of the plot to attack colonial settlements. Metacomet’s father Massasoit earlier established relations with William Bradford and Myles Standish of this colony.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [E] Much of the fighting in King Philip’s war took place in what is now this state, where Native Americans attacked the settlement of Sudbury. Over 50 Native Americans were executed in Boston Common in what is now this state.

topics.description: A U.S. national park primarily in Wyoming and extending into Montana and Idaho, renowned for geysers, hot springs, and other geothermal features including Old Faithful and the Grand Prismatic Spring.

parts.label: L
parts.question: A geyser basin in this national park is home to the bright blue Grand Prismatic Spring, the largest hot spring in the United States. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [10] Name this national park, which is home to a geyser named "Old Faithful" because it erupts at regular, predictable intervals.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [10] The majority of Yellowstone National Park is in this least-populous U.S. state, with capital at Cheyenne.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [10] This national park directly south of Yellowstone, the other national park in Wyoming, contains part of a valley called Jackson Hole. This park shares its name with its tallest mountain.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: One of these places in Utah has multiple spires of rock called hoodoos. Climbers visit monoliths like Half Dome and El Capitan in another one of these places. A tri-state one of these places is home to multiple geysers including Old Faithful. Some of these places in California include (*) Joshua Tree and Yosemite. For 10 points, name these protected areas in the United States, the oldest one of which is Yellowstone.
parts.answer: American national parks [accept Arches National Park or Yosemite National Park or Joshua Tree National Park or Yellowstone National Park until mentioned; prompt on park alone; prompt on Arches or Yosemite or Joshua Tree or Yellowstone alone before mentioned with “What designation is given to this place?”] <Geography–Sareddy>

topics.description: A Polynesian island in the southeastern Pacific Ocean administered by Chile, renowned for its moai statues and Rapa Nui culture.

parts.label: L
parts.question: The Pacific is divided into three main regions. Answer some questions about them, for ten points each.

parts.label: A
parts.question: [M] This is the largest of the three regions, and is the namesake of a French territory and a wayfaring people, of which Moana is one.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] Polynesia is shaped roughly like a triangle, its eastern terminus being this island under the control of Chile. This island is home to large head statues called Moai.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [H] This other Pacific region is named for the small islands within it. A country named the Federated States of this region has its capital at Palikir.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: A study by Carl Lipo argued that statues in this location were “walked” by being moved side-to-side with rope. Settlers of this location came from hiva and were first ruled by kings called araki. Residents of this location would compete in a swimming contest for eggs to be named the Birdman and lead worship to the god Makemake [Mah-kay-mah-kay]. Deforestation caused by the (*) Polynesian rat led to societal collapse amongst this island’s Rapa Nui people. Statues built on this island sit atop platforms called ahu and may represent elongated versions of a chieftain’s head. For 10 points, name this Pacific Island whose residents built massive stone heads called moai.
parts.answer: Easter Island [accept Isla de Pascua; accept Rapa Nui before mention]

topics.description: Crete is the largest Greek island in the eastern Mediterranean and the historical homeland of the Minoan civilization, associated in mythology with King Minos and the Minotaur.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: Procris cured a king of this place from a curse that caused him to produce deadly animals when being unfaithful. Megara fell to that king of this place after Scylla cut off a lock of hair from her father’s head. One prince of this place was revived by Polyidus after drowning in a cask of honey. A king of this place adopted Sarpedon, (*) Rhadamanthus, and a man who earned the ire of Poseidon after refusing to sacrifice a great white bull. Seven young men and seven virgin maidens were sent to this island every year to be sacrificed to a son of Pasiphaë. For 10 points, name this island where King Minos oversaw the Minotaur’s imprisonment in the Labyrinth.

parts.label: L
parts.question: This civilization’s site of Akrotiri was destroyed in the Thera eruption. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [H] Name this seafaring civilization, who were opposed by the Mycenaeans to their north.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [M] The Minoans were based on this island, where Arthur Evans excavated Knossos.
parts.answer: Crete [or Candia; or Creta; or Kirid; or Kriti; or Krete]

parts.label: C
parts.question: [E] The Minoans invented Kamares ware, a type of these objects later Greeks painted in “red-figure” and “black-figure” styles. These objects are made from ceramics.

topics.description: An active volcano near Naples, Italy, whose eruption in 79 CE destroyed or buried the ancient cities of Pompeii and Herculaneum.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Julius Caesar used this method of execution to kill a group of pirates that had kidnapped him. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [E] Name this method used by Pontius Pilate to execute Jesus.
parts.answer: crucifixion [or crucify or nailed to cross]

parts.label: B
parts.question: [H] Crasuss executed this man’s followers along the Appian Way. This former gladiator led a major slave revolt against the Roman Republic beginning in 73 BC.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [M] Shortly after beginning his revolt, Spartacus and his men set up a position on this volcano, where they used vines to descend on Roman soldiers. The eruption of this volcano destroyed Pompeii in 79 AD.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: Spartacus led a slave rebellion which rappelled down this mountain to win a battle. The ancient city of Herculaneum was located near this mountain. Pliny the Elder died during a natural disaster caused by this (*) volcano, whose eruption buried an ancient Roman city in volcanic ash, preserving it. For 10 points, name this volcano which destroyed Pompeii.

topics.description: A large marginal sea of the Atlantic Ocean bordered by the southern United States, eastern Mexico, and western Cuba.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: Resort towns like Destin and Pensacola are located on this body of water, and they are threatened by toxic algal blooms known as red tide. In 2015, British Petroleum reached an $18.7 billion settlement over damage caused by an oil spill in this body of water, known as the Deepwater Horizon disaster. The (*) Yucatan Peninsula and Florida help define, for ten points, what gulf between its namesake country and the U.S.?

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: Surges from this larger body of water breached the levees of Lake Pontchartrain during a 2005 hurricane. The Deepwater Horizon Oil Spill occurred in this body of water, whose coast is home to popular beaches like Panama City and Destin. (*) Hurricane Katrina gained strength on this gulf before it hit New Orleans. This gulf lies west of the Florida Keys. For 10 points, name this gulf that shares its name with a country south of the United States.

topics.description: A city in Provence, southern France, located along the Rhône River and historically associated with Roman heritage and Vincent van Gogh.

parts.label: L
parts.question: This painting’s artist also made a painting titled for it “over the Rhone." For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [M] Name this painting, in which a large cypress tree appears in its foreground. Swirling yellow brushstrokes were used to depict objects in the sky in this painting, completed while its artist stayed in an asylum in Saint-Remy.
parts.answer: The Starry Night [or Starry Night over the Rhone; or La Nuit etoilee; accept De sterrennacht]

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] The Starry Night and Starry Night over the Rhone were both painted by this Dutch artist, who is also known for painting sunflowers.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [H] Starry Night over the Rhone depicts the title river flowing through this French city, where Van Gogh lived. Van Gogh painted the blue walls of the title room in a painting titled Bedroom in [this city].
parts.answer: Arles [or Bedroom in Arles; or La Chambre a Arles]

parts.label: L
parts.question: This river's valley is the home of “Papal wine,” descended from the 14th-century estate of John XXII  (the twenty-second). For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this river of southeastern France that flows through Avignon (AA-veen-yohn) and into  southern Switzerland before draining Lake Geneva and meeting the Saône (SUH-nuh) at Lyon (LEE-on).

parts.label: B
parts.question: Near this city, the Rhône divides into the Great and Little Rhône near its mouth. Many sites in this  city are named for Vincent Van Gogh, who made 300 paintings here from 1888 to 1889.

parts.label: C
parts.question: The Rhône is the only major European river discharging directly into this large body of water,  which separates Europe from Africa.

topics.description: A Southeast Asian country formerly known as Siam, with a constitutional monarchy established after the 1932 revolution and a history including the Ayutthaya and Chakri kingdoms.

parts.label: L
parts.question: The Chakri Dynasty has been ruling this country since 1782, but a bloodless 1932 revolution transformed it from an absolute monarchy into a constitutional monarchy. For ten points each,

parts.label: A
parts.question: Give the modern name of this Southeast Asian country that is currently led by Vajiralongkorn [va-jee-ra-long-kon], who rules as Rama X [tenth].
parts.answer: Kingdom of Thailand (do not accept, prompt on, or reveal “Siam”)

parts.label: B
parts.question: In 1939, the country officially changed its name to Thailand from this name.

parts.label: C
parts.question: This capital city of Thailand was industrialized under Monkgut and Chulalongkorn, who ruled as kings Rama IV and V [fourth and fifth].

parts.label: L
parts.question: A king in this modern-day country apocryphally killed the prince Mingyi Swa in a 1593 duel. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [M] Name this country where King Naresuan ruled the Kingdom of Ayutthaya. The Chakri dynasty would later take power in this country under the leadership of Rama I.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] Naresuan’s duel with Mingyi Swa took place on the back of these animals. These animals were often used for war in Southeast Asia, where ivory was also harvested from their tusks.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [H] A 1688 coup in Ayutthaya saw the general Phetracha kill the heir to the throne, who was one of these people. The Shimabara rebellion in Japan was led by these people, who also make up the Twenty-Six Martyrs.
parts.answer: Roman Catholics [prompt on Christians by asking, “what denomination?”]

topics.description: A Caribbean island in the Greater Antilles divided politically between Haiti and the Dominican Republic.

parts.label: L
parts.question: A bay in this island contains the smaller Gonave Island. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this Caribbean island split between two countries, the French-colonized Haiti in the west and a larger Spanish-speaking country in the east.
parts.answer: Hispaniola [or La Española, or Ispayola; note that the indigenous name for the island is "Haiti" but we cannot accept that as it's already in the question]

parts.label: B
parts.question: This country occupies the eastern portion of Hispaniola. Its tourist attractions include Pico Duarte and Lake Enriquillo, and its capital is Santo Domingo.
parts.answer: Dominican Republic [or Repúblicana Dominicana, do NOT accept or prompt on Dominica as that is a completely different Caribbean island country]

parts.label: C
parts.question: This is the most popular sport in the Dominican Republic. David Ortiz, Sammy Sosa, Bartolo Colón, and Albert Pujols are among the many Dominicans who have achieved success as professional athletes in this sport.

parts.label: L
parts.question: This sea is home to the Greater Antilles. For ten points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [E] Name this sea, the location of beach destinations like the Cayman Islands and Saint Kitts. The Bahamas lie just north of this sea, which is bounded by South America on the South and Central America on the west.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [M] This is the second-largest island in the Greater Antilles. This island was the site of the first settlement in the Americas, La Navidad, and it is currently split between Haiti and the Dominican Republic

parts.label: C
parts.question: [H] This other island nation of the Greater Antilles had its capital at Port Royal until that city sunk into the ocean. This is the only country in the world without red, white, or blue on its flag.

topics.topic: National parks of the United States
topics.description: Federally protected natural areas in the United States established to preserve significant landscapes, ecosystems, and cultural resources for public enjoyment.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: One of these places in Utah has multiple spires of rock called hoodoos. Climbers visit monoliths like Half Dome and El Capitan in another one of these places. A tri-state one of these places is home to multiple geysers including Old Faithful. Some of these places in California include (*) Joshua Tree and Yosemite. For 10 points, name these protected areas in the United States, the oldest one of which is Yellowstone.
parts.answer: American national parks [accept Arches National Park or Yosemite National Park or Joshua Tree National Park or Yellowstone National Park until mentioned; prompt on park alone; prompt on Arches or Yosemite or Joshua Tree or Yellowstone alone before mentioned with “What designation is given to this place?”] <Geography–Sareddy>

parts.label: L
parts.question: This man photographed a “moonrise” above Hernandez, New Mexico illuminating the crosses in a cemetery. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [H] Name this photographer, a member of the group f-stop-64. With Fred Archer, this photographer formulated the Zone System to determine the correct exposure to use in any lighting condition.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] In his “Mural Project,” Ansel Adams was commissioned to take pictures of these federally protected natural areas. Adams photographed Half Dome and El Capitan in Yosemite, another one of these places.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [M] Like Adams, this photographer took many photos of the Manzanar internment camp. This photographer is most famous for featuring Florence Owens Thompson in Migrant Mother.

topics.description: An ancient Roman city near the Gulf of Naples destroyed and preserved by the eruption of Mount Vesuvius in 79 CE.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Along the Loango Coast of the Kongo Kingdom, “scepter-slates” called lusumu made of this material were used by elders for storytelling. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [E] Name this material used to create Chinese puzzle balls. This material is harvested from the tusks of elephants.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [H] An ivory head of Queen Esigie was one of the thousands of artworks looted from this African kingdom in the 1800s. Brass plates depicting obas of this kingdom make up its namesake “bronzes” at the British Museum.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [M] An ivory yakshi depicting Lakshmi was discovered at this site in 1938. Darius III retreats from the Battle of Issus in the Alexander Mosaic found at this site’s House of the Faun.

parts.label: L
parts.question: The Italian city of Ravenna is home to many ancient Christian works in this art form, including ones at the Mausoleum of Galla Placidia and at the Basilica of San Vitale. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [H] Name this art form common in both Classical and Christian art. The House of the Faun was once the site of a work in this art form depicting the Battle of Issus.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] The Alexander Mosaic was discovered on the floor of the House of the Faun in this city. Many mosaics have been preserved in this city because, like Herculaneum, it was buried in ash by the 79 AD eruption of Mt. Vesuvius.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [M] Like Ravenna, this city is home to many Christian mosaics, including one depicting the ascended Christ in front of a starry blue sky. Those mosaics are found in this city’s Basilica of Saint Mark.

topics.description: Dublin is the capital and largest city of Ireland, situated on the east coast at the mouth of the River Liffey.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Douglas Hyde and Patrick Pearse were members of a League founded in 1893 to promote a language known by  this term. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [H] Name this cultural term, which underwent a “revival” in the late 1800s that opposed English influence in  Ireland. This term refers to Irish and Scottish culture before English invasions.
parts.answer: Gaelic [accept Gaeilge; or the Gaelic Revival; prompt on Irish or Celtic]

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] The Gaelic League was centered on this city, which became the capital of Ireland.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [M] Celtic culture spread as far as this country after the ancient Galatians settled down. This country warred with  Greece after World War I under its leader, Mustafa Kemal Ataturk.

parts.label: L
parts.question: This city's St. Stephen's Green contains a rock adorned with a statue of Oscar Wilde sassily reclining. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [10] Name this European capital city on the River Liffey, whose other statues include one of the folk song figure Molly Malone, as well as a memorial to the victims of an 1840s potato famine.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [10] Dublin is the capital of this country, from which millions of people emigrated to the United States during the potato famine.
parts.answer: Republic of Ireland [or Poblacht na hÉireann, or Éire]

parts.label: C
parts.question: [10] One of these buildings on Dublin’s O’Connell Street is famous for serving as the headquarters of the Easter Rising. One of these buildings in New York City is engraved with a motto beginning “neither rain nor snow nor heat nor gloom of night”.
parts.answer: post offices [or the General Post Office, or Oifig an Phoist]

topics.description: An artificial sea-level waterway across Egypt connecting the Mediterranean Sea with the Red Sea.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: The nationalization of one of these structures by Gamal Nasser caused a namesake 1956 crisis. China’s Sui dynasty completed a “Grand” one of these structures. Yellow fever afflicted workers who built one of these structures across the (*) Isthmus of Darien. Egypt controls the Suez example of these structures. For 10 points, what kind of artificial waterway connects the Atlantic and Pacific Oceans in Panama?
parts.answer: canal [accept Suez Canal or Grand Canal or Panama Canal]

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: This country’s planned administrative capital will contain a military complex called the Octagon. Jumel’s Cotton was historically grown in this country, which contains the oldest known Christ Pantocrator icon at its St. Catherine’s Monastery. This country disputes its southern neighbor’s Hala’ib Triangle, claiming the other country owns Bir Tawil instead. Nuclear bombs have been proposed as a way of turning its (*) Qattara Depression into a lake. A statue at Abu Simbel was nearly submerged by this country’s Aswan High Dam, which created Lake Nasser. For 10 points, name this African country that controls the Suez Canal and the Sinai Peninsula.
parts.answer: Egypt [or Arab Republic of Egypt or Jumhuriyat Misr al-Arabiyah]

topics.description: A country in southeastern Europe, centered on Bucharest and including historic regions such as Moldavia and Transylvania.

parts.label: L
parts.question: A revolution based in this city culminated in a show trial that lasted one hour, after which the President and his wife were executed so quickly that the TV cameras couldn’t even get set up. For ten points each,

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this Eastern European capital city. It was the home of Nicolae and Elena Ceausescu [show-CHESS-koo] until they fled amidst a 1989 anti-Communist revolution.

parts.label: B
parts.question: Bucharest is the capital of this Eastern European country.

parts.label: C
parts.question: Nicolae and Elena Ceausescu were executed on this holiday in 1989. Other historical events on this day include Mikhail Gorbachev’s resignation as Soviet President and, much earlier, Charlemagne’s crowning as Emperor of the Romans in 800 CE.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: Police forces in this country supposedly gave political dissidents cancer using a weapon called the “Radu gun.” Decree 770 outlawed contraceptives and abortion in this country, which was issued by a dictator who wrote the July Theses. This country’s secret police force, the Securitate, was founded during the tenure of its first communist leader Gheorge Gheorghiu-Dej (“GHE-yor-GE GHE-yor-gi-yoo Dej”). This country’s communist regime ended when that dictator and his wife (*) Elena were executed on live TV on Christmas day in 1989. Historic regions of this country include Moldavia and Transylvania. For 10 points, name this Eastern European country where the dictator Nicolae Ceausescu ruled from Bucharest.
parts.answer: Romania [accept the Socialist Republic of Romania; accept the Romanian People’s Republic; accept Republica Socialista Romania; accept Republica Populara Romania]

topics.description: A Caribbean island and self-governing U.S. territory whose capital is San Juan, with a history of Spanish colonial rule.
aliases: Estado Libre Asociado de Puerto Rico

parts.label: L
parts.question: In his book The Open Veins of Latin America, Eduardo Galleano argues that returns on Dutch investments in this crop were responsible for the growth of capital in Europe. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [E] Name this crop which was stored as molasses or distilled into rum after being harvested in the Caribbean.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [H] Caribbean sugar plantations were centered on these estates that evolved from the encomienda system and bound workers with debt to the land. Hernán Cortés was the first patrón of one of these estates in Oaxaca [wha-HAH-kuh].
parts.answer: haciendas [accept the hacienda system; accept haciendas azucareras]

parts.label: C
parts.question: [M] On this island, the colono sugar farmer class emerged with the opening of its first sugar mill in 1873. Ponce de León was the first governor of this island, which was defended by a fort called El Morro.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Answer the following about American holdings in the Caribbean, for ten points each.

parts.label: A
parts.question: [E] This U.S. island territory contains the fort Castillo (cah-STEE-yo) San Cristobal in its capital of San Juan. This territory is often thought to be the most likely candidate for the 51st state.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [M] The US Virgin Islands were the only Caribbean holding of this Scandinavian kingdom until their sale to the US in 1917. This country’s only current overseas colonies are the Faroe Islands and Greenland.
parts.answer: the Kingdom of Denmark [or Kongeriget Danmark]

parts.label: C
parts.question: [H] A US naval base at this location in Cuba is held in defiance of the Cuban government and has been the site of Geneva Convention-violating torture of enemy prisoners during the War on Terror.
parts.answer: Guantanamo Bay [or Gitmo or the Guantanamo Bay Naval Base or Base Naval de la Bahía de Guantánamo]

topics.description: A major river of northern China that flows into the Bohai Sea and is named for the yellow loess sediment in its waters.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Asia is home to some of the largest river systems in the world. For ten points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [M] What river is named after the color of the soil that it drains into a sea of the same name? That river flows through the city of Luoyang.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [H] The Yellow River and Yangtze River are connected by this structure, which was built by the Sui Dynasty and restored by the Ming Dynasty.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [E] Both the Yellow and Yangtze are in this country, the most populous in the world.
parts.answer: People’s Republic of China [do not accept or prompt on “Republic of China”]

parts.label: L
parts.question: In 1855, army generals intentionally flooded this waterway to quell an ongoing rebellion. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [H] Name this longest constructed waterway in the world. The Golden Dragon Great King river god was promoted by the state to build support for the construction of this waterway.
parts.answer: Grand Canal [or Jing-Hang Grand Canal or Dà Yùnhé or Ta Yün-ho or Jing-Hang Yunhe or Capital–Hangzhou Grand Canal]

parts.label: B
parts.question: [M] The Grand Canal was long made unusable due to the flooding and a course change in this major river connected to it. This river in north China empties into the Bohai Sea in Shandong Province.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [E] Today, the Grand Canal runs from Hangzhou to this capital of China. This city is home to Tiananmen Square and the Forbidden City.

topics.description: A major historic metropolis in northern India encompassing Old Delhi and New Delhi and serving as the seat of major imperial and national capitals.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Mu’izz al-Din, commonly known by this name “of Ghor,” helped expand the Afghanistan-based Ghorid Empire into northern India. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: Give this name, also held by the founding “Prophet” of Islam.

parts.label: B
parts.question: After Muhammad of Ghor was assassinated, his general Qutb al-Din took power in this city, thus beginning the rule of its namesake “sultanate.” Shah Jahan built the Red Fort in this city north of Agra.
parts.answer: Delhi [or the Delhi Sultanate; or New Delhi]

parts.label: C
parts.question: Qutb al-Din Aibak commissioned one of these structures in Delhi, which now resides in the Qutb complex. After the Ottomans conquered Constantinople, these structures were added to the Hagia Sophia.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: In this city, Sir Edwin Lutyens developed a Bungalow Zone for the British in the early 20th century. After the Battle of Karnal, the looting of this nearby city included the capture of the Koh-i-Noor diamond and the Peacock Throne. The Lahori Gate is the main entrance to this city’s Red Fort, which became the imperial residence of the (*) Mughals under Shah Jahan. Prior to 1911, Calcutta held this city’s primary status. For ten points, name this city whose “New” district is the capital of India.

topics.description: A strategically important strait between Iran and Oman that connects the Persian Gulf with the Gulf of Oman and the Arabian Sea.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: A city on this body of water contains a “Little Venice” neighborhood on its Pearl Islands. Two countries on this body of water dispute the Hawar Islands. The King Fahd Causeway leads to an island nation in this body of water, which contains the World and Palm Jumeirah artificial islands. High casualties amongst Indian migrant workers have occurred while constructing (*) 2022 FIFA World Cup stadiums along this body of water. Qeshm is a large island near the Strait of Hormuz, which separates this body of water from the Gulf of Oman and the Indian Ocean. For 10 points, name this gulf located between the Arabian Peninsula and Iran.
parts.answer: Persian Gulf [accept Arabian Gulf before “Arabian”; accept just Persian after “(name this) gulf”; accept just Arabian after “(name this) gulf” and before “Arabian”]

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: In this body of water, Harra trees are native to mangroves on the island of Qeshm. Oil fields in this body of water were the subject of a 1990s war named after it. One country has built stadiums overlooking this body of water for the 2022 World Cup. This body of water is connected to the Gulf of (*) Oman by the Strait of Hormuz. Bahrain is completely surrounded by, for 10 points, what gulf named after the ancient name for Iran?
parts.answer: Persian Gulf [accept Persian Gulf War; prompt on Gulf War]

topics.description: Dubai is the most populous city in the United Arab Emirates and the capital of the Emirate of Dubai, located on the Persian Gulf coast.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: This country contains a man-made island chain shaped like a map of the world. An airline based in this country sponsors the soccer team Arsenal, whose stadium is named after it. Another airline in this country, Etihad, is based in its city of (*) Abu Dhabi. The world's tallest skyscraper, the Burj Khalifa, is found in, for 10 points, what country whose largest city is Dubai?
parts.answer: United Arab Emirates [or the UAE or al-ʾImārāt al-ʿArabīyah al-Muttaḥidah; prompt on Emirates]

parts.label: L
parts.question: The financial crisis of 2008 scuttled plans to finish developing a series of artificial islands in the Persian Gulf, including one set in the shape of the world and several sets in the shape of this plant. For ten points each,

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this tropical tree.
parts.answer: palm tree (accept Palm Islands; accept Palm Jumeirah, Palm Jebel Ali, or Palm Deira; accept Arecaceae)

parts.label: B
parts.question: Oil revenue fueled the construction of the Palm artificial islands, which lie off the coast of this most populous city in the United Arab Emirates.

parts.label: C
parts.question: Dubai’s Palm islands lie unfinished, but this tallest building in the world stands nearby and actually was completed in 2009.

topics.description: The fortified rocky hill and citadel in Athens that contains the Parthenon and other major ancient Greek monuments.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: Architects Ictinus and Callicrates designed this building. Phidias created many sculptures for this building, including the Elgin Marbles and a chryselephantine statue of Athena holding Nike. A 1687 ammunition explosion severely damaged the ceiling of this building, which is located at the peak of the (*) Acropolis in Athens. Pericles commissioned, for ten points, what temple to Athena?
parts.answer: Parthenon [prompt on answers indicated a temple to Athena]

parts.label: L
parts.question: All but one of this man’s laws were repealed by his successor, Solon. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [H] Name this man, who developed a harsh Athenian law code. This man’s name is often used to describe laws that are excessively severe.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [M] Under Solon, all Athenian citizens were allowed to participate in the ekklesia assembly that met in a building southwest of this elevated part of the city, which is home to the Parthenon.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [E] Another lawgiver, Cleisthenes, is known as the father of the Athenian form of this system of government, in which the people have a say in the government.

topics.description: The northernmost and smallest major ocean, surrounding the North Pole and bordered by Eurasia and North America.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Sir Charles Wyville Thomson predicted the existence of one of these features after detecting a great temperature disparity between parts of the Faroe-Shetland channel. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [M] Name these long chains of elevated seafloor. Seafloor spreading causes these features to form in the middle of oceans, including in the Mid-Atlantic.
parts.answer: ridges [accept Mid-Atlantic Ridge or mid-ocean ridges or Wyville Thomson Ridge; prompt on underwater mountains or underwater mountain ranges or submarine mountains or submarine mountain ranges; do NOT accept or prompt on “seamount chains”]

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] The Gakkel Ridge is a mid-ocean ridge in this body of water. The Wyville Thomson Ridge separates the deep waters of this polar ocean from the Atlantic Ocean to its south.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [H] The Mid-Atlantic Ridge is mostly underwater, but reaches almost eight thousand feet above sea level at Mount Pico in this archipelago. This archipelago is the site of a triple junction of the Eurasian, North American, and African plates.

parts.label: L
parts.question: The Airbus A380, the largest passenger airplane in the world, underwent cold-weather testing in this territory's capital of Iqaluit. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this northernmost territory of Canada, which separated from its Northwest Territories in 1993. It is the only Canadian province in which the majority language is neither English nor French.

parts.label: B
parts.question: Indigenous people in Nunavut are some of the few populations in the world who still legally hunt these animals. These animals' bowhead and minke types are hunted, sometimes with instruments such as harpoons.
parts.answer: whales [accept any specific types of whales]

parts.label: C
parts.question: Along with Yukon and the Northwest Territories, Nunavut is one of the three Canadian territories to border this northernmost ocean in the world. The North Pole is located on this ocean, much of which is covered in sea ice year-round.

topics.description: A southeastern U.S. state known for cities including Nashville and Memphis and for its major role in American country music and regional history.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Answer some questions about country music. For ten points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [M] This woman is arguably the most famous female country artist. Songs from her 51 studio albums include “Jolene” and “Nine to Five.”

parts.label: B
parts.question: [H] This other classic country music star has also become a symbol of the genre with his songs “On the Road Again” and “Blue Eyes Crying in the Rain.”

parts.label: C
parts.question: [E] The country music industry is mostly centered in this state, where the Country Music Hall of Fame is located in the city of Nashville. Other major cities in this state include Knoxville and Memphis.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: A senator from this state proposed the High Performance Computing Act of 1991. A violation of the Butler Act in this state was argued in court by (*) Clarence Darrow and Williams Jennings Bryan, and focused on a man who claimed to have taught evolution in a public school in Dayton, John Scopes. Al Gore has represented, for ten points, what state whose cities include Memphis and Nashville?
parts.answer: Tennessee (accept Tennessee Valley Authority; Note: David Lilienthal was nicknamed “Mr. TVA”)

topics.description: A marginal sea of the Indian Ocean between the Arabian Peninsula and Iran, connected to the Gulf of Oman through the Strait of Hormuz.

parts.answer: Persian Gulf [accept Arabian Gulf before “Arabian”; accept just Persian after “(name this) gulf”; accept just Arabian after “(name this) gulf” and before “Arabian”]

parts.label: tossup

Bahrain is completely surrounded by, for 10 points, what gulf named after the ancient name for Iran?
parts.answer: Persian Gulf [accept Persian Gulf War; prompt on Gulf War]

topics.description: A landlocked Eastern European country that became independent after the dissolution of the Soviet Union and has been ruled by Alexander Lukashenko since 1994.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Protesters in this leader's country's chanted for this man to "have some tea" after this leader was accused of having the tea of his political opponent Alexei Navalny poisoned. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [10] Name this world leader, who recently gained the power to potentially stay in office until 2036 after his country voted for constitutional changes that extended term limits.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [10] For years, Vladimir Putin has served as the president of this largest nation in the world by area.
parts.answer: Russia [or the Russian Federation; accept Rossiya]

parts.label: C
parts.question: [10] Amid August 2020 protests in this country, Putin gave military support to this country's leader Alexander Lukashenko, who is often called "Europe's last dictator."

parts.label: L
parts.question: The Budapest Memorandum of 1994 got three countries to give up their stockpiles of these weapons in exchange for guaranteeing their sovereignty. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [E] Name these weapons, examples of which included the Tsar Bomba in the Soviet Union. The Soviets first developed these weapons four years after the U.S. used them against Hiroshima and Nagasaki to end World War II.
parts.answer: nuclear weapons [accept nuclear bombs or nukes or atomic bombs]

parts.label: B
parts.question: [M] One of the countries that gave up its Soviet-era nukes was this country where Alexander Lukashenko took power just five months prior to the agreement. Lukashenko has ruled this “last dictatorship in Europe” ever since.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [H] This other signatory to the memorandum claimed it was violated when “little green men” invaded its southernmost region in 2014. That invasion took place after the Euromaidan protests in this country.

topics.description: A large Indonesian island in Southeast Asia, separated from the Malay Peninsula by the Strait of Malacca and historically associated with the Srivijayan Empire.

parts.label: L
parts.question: On this island, the Telaga Batu Inscription helpfully informed nobles that if they were disloyal, they would be  struck dead by a magic spell. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [H] Name this Southeast Asian island, which was once ruled by the Srivijayan Empire.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] Srivijaya’s capital was sacked in the 11th century by the Chola dynasty, which followed this religion. Srivijaya  was named based on this religion’s sacred language of Sanskrit.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [M] Rajendra Chola also defeated this island’s kingdom of Anuradhapura. Arab merchants monopolized this  island’s city of Colombo to trade with its Sinhalese kingdoms.
parts.answer: Sri Lanka [or Ceylon; or the Democratic Socialist Republic of Sri Lanka; or Ilangai Jananayaka  Socialisa Kudiarasu; or Sri Lanka Prajatantrika Samajavadi Janarajaya]

parts.label: L
parts.question: The song Yakko’s World claims to list the world’s countries. Answer the following about some things Yakko didn’t quite get right. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [E] Yakko’s first mistake is naming this sea as a country, though he does correctly name several countries within this sea, such as Cuba, Jamaica, and Haiti.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [M] Yakko also incorrectly lists this island as its own country. The strait of Malacca separates the Malay peninsula from this island, which has the largest area of any island completely within Indonesia.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [H] When going through the nations of South America, Yakko incorrectly listed this department of an overseas country. The European Space Agency launches its rockets from its Spaceport located in this region.

topics.description: The capital of New South Wales and Australia’s largest city, located on the southeastern coast of Australia around Port Jackson.

parts.label: L
parts.question: One of these buildings in Oslo advertises on its website “please walk on the roof” in reference to its large ramp that allows pedestrian access to its roof. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [M] Name these buildings. Ove Arup helped engineer the concrete ribs that support another one of these buildings designed by Jørn (“yearn”) Utzon.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] That aforementioned opera house is adorned with white, sail-like concrete shells and occupies Bennelong Point in this Australian city.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [H] This architect designed an opera house in Guangzhou (“gwong-joe”) meant to resemble two pebbles washed up by the Pearl River. This architect’s futuristic design for the 2020 Olympics Stadium was scrapped because it was too expensive.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: This city's skyscrapers include the misleadingly named Greenland Centre and the Crown in  Barangaroo. The City to Surf Fun Run goes from this city's business district to Bondi Beach. “The  Coathanger” is a nickname for a bridge that connects the (*) North Shore to this city, the Harbour  Bridge, which crosses Port Jackson. This city on Botany Bay hosted the 2000 Summer Olympics and  features a Jørn Utzon (YORN OOT-zahn)-designed structure whose roof resembles sails. For 10 points,  name this Australian city that contains a landmark opera house.

topics.description: A major Pennsylvania city known for Independence Hall, the Liberty Bell, and its central role in early United States history.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: This city's Kimmel Center is home to a non-opera orchestra conducted by Montreal-born  Yannick Nezet-Seguin (yah-NEEK NEZ-eh-say-gah). The Curtis Institute of Music is in this city.  Eugene Ormandy (OR-man-dee) was the longtime conductor of a “Big Five” orchestra in this city  that uses a “sound” pioneered by (*) Leopold Stokowski (staw-KAWV-skee) and plays the score in  most of Fantasia. The theme to Monty Python's Flying Circus was a Sousa march named for an object in  this city that legendarily rang on July 8, 1776. For 10 points, name this city whose Independence Hall is  adjacent to the Liberty Bell.

parts.label: L
parts.question: The Constitution and Declaration of Independence were both signed in this city, which was the de facto early capital of the United States. For ten points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [E] Name this city, whose Independence Hall was the site of many important events in early American history. This city is the most populous in Pennsylvania.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [M] This iconically cracked bell was long hung in the steeple of Independence Hall in Philadelphia, and is said to have been rung to commemorate the reading of the Declaration of Independence.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [H] Before the building of Washington DC, American congresses met elsewhere. This city in New York was the site of a 1754 convention about the French and Indian War that served as precursor to many later congresses.
