parts.question: This sea is home to the Greater Antilles. For ten points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [E] Name this sea, the location of beach destinations like the Cayman Islands and Saint Kitts. The Bahamas lie just north of this sea, which is bounded by South America on the South and Central America on the west.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [M] This is the second-largest island in the Greater Antilles. This island was the site of the first settlement in the Americas, La Navidad, and it is currently split between Haiti and the Dominican Republic

parts.label: C
parts.question: [H] This other island nation of the Greater Antilles had its capital at Port Royal until that city sunk into the ocean. This is the only country in the world without red, white, or blue on its flag.

parts.label: L
parts.question: The song Yakko’s World claims to list the world’s countries. Answer the following about some things Yakko didn’t quite get right. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [E] Yakko’s first mistake is naming this sea as a country, though he does correctly name several countries within this sea, such as Cuba, Jamaica, and Haiti.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [M] Yakko also incorrectly lists this island as its own country. The strait of Malacca separates the Malay peninsula from this island, which has the largest area of any island completely within Indonesia.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [H] When going through the nations of South America, Yakko incorrectly listed this department of an overseas country. The European Space Agency launches its rockets from its Spaceport located in this region.

topics.description: A cold, sparsely populated region at the southern end of South America, extending across southern Argentina and Chile from roughly the Colorado River to Tierra del Fuego.

parts.label: L
parts.question: The “ABC Powers” mediated a conference between American and Mexican diplomats in 1914. For ten points each,

parts.label: A
parts.question: The “ABC Powers” are Argentina, Brazil, and this South American country whose capital is Santiago.
parts.answer: Chile (accept Republic of Chile; accept Republica de ´ Chile)

parts.label: B
parts.question: Among the relatively few conflicts between the ABC powers is a border dispute between Chile and Argentina over this cold region of South America south of the Pampas.

parts.label: C
parts.question: Before they were the “ABC Powers”, Argentina and Brazil joined with Uruguay in the 19th century War of the Triple Alliance against this country, which lost the war decisively.
parts.answer: Paraguay (accept Republic of Paraguay; accept Republica del ´ Paraguay; accept Tavakuaireta Paraguai´ )

parts.label: L
parts.question: These people often hunted with a throwing weapon made of weights attached to leather cords called a bola. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [H] Name these people, whose payada ballads influenced the epic poem Martín Fierro. These cowboys roamed the plains of Argentina and Uruguay in the 18th and 19th centuries.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] Many gauchos carried a long one of these tools called a facón, which they also used for fighting. The Swiss Army type of these tools combines one of them with other things like a screwdriver and a can-opener.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [M] Most Argentine gauchos lived in the Pampas or in this region, which stretches from the Colorado River to Tierra del Fuego. The Tehuelche people are indigenous to this region in the south of Argentina and Chile.

topics.description: Houston is the largest city in Texas and a major Gulf Coast city in the United States.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Since this city is the only major American city without zoning laws, many single-family houses are in this city’s flood-prone coastal areas. For ten points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [E] Name this largest city in Texas. Since the Johnson Space Center, which contains NASA’s mission control center, is located in this city, Apollo 13 reported to this city that “we have a problem.”

parts.label: B
parts.question: [M] Houston had its own problem in 2017 when this hurricane overfilled its Buffalo Bayou, causing widespread flooding in its downtown. This hurricane was the most costly since Katrina.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [H] Houston replaced this other nearby city as Texas’s central port after a 1900 hurricane named after this city devastated it, in the deadliest natural disaster in U.S. history.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: This city’s MLB ballpark had a slope in center field called Tal’s Hill that was removed in 2016. This city was nicknamed “Clutch City” after its NBA team came back from 0-2 down in the playoffs against the Suns, eventually defeating the Patrick Ewing-led Knicks in the finals. (*) George Springer won the World Series MVP for this city’s MLB team in 2017, before the discovery that the team cheated during the season by illegally stealing signs and banging on a trash can to warn of opponents’ upcoming pitches. In 2021, the Brooklyn Nets traded for James Harden from this city’s NBA team. For 10 points, name this city home to MLB’s Astros and the NBA’s Rockets.
parts.answer: Houston [accept Houston Astros or Houston Rockets]

topics.description: A southwestern U.S. state in the American Southwest, including cities such as Phoenix and Tucson.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Give the following about 2021 electoral efforts that have been derided as wasteful, for ten points each.

parts.label: A
parts.question: This country’s Prime Minister, Justin Trudeau, called for a snap election in September. Only twenty-four of three hundred thirty-eight seats changed parties in the election, which cost this country over six hundred million dollars.

parts.label: B
parts.question: Republican efforts to recount the 2020 Presidential election in Maricopa County in this southwestern state concluded in September and found that Joe Biden won the state by even more votes than previously indicated.

parts.label: C
parts.question: On September 14th, polls closed in the election to recall this Governor of California. The effort to recall this man failed by more than three million votes and cost roughly three hundred million dollars.

parts.label: L
parts.question: In 2018, Kyrsten Sinema narrowly defeated Martha McSally in this state's U.S. Senate race. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this state where former congresswoman Gabby Giffords was shot in Tucson in 2011.

parts.label: B
parts.question: Despite McSally's loss in the election, she would be appointed to the Senate two months later after this long-time Arizona senator and 2008 Republican presidential candidate died of brain cancer.

parts.label: C
parts.question: In 2020, McSally lost in a special election against this Democrat, a former astronaut and the husband of Gabby Giffords.

topics.description: A vast East African grassland ecosystem centered in northern Tanzania and extending toward Kenya, renowned for its annual wildebeest and zebra migration and abundant wildlife.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Give the following about conservation areas in Africa, for ten points each.

parts.label: A
parts.question: An annual migration of hundreds of thousands of zebras and wildebeests takes place in this region of East Africa. The world’s largest wild lion population lives within the national park of the same name.

parts.label: B
parts.question: Just east of the Serengeti National Park is a UNESCO World Heritage Site protecting one of these geographic landforms called Ngorongoro [en-GORO-en-goro], which formed from the collapse of a volcano.

parts.label: C
parts.question: The Serengeti and Ngogongoro national parks are found in this east African country. Its capital is now Dodoma, having moved last century from its largest city, Dar es Salaam.

parts.label: L
parts.question: In 2017, an armed, all-female unit was established in Zimbabwe to help combat this crime. For ten points each,

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this illegal act of hunting or capturing wild animals. A common form of this crime is killing elephants for their ivory.

parts.label: B
parts.question: Black rhinos have nearly gone extinct due to poaching in this African region. This grassland is the namesake of a national park in Tanzania, and reaches the Maasai Mara National Park in Kenya.

parts.label: C
parts.question: During migration season, thousands of wildebeests and this striped equine cross the Serengeti in search of new grass.

topics.description: A large island in Southeast Asia shared by Indonesia, Malaysia, and Brunei, known for tropical rainforests and orangutans.

parts.label: L
parts.question: In 2002, this country granted independence to the smaller country of East Timor, which it had invaded in 1975. For ten points each.

parts.label: A
parts.question: [E] Name this Islamic Southeast Asian country that has its capital on the island of Java and experiences many earthquakes on its island of Sumatra.
parts.answer: Indonesia [or Republic of Indonesia or Republik Indonesia]

parts.label: B
parts.question: [H] This island and Sumatra are the original homes of the orangutan. Kalimantan is the Indonesian portion of this island, which is also split between two other countries, Brunei and Malaysia.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [M] Though this city, Indonesia’s capital, is rapidly sinking into the Java Sea, it remains the nation’s largest. Some models predict that 95% of this city could be submerged by 2050, a result of the swampy terrain of the region and rising sea levels.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Answer the following about countries that have recently changed capitals, for 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [E] Indonesia’s new capital of Nusantara is being built on this island shared with Brunei and Malaysia. The popular online Orangutan Jungle School is located on this island.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [M] This country moved its capital to Naypyidaw in 2005. This Asian country also contains the city of Mandalay, and the Irrawaddy River flows through this country into the Andaman Sea.
parts.answer: Myanmar [or Burma; or Union of Burma; or Pyidaungzu Thammada Myanma Naingngandaw; or Republic of the Union of Myanmar]

parts.label: C
parts.question: [H] This country began moving its capital from Bujumbura to Gitega in 2018. A giant man-eating crocodile named Gustave ate over 300 people along this country’s northern shores of Lake Tanganyika.
parts.answer: Burundi [or Republic of Burundi; or Republique du Burundi; or Republika y’u Burundi]

topics.description: A major concrete arch-gravity dam on the Colorado River between Nevada and Arizona that created Lake Mead and opened in 1935.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: A long-debated proposal would build, near this state’s Frenchman Flat, a proposed nuclear waste facility under Yucca Mountain. The Truckee River flows through this state’s self-proclaimed “Biggest Little City in the World” on its way out of Lake Tahoe, which this state shares with its western neighbor. The Hoover Dam lies on the Colorado River between Arizona and, for ten points, what state whose economy is fueled by gambling in Reno and Las Vegas?

parts.label: L
parts.question: This river was accidentally diverted into the Coachella Valley of Southern California in 1905, which formed the modern Salton Sea. For ten points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [M] Name this river of the southwestern United States, which forms the border between California and Arizona.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] The Colorado River has now been tamed by measures such as this massive dam, the largest in the world when it was opened in 1935. This dam is named after a Depression-era president.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [H] This artificial lake between Nevada and Arizona was formed by the accumulation of the Colorado River behind Hoover Dam. This lake and Lake Powell are the two largest artificial water reservoirs in the United States.

topics.description: A U.S. state in the Appalachian region of the eastern United States.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Wallace Saunders wrote a ballad about Casey Jones who died preventing a crash between two of these vehicles. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [E] Name these vehicles, one of which stops clocks as it recreates its travel to Springfield, Illinois with Abraham Lincoln’s body. Phantom conductors and weird tunnel lights appear in ghost sightings of these vehicles.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [M] During a contest to mine a train tunnel, this freed slave proclaims “I'll die with the hammer in my hand” while competing against a mechanical drill. This “steel-driving man” is often depicted with a sledgehammer.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [H] John Henry’s contest took place at the Big Bend Tunnel near this state’s city of Talcott. The collapse of this state’s Silver Bridge near Point Pleasant is believed to have been caused by the Mothman.

parts.label: L
parts.question: For 10 points each, answer the following about geographical locations related to the song "Take Me Home, Country Roads":

parts.label: A
parts.question: "Take Me Home, Country Roads" is the official state anthem of this U.S. state. The song claims that this state is "almost heaven" and compares its mountains to a motherly figure.

parts.label: B
parts.question: This is the last name of the singer of "Take Me Home, Country Roads." This is also the name of a city nicknamed the "Mile High City", the capital of Colorado.

parts.label: C
parts.question: The second line of "Take Me Home, Country Roads" mentions both the Blue Ridge Mountains and this Virginia river, the largest tributary of the Potomac. A folk song with the same name as this river says "we're bound away / across the wide Missouri".

topics.description: A five-sided government building in Arlington, Virginia, serving as the headquarters of the United States Department of Defense.
aliases: United States Department of Defense headquarters

parts.label: L
parts.question: This event was planned by the “Hamburg Cell” and Khalid Sheikh Mohammed. For ten points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [E] Name this terrorist attack in which four hijacked airplanes destroyed the World Trade Center in New York.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [M] On 9/11, a hijacked plane was also crashed into this building, killing over 100 employees. This Arlington building, the headquarters of the Department of Defense, is named for its shape.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [H] The fourth hijacked flight on 9/11 is thought to have been intended for this building. Instead, passengers such as Todd Beamer stormed the cockpit, crashing the plane into a field in Pennsylvania.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Answer the following questions about protests against the Vietnam War. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [H] It was observed that students don’t “shed their constitutional rights to freedom of speech…at the schoolhouse gate,” in this Supreme Court case involving students wearing black armbands to protest the war.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] A photo taken during an anti-war march on this building shows a protester placing a flower in the barrel of a soldier’s gun. Abbie Hoffman failed to levitate this five-sided government building in Arlington, Virginia.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [M] A symbolic form of protesting against the war involved burning these pieces of paper, which are issued to those registered in Selective Service.

topics.description: A North African country and kingdom whose territory, cities, political history, and international relations are described across the candidates.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Answer the following about American paratroopers, for 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [E] Aubrey Eberhardt began the tradition of shouting the name of this Apache chief in reference to him jumping off a cliff near Fort Sill.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [M] The 101st Airborne Division was deployed to protect this group of students who were barred from entering a Southern high school by Orval Faubus’s National Guard.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [H] During Operation Torch, paratroopers attacked Vichy forces in the eastern neighbor of this country to provide support for Operation Goalpost. This country was the first to recognize the United States under Mohammed III.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Africa is home to more countries than any other continent, therefore making it home to more capital cities than any other continent. For ten points each,

parts.label: A
parts.question: [E] Rabat is the capital of this North African kingdom that lies across the Strait of Gibraltar from Spain. Other cities in this country include Casablanca and Marrakech (mAA-ruh-kEHsh).

parts.label: B
parts.question: [M] This most populous country in Africa moved its capital to the master-planned Abuja from the more populous Lagos in 1991 in an attempt to move the capital to a more neutral position between contesting peoples.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [H] While countries like Tanzania and Ivory Coast have two capitals, South Africa is the only country that has three: Bloemfontein, Pretoria, and this city.

topics.description: The capital and largest city of Iceland, located on its southwest coast.

parts.label: L
parts.question: For a week in 2010, a volcanic eruption on this island disrupted air travel throughout Europe. For ten points each,

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this North Atlantic island, the site of Eyjafjallajokull [AY-yuh–f’YAT-luh–YO-kull] and numerous other volcanoes, geysers, and hot springs.

parts.label: B
parts.question: Almost all of Iceland’s energy production is renewable; it has ample sources of both hydroelectric power and this type of power, generated by its hot springs and geysers.

parts.label: C
parts.question: More than half of Iceland’s population lives in this city, the northernmost world capital.

parts.label: L
parts.question: You want to see the Aurora Borealis. Name some places you might visit, for 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [M] You may fly up to this country’s city of Tromsø, where a cable car takes tourists up a peak translating as “the big rock.” The aurora is also visible from a seed vault in this country’s archipelago of Svalbard.
parts.answer: Norway [or Kingdom of Norway or Kongeriket Norge]

parts.label: B
parts.question: [H] Transparent living spaces that let you sleep under the Northern Lights are found in this northernmost province of Finland, where a line denotes the Arctic Circle in Santa Claus Village. This region is home to the Sami people.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [E] If you haven’t seen the Northern Lights enough, you could also go to this capital of Iceland.

topics.description: Ontario is Canada's most populous province, located in the Great Lakes region and containing Toronto and Ottawa.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: This province is home to Lester Pearson International Airport, which has the airport code YYZ. In this province, a statue of Colonel John By stands across the Rideau [rye-doh] Canal from Parliament Hill. Windsor and Hamilton are among the cities in the southern arm of this province. Both Minnesota and New (*) York border this province, the only one that shares its name with a Great Lake. For ten points, name this most populous Canadian province, the home of Ottawa and Toronto.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Lake St. Clair and Lake Erie are connected by a river named after this city. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [E] Name this center of the American automotive industry, the largest city in Michigan.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [H] Detroit is linked by the Ambassador Bridge to Windsor, a city in this Canadian province. This province is home to Canada's most populous city, Toronto, and its capital, Ottawa.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [M] Before passing under the Ambassador Bridge, the Detroit River is joined by the River Rouge, which names a large factory for this automotive company, a longtime rival of General Motors.

topics.description: A historical and modern region of northwestern France, associated with the Norman people and the Duchy of Normandy.

parts.label: L
parts.question: The loser of this battle, Harold Godwinson, had defeated Tostig and Harald Hardrada only five days earlier at Stamford Bridge. For ten points each,

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this 1066 battle. At this battle, Harold Godwinson was defeated by William the Conqueror as they fought for succession after the death of Edward the Confessor.

parts.label: B
parts.question: William the Conqueror claimed legitimate succession to the English throne, although he was born and raised in this region in what is now northwestern France.

parts.label: C
parts.question: Before the battle, William the Conqueror interpreted this astronomical object as an omen of his victory. This object appears in the Bayeux Tapestry’s depiction of the Battle of Hastings.

parts.label: L
parts.question: William Longsword succeeded a duke of this region who acquired it in the Treaty of Saint-Clair-sur-Epte (SAH-klair-soor-EP-tuh). For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [10] Name this region, now in northern France, whose first Scandinavian duke took control here 175  years before a descendant commissioned the Domesday (dooms-day) Book.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [10] France reconquered Normandy from England at this war's Battle of Formigny (FOR-meen-yee).  Henry V (the fifth) was victorious in this war's Battle of Agincourt (AH-jin-kor).

parts.label: C
parts.question: [10] This Viking, who was baptized as Robert I (the first), was the first Duke of Normandy. He often  clashed with Charles the Simple.

topics.description: An autonomous community and historical region in northeastern Spain, centered on Barcelona and associated with a distinct Catalan language, culture, and independence movement.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: This country is home to the world's oldest lighthouse still in use, the Tower of Hercules, in its city of A Coruña. This country's Basque-speaking minority lives in cities like Bilbao, while its eastern portion is known as (*) Catalonia. The slogan "more than a club" is used by a world-famous soccer team from this country's city of Barcelona. For 10 points, what European country is led from Madrid?
parts.answer: Kingdom of Spain [or Reino de España, or Espainiako Erresuma, or Regne d’Espanya]

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: A yellow ribbon symbolizes the independence movement of a region in this country. The cantera policy of a soccer team in this country to only use local players emphasizes Basque pride. Architecture designed by Antoni Gaudí is prominent in this country’s region of (*) Catalonia, and especially the city of Barcelona. For ten points, name this country formed by the union of Castile and Aragon whose capital is Madrid.
parts.answer: Spain [or the Kingdom of Spain or España or Reino de España]

topics.description: Illinois is a Midwestern U.S. state that includes Chicago and is associated with the historical, political, and architectural references described in all three candidates.

parts.label: L
parts.question: For ten points each, answer some questions about American architects named Frank.

parts.label: A
parts.question: [H] Frank Lloyd Wright designed this building in southwestern Pennsylvania for the Kaufmann family. This building uses cantilevered floors to extend over a waterfall.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] Architect Frank Shaver Allen designed the Kenosha High School and Christ Episcopal Church in Joliet, a city in this state. Frank Lloyd Wright designed the Robie House in this state’s city of Chicago.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [M] Frank Gehry designed a building of this type in Bilbao for the Guggenheim Foundation. Frank Lloyd Wright also designed one of these buildings for the Guggenheims, which is down the street from another one called MoMa.
parts.answer: art museum [do not accept or prompt on answers containing “gallery”]

parts.label: L
parts.question: One of these entities, named after Abraham Lincoln, was sponsored by businessman Carl G. Fisher. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name these entities, which were landscaped by Lady Bird Johnson’s “beautification act." The most extensive system of these entities in the United States was initially meant for military convoys.
parts.answer: highways [or freeways or interstates; prompt on roads]

parts.label: B
parts.question: The Interstate Highway System was developed during the 1950s under this President, who was inspired by the Autobahn while Supreme Commander of Allied forces during World War II.

parts.label: C
parts.question: Eisenhower twice defeated a politician from this state, Adlai Stevenson, to become President. William Ogden was the first mayor of this state’s city of Chicago.

topics.description: A vast system of defensive walls and fortifications built and expanded across northern China over many centuries.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Answer the following about the works of female performance artists, for 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [E] Marina Abramovic's last performance with her partner Ulay, titled Lovers, involved walking from opposite ends of this structure. This 13,000-mile-long structure is not actually visible from space.
parts.answer: Great Wall of China [or Wànlǐ chángchéng]

parts.label: B
parts.question: [M] This performance artist allowed participants to cut off parts of her clothing in Cut Piece. This author of Grapefruit helped write the lyrics to her husband’s song “Imagine.”

parts.label: C
parts.question: [H] While more famous for her Infinity Mirror Room pieces, this artist often painted nude New Yorkers with polka dots. In Walking Piece, this artist walks through New York City in a brightly-colored kimono.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Though many authors have written that this structure is large enough to be seen from the moon, it is sometimes not even visible from low Earth orbits. For ten points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [E] Name this defensive fortification which, stretching from Liaodong to Lop Lake, protected China from Xiongnu (shong-NU) raids.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [H] This Chinese emperor combined numerous pre-existing walls to form the Great Wall of China. This emperor, who ended the Warring States period by founding the Qin (chin) dynasty, was buried with an army of terracotta soldiers.
parts.answer: Shi Huangdi [or Qin Shi Huang or Ying Zheng or Zhao Zheng; prompt on Qin]

parts.label: C
parts.question: [M] Shi Huangdi ironically died due to ingesting mercury pills, thinking that they would help him obtain this trait. In Chinese myth, eight people with this trait are thought to have lived on Bohai islands since the Shang dynasty.

topics.description: The Polynesian volcanic archipelago in the central Pacific that includes the U.S. state of Hawaii.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Some stories describe the origins of this activity as the volcano goddess Pele performing it to celebrate finding land in spite of Namakaokahaʻi [“nah-mah-koh-KAH-ah-ee”]. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [M] Name this activity whose ku’i genre involves oli chants. Performers of this activity wear kī leaf dresses and lei.
parts.answer: hula dancing [prompt on dancing with “What type of dancing?”]

parts.label: B
parts.question: [H] Pele sends Hi’iaka [“hee-ah-ka”] on a journey to Kawai’i to find a husband after being awoken by these jula instruments. Griots of West Africa sing mythical stories while playing one of these instruments called the djembe.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [E] Hula dancing is a tradition in this archipelago, which was raised from the sea by Māui’s fish hook.

parts.label: L
parts.question: In these islands’ religion, the deity Ku’ula controls the fish in the sea. For ten points each,

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this set of islands, an American state whose native religion considers sites like Mauna Loa and Mauna Kea to be sacred.

parts.label: B
parts.question: This traditional dance in Hawaii is often accompanied by chant or song and was used for storytelling and rituals. Before performing, dancers may make offerings to Laka, a patron of this dance.

parts.label: C
parts.question: This Goddess of volcanoes brought fire to the Hawaiian islands and lives in Mount Kilauea. During a sled race, she started a fight with the snow Goddess Poli’ahu [poh-lee-ah-hoo] due to jealousy.
parts.answer: Pele [peh-leh] (accept Madame Pele or Tutu Pele)

topics.description: Moscow is the capital and largest city of Russia, with a central role in Russian history and modern political and economic life.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: A monarch from this city initiated a process of “gathering lands” under its rule using highinterest loans and thus became known as “Kalitá” (KAH-lit-AH) or “moneybags.” A “Grand  Prince” from this city reclaimed autonomy from the Tatars at the Great Stand on the (*) Ugra  River. That prince of this city married the former Byzantine princess Zoe Palaiologina (PAIL-ee-ohLOWG-ee-nah) and promoted the idea of this city as “the third Rome.” A form of the word “Caesar”  began to be used in 1547 by the grand princes of this city. For 10 points, name this city where Ivan IV  (ee-VAN the fourth) proclaimed himself “tsar.”
parts.answer: Moscow [or Grand Duchy of Moscow; do not accept or prompt on “Muscovy”]

parts.label: L
parts.question: This politician ordered the disassembly of several mail-sorting machines across the country prior to  the 2020 return of mail ballots. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [10] Name this current Postmaster General of the United States.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [10] DeJoy was named a deputy finance chairman to the Republican National Committee in 2017, as  was this now-disbarred lawyer who previously served as Donald Trump's personal attorney.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [10] Cohen pleaded guilty to perjury after lying to Congress regarding his knowledge of a proposal to  build a Trump Tower in this European city. The tower here was to include a penthouse for Vladimir  Putin.

topics.description: The sovereign country and constitutional monarchy in Western Europe, established as an independent state in 1830–1831.

parts.label: L
parts.question: This man named his only son Georges [zhorzh] Washington, in honor of his commander. For ten points each,

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this Frenchman who assisted the Americans at the Battle of Yorktown. Thomas Jefferson later helped this member of the Estates General [eh-STAHT zhen-ay-rall] write the Declaration of the Rights of Man.
parts.answer: Marquis de Lafayette (accept Marie-Joseph Paul Yves Roch Gilbert du Motier)

parts.label: B
parts.question: The Marquis de Lafayette was named in honor of an ancestor who fought against the English in this war, which lasted from 1337 to 1453.

parts.label: C
parts.question: Lafayette’s modern descendants include Philippe, the current king of this country. The Duchess of Brabant is in line to be this country’s first queen.

parts.label: L
parts.question: This queen was appointed Empress of India in a political stunt orchestrated by Benjamin Disraeli. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [E] Name this longest-reigning queen of England prior to Elizabeth II, who names an “era” during the 1800s.
parts.answer: ANSWER: Queen Victoria [or the Victorian Era]

parts.label: B
parts.question: [H] Victoria married this first cousin of hers, a prince of Bavaria who died at 42. This “royal consort” was advised by Baron Stockmar.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [M] Baron Stockmar was sent to advise Albert and Victoria by a king of this country, nicknamed the “Nestor of Europe.” This European country was later ruled by the rubber-coveting Leopold II.
parts.answer: ANSWER: Kingdom of Belgium [or Konigreich Belgien; or Koninkrijk België; or Royaume de Belgique]

topics.description: Cleveland is a major city in northeastern Ohio on the southern shore of Lake Erie, known for institutions including the Cleveland Orchestra and neighborhoods such as Ohio City and the Flats.

parts.label: L
parts.question: The composer included many abrupt stops in the last movement of a string quartet nicknamed “The Joke.” For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [M] Name this composer from the Classical period. A symphony by this composer is nicknamed for the musical joke of a loud and unexpected G-major chord.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] Haydn’s 93rd symphony contains another joke, in which this instrument interrupts a quiet interlude with what some critics have compared to a musical “fart.” This lowest-pitched double reed woodwind has a “contra-” variant.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [H] That bassoon exclamation in Haydn’s 93rd symphony is especially loud in George Szell’s performance with this city’s Orchestra. Among the Big Five American orchestras, only Chicago and this city’s are located in the Midwest.

parts.label: L
parts.question: One of these places in Philadelphia is named for Reading Terminal. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [E] Name these retail facilities such as Seattle’s Pike Place one, which sell products such as fresh produce and meats. As opposed to traditional grocery stores, goods at these facilities are sold by their producers.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [H] The West Side Market is located in this city’s “Ohio City” neighborhood. This city’s Flats neighborhood is located on the Cuyahoga River.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [M] The Ferry Building Marketplace can be found along this city’s Embarcadero. Near the Ferry Building, passengers can take boat rides to Oakland across this city’s namesake bay.

topics.description: A dormant volcanic mountain in Tanzania and the highest mountain in Africa, comprising the volcanic cones Kibo, Mawenzi, and Shira.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: German missionary Johann Rebmann names a glacier near the summit of this mountain,  which contains the hiking area of Barranco (bah-RAHN-koh) Wall. The nearby town of Moshi is  the starting point for some climbs on this mountain, whose three volcanic cones include (*) Kibo  (KEE-boh), Shira (SHEE-rah), and Mawenzi (mah-WEN-zee). The summit of this mountain, the highest  in the world that is not part of an adjacent range, was renamed to mean “freedom peak” in Swahili. For  10 points, name this dormant volcano in Tanzania, the tallest mountain in Africa and the tallest volcano  in the Eastern Hemisphere.

parts.label: L
parts.question: This country contains the Serengeti grassland, home to the second largest terrestrial animal migration in the world. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [10] Name this nation, Kenya's southern neighbor, which also contains the highest point in its continent. Its capital was moved to Dodoma in 1996.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [10] This dormant volcano in Tanzania is the highest mountain in Africa.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [10] Tanzania has a significant coastline on this ocean, part of the greater "Swahili Coast" region next to it. The Bay of Bengal and the Arabian Sea are separated by the country this ocean is named for.

topics.description: Arthur Rimbaud was a French Symbolist poet known for works including A Season in Hell and “The Drunken Boat.”

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: In his translation of a poem from this country, William Aggeler added “-ish” to an adjective appearing in a final line which also includes an exhortation varyingly translated as “fellow,” “likeness,” and “twin.” An object that narrates a poem from this country describes itself as “going down impassive Rivers.” A poem from this country describes an emotion who “smokes his (*) hookah pipe” and is addressed to a “hypocrite reader.” A poet from this home country of the author of “The Drunken Boat” included “The Swan” and “Spleen” in The Flowers of Evil. For 10 points, name this home country of the “decadent” Symbolist poets Arthur Rimbaud (“ram-BOW”) and Charles Baudelaire.
parts.answer: France [or French Republic or République française; accept Kingdom of France or French Second Republic or Second French Empire or French Third Republic]

parts.label: L
parts.question: After going to jail for shooting this author, the poet Paul Verlaine wrote a poem called “The Crime of Love.” For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [H] Name this French Symbolist poet, who wrote about his tempestuous relationship with Verlaine in A Season in Hell.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [M] In A Season in Hell, Rimbaud calls for these events to choke him with sand and blood. Thousands of rats die in the streets of Oran in a novel titled for one of these deadly events by Albert Camus.
parts.answer: Plague [or The Plague; or La Peste]

parts.label: C

parts.answer: Robinson Crusoe (accept The Life and (Strange Surprizing) Adventures of Robinson Crusoe of York, Mariner: Who Lived Eight and Twenty Years, All Alone in an Un-inhabited Island on the Coast of America, Near the Mouth of the Great River of Oroonoque; Having Been Cast on Shore by Shipwreck, Wherein All the Men Perished but Himself. parts.answer: The Tale of Genji (accept Genji Monogatari)

parts.label: B
parts.question: A chapter of The Tale of Genji, “Vanished into the Clouds” is left entirely blank, implying this event happened to the main character. After this event, the story instead follows Kaoru [kah-oh-roo] and Niou [nee-oh].
parts.answer: Genji’s death (accept word forms or equivalents like Genji dying or passing away)

parts.label: C
parts.question: Genji is the son of a man with this title. Lady Murasaki served in the household of a leader with this title who claimed to be descended from the goddess Amaterasu [ah-mah-tay-rah-soo].

parts.question: The protagonist of this novel compares the robe of one love interest to a cast-off cicada shell. After arguing with Lady Rokujo, the daughter of the Minister of the Left suffers a seizure in this novel. parts.answer: The Tale of Genji [or Genji Monogatari]

topics.description: A 1981 dystopian novel by Nadine Gordimer about a white South African family sheltered by their Black servant July during a violent revolution that ends apartheid.

parts.answer: South Africa (accept Republic of South Africa)

topics.description: The young protagonist of Robert Louis Stevenson's novel Treasure Island, who serves as a cabin boy aboard the Hispaniola and becomes involved in the pirate mutiny and search for hidden treasure.

parts.question: A character in this novel carries a snuff-box filled with parmesan cheese while on a trip funded by Squire Trelawney. parts.question: [E] Long John Silver is one of these seafaring bandits in Treasure Island. Calico Jack and Blackbeard are two of these people who plunder at sea.

topics.description: A Belgian private detective created by Agatha Christie, known for solving crimes through psychological insight and his celebrated “little grey cells.”

parts.label: L
parts.question: This character requires that any two eggs he eats must be of equal size. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [H] Name this man, who refers to his intelligence as his “little grey cells.” In one novel, this character unknowingly encounters the gangster Lanfranco Cassetti.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [M] In this novel, Poirot solves a murder while stranded in Croatia due to a snowdrift. In this novel, it is determined that all twelve possible suspects in the stabbing of Samuel Ratchett committed the crime.

parts.question: [E] Murder on the Orient Express is a crime novel by this English writer. This prolific murder mystery author also created Miss Marple.
parts.answer: Agatha Christie [or Agatha Mary Clarissa Christie; accept Agatha Mary Clarissa Miller]

parts.label: L
parts.question: The murder of Samuel Ratchett is solved by this character, who often boasts of his “little gray cells.” For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this Belgian detective, who solves the mystery of the title Murder on the Orient Express.

parts.question: This author of The Murder on the Orient Express also writes about Poirot in her novel The Murder of Roger Ackroyd. Justice Holgrave fakes his death in this mystery author’s novel And Then There Were None.

parts.question: Christie also wrote this play, in which the residents of Monkswell Manor are interrogated by Sergeant Trotter. This play, with over 27,000 performances, frequently uses the song “Three Blind Mice.”

topics.topic: The Charge of the Light Brigade (poem)
topics.description: A narrative poem by Alfred, Lord Tennyson depicting the doomed British cavalry charge at the Battle of Balaclava.
aliases: The Charge of the Light Brigade
Tennyson's Charge of the Light Brigade

parts.label: L
parts.question: This man penned an elegy for himself, writing that “I hope to see my Pilot face to face / when I have crossed the bar”. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this British poet of "Crossing the Bar". Another of his poems is set during the Crimean War and describes a cavalry unit at the Battle of Balaclava.

parts.label: B
parts.question: This Tennyson poem opens "Half a league, half a league / half a league onward”. Its final stanza asks "When can their glory fade? / O the wild charge they made!".

parts.label: C
parts.question: “The Charge of the Light Brigade” describes the cavalry riding into the “valley of” this concept. An Emily Dickinson poem begins “Because I could not stop for [this concept] -- / He kindly stopped for me”.

parts.label: L
parts.question: In a poem titled for this form, George Oppen described “small nouns / Crying faith” in a “forest” where “wild deer / Startle, and stare out.” For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [E] Name this form of sacred poetry. A book of the Old Testament titled for this form includes a poem that states, “the Lord is my shepherd; I shall not want.”
parts.answer: psalm [accept the Book of Psalms; prompt on hymn]

parts.label: B
parts.question: [H] A young man exclaims, “Life is real! Life is earnest! / And the grave is not its goal” in this poet’s “A Psalm of Life.” A woman “thought of Christ, who stilled the wave / On the lake of Galilee” in this poet’s “The Wreck of the Hesperus.”

parts.label: C
parts.question: [M] This poem’s repeated reference to a “valley of death” originates from a line in Psalm 23, which describes “the valley of the shadow of death.” This poem describes a journey “into the jaws of Death, / into the mouth of hell.”
parts.answer: “The Charge of the Light Brigade” (by Alfred, Lord Tennyson)

topics.topic: The Misfit (A Good Man Is Hard to Find)
topics.description: A murderous escaped convict and philosophical antagonist in Flannery O’Connor’s short story “A Good Man Is Hard to Find.”

parts.label: L
parts.question: This character shoots an old woman three times after she touches his shoulder and calls him “one of [her] own children." For 10 points each:

parts.question: [H] Name this character, who claims “Jesus thrown everything off balance” while he and his partners Hiram and Bobby Lee murder a family.

parts.question: [M] The Misfit kills the grandmother, while his associates kill the rest of Bailey’s family, in this Flannery O’Connor short story.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [E] In “A Good Man Is Hard to Find," Bailey’s family dies while traveling to Florida from this state’s city of Atlanta.

parts.question: A sign in this short story describes one character as “THE FAT BOY WITH THE HAPPY LAUGH.” Two characters discuss Jesus’ power to resurrect in this story, which ends with a man saying there is “no real pleasure in life.” Mr. Edgar Atkins Teagarden buys a character in this story a watermelon carved with his initials, E.A.T. In this short story, (*) Red Sammy runs a barbecue restaurant called “The Tower.” The cat Pitty Sing causes a car accident in this story that leads a family driving to Florida to be shot by an escaped criminal, the Misfit. parts.answer: “A Good Man is Hard to Find”

topics.description: A fictional Great Old One created by H. P. Lovecraft who sleeps in the sunken city of R'lyeh and appears centrally in the Cthulhu Mythos.

parts.question: Many authors create a powerful feeling of a setting by setting otherwise unrelated works in a single fictional location based on real life. For ten points each,

parts.label: A
parts.question: This Nobel laureate from the American South set Absalom, Absalom!, The Sound and the Fury, and nearly every other one of his works in the fictional Yoknapatawpha [yawk-na-pa-TAW-fa] County in Mississippi.

parts.label: B
parts.question: This English author’s setting of Wessex shares its name with a real medieval English kingdom, but is otherwise fictional. In one book, Jude Fawley moves to Christminster, this author’s version of Oxford.
parts.answer: Thomas Hardy (Jude is the protagonist of Hardy’s Jude the Obscure.)

parts.question: New England was heavily fictionalized by H.P. Lovecraft for his “Mythos” of this eldritch horror, who “waits dreaming” according to a cultist chant in one story.
parts.answer: Cthulhu ([k’THOO-loo], but be incredibly lenient; accept The Call of Cthulhu)

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: A clay bas-relief of this figure, sculpted by Henry Wilcox in his sleep, sparks an investigation in which Professor Angell finds high rates of disturbing dreams in artists and poets. The Norwegian sailor Johannsen describes stumbling across this figure’s “damp Cyclopean city of slimy green stone.” In a story about this figure, a couplet ending, “And with strange aeons even death may die,” parallels a cult chant translating to “in his house at (*) R’lyeh [this creature] waits dreaming.” This Great Old One inspired a namesake “mythos,” starting with a short story titled “The Call of [this creature].” For 10 points, name this octopus-headed monster created by H. P. Lovecraft.
parts.answer: Cthulhu [accept any reasonable pronunciations like “cuh-thoo-loo” or “too-loo” or “k’too-loo”]

parts.question: This character visits Balnibarbi, a kingdom ruled from the floating island of Laputa, where he observes crazy experiments like softening marble to use in pillows and extracting sunbeams from cucumbers. For ten points each:

topics.description: A fictional Colombian town that is the principal setting of Gabriel García Márquez's One Hundred Years of Solitude and appears in several of his other works.

In this novel, only one man remembers the massacre of three hundred plantation workers. A character from  this novel fears that babies born from incest will grow a (*) pig’s tail. parts.question: For 10 points each, answer the following about the lexicon of Edgar Allen Poe:

parts.question: [E] Poe wrote this poem about a bird who repeatedly croaks “Nevermore.” This poem also describes a “pallid bust of Pallas just above my chamber door.”

parts.question: [H] In Poe’s short story, “The Murders in the Rue Morgue” C. topics.description: The mischievous fictional Missouri boy and title character of Mark Twain's The Adventures of Tom Sawyer.

topics.description: An ancient Greek tragedian and playwright best known for works including Oedipus Rex, Oedipus at Colonus, and Antigone.

parts.question: A prophecy in a play about this character foretells that he will die in a grove sacred to the Furies. Another play about this character “at Colonus” follows the play Antigone (an-TI-guh-nee) chronologically and describes his life after he stabs his eyes out with pins from his mother’s dress. This character marries his (*) mother Jocasta in the first of Sophocles’ Theban Trilogy. The Sphinx’s riddle about man was solved by, for ten points, what Greek hero, the namesake of an incestual “complex”?
parts.answer: Oedipus [accept Oedipus Rex or Oedipus the King or Oedipus at Colonus or Oedipus Coloneus]

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: This character’s daughter is sentenced to being entombed alive in a cave because she scattered earth over the corpse of her brother, Polynices [poly-NIGH-sees]. Tiresias [ti-REE-see-us] reluctantly advises this ruler that he is the uncaptured murderer of the previous king of (*) Thebes. The riddle of the Sphinx was solved by this man, whose response to the death of Jocasta is to blind himself. A trilogy by Sophocles is about, for ten points, what ancient Greek figure who killed his father and married his mother?

topics.description: Art Spiegelman's graphic memoir recounts his father Vladek Spiegelman's experiences during the Holocaust and explores their relationship and its lasting effects.

parts.label: L
parts.question: One character in this work survives because of his ability to repair shoes. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [M] Name this book, in which the narrator’s father, Vladek, recounts his experiences in the Holocaust. In 2015, this Art Spiegelman book was removed from store shelves in Russia due to its use of a swastika on the cover.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [H] In Maus, nationalities are represented by various animals, with Polish people being this animal. In another novel, one of these animals and a human set down the Ace of Spades at the same time during a poker game.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [E] Maus illustrates Vladek’s story in this medium. Examples of works in this medium, which combine words and images to tell a story, include the Amulet series and Persepolis.

parts.question: In a story set during this event, the infant Magda screams after a shawl is taken from her. A chemist contemplates the difference between the “drowned” and the “saved” in a book set during this event. In another book set during this event, Mrs. Schächter (“SHECK-ter”) repeatedly claims that she can see fire in the distance. People are represented as (*) cats and mice in a graphic novel about this event by Art Spiegelman. The memoir If This Is a Man is set during this event, as is a book in which the townspeople of Sighet ignore warnings given by Moishe the Beadle. For 10 points, Night by Elie Wiesel describes life during what genocide of Jews during World War II?
parts.answer: the Holocaust [or the Shoah; prompt on World War II or WWII or the Second World War before “World War II”]

topics.description: A 1985 play by August Wilson about Troy Maxson and his family in 1950s Pittsburgh.

parts.label: L
parts.question: A character in this play says to his wife Rose, “I give you my sweat and my blood. I ain't got no  tears.” For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [10] Name this play featuring the garbage truck driver Troy Maxson and his brother Gabriel, a veteran  who suffered a head injury in the war.

parts.question: [10] Gabriel fervently believes that he is this sort of being. Tony Kushner wrote a two-part play titled for  these beings in America.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [10] Gabriel ends the play by performing this action with a prop he holds, inspired by the actions of such  biblical characters as Gideon, in an attempt to get St. Peter to “open the gates.”
parts.answer: blowing a trumpet [or playing or sounding a trumpet]

parts.label: L
parts.question: One character in this play prohibits his son, Cory, from accepting a football scholarship. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [H] Name this play by August Wilson about the black garbage truck driver Troy Maxson. Denzel Washington plays Troy in a film adaptation of this play.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] Fences is part of the “Pittsburgh Cycle,” which includes a play titled for “[this instrument’s] Lesson.” This keyboard instrument often has black and white keys.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [M] In Fences, Troy Maxson is a former player of this sport. This sport is the subject of The Natural and “Casey at the Bat.”

topics.description: Sanskrit is an ancient Indo-Aryan language of South Asia used extensively in Hindu scriptures, classical Indian literature, religion, and scholarship.

parts.label: L
parts.question: The title character of one play by this author is forgotten by King Dushyanta after she loses a signet ring in a river. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this Indian author of “The Recognition of Shakuntala” and “The Cloud Messenger.”

parts.label: B
parts.question: Kalidasa wrote in this ancient Indian language, which was also used to write Hindu texts, such as the Vedas.

parts.label: C
parts.question: In “The Cloud Messenger," a yaksha asks a cloud to take a message to his wife after being exiled from his home in this mountain range. This Asian mountain range includes Mount Everest.

parts.label: L
parts.question: In a play written in this language, a beggar brawls with a Buddhist monk because he thinks he stole a bowl, only for it to later be discovered that the bowl was in fact stolen by a dog. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [M] Name this language that the playwright Kālidāsa [kaa-lee-daa-suh] wrote in.
parts.answer: ANSWER: Sanskrit (The play in the leadin is A Farce of Drunken Sport by Pallava emperor Mahendravarman I.)

parts.label: B
parts.question: [H] Sanskrit was used to write adaptations of stories from the Mahabharata [mah-ha-BAH-ruh-tuh], including the tale of this wife of Dushyanta [doo-shyun-tah]. A Kālidāsa play retells the story of this character.
parts.answer: ANSWER: Shakuntala [accept The Sign of Shakuntala or The Recognition of Shakuntalam or The Sign of Shakuntalam or Abhijnanashakuntala or Abhijñāna Shākuntalam]

parts.label: C
parts.question: [E] Virtually every surviving classical Indian play has a happy ending, meaning that there are no Sanskrit plays that could be classified as this genre. Aristotle’s Poetics contrasts this genre with comedy.

topics.description: A mischievous fairy and servant or jester of Oberon in William Shakespeare’s A Midsummer Night’s Dream, known for transforming Nick Bottom’s head into that of a donkey.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: Six “rude mechanicals” in this play act out Pyramus and Thisbe. The male lead in that play within this play is Nick Bottom, whose head is turned into a donkey’s head by a character called Robin Goodfellow. This play centers around romantic conflict between (*) Helena, Lysander, Demetrius, and Hermia, as well as the trickster sprite Puck. For ten points, name this Shakespeare comedy about the marriage of Theseus and Hippolyta.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Oberon and Titania are considered the king and queen of these beings in one play. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [E] Name these mythical beings. J.M Barrie created one of these beings, named Tinker Bell, in Peter Pan.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [M] The fairies Oberon and Titania appear in this play by William Shakespeare. This play ends with the double wedding of Hermia and Lysander and Helena and Demetrius.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [H] This mischievous fairy from A Midsummer Night’s Dream serves as Oberon’s jester. This character transforms Nick Bottom’s head into that of a donkey.

topics.description: Portuguese novelist and 1998 Nobel Prize in Literature laureate, known for works including Blindness, The Stone Raft, and The Gospel According to Jesus Christ.

parts.label: L
parts.question: One character in this novel is overwhelmed after observing a huge mass of rotting bodies in a supermarket  storeroom. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [H] Name this novel, in which the doctor’s wife is never afflicted by the title “white sickness.”
parts.answer: Blindness [or Essay on Blindness; or Ensaio sobre a cegueira]

parts.label: B
parts.question: [M] Blindness is by this Portuguese author, who died in 2010. This 1998 Nobel Prize winning author also wrote The  Stone Raft.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [E] Another novel by Saramago retells the New Testament from the perspective of this figure in The Gospel  According to [this figure]. This figure from Nazareth is the “Son of God” and is crucified on the True Cross.
parts.answer: Jesus Christ [accept either underlined portion; or The Gospel According to Jesus Christ; or O  Evangelho Segundo Jesus Cristo]

parts.label: L
parts.question: In one novel by this author, Joseph is plagued by nightmares after learning of the Massacre of the Innocents, but choosing to only save his son. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [M] Name this author of The Gospel According to Jesus Christ. In another novel by this author, everybody but the doctor’s wife is afflicted with the title plague of Blindness.
parts.answer: José Saramago [or José de Sousa Saramago]

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] José Saramago was born in this Iberian country. One work by Saramago describes an alternate history of this country in which crusaders did not help capture its city of Lisbon.
parts.answer: Portugal [or the Portuguese Republic or República Portuguesa]

parts.label: C
parts.question: [H] In this José Saramago novel, the Iberian peninsula breaks off from Europe and floats into the Atlantic Ocean. Characters in this novel include “The King of Starlings,” a girl who finds an endless ball of yarn, and a mute dog.
parts.answer: The Stone Raft [or A Jangada de Pedra]

topics.description: Daniel Defoe’s 1719 novel about the sailor Robinson Crusoe, who survives for twenty-eight years after being shipwrecked on a deserted island and encounters Friday.
aliases: The Life and Strange Surprizing Adventures of Robinson Crusoe
The Life and Strange Surprising Adventures of Robinson Crusoe
The Life and Strange Surprizing Adventures of Robinson Crusoe of York, Mariner

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: In the final section of a novel by this author, the title character and a “Lancashire (LAIN-kuh-sher) husband” Jemmy are transported to colonial Maryland and Virginia. This author was  inspired by a real woman whom he met while imprisoned at Newgate to write (*) Moll Flanders.  This man discussed an epidemic of 1665 in his fictionalized Journal of the Plague Year. A character  created by this author employs Xury (ZUR-ee) and Friday during 28 years on a pre-modern island. For  10 points, name this English author of Robinson Crusoe.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: This novel’s protagonist escapes from slavery with Xury, whom he immediately sells as an indentured servant. While stranded near the Orinoco River, this novel’s protagonist builds a house in a cave and rescues a man he names “Friday” from local cannibals. For ten points, name this novel by Daniel Defoe in which the title sailor is returned to England after being shipwrecked for twenty-eight years on a deserted island.
parts.answer: Robinson Crusoe (accept The Life and (Strange Surprizing) Adventures of Robinson Crusoe of York, Mariner: Who Lived Eight and Twenty Years, All Alone in an Un-inhabited Island on the Coast of America, Near the Mouth of the Great River of Oroonoque; Having Been Cast on Shore by Shipwreck, Wherein All the Men Perished but Himself. With an Account how he was at last as Strangely Deliver’d by Pyrates. Written by Himself.)

topics.description: An American writer of weird, cosmic, and horror fiction who created the Cthulhu Mythos.

parts.label: L
parts.question: A 2020 HBO series titled [this man] Country starred Michael K. Williams in his final TV role. For ten points each,

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this racist horror and speculative fiction author who created horrifically unimaginable, impossibly ancient gods called the “Great Old Ones,” including Yog-Sothoth, in the magazine Weird Tales.

parts.label: B
parts.question: Perhaps the most famous of H.P. Lovecraft’s “Great Old Ones” is this underwater creature, who is often depicted with enormous wings and a face full of tentacles.
parts.answer: Cthulhu ([kah-THOO-loo], but be lenient with pronunciation)

parts.label: C
parts.question: Lovecraft Country’s producers included this longtime collaborator of Keegan-Michael Key. This man’s directorial debut was the 2017 horror smash hit Get Out.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: A clay bas-relief of this figure, sculpted by Henry Wilcox in his sleep, sparks an investigation in which Professor Angell finds high rates of disturbing dreams in artists and poets. The Norwegian sailor Johannsen describes stumbling across this figure’s “damp Cyclopean city of slimy green stone.” In a story about this figure, a couplet ending, “And with strange aeons even death may die,” parallels a cult chant translating to “in his house at (*) R’lyeh [this creature] waits dreaming.” This Great Old One inspired a namesake “mythos,” starting with a short story titled “The Call of [this creature].” For 10 points, name this octopus-headed monster created by H. P. Lovecraft.
parts.answer: Cthulhu [accept any reasonable pronunciations like “cuh-thoo-loo” or “too-loo” or “k’too-loo”]

topics.description: Jacob Grimm and Wilhelm Grimm were German philologists, folklorists, and siblings best known for collecting and publishing folk and fairy tales in Children’s and Household Tales.
aliases: Jacob Ludwig Karl and Wilhelm Carl Grimm

parts.label: L
parts.question: One story by these people sees a straw, a coal, and a bean meet an unfortunate end after the coal burns up the straw and the bean splits itself laughing. For 10 points each:

parts.question: [E] Name these German brothers who collected many fairy tales in their Children’s and Household Tales. That collection includes the stories of Cinderella and The Little Red Riding Hood.

parts.question: [M] The title girl of this story is named after a vegetable grown in a witch’s garden that her mother craved while she was pregnant. In this story, a man is blinded after being thrown into a thorn bush from a tower.

parts.question: Name this folk tale in which the title girl is forced to be a servant in her family’s house, but marries a prince after her fairy godmother gives her a pair of glass slippers.
parts.answer: Cinderella (accept Cenerentola; accept Aschenputtel before it is read)

parts.label: B
parts.question: A German version of “Cinderella” appears in the Children’s and Household Tales collected by these folk-tale-obsessed brothers.
parts.answer: Grimm brothers (accept Brothers Grimm; accept Jacob Ludwig Karl and/or Wilhelm Carl Grimm)

parts.label: C
parts.question: In addition to studying fairy tales and German mythology, Jacob Grimm worked in this field of study; he is the namesake of Grimm’s Law, a rule that describes a shift between Proto-Indo-European and German.

topics.description: Winnie-the-Pooh is A. A. Milne’s honey-loving bear who lives in the Hundred Acre Wood and befriends Christopher Robin, Eeyore, Tigger, and others.

parts.label: L
parts.question: This author wrote about the title talking cat, which angers guests at a dinner party by spreading overheard gossip,  in his short story “Tobermory.” For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [H] Name this author, who ends his short story “The Open Window” with the line “romance at short notice was her  specialty.”

parts.label: B
parts.question: [M] Saki’s “The Interlopers” follows two characters with this profession. A character with this profession is the  protagonist of “The Most Dangerous Game.”

parts.label: C
parts.question: [E] An introduction to Saki’s The Chronicles of Clovis was written by A. A. Milne, who created this fictional bear.  This resident of the Hundred Acre Wood is friends with characters such as Eeyore and Tigger, and loves honey.

parts.question: When one of these animals gets trapped in a Very Big Pit, he is mistaken for a Heffalump. Another of these animals from “darkest Peru” is raised by his Uncle Pastuzo and Aunt Lucy and loves marmalade. In a work by A.A. Milne, (*) the Hundred Acre Wood is home to a honey-loving one of these animals that is the best friend of Christopher Robin. For 10 points, Winnie-the-Pooh and Paddington are what type of animals?

topics.description: Charles Dickens's historical novel set in London and Paris during the French Revolution, featuring Sydney Carton's sacrifice in place of Charles Darnay.

parts.question: The opening lines of this novel contrast the “age of wisdom” with the “age of foolishness” and the “spring of hope” with the “winter of despair”. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [10] Name this novel in which Sydney Carton takes the place of Charles Darnay.

In that novel by this author, a character traumatized by his long imprisonment compulsively makes shoes. The protagonist of a novel by this author is arrested after two companions steal a handkerchief from (*) Mr. Brownlow. A novel by this author begins with the contrasting extremes, “It was the best of times, it was the worst of times.” For 10 points, name this author of A Tale of Two Cities and Oliver Twist.
parts.answer: Charles Dickens [or Charles John Huffam Dickens]

topics.description: The Prince of Denmark and protagonist of Shakespeare’s Hamlet, who feigns or experiences madness while seeking revenge against Claudius.

parts.question: In this character’s first soliloquy, he exclaims “frailty, thy name is woman.” This character, who calls Yorick a “fellow of infinite jest,” hires an acting troupe to perform The Murder of Gonzago. (*) Rosencrantz and Guildenstern are friends of this character, who tells Ophelia to “get thee to a nunnery.” A soliloquy beginning “to be or not to be” is given by, for 10 points, what Prince of Denmark, who titles a Shakespeare tragedy?

parts.question: This character describes Yorick as a "fellow of infinite jest" in its graveyard scene while holding up the latter's skull. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [10] Identify this title character of a Shakespeare play who attempts to expose King Claudius's treachery.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [10] This lover of Hamlet and daughter of Polonius drowns herself in the play's 4th act. She too gives her own soliloquy after Hamlet rejects her in a fit of madness.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [10] Hamlet is an example of a Shakespearean tragedy, a genre of play contrasted with this other genre. This genre describes plays and other works intended to cause laughter or amusement, and modern performers like John Mulaney practice its "stand-up" variety.

topics.description: A 1944 existentialist play by Jean-Paul Sartre in which Estelle, Garcin, and Inez are confined together and conclude that hell is other people.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: A character in this play describes missing “Four thousand little rests per hour” and asks “how  shall I endure my own company?” While giving a climactic speech in this play, a character strokes  a mantelpiece dubbed a “bronze atrocity” by Barbedienne (BAR-bud-ee-EN). A valet lacks (*) eyelids in this play and brings the main characters into a room with Second Empire furniture. Inez is  stabbed by Estelle in this play, which ends with a character realizing that “Hell is other people.” For 10  points, name this existentialist play by Jean-Paul Sartre.
parts.answer: ANSWER: No Exit [or Huis Clos; or In Camera; or No Way Out; or Dead End]

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: One character in this play states that his wife is a “sensitive-plant” after acknowledging she clings onto a coat he owns with twelve bullet holes in it. That character in this play also complains about the lack of nighttime and his missing toothbrush. Another character in this play is summoned by the sound of a (*) faulty bell, and lacks eyelids. While stroking a bronze ornament in a Second Empire-style room, one character in this play declares “Hell is - other people!” For 10 points, name this play about Estelle, Garcin [gar-SAN], and Inez [ee-NESS], written by Jean-Paul Sartre [SAR-truh].
parts.answer: ANSWER: No Exit [or Huis Clos] (The character who lacks eyelids is the valet.)

topics.description: A tragic character in Shakespeare's Hamlet, the daughter of Polonius and lover of Hamlet who descends into madness and drowns.

parts.question: This character describes Yorick as a "fellow of infinite jest" in its graveyard scene while holding up the latter's skull. For 10 points each:

parts.question: [10] Identify this title character of a Shakespeare play who attempts to expose King Claudius's treachery.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [10] This lover of Hamlet and daughter of Polonius drowns herself in the play's 4th act. She too gives her own soliloquy after Hamlet rejects her in a fit of madness.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [10] Hamlet is an example of a Shakespearean tragedy, a genre of play contrasted with this other genre. This genre describes plays and other works intended to cause laughter or amusement, and modern performers like John Mulaney practice its "stand-up" variety.

parts.question: A character in this play offers columbine, rue, and daisies to a group gathered at Elsinore, but says that violets “withered all when [her] father died.” This play’s title character says “frailty, thy name is woman” when his mother (*) Gertrude marries his uncle Claudius, and duels Laertes, the brother of Ophelia, over the death of Polonius. topics.description: A poem by Robert Frost about birch trees, childhood imagination, escape, and returning to earthly life.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: In a parody of a poem titled for one of these objects, Ogden Nash claimed “I’ll never see [one of these objects] at all”. That original poem titled for these objects ends “poems are made by fools like me / But only God can make [one of these objects]” and was written by Joyce Kilmer. Another poem describes a “stop without a farmhouse near” while surrounded by these objects and ends by repeating “and (*) miles to go before I sleep.” One poem ends by claiming “one could do worse than be a swinger of [these objects]”. For 10 points, “top branches” and a “snow-white trunk” describe what objects, the subject of Robert Frost’s “Birches”?
parts.answer: ANSWER: trees [accept “Birches” until read; accept woods or “Stopping by Woods on a Snowy Evening”]

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: A “Witness” one of these objects titles a Pulitzer-winning poetry collection by Robert Frost. In the poem “Mending Wall,” Frost argues that objects of this type cannot “get across and eat the (*) cones” under another type of these plants. In a poem titled for a type of these plants, Frost describes boys “swinging” in these things after “climbing carefully to the top branches.” For ten points, name these tall plants in the poem “Birches.”
parts.answer: trees (accept A Witness Tree; accept apple trees or pine trees; accept Birches; prompt on “apple” after “get across” is read)

topics.description: Virgil was an ancient Roman poet best known for the epic Aeneid.

parts.label: L
parts.question: As a fictional character, this poet explains that unbaptized babies and virtuous pagans inhabit Limbo. For ten points each,

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this Roman poet who, in real life, wrote the Aeneid.

parts.label: B

parts.label: C

parts.label: L
parts.question: For 10 points each:

parts.question: Name this author who wrote about the love between Raina and the Serbian officer Bluntschli in the play Arms and the Man. In another play by this author, the professor Henry Higgins trains a flower girl to speak like a duchess.
parts.answer: George Bernard Shaw (The second play is Pygmalion.)

parts.label: B
parts.question: Shaw’s Arms and the Man takes its title from the opening line of this poet’s The Aeneid.

topics.description: South African playwright and director known for anti-apartheid dramas including The Blood Knot, The Island, and Master Harold...and the Boys.

parts.question: In one play from this country, a Sarah Vaughn song is played to cheer up the target of a racist joke. parts.question: Name this poet of “Stopping By Woods On A Snowy Evening” and “The Road Not Taken.”

parts.label: B
parts.question: In Frost’s poem “Mending Wall,” the speaker’s neighbor repeats the phrase “good [these objects] make good neighbors” as they both build one of these objects.

parts.question: In another poem, Frost muses how the world could end with these two substances. A Game of Thrones is the first book in a fantasy series titled A Song of [these two substances] by George R. R. Martin.

parts.question: This writer describes woods that are “lovely, dark, and deep” and a choice between two equal paths in two of his poems. For ten points each,

parts.question: Name this American poet who wrote “Stopping By Woods on a Snowy Evening” and “The Road Not Taken.”

parts.label: B
parts.question: In a poem about “Mending” one of these structures, Frost describes the natural forces that disturb one of these structures between his property and his neighbor’s.

parts.question: Analytic geometry uses the coordinate plane, which is centered at this point. This point is the intersection of the x- and y-axes and has coordinates (0,0) (“zero comma zero”).

parts.question: Pick’s theorem states that for a polygon on the coordinate plane, this quantity is equal to the number of lattice points contained inside the polygon plus half the number of lattice points on the boundary. topics.description: The mathematical operation of raising a base to an exponent or power.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Give the following about the traditional order of operations in arithmetic, for ten points each.

parts.label: A
parts.question: Multiplication comes before addition in the order of operations because multiplication is repeated addition; similarly, this operation of repeated multiplication comes before multiplication and division.
parts.answer: exponentiation (accept word forms like exponents; accept “raising to a power”; prompt on “squaring”, “cubing”, or other specific examples of an exponent)

parts.label: B
parts.question: These symbols are used to escape the normal order of operations; that is, “3 plus 4 minus 5” will be different if these symbols are placed around the “4 minus 5”.
parts.answer: parentheses (or parenthesis; accept brackets; accept braces)

parts.label: C
parts.question: With that said - addition has this property, so “3 plus 4 plus 5” gives the same result even if you do put parentheses around two of the numbers. Multiplication also has this property, but subtraction does not.

topics.description: Pierre de Fermat was a French mathematician whose contributions to number theory include Fermat's Last Theorem and Fermat's little theorem.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [10] This theorem concerns a general class of Diophantine equations. It states that if you know the remainders when a number is divided by several integers, you can uniquely determine the remainder when that number is divided by their product.

parts.question: [10] One of the most famous Diophantine equations is the subject of this French mathematician’s “last theorem”, which states that that the equation "a to the n plus b to the n equals c to the n" has no solutions in the integers if n is greater than 2 and was finally proved by Andrew Wiles in 1995.

parts.question: One theorem developed by this mathematician states that for any prime number p and any integer a, a to the p minus a is an integer multiple of p. For ten points each:

parts.label: B
parts.question: [M] Fermat’s Last Theorem states that no three positive integers a, b, and c satisfy the equation a to the n plus b to the n equals c to the n, for any n greater than this number. This number is the degree of quadratic polynomials.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [E] Pierre de Fermat was from this country, where he went to university in Orleans (or-lay-ON) and lived in Bordeaux (bore-DOH). This European country was also home to mathematicians such as Blaise Pascal and Rene Descartes.
