parts.question: Name this religious denomination whose adherents believe in an “inner light,” a metaphor for the inward light of God. William Penn was a wealthy member of this religious denomination.

parts.label: B
parts.question: William Penn founded this modern-day state after Quakers were persecuted by the Puritans of the Massachusetts Bay colony. Quakers founded many small colleges in this state like Bryn Mawr and Swarthmore, both of which are just outside of Philadelphia.

parts.label: C
parts.question: Some Quakers profess the universal priesthood, a belief that discards the idea of a separate class of priests. That belief comes from a verse in the First Epistle of this apostle, who is considered the first Pope.

parts.label: L
parts.question: The apocryphal “Acts of” this person contains the earliest known attestation of the tradition that he asked to be crucified upside-down. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [M] Name this person considered to be the first Pope. The doctrine of papal infallibility holds that the pope cannot err when speaking “from the chair” of this person.
parts.answer: ANSWER: Saint Peter [or Simon Peter; prompt on Simon]

parts.label: B
parts.question: [H] The doctrine of papal infallibility draws on this idea, which holds that the authority of bishops has been passed down continuously from the first followers of Christ. Rome claims special eminence according to this idea, since the church there was founded by Peter.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [E] In Catholicism, apostolic succession is transferred during Ordination through the laying on of these body parts. The wounds of Christ include stigmata on his feet and these body parts, which were nailed to the cross.
parts.answer: ANSWER: hands [accept laying on of hands; accept palms or wrists]

topics.description: A form of Mahayana and Vajrayana Buddhism practiced in Tibet and organized into schools including Nyingma, Sakya, Kagyu, and Gelug.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: The founding of a religious tradition from this region is recorded in the Testament of Ba, in  which Samye (SAHM-yay) is begun by Rinpoche (rin-poh-CHAY). The Nyingma (NING-mah) literature of this region includes the Bardo Thodol (BAR-doh thud-AHL). A religious tradition from  this region includes a high-ranking (*) “Panchen” (PON-chen) position. A leader of a tradition from  this region known as the “Yellow Hat” sect, who was born as Tenzin Gyatso (TEN-zin gee-AHT-soh),  was exiled and now lives in India. For 10 points, what region's religious literature includes the Buddhist  writings of the Dalai Lama?
parts.answer: Tibet [or Bod; or Xizang; do not accept or prompt on “Xinjiang”]

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: In one religion from this region, which is home to the Bon religion, deceased people travel through bardos,  as detailed in a non-Egyptian Book of the Dead. The Nyingma, Sakya, and Kagyu schools make up a “red  hat” sect, contrasted with the Tenzin Gyatso-led Gelug school in this region. The “yellow hat” sect of (*) Mahayana Buddhism is centered in this region. For 10 points, name this region, which was once led by the Dalai  Lama.
parts.answer: Tibet [or Bod or Xīzàng; prompt on People’s Republic of China, prompt on Himalayas]

topics.description: Asgard is the fortified realm and home of the Aesir gods in Norse mythology.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: In the poem Völuspá, three of the roots of Yggdrasil [igg-drah-sill] sit over this realm, which contains the home of Heimdallr. Loki transformed into a horse to distract a giant trying to build a wall around this (*) home of the Aesir. Warriors slain in battle are carried to two of this realm’s mead-halls, Fólkvangr and Valhalla. Bifrost, the rainbow bridge, connects Midgard to, for ten points, what realm of the gods in Norse myth?
parts.answer: Asgardr (anti-prompt on “Valhalla” by asking, “What realm contains Valhalla?”)

parts.label: L
parts.question: This event will be preceded by Fimbulwinter, a series of three successive winters that will kill all humans except for Líf and Lífþrasir (LEEF-thraa-seer). For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: Identify this event whose name means "Fate of the Gods" in Old Norse. During this event, Odin will be swallowed whole by the wolf Fenrir.

parts.label: B
parts.question: During Ragnarök, this god of thunder will kill and be killed by the sea serpent Jörmungandr (YOR-moon-gahn-der). He is probably better known for wielding the weapon Mjölnir (myol-neer).

parts.label: C
parts.question: Heimdallr will blow the Gjallarhorn (GYAH-lar-horn) to warn the occupants of this home of the gods about Ragnarök starting. In another myth, a giant and his horse attempted to build walls around this location.

topics.description: The anticipated final destruction, transformation, or consummation of the world in religious and eschatological traditions.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Czesław Miłosz (CHESS-woff MEE-woash) wrote that "those who expected lightning and thunder / are disappointed" in a poem he wrote titled "A Song on [this event]". For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: Describe this event which one poem predicted would occur "not with a bang but a whimper". Another poet wrote that "some say [this event will occur] in fire / some say in ice".
parts.answer: the end of the world [accept any alternate phrasings like the world will end or reasonable equivalents like the apocalypse or armageddon or eschaton]

parts.label: B
parts.question: This American poet wrote "Fire and Ice". In another poem, he wrote that "I have promises to keep / and miles to go before I sleep / and miles to go before I sleep".

parts.label: C
parts.question: This other poet wrote "this is the way the world ends / this is the way the world ends / this is the way the world ends / not with a bang but a whimper" in The Hollow Men. He also opened his poem The Waste Land by declaring that "April is the cruelest month".
parts.answer: T. S. Eliot [or Thomas Stearns Eliot]

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: This event is called frashokereti (FRA-sho-kuh-REH-tee) in Zoroastrianism. During an event of this kind, Frigga experiences her second sorrow when her husband is swallowed whole by Fenrir. Seven trumpets are sounded during this event in the Book of Revelation, and the (*) Four Horsemen of Conquest, War, Famine, and Death serve as its harbingers. For ten points, name this event in many religions wherein the Earth is destroyed.
parts.answer: the end of the world [accept the apocalypse or the end times or the Second Coming; accept equivalent answers; prompt on Armageddon or the Rapture or Ragnarok or doomsday or Judgement Day]

topics.description: The legendary king of Thebes who unknowingly kills his father Laius, marries his mother Jocasta, solves the Sphinx’s riddle, and blinds himself after learning the truth.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Martin Heidegger’s analysis of this play’s “Ode to Man” casts man as “the strangest of the strange.” For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [M] Name this play in which the title character kills herself after Creon sentences her to death for burying the body of Polynices.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] Antigone is the daughter of this character who appears in plays by Sophocles titled for him “at Colonus” and “Rex.” This king of Thebes unknowingly kills his father Laius at a crossroads and marries his mother Jocasta.
parts.answer: Oedipus [accept Oedipus at Colonus or Oedipus Rex]

parts.label: C
parts.question: [H] In Oedipus Rex, Oedipus accuses this man of treachery after this man tells him that Oedipus killed Laius. This man blames Creon’s refusal to bury Polynices for his inability to make sacrifices to the gods in Antigone.

parts.label: L
parts.question: As a baby, this mythical Greek king is sent out to die because his parents fear he will fulfill a dire prophecy. For ten points each,

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this mythical Greek figure who fulfills part of the prophecy when he kills his father, Laius [LAH-yuss], and becomes the king of Thebes in a series of plays by Sophocles.
parts.answer: Oedipus (accept Oedipus Rex or Oedipus Tyrannus; accept Oedipus at Colonus)

parts.label: B
parts.question: Oedipus becomes the king of Thebes by solving a riddle posed by this mythical creature, which has the body of a lion and the head of a human.

parts.label: C
parts.question: Oedipus fulfills the second part of his prophecy by marrying Jocasta, a woman who unknowingly has this familial relationship with Oedipus.
parts.answer: she is his own mother (accept equivalents like she is his mom; accept reversed and equivalent descriptions like he is her son or her child)

topics.description: Kali is a fierce Hindu goddess of destruction, commonly understood as an aspect of Parvati and associated with the defeat of demons such as Raktabija.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Answer these questions about a group of Hindu deities collectively nicknamed the Tridevi, for ten points each.

parts.label: A
parts.question: The Tridevi are often described as being similar to the Trimurti, except that all three deities have this quality. Lakshmi is a deity with this quality, which sets her apart from her husband,
parts.answer: they are female (accept equivalents like women or goddesses)

parts.label: B
parts.question: This member of the Tridevi is the goddess of wisdom and the wife of Brahma. She is often depicted with four arms, and carries a veena, a type of lute, to represent her love of music.

parts.label: C
parts.question: The third member of the Tridevi, Parvati, is also known by this name in her aspect as the goddess of destruction. This blue-skinned goddess slays demons and other evil spirits.

parts.label: L
parts.question: This deity has ten arms in her most powerful Maha form. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [H] Name this goddess who is summoned to a battlefield through the frown lines on another deity’s forehead. This goddess of destruction then goes on to slay the demon Raktabija.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] Kali is often depicted standing on top of this god. Since Kali is an aspect of Parvati, her consort is this Hindu destroyer god who composes the Trimurti along with Brahma and Vishnu.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [M] After drinking Raktabija’s blood, Kali goes on a rampage and performs this action over the dead bodies of her victims. Shiva performs the tandava when he takes the form of Nataraja, the lord of this action.
parts.answer: dance [accept word forms such as dancing or Lord of the Dance]

topics.description: The title and reincarnate lineage of the spiritual and traditionally political leaders of Tibetan Buddhism.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: Holders of this title owned the summer residence of Norbulingka. Holders of this position presided over the Ganden Phodrang and were subject to kidnapping attempts by the Dzungars. The name for this position originated from Altan Khan describing their “ocean of wisdom.” Because of government control over the Golden Urn selection process, this current head of the Yellow (*) Hat School has declined to create a tulku, or rebirth. The current holder of this position has been unable to occupy the Potala Palace after the People’s Liberation Army invaded Lhasa in 1959. Tenzin Gyatso is the 14th incarnation of, for 10 points, what spiritual leader of Tibet?

parts.label: L
parts.question: The current holder of this position, Tenzin Gyatso, is one of only two living people who were heads of state during World War II. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this position held by the spiritual leader of Tibetan Buddhism, currently occupied in exile in Dharamsala, India due to oppression by the Chinese government.

parts.label: B
parts.question: Tibetan Buddhists often worship by repeatedly chanting these sacred phrases, which include "om mani padme hum".

parts.label: C
parts.question: Tibetan Buddhists are split into schools named after "Red" and "Yellow" types of these garments. Muslims often wear one of these garments called a taqiyah during prayer.
parts.answer: hats [accept specific types of hats like skullcaps]

topics.description: The condition of living forever or being exempt from death, appearing as a supernatural ideal or attribute in multiple mythological traditions.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Though many authors have written that this structure is large enough to be seen from the moon, it is sometimes not even visible from low Earth orbits. For ten points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [E] Name this defensive fortification which, stretching from Liaodong to Lop Lake, protected China from Xiongnu (shong-NU) raids.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [H] This Chinese emperor combined numerous pre-existing walls to form the Great Wall of China. This emperor, who ended the Warring States period by founding the Qin (chin) dynasty, was buried with an army of terracotta soldiers.
parts.answer: Shi Huangdi [or Qin Shi Huang or Ying Zheng or Zhao Zheng; prompt on Qin]

parts.label: C
parts.question: [M] Shi Huangdi ironically died due to ingesting mercury pills, thinking that they would help him obtain this trait. In Chinese myth, eight people with this trait are thought to have lived on Bohai islands since the Shang dynasty.

parts.label: L
parts.question: When she’s not flying around in a mortar and pestle, Baba Yaga lives in a hut with the legs of this animal. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [H] Name this animal, one of whom tricks Reynard the Fox into opening his mouth to taunt in the Nun’s Priest’s Tale.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [M] The Slavic figure Koschei [kuh-SHAY] hides his soul inside a needle inside an egg inside a duck inside a hare inside a chest on a deserted island to maintain this trait. Tantalus tried to steal ambrosia and nectars, which grant this trait.
parts.answer: immortality [accept word forms such as being immortal; accept equivalents such as not dying or living forever; accept being deathless]

parts.label: C
parts.question: [E] In Polish and Hungarian folklore, cockatrices and basilisks hatch from chicken eggs and kill people in this manner. Staring into Medusa’s eyes caused this fate in Greek myth.
parts.answer: turning to stone [accept obvious equivalents; accept petrification; prompt on death or dying]

topics.description: A Haitian Vodou lwa who guards or presides over crossroads and serves as an intermediary between humans and the spirit world.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Members of this religion speak with the lwa [low-UH] Maman Brigitte by offering her dark rum with chili peppers. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [E] Anthropologists popularized the inaccurate idea that members of what Haitian religion stick pins in dolls?
parts.answer: voodoo [or vodun; or vodoun; accept voodoo dolls]

parts.label: B
parts.question: [H] Offering grilled steak and potatoes catches the attention of this lwa who appears as an old man with a cane, straw hat, and dog. This lwa offers to communicate with spirits at crossroads.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [M] Communicating with the orisha of love, Oshun, involves leaving offerings at these places. The largest gathering of humans in the world is the Kumbh Mela [cumb MAY-luh], a Hindu pilgrimage to one of these places that has issues with pollution.
parts.answer: rivers [accept streams; prompt on bodies of water; prompt on the Ganges]

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: One figure in this religion is portrayed wearing a tuxedo and a top hat while holding a cigar. The supreme god of this religion, Bondye, can be reached through (*) loa, such as the death spirit Baron Samedi and the spirit of the crossroads, Papa Legba. For 10 points, name this Haitian syncretic religion, which, contrary to popular belief, does not prominently feature pricking dolls with pins.
parts.answer: Voodoo [or Vaudou; or Voudou; or Vodun; or Vodon; or Vodou]

topics.description: American religious leader and founder of the Latter-day Saint movement, traditionally regarded by its adherents as a prophet and the translator of the Book of Mormon.

parts.label: L
parts.question: For ten points each, answer the following regarding Mormonism and the Latter Day Saint movement.

parts.label: A
parts.question: [H] This founder of the Mormon church published the Book of Mormon, which he claimed was translated from golden tablets with guidance from the angel Moroni. He was killed at Carthage Jail in 1844 by an armed mob.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] After Smith’s murder, a majority of Mormons followed Brigham Young to settle in what would become this state. The largest Mormon temple stands in this Western state’s Salt Lake City.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [M] Smith was murdered partly because of his claim that this practice is biblically permitted. This practice of taking multiple spouses was officially renounced by the mainline Mormon church in 1890.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: This religious movement’s Doctrine and Covenants was controversially edited in 1876. A set of six lessons called “Missionary Discussions” are used by some of this church’s missionaries. In 1978, this church ended its ban on having Black priests, and in the nineteenth century, this church was criticized both for its support of slavery as for its support of polygamy. Joseph Smith and Brigham Young were early leaders of, for ten points, what Christian church based in Utah?
parts.answer: LDS Church (accept the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints; accept Mormon Church)

topics.description: A Greek goddess of love and beauty, traditionally said to have been born from sea foam after Ouranos was castrated.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Gaia had many children with this deity, including a set of 6 pairs of twins. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [10] Name this Greek primordial deity, father of the Titans, who was defeated by his son, Kronos. He is the personification of the sky, and is the only specifically Greek deity to have a planet named after them.
parts.answer: Uranus [or Ouranos, do not accept or prompt on "Caelus"]

parts.label: B
parts.question: [10] These fifty-headed, many-armed giants, another set of children of Ouranos and Gaia, helped the Olympians overthrow the Titans. They included Cottus, Gyges, and Briares.
parts.answer: the Hekatonkheires [or the Hundred-Handed Ones or the Centimani]

parts.label: C
parts.question: [10] According to Hesiod, the fight between Kronos and Ouranos led to the birth of this Greek goddess of love and beauty after Ouranos's blood dripped into the sea.
parts.answer: Aphrodite [do not accept or prompt on "Venus"]

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: According to Homer, this deity is served by Euphrosyne (yoo-FRAHZ-ih-nee), Aglaea, and Thalia, otherwise called the Charites or Graces. This deity, who fought a custody battle against Persephone over the handsome Adonis, was born from seafoam following the castration of Uranus. Along with Ares, this goddess was trapped and humiliated in a (*) magic net crafted by her husband Hephaestus. For ten points, name this Greek goddess of love and beauty.

topics.description: The Christian event in which the angel Gabriel announces to Mary that she will conceive and bear Jesus.
aliases: Annunciation to the Blessed Virgin Mary

parts.label: L
parts.question: This city is depicted in the Allegory of Good and Bad Government, which it commissioned from a  native artist. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this home city of Ambrogio Lorenzetti (ahm-BRO-joh lor-en-zet-EE), as well as Duccio  (DOO-chee-OH), whose Maestà (my-est-ah) is likewise housed here.

parts.label: B
parts.question: Sienese artist Simone Martini included St. Margaret and St. Ansanus in a painting of this religious  scene. Sandro Botticelli's version of this scene for a church in Cestello (CHEST-el-oh) depicts Mary  stretching her hand towards a winged being.
parts.answer: the Annunciation [or Annunciation to the Blessed Virgin Mary; or Annunciation of Our  Lady]

parts.label: C
parts.question: Siena rivaled this Tuscan city, which was home to the Uffizi (OO-feet-see) Gallery and Botticelli.  The Medici family ruled over this city.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: A demonym for people from this city sometimes names the Saint Thomas Christians of India  and became a Quranic term for Christians. ISIS soldiers sprayed the first letter of that demonym  for this city onto Christian homes, inspiring a protest symbolized by the Arabic letter “nun.” In  this city, competing Catholic and Greek Orthodox churches mark proposed sites of the (*) Annunciation. After the flight into Egypt, Joseph returned to this city with Mary and a child born in  Bethlehem. For 10 points, name this childhood hometown of Jesus.
parts.answer: Nazareth [or an-Nasira; or Natsrat; or Nasrath]

topics.description: The Christian liturgical season of fasting, penitence, and spiritual preparation commemorating Jesus’s forty days in the desert and leading up to Easter.

parts.label: L
parts.question: During this period, religious images are often covered with purple veils. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [M] Name this approximately 40-day period where Christians fast or give up some luxuries to imitate the 40 days Jesus spent avoiding temptation in the desert.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [H] Lent begins on this day. This day’s namesake substance is used to mark crosses on the foreheads of participants and is accompanied by the phrase “thou art dust, and to dust thou shalt return” from the Book of Genesis.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [E] The solemn period of Lent leads up to this Sunday celebration of Jesus’s resurrection.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: Clean Monday marks the beginning of the “Great” form of this holiday in Orthodox Churches. This  holiday celebrates Jesus’s refusal to make bread out of stone for Satan during a period of 40 days spent in the  desert. (*) Ash crosses are drawn on the forehead of Western Christians on the first Wednesday of this period,  which ends on Good Friday. For 10 points, name this period, during which many Catholics give something up.

topics.description: The biblical paradise garden in Genesis where God places Adam and Eve before banishing them after their disobedience.

parts.label: L
parts.question: This poem claims it will “justify the ways of God to man.” For ten points each,

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this epic poem by John Milton that follows the creation, temptation, and downfall of Adam and Eve.

parts.label: B
parts.question: Paradise Lost fulfills its title when Adam and Eve take “their solitary way” and leave the paradise of this biblical garden.
parts.answer: Garden of Eden (accept Garden of God or gan-Yahweh)

parts.label: C
parts.question: Despite the angels’ efforts, Eve is tempted by this character, who was called Lucifer before the Angelic War. This figure thinks it is “better to reign in Hell than serve in Heaven.”

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: The name of this place is thought to come from the Akkadian word for a plain or steppe. Mormons believe this location to be placed in Jackson County, Missouri. Two of the four rivers flowing from this location are the Pishon and Gihon. The Land of Nod is found to the east of this place, which is guarded by a (*) flaming sword and cherubim. The principle of “original sin” is derived from an event in this location that caused its residents to flee in shame due to their nakedness. A serpent tricks a resident of this place into eating the forbidden fruit. For 10 points, name this location in Genesis from which God banishes Adam and Eve.
parts.answer: Garden of Eden [prompt on Paradise; prompt on the Garden]

topics.description: The ancient Egyptian sun god associated with the solar barque and the battle against the serpent Apep.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: This goddess created a serpent out of saliva to trick Ra into telling her his secret name. Along with Nephthys, this goddess was a daughter of Geb and Nut. After her husband is murdered by Set, this goddess searches across Egypt for the (*) fourteen pieces of his body. This goddess of magic was the mother of Horus. For 10 points, name this Egyptian goddess who was the wife of Osiris.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Sacrifices were often made to this god in Heliopolis. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [10] Name this Egyptian god who piloted the solar barque and fought the serpent Apep.
parts.answer: Ra [or Re or Ria or Riu or Riʕuw]

parts.label: B
parts.question: [10] Ra was also sometimes fused with this other falcon-headed deity, the rival of Set.
parts.answer: Horus [or Her or Heru or Hor or Har or Ḥaruw]

parts.label: C
parts.question: [10] One of these body parts belonging to Horus was a common protective symbol in Ancient Egypt. In Greek mythology, Argus Panoptes was a giant who had a hundred of these body parts.

topics.description: Tenzin Gyatso, the fourteenth Dalai Lama and exiled Tibetan Buddhist spiritual leader.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: The founding of a religious tradition from this region is recorded in the Testament of Ba, in  which Samye (SAHM-yay) is begun by Rinpoche (rin-poh-CHAY). The Nyingma (NING-mah) literature of this region includes the Bardo Thodol (BAR-doh thud-AHL). A religious tradition from  this region includes a high-ranking (*) “Panchen” (PON-chen) position. A leader of a tradition from  this region known as the “Yellow Hat” sect, who was born as Tenzin Gyatso (TEN-zin gee-AHT-soh),  was exiled and now lives in India. For 10 points, what region's religious literature includes the Buddhist  writings of the Dalai Lama?
parts.answer: Tibet [or Bod; or Xizang; do not accept or prompt on “Xinjiang”]

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: This activist has promoted the Middle Way Approach, which seeks cultural protection but not independence. This leader of the Gelug school lives in Dharamshala, having been forced to leave the Potala Palace in 1959 after a (*) pro-Chinese uprising took place in Lhasa. At age four, this bodhisattva was announced as the fourteenth man to hold his title. Tenzin Gyatso is the spiritual name of, for ten points, what exiled Tibetan Buddhist leader?
parts.answer: Dalai Lama (accept Tenzin Gyatso until it is read; accept Lhamo Thondup; accept Gyalwa Rinpoche)

topics.description: The Iranian or Persian New Year festival celebrated at the spring equinox, with roots in Iranian traditions and observance in Zoroastrian, Baháʼí, and related cultural contexts.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: In Bahai, the Nineteen Day Fast ends on one of these holidays, called Nowruz. On one of these holidays, which occurs fifteen days before the Lantern Festival, children are given red envelopes filled with money. A Jewish one of these holidays is the first of the (*) High Holy Days and takes place nine days before Yom Kippur. For 10 points, Rosh Hashanah is what type of holiday, which falls on January 1st in the Gregorian Calendar?
parts.answer: New Year’s Day [accept Nowruz until it is read, accept Chinese New Year; accept Lunar New Year; accept Rosh Hashanah until it is read]

parts.label: L
parts.question: The leadup to one of these holidays in the Bahá’í faith is marked by a nineteen-day fast. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [M] Name these holidays. The shofar is blown 100 times in the Jewish occurrence of this holiday, which also includes eating apples dipped in honey and throwing bread into water.
parts.answer: New Years [accept Baháʼí Naw-Rúz; accept Rosh Hashanah]

parts.label: B
parts.question: [H] Haft Sin tables, children banging on pots asking for candy, and jumping over bonfires are a few ways that the Iranian diaspora celebrates this Persian New Year on the spring equinox.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [E] The Hebrew calendar is based on the phases of this celestial object, which also gives the date for the Chinese New Year.

topics.description: Demeter is the Greek goddess of agriculture and fertility, mother of Persephone, whose myths include the changing seasons and the Eleusinian Mysteries.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: This deity was the mother of Zagreus and Melinoe, and raised Adonis, over whom she feuded with Aphrodite. Thsi goddess was also known by the name Kore [koh-ray], and was nearly kidnapped by (*) Pirithous. This goddess causes the changing of the seasons by spending part of each year with her mother, Demeter, and part with her abductor, Hades. For ten points, name this queen of the underworld in Greek myth.
parts.answer: Persephone (accept Kore before it is read; accept Proserpina before “Greek” is read)

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: This goddess is the mother of a figure who was worshipped under the title Despoina. This goddess transforms a Scythian king into a lynx for attempting to kill a man to whom she had earlier gifted a winged chariot pulled by snakes. A boy who makes fun of this goddess for drinking water is turned into a lizard. (*) Triptolemus is a student of this goddess. This goddess attempts to make Demophon immortal by placing him in a fire while searching for her missing daughter, who was abducted by Hades. For 10 points, name this Greek goddess of agriculture, the mother of Persephone.

topics.description: The first human pair in the Genesis tradition, whose disobedience leads to their expulsion from the Garden of Eden and represents humanity's Fall.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: The name of this place is thought to come from the Akkadian word for a plain or steppe. Mormons believe this location to be placed in Jackson County, Missouri. Two of the four rivers flowing from this location are the Pishon and Gihon. The Land of Nod is found to the east of this place, which is guarded by a (*) flaming sword and cherubim. The principle of “original sin” is derived from an event in this location that caused its residents to flee in shame due to their nakedness. A serpent tricks a resident of this place into eating the forbidden fruit. For 10 points, name this location in Genesis from which God banishes Adam and Eve.
parts.answer: Garden of Eden [prompt on Paradise; prompt on the Garden]

parts.label: L
parts.question: This poem attempts to “justify the ways of God to man.” For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [M] Name this epic poem by John Milton about “man's first disobedience.”

topics.description: An ancient Sanskrit Hindu epic traditionally attributed to Valmiki, recounting Rama’s exile, Sita’s abduction, the war in Lanka, and Ravana’s defeat.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: This holiday begins on Dhanteras and ends with Bhai Duj, which celebrates the relationship between siblings. Celebrations during this festival commemorate the defeat of the demon Narakasura and the return home of (*) Sita and Rama in the Ramayana. Offerings are given to Lakshmi during this holiday to celebrate the fiscal new year in autumn. For ten points, name this Hindu holiday celebrated with diya lamps, nicknamed the festival of lights.

parts.question: As a young boy, this figure hurls a demon many miles away into the ocean after the demon disrupts a sacrifice. In one myth, another character tears his chest open to reveal this character and his wife. An evil maidservant convinces this character’s aunt Kaikeyi to force him out of the kingdom. This character makes an alliance with the vanara king Sugriva while spending fourteen years in exile in the Dandaka forest. The monkey army helps this character and his brother Lakshmana attack Lanka. This character and his wife Sita are fervently worshiped by Hanuman. For 10 points, name this character who slays Ravana at the end of a Hindu epic, the seventh avatar of Vishnu.
parts.answer: Rama [or Ram; accept Ramayana or Ramayan; prompt on Vishnu before it is read]

topics.description: The cuboid sanctuary in the Masjid al-Haram in Mecca, Islam’s holiest site and the direction toward which Muslims pray.

parts.question: This structure was built by Ismail and his father, and is the focus of the qibla [kee-blah]. For ten points each,

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this cuboid, black shrine inside the Masjid al-Haram.

parts.label: B
parts.question: Believers circle the Kaaba during this holy pilgrimage, which all Muslims who are able-bodied and financially able must perform once in their life.
parts.answer: Hajj (accept, but do not otherwise reveal, pilgrimage to Makkah or pilgrimage to Mecca)

topics.description: The four symbolic horsemen in the Book of Revelation associated with conquest, war, famine, and death.

topics.description: The vigorous sacred and cosmic dance associated with Shiva, especially in his Nataraja form, symbolizing destructive and creative forces.

parts.question: This deity has ten arms in her most powerful Maha form. For 10 points each:

parts.question: Answer the following about the different forms of the Hindu god Shiva, for 10 points each:

parts.question: [H] In his hermaphrodite form Ardhanarishvara [uhr-duh-nuh-REESH-vuh-ruh], Shiva is combined with this other god. This goddess was born after Sati [SUH-tee] threw herself into a funeral pyre.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] Shiva is often depicted riding Nandi [NUN-dee], a white one of these animals. The slaughter of these animals is taboo across many Hindu states in India.

parts.question: [M] In his Nataraja [NUH-tuh-rah-juh] form, Shiva performs this action. Kali performs this action on top of Shiva in an attempt to destroy the world.

topics.description: A legendary cryptid reputed to attack livestock and drink their blood, associated with Puerto Rico, Mexico, and broader Latin American folklore.

parts.question: According to a text from the sixth century, this creature was stopped from attacking a monk’s follower when Saint Columba made the sign of the cross and told it to back off. For ten points each:

parts.question: [M] Name this creature of which a “surgeon’s photograph” was taken in 1934 that has since been mostly debunked as a hoax. This large and long-necked creature supposedly inhabits a body of water in the Scottish Highlands.

parts.question: [E] Like the Loch (lock) Ness Monster, this creature is a cryptid, since its existence is unsubstantiated. This creature is described as a hairy and ape-like humanoid creature in North American forests which leaves giant footprints.

parts.question: [H] Sightings of this cryptid whose name means “goat-sucker” have mostly been in northern Mexico. This spiny creature supposedly the size of a large dog is said to attack and suck the blood from livestock.

parts.question: The most famous photo of this creature, the so-called “surgeon’s photograph,” was revealed to be an elaborate hoax. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [M] Name this long-necked, humped cryptid that is named for and supposedly inhabits a lake in the Scottish highlands.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] The Patterson-Gimlin film supposedly shows this North American cryptid turning to face the camera as it runs away. This cryptid’s name comes from the large tracks it leaves behind.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [H] This reptilian-like cryptid, first purportedly sighted in Puerto Rico, is known for drinking the blood of goats and other livestock.

topics.description: Mythical aquatic beings traditionally depicted with human upper bodies and fish tails, including mermaids and mermen.

parts.question: A chair depicting one of these creatures commemorates a visit to Zennor in Cornwall by a ceasg [keask]. Barnum hoax. One of these creatures refuses to kill a Danish prince with a dagger from the Sea Witch in a fairy tale by (*) Hans Christian Andersen. Christopher Columbus likely saw a manatee and not one of these creatures, myths of which were inspired by the Sirens. For 10 points, name these creatures with the torso of a human and a fishtail.

parts.question: This character asks “do I dare to eat a peach?” in one poem. For 10 points each:

parts.question: [H] Name this subject of a “love song” in which “women come and go, talking of Michelangelo.”

parts.label: B
parts.question: [M] “The Love Song of J. Alfred Prufrock” is by this poet, who also wrote “The Wasteland.”

parts.label: C
parts.question: [E] Prufrock claims to hear these figures singing “each to each” but laments that they will not sing to him. These mythological figures have the torso of a woman and the tail of a fish.

topics.description: A monotheistic religion founded by Baháʼuʼlláh in the nineteenth century that teaches the unity of the world's major religions and includes practices such as Obligatory Prayer.

parts.question: Answer the following about prayer in Abrahamic religions, for ten points each.

parts.question: Members of this faith are encouraged to engage in five daily personal prayers, which should be performed facing the qibla, the direction of the Kaaba, whenever possible.

topics.description: A Chinese philosophical and religious tradition associated with Laozi, the Tao or “the way,” wu wei, and the complementary yin-yang forces.

parts.question: Name this religion founded by Li Hongzi. The five exercises in this religion are intended to turn the “Dharma wheel.”

parts.answer: Tao (accept Dao; accept Daoism and word forms like Daoist)

topics.description: Muhammad was the founder and central prophet of Islam, traditionally regarded as its final prophet and the recipient of the Quranic revelations.

parts.question: During the Night Journey, this man traveled to the seventh heaven and spoke with Moses and God. For 10 points each:

topics.description: Hagar is the Egyptian servant of Sarah in Genesis and the mother of Ishmael, who was sent into the wilderness with him.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Edmonia Lewis was an American artist who drew on the history of her African-American and Ojibwe parents to create iconic neoclassical marble sculptures in the late 1800s. For ten points each,

parts.label: A
parts.question: Lewis sculpted a series of depictions of this fictional Ojibwe warrior and his wife, Minnehaha, who appear in a namesake “Song” written by Henry Wadsworth Longfellow.

parts.label: B
parts.question: Lewis created a shockingly realistic sculpture of this Egyptian pharaoh lying dead across her throne. This ruler committed suicide with an asp after losing the Battle of Actium.

parts.question: Although many of her works have been destroyed, Lewis’s surviving masterpiece is a sculpture of this biblical woman, an Egyptian maidservant who was the mother of Abraham’s first son, Ishmael.
parts.answer: Hagar (accept Hagar in the Wilderness; accept Hajar)

parts.question: Answer the following about American sculptor Edmonia Lewis, who depicted an old man teaching a young child in the sculpture Old Arrow Maker, for ten points each.

parts.label: A
parts.question: Sculptures like Old Arrow Maker and Minehaha were inspired by Edmonia Lewis’s one-quarter heritage from this American ethnicity.
parts.answer: Native American (accept indigenous Americans; accept American Indian; accept Mississauga; accept Mississauga-Ojibwe)

parts.label: B
parts.question: Edmonia Lewis stunned the attendees of the Centennial Exposition in 1876 with her sculpture The Death of this Egyptian queen, who killed herself with an asp after the death of Mark Antony.

parts.label: C
parts.question: In another sculpture, Lewis depicted this biblical woman folding her hands in prayer as an empty water jug sits at her feet after she was sent into the desert with her son Ishmael.

topics.description: A giant lumberjack and folk hero of American tall tales, commonly accompanied by Babe the Blue Ox and credited with creating natural landmarks.

topics.description: A primordial or colossal sea monster in the Hebrew Bible and later Jewish and Christian traditions, associated with God's power and eschatological judgment.

parts.question: The Biblioteca Ambrosiana library in Milan holds a manuscript showing these two creatures below  the Ziz, all above an illustration of the Feast of the Righteous. For 10 points each:

parts.question: [10] Name these two great beasts of the land and the sea, respectively described in chapters 40 and 41 of  the Book of Job (joab).
parts.answer: Behemoth [or Behemot] and Leviathan [or Livyatan; or Lotan; or Rahab] [all acceptable  answers may be given in either order, but do not accept or prompt if only one answer is given]

parts.question: [10] The role of the Leviathan and Behemoth in the Day of Judgment is described in the apocryphal  book named for this father of Methusaleh, who directly “walked with God” into heaven without dying.

parts.question: [10] The word “ziz” appears in the Hebrew text of two of the 150 songs collected in this poetic book of  the Bible.

parts.label: L
parts.question: According to the Book of Enoch, one of these creatures lives in the abyss of the ocean, while the other lives in a waste land east of Eden. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [H] Name these two creatures described to emphasize God’s might in the Book of Job.
parts.answer: Behemoth AND Leviathan [accept answers in either order]

parts.question: [M] The Revised Standard Version suggests that Behemoth may be a hippo and Leviathan one of these animals. An Egyptian god of the Nile, Sobek, has the head of one of these animals.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [E] On the other hand, medieval Christian writers often considered Leviathan to be one of these beings charged with punishing envious sinners. These beings may be banished from a person with an exorcism.

parts.question: According to Homer, one of these objects made by Hephaestus depicted heavenly bodies and flourishing cities. parts.question: For sleeping with Poseidon in Athena’s temple, this mythical woman was punished by having her hair turned into writhing snakes. For ten points each,

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this gorgon who could turn humans to stone with her gaze.

parts.label: C
parts.question: After Perseus killed Medusa, he took her head to Athena, who set it onto this legendary shield.

topics.description: The practice of seeking hidden knowledge, supernatural guidance, or information about future events through signs, rituals, or other purportedly supernatural means.

parts.label: L
parts.question: One holder of this position was exiled for three years by his prime minister, Yi Yin, until he learned to behave  himself. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this general position, which was held by rulers of people centered around the Yellow and Yangtze Rivers.
parts.answer: emperor of China (prompt on partial answer)

parts.label: B

parts.question: [10] Name this practice, which onmyodo bases on the yin-yang cosmology, that is also key to a method  using the I Ching (EE ching). Shang oracle bones were used in this practice.

parts.question: [10] The I Ching's term for the “way of the gods” morphed into the name of this Japanese religion that  venerates kami (KAH-mee).

parts.label: C
parts.question: [10] The Japanese tale of Tajima Mori (TAA-jee-MAA mor-ee) mirrors a Daoist legend about one of these  locations named for the island of Penglai (pung-LAI). The Queen Mother of the West's abode is located  at this kind of feature called Kunlun (koon-LOON).

topics.description: The Christian doctrine that humanity inherits a fallen, morally corrupted condition as a consequence of Adam and Eve's Fall.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: Pelagianism holds that this thing does not significantly affect free will, unlike Jansenism, which holds that this thing completely removes free will. Because of this thing, Old Testament figures like David were in the Limbo of the Patriarchs before the Harrowing of Hell. The doctrine of the immaculate conception holds that Mary was conceived without this thing. parts.answer: original sin [prompt on sin or ancestral sin]

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: The name of this place is thought to come from the Akkadian word for a plain or steppe. Mormons believe this location to be placed in Jackson County, Missouri. Two of the four rivers flowing from this location are the Pishon and Gihon. The Land of Nod is found to the east of this place, which is guarded by a (*) flaming sword and cherubim. parts.question: One sect of this religion worships an androgynous god of space and time, called Zurvan. The dead in this religion are left on Towers of Silence to be eaten by vultures. parts.answer: Zoroastrianism [or Behdin; accept Mazdaism or Mazdayasna until “Mazda” is read and prompt afterwards; accept Zarathustrism or Zarathustrianism until “Zarathustra” is read and prompt afterwards]

parts.question: This figure stole the secret of fire from the goddess Mahuika (mah-WEE-kah) after she threw her burning fingernails at him. For ten points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [M] Name this hero who crawled into the body of the Goddess of the Night in an attempt to make mankind immortal. This figure sings “You’re Welcome” and is voiced by Dwayne The Rock Johnson in Moana.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] Maui (mah-wee) is credited with the creation of the Hawaiian islands, which lie on this large body of water. Polynesian mythology originates from the culture of native people who live on islands in this largest ocean.

parts.question: Answer the following about the work of Caribbean poet Derek Walcott, the author of the poem Omeros, for ten points each.

parts.question: In the Iliad, this nearly-invincible hero carries a shield showing a city at peace and at war. This hero and his enemy, Hector, are characterized as fishermen in Omeros.

parts.label: C
parts.question: In Omeros, Achille and Hector are in love with this housemaid, whose name is a reference to the “face that launched a thousand ships” to begin the Trojan War.
parts.answer: Helen (accept Helen of Troy; accept Helen of Sparta)

parts.label: L
parts.question: The speaker of this author’s poem “Spelling” says, “A child is not a poem, / a poem is not a child. / there is no either/or.” For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [E] Name this author, who created the character Aunt Lydia, “who was in love with either/or,” in the novel The Handmaid’s Tale.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [H] The speaker of Atwood’s poem “[you fit into me]” says, “you fit into me / like a hook into [one of these body parts.]” In The Handmaid’s Tale, Gilead’s police force is named after this body part.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [M] This woman declares “This is a torch song. / Touch me and you'll burn” in an Atwood poem titled for her doing “Countertop Dancing.” In Doctor Faustus, this woman is referred to as “the face that launched a thousand ships.”
parts.answer: Helen of Troy [accept “Helen of Troy Does Countertop Dancing”]

topics.description: An ancient Egyptian funerary judgment in which the deceased’s heart is weighed against the Feather of Ma’at to determine access to the afterlife.

parts.label: L
parts.question: In ancient Egyptian burials, these containers were guarded by representations of the four sons of Horus. For ten points each,

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name these containers that held the lungs, stomach, liver, and intestines of a mummified person.
parts.answer: canopic jars (accept canope; accept canopic chests)

parts.label: B
parts.question: After mummification, the deceased would undergo a ritual called the “Opening of” this body part, which was believed to allow the person to eat and drink in the afterlife.

parts.label: C
parts.question: After mummification, the soul of the deceased would be judged by Anubis by having this bodily organ weighed against the Feather of Ma’at to determine whether they could enter the afterlife.

parts.label: L
parts.question: At the end of this process, the subject either continues to the Field of Reeds or their soul is devoured by Ammit. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [H] Name this process in the Egyptian afterlife, where one of the subject’s organs is compared against the feather of Maat.
parts.answer: weighing of the heart [or judging the dead]

parts.label: B
parts.question: [M] The weighing of the heart is overseen by this jackal-headed Egyptian god of the afterlife, who also presides over the mummification process.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [E] Ammit, the devourer of souls, has the head of one of these reptiles, whose snout shape differentiates them from alligators.

topics.description: An ancient Egyptian lioness-headed goddess associated with war, destruction, plague, healing, and divine retribution.

parts.label: L
parts.question: When Ra sent Hathor to punish humanity for conspiring against him, she transformed into this goddess and was only stopped when she drank 7,000 gallons of beer stained to resemble blood. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [H] Name this “Lady of Terror,” an Egyptian goddess who defended Ma’at and had the head of a lioness.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [M] Sekhmet is one of many goddesses recognized as these body parts belonging to Ra. Thoth magically restored one of these body parts belonging to Horus called the wedjet.
parts.answer: ANSWER: eyes [accept Eye of Ra or Eye of Horus]

parts.label: C
parts.question: [E] Prayers to Sekhmet were whispered into the ears of cats who had undergone this process. Canopic jars contained organs that were removed from bodies before they were wrapped in bandages as part of this process.
parts.answer: ANSWER: mummification [accept descriptive answers such as turning into a mummy; prompt on embalming; prompt on burial; prompt on entombment; prompt on preservation; prompt on dying]

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: A deity with the head of this creature was called Ailuros [“eye”-loo-rohs] in Greece, and was worshipped at Bubastis [boo-bahs-tiss]. One of these creatures, named Ta-Miu [tah-myew], was entombed with Prince Thutmose. A fierce counterpart for a goddess with the head of this creature was Sekhmet, who had the head of a lion. Bastet had the head of, for ten points, what felines that were domesticated to control populations of mice in grain stores?
parts.answer: cat (accept synonyms like kitty; prompt on “feline” before it is read)

topics.description: A biblical patriarch and son of Jacob who was sold into slavery in Egypt, interpreted Pharaoh’s dreams, and rose to prominence by preparing Egypt for famine.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: One of these people was spared to tell of an event recognized by all-night study of the Torah on Shvi’i Shel. Yochnan ben Zakai argued that God took away one of these people’s free will by “hardening [his] heart.” One of these people dreams of seven lean cows eating seven fat cows, which is interpreted as a sign to stock grain by (*) Joseph. A baby set adrift down a river to escape an order from one of these people to kill all newborn children. One of these people’s soldiers were drowned in the Red Sea after it was earlier parted by Moses. For 10 points, Exodus describes the Jews escaping the rule of what leaders of ancient Egypt?
parts.answer: ANSWER: pharaohs [prompt on Kings of Egypt; prompt on rulers of Egypt; prompt on Egyptians]

parts.label: L
parts.question: A blessing on this man describes him as a “ravenous wolf” who “in the morning devours the prey.”  For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this youngest son of Rachel, who does not participate in the assault on another of his  brothers.

parts.label: B
parts.question: This patriarch, whose sons became the namesakes of the Tribes of Israel, delivered the fatherly  blessing to Benjamin and was married to Leah and Rachel.

parts.label: C
parts.question: The fatherly blessing to this person describes a “fruitful vine.” This person was sold into slavery in  Egypt after being given a “coat of many colors” by Jacob.
parts.answer: Joseph [or Yōsef; or Yōsēp̄; or Yehōsef; or Yо̆hōsēp̄; or Yūsuf]

topics.description: An Afrocentric religious and cultural movement that developed in Jamaica and venerates Ethiopian emperor Haile Selassie I as a messianic figure while identifying Africa with Zion and Western society with Babylon.

parts.label: L
parts.question: This religion’s adherents follow an ital [“eye”-tahl] diet and believe that western society, or “Babylon,” is harmful to people from Africa, or “Zion.” For ten points each,

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this religion founded in Ethiopia, in which wearing dreadlocks honors the Lion of Judah
parts.answer: Rasta (accept Rastafari; accept word forms like Rastafarianism)

parts.label: B
parts.question: In Rastafari, the Lion of Judah is a symbol of this emperor of Ethiopia, who is sometimes considered the second coming of Jesus.

parts.label: C
parts.question: In Rastafari, grounding ceremonies often incorporate the smoking of this substance, which is valued for its
parts.answer: marijuana (accept ganja; accept synonyms like cannabis; accept slang like pot)

parts.label: L
parts.question: This decentralized religion has many “mansions” like the Nyabinghi, the Bobo Ashanti, and the Twelve Tribes of Israel. For ten points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [M] Name this Afrocentric Abrahamic religion that developed in Jamaica during the early 1900s. Many followers of this religion believe that the Ethiopian emperor Haile Selassie I was the second coming of Christ.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [H] Followers of the Rastafarian Movement refer to God by this name. This name comes from a short form of the Hebrew tetragrammaton, the personal name of God used by the ancient Israelites.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [E] Followers of the Rastafarian Movement also abide by the i-tal one of these restrictions. Kosher foods refer to those that conform to the kashrut, the Jewish one of these general restrictions on food that one can eat.

topics.description: A New Testament Pauline epistle addressed to the church at Corinth that discusses spiritual gifts and contains the famous passage on faith, hope, and love, including “love is patient, love is kind.”
aliases: First Epistle of Paul to the Corinthians

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: Liberal outlooks like subjectivism and immanentism are criticized in a commentary on this thinker by Karl Barth. A passage by this thinker criticizes those who follow the law instead of the “culmination of the law” and remarks, “if you declare with your mouth… and believe in your heart… you will be saved.” A line by this thinker about the “righteousness of God” inspired Martin Luther’s doctrine of justification by faith alone. Another passage by this thinker declares, “love is patient, love is kind.” After this thinker was blinded on the road to Damascus, he converted to Christianity. For 10 points, name this apostle who wrote epistles to the Romans and Corinthians.
parts.answer: Paul the Apostle [or Saint Paul or Saul of Tarsus; prompt on Saul]

parts.label: L
parts.question: After a mass performance of this activity at the Bethel Bible School, William Seymour argued it was evidence of the “third work of grace.” For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [M] Name this activity that a “mighty rushing wind” compels the Apostles to do on Pentecost. This act involves uttering syllables to mimic a divine language.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] Pentecostalists argue that speaking in tongues is proof that someone has been baptized by this figure. A dove often represents this member of the Trinity alongside the Father and the Son.
parts.answer: Holy Spirit [or the Holy Ghost; prompt on partial answers; prompt on God]

parts.label: C
parts.question: [H] Paul discusses speaking and interpreting tongues in the first of his two epistles addressed to these people. Paul advises members of this Greek Church that “faith, hope, and love abide” and “love is patient, love is kind.”
parts.answer: Corinthians [accept 1 Corinthians or 2 Corinthians; accept the First Letter to the Corinthians; accept the First Epistle to the Corinthians; accept the Second Letter to the Corinthians; accept the Second Epistle to the Corintians]

topics.description: The supreme creator deity and embodiment of goodness in Zoroastrianism.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: One sect of this religion worships an androgynous god of space and time, called Zurvan. The dead in this religion are left on Towers of Silence to be eaten by vultures. Worship in this religion takes place in fire temples, whose central flame is called atar. This religion’s (*) Avesta details the struggle between Good and the evil Ahriman. For 10 points, name this Ancient Persian dualistic religion, which venerates the god Ahura Mazda.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: This substance and lawfulness are the domain of Asha Vahista, one of six divine beings created by Ahura Mazda. Atash Bahram is the highest classification of this substance, which is always present at an (*) agiary. Holy ones of this substance may never be extinguished, so priests must wear a face mask when handling it. Atar is, for ten points, what substance venerated as wisdom and light in Zoroastrianism, and which is kept burning in namesake temples?
parts.answer: holy fires (accept flames; accept Atar before it is read; accept Atash or Azar before “Atar” is read)

topics.description: A Greek hero who slew the Chimera and the Amazons and later fell while attempting to reach Mount Olympus on Pegasus.

parts.label: L
parts.question: This creature is an offspring of Typhon and Echidna, making it a sibling of such beasts as Cerberus and the Hydra. For ten points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this monster from Greek mythology. This part-lion, part-goat, and part-snake creature was slain at the command of King Iobates (eye-OBB-uh-teez) of Lycia after terrorizing his lands.

parts.label: B
parts.question: This hero is credited with the slaying of the Chimera and once defeated the Amazons by dropping boulders on them. After sleeping in a temple to Athena, this hero met his most famous steed, a flying horse.

parts.label: C
parts.question: This was the name of Bellerophon’s (beh-LAIR-uh-fonz) steed. This winged horse was stung by a gadfly sent by Zeus when an egotistic Bellerophon tried to fly to Mount Olympus.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: In the Theogony, an anvil is described as taking nine days to fall to earth from this location. After defeating the Chimera, Bellerophon attempts to reach this location by riding Pegasus, but a gadfly stings Pegasus, causing Bellerophon to fall. Hebe and Ganymede work as cupbearers to residents of this location, such as Ares and Aphrodite. For 10 points, name this mountain ruled by Zeus, the home of the gods.

topics.description: Funerary containers used in ancient Egypt to preserve the internal organs removed during mummification for the deceased's use in the afterlife.

parts.label: L
parts.question: One of these jars is personified by the baboon-headed god Hapi, while another depicts the human face of Imsety. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [M] Name these jars that held the lungs, liver, intestines, and stomach of an Egyptian mummy. These jars preserved those organs for the buried person to use in the afterlife.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] The canopic jars are protected by the four sons of this deity. The wadjet eye is a symbol of this falcon-headed god who loses one of his eyes in a battle against Set.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [H] Instead of being kept in a canopic jar, the heart was left in the body to be weighed against the feather of Ma’at. If the heart was heavier, it was devoured by this demoness, who is part hippopotamus, part lion, and part crocodile.

parts.label: L
parts.question: In ancient Egyptian burials, these containers were guarded by representations of the four sons of Horus. For ten points each,

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name these containers that held the lungs, stomach, liver, and intestines of a mummified person.
parts.answer: canopic jars (accept canope; accept canopic chests)

parts.label: B
parts.question: After mummification, the deceased would undergo a ritual called the “Opening of” this body part, which was believed to allow the person to eat and drink in the afterlife.

parts.label: C
parts.question: After mummification, the soul of the deceased would be judged by Anubis by having this bodily organ weighed against the Feather of Ma’at to determine whether they could enter the afterlife.

topics.description: A Christian initiation rite involving water and traditionally associated with purification from sin and incorporation into the church.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Banna’i tilework and hazarbaf brickwork were developed in Iran to display this artform’s evenly thick Kufic style. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [E] Name this Islamic artform in which a kalam pen is used to create artistic handwriting in ink.
parts.answer: calligraphy [accept word forms like calligraphic writing; prompt on writing alone]

parts.label: B
parts.question: [M] Ilkhanid artists incorporated calligraphy into depictions of the Shahnameh in these artworks. Marginalia and heavy use of gold foil appear in these artworks, which include the Lindisfarne Gospel and Books of Hours.
parts.answer: illuminated manuscripts [prompt on partial answers; prompt on codex, codices, books or similar answers referring to writing collections]

parts.label: C
parts.question: [H] The calligraphic signature of Syrian artisan ibn al-Zayn appears on a silver object used for this purpose named after Saint Louis. Lorenzo Ghiberti sculpted the Gates of Paradise for a building with this purpose.
parts.answer: baptisms [accept word forms such as baptizing people; accept the Baptistère de Saint Louis; accept the Florence Baptistery; accept the Baptistery of St. John]

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: After one account of this practice, a “voice from heaven” praises a figure with whom it is “well pleased.” Most Christian denominations agree that this practice cleanses one of original sin. A son of Elizabeth with a title referring to this practice performed this action on Jesus in the (*) Jordan River. For ten points, name this Christian religious practice often performed by sprinkling or pouring water on the head.

topics.description: A Hindu religious and social marriage ceremony involving vows before a sacred fire, ritual circumambulation, and other regional customs.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: A ritual during this practice sees participants walk around a fire seven times. After this practice has been completed, women apply red sindoor powder to their foreheads along with bindi, a colored red dot. The father gives away his daughter in this practice, during which (*) promises are made to keep a home and raise a family. Vows of love are exchanged during, for 10 points, what practice that involves a bride and groom?

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: Before these events, houses are decorated with banana leaves and coconuts; later, milk is poured over a coconut during them. A participant who enters these events carrying a lamp from a parade traditionally has his shoes stolen after entering a canopy called a mandap. Red sindoor powder is placed in the hair of a participant in these events who has a prior (*) mehndi ceremony and wears a red sari. Jai mala garland exchanges and a shower of rice called a talambralu occur during these events whose central participants walk around a fire seven times. For 10 points, name these events in which Agni witnesses the vows of a Hindu bride and groom.
parts.answer: Hindu weddings [accept marriages; or vivaha; or lagna; or kalyanam]

topics.description: A biblical judge of Israel whose divinely associated strength depended on his uncut hair and who ultimately brought down the Temple of Dagon.

parts.label: L
parts.question: God allowed this figure to regain his super strength one last time so he could collapse the Temple of Dagon, killing the people gathered within. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [M] Name this Biblical judge who originally loses his super strength when his lover Delilah cuts his hair.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] Samson was constantly at odds with the Philistines, who were later defeated when David killed this giant with a slingshot.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [H] Samson once destroyed an entire Philistine army with the jawbone of one of these animals. Balaam owned a talking one of these animals.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: In Sikhism, a kanga is used to take care of this thing, and kes is the practice of maintaining this thing naturally out of respect for God’s creation. In the Book of Judges, this thing was the source of Samson’s superhuman strength until it was (*) cut by Delilah. For ten points, name this religiously significant part of the body that is covered up by turbans and grows out of the top of one’s head.
parts.answer: hair [accept answers describing facial hair; prompt on beard]

topics.topic: Serpents and Dragons in Norse Mythology
topics.description: The class of serpent- and dragon-like creatures in Norse mythology, including Fáfnir, Jörmungandr, and Níðhöggr.

parts.label: L
parts.question: One of Ran’s nets is used to obtain one of these objects after Andvari turns into a pike. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [H] Name these objects, one of which is used to cover the last hair of an otter pelt to pay off a weregild. Odin owns one of these objects named Draupnir which creates eight copies of itself every nine nights.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [M] Loki uses Andvari’s ring to pay for accidentally killing Otr, a shapeshifting one of these creatures. Brokkr and Eitri, two of these creatures, forged Draupnir and two other magic items to win a bet against Loki.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [E] Andvari’s ring later transforms Fafnir into one of these creatures that is slain by Sigurd. These creatures are often associated with greed, so many of them like Fafnir have hoards of gold.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: One of these creatures is slain while crawling over a pit to get to a stream. After Hymir refuses to provide bait for one of these creatures, a god kills Hymir’s largest ox and uses its head to hunt for one of these creatures. The spring Hvergelmir houses one of these creatures named (*) Nidhogg who gnaws on the roots of Yggdrasil. After stealing Andvari’s ring, Fafnir’s greed causes him to transform into one of these creatures. During Ragnarök, Thor will kill and be killed by one of these creatures. For 10 points, Jormungandr is known as the “Midgard” type of what creature?
parts.answer: serpents [or dragons or snakes or ormr; accept Midgardsormr] (In Norse mythology serpents and dragons are the same type of creature.)

topics.description: Abraham’s son by Hagar, known as a prophet in Islam and traditionally regarded as an ancestor of Arab peoples and Muhammad.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: According to this Quran, this figure used the transience of the stars, moon, and sun in the sky to argue for worshipping God. In both the Quran and Jewish exegesis, this figure defies his father’s idol worship, leading Nimrod to cast him in a fire. In the Book of Genesis, this person lies to both the Pharaoh and Abimelech about the identity of his (*) first wife in order to protect her, claiming that she is his sister. Muslims believe that this person’s son Ishmael was actually the one chosen for sacrifice in the traditional biblical narrative of the binding of Isaac. For 10 points, name this religious patriarch who names a grouping of monotheistic religions including Judaism and Islam.

parts.label: L
parts.question: The qibla [kee-blah], the direction Muslims should face to pray, points toward the Kaaba in this city. For ten points each,

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this Saudi Arabian city, the birthplace of Muhammad.

parts.label: B
parts.question: Any Muslim who is both financially and physically able is expected to perform this pilgrimage to Mecca at least once in their life. During this pilgrimage, Muslims circle the Kaaba and perform the metaphorical Stoning of the Devil.

parts.label: C
parts.question: According to the Quran, this prophet and ancestor of Muhammad helped build the Kaaba with his father, Ibrahim.

topics.description: The four foundational collections of ancient Sanskrit sacred texts in Hinduism: the Rigveda, Samaveda, Yajurveda, and Atharvaveda.

parts.label: L
parts.question: This deity rides the white elephant Airavata (ai-RAH-vah-tah). For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this king of the Devas, who wields a thunderbolt called the Vajra.

parts.label: B
parts.question: Indra is the most-mentioned deity in the Rig, the oldest of this set of ancient Sanskrit scriptures.

parts.label: C
parts.question: There are this many Vedas. This is also the number of Puruṣārtha (POO-roo-shah-AR-tuh), or proper  goals of life, in Hinduism.

parts.label: L
parts.question: For 10 points each, answer the following about the self, or Atman [AHT-mun], in Hindu philosophy:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [E] Along with the closely related samkhya [SAM-kyuh] school, this school of Hindu philosophy believed that the self was the soul. In the West, this school shares its name with a system of exercise based on meditation and poses.
parts.answer: yoga [accept laya yoga or kundalini yoga or raja yoga or bhakti yoga or karma yoga or jnana yoga]

parts.label: B
parts.question: [H] Like many Hindu schools of thought, the Charvaka school rejects the existence of the self, while also espousing this position. The term nāstika [NAH-stih-kuh] is often mistranslated as referring to this heterodox view.
parts.answer: atheism [accept descriptive answers like not believing in God; prompt on “materialism”] (It’s unclear what the most correct English translation of nāstika is, but common translations include “heterodox,” “not existent,” “heretic,” or even “no-self.”)

parts.label: C
parts.question: [M] The existence of the self is affirmed by āstika thinkers, as they accept the authority of these ancient Hindu scriptures. The Rig is the longest text in this collection of four Sanskrit sacred works.

topics.description: A creator and ancestral serpent being in the traditions of numerous Aboriginal Australian peoples, associated with the Dreamtime, water, fertility, rainfall, and the shaping of landscapes.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Frisky tourist agencies in this country warn of drop bears, which are predatory marsupials that will fall out of trees and attack visitors. For ten points each,

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this country whose most dangerous animals tend to look more like taipan snakes or redback spiders, and less like koala bears.

parts.label: B
parts.question: By any reasonable set of criteria, the best Australian cryptid is this monster of Aboriginal myth that feasts on unsuspecting humans visiting billabongs. This animal is some sort of linear combination of bird, frog, and alligator.

parts.label: C
parts.question: Aboriginal creation myths speak of a “Rainbow” one of these creatures that inhabited the pre-historic Dreamtime and is associated with rainfall.
parts.answer: serpent (accept snake; accept Rainbow Serpent or Rainbow Snake)

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: A serpent named for this phenomena is a creator god in Australian mythology. Heimdall guards a bridge made of this phenomenon that connects Asgard and Midgard called the Bifrost. Iris is a goddess of this phenomena in Greek myth. A (*) “pot of gold” guarded by a leprechaun is said to be found at the end of these phenomena in Irish legend. For 10 points, name these colorful phenomena that appear in the sky after it rains.

topics.description: The Aztec or Mexica deity of war and the sun, and patron god of the Mexica, traditionally represented by a hummingbird.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: One god from this culture made the sun appear halved because he was missing a leg, causing his brother to club him out of the sky. While fighting a crocodilian monster to create the earth, one god from this culture lost his foot. This culture’s war god flayed himself to bring food to humanity. A god from this culture was born from an impregnated (*) ball of feathers and was represented by the hummingbird. This culture’s first humans were created when a “feathered serpent’s” blood mixed with the bones of its underworld, Mictlan [MEEK-tlan]. For 10 points, name this Mesoamerican culture that venerated gods like Quetzalcoatl [keet-zal-co-ATT-ll] and Huitzilopochtli [hwee-zil-oh-POKE-tlee].

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: A god in this culture, Ometeotl [oh-MEH-tay-oh-tull] split into two gods to create the world. A heroic god in this culture used the bones of previous humans and his own blood to create the (*) Fifth Sun after journeying through Mictlan. This culture venerated a “Left-Handed Hummingbird” and a “Feathered Serpent” named Huitzilopochtli [HWEE-tsih-loh-POCK-tlee] and Quetzalcoatl [KET-zahl-koh-ah-tull]. For ten points, name this culture whose myths included the story of the founding of Tenochtitlan [teh-NOSH-tiht-lahn] in modern Mexico City.
parts.answer: Aztecs (accept Aztec empire; prompt on “Mexica” or “Mexicatl;” prompt on “Nahua” or “Nahuatl”)

topics.description: A figure in Greek mythology, daughter of King Minos, who aided Theseus by giving him thread to navigate the Labyrinth and was later associated with Dionysus.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: A woman who aided in the defeat of this creature is abandoned on Naxos, where she weds Dionysus. Pasiphaë gave birth to this creature, also known as Asterion, after mating with a white animal her husband refused to sacrifice. A ball of yarn belonging to (*) Ariadne assisted the hero that slew this creature, which was located inside of an elaborate location commissioned by King Minos. Theseus slew, for 10 points, what half-bull creature, who inhabited a labyrinth?
parts.answer: Minotaur [accept Asterion before it is read; accept Asterius before “Asterion” is read]

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: This hero defeated the bandit Sinis (SIGH-nus), who killed victims by tying them between two pine trees and tearing them apart. This hero’s father jumped into the sea after this hero forgot to switch his black sails with white ones on his way back from (*) Crete. Ariadne fell in love with and gave magical golden thread to this hero to allow him to navigate the Labyrinth. For ten points, what Greek hero slew the Minotaur?

topics.description: The major Protestant revival waves in colonial and early national America, especially the First and Second Great Awakenings.

parts.label: L
parts.question: One speech delivered in this country claimed man is held “over the pit of Hell, much as one holds a spider” over a fire. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this modern-day country, where both the speeches “Sinners in the Hands of an Angry God” and “City Upon a Hill” were delivered.

parts.label: B
parts.question: “Sinners in the Hands of an Angry God” is one of these lectures, which are often delivered by preachers. Jesus claims “blessed are the meek, for they shall inherit the earth” in one of these speeches “On the Mount.”
parts.answer: sermons [or the Sermon on the Mount]

parts.label: C
parts.question: “Sinners in the Hands of an Angry God” was written by Jonathan Edwards, a leader of a 1730s religious revival with this name. The Burned-Over District was a hotspot for another movement with this name.
parts.answer: Great Awakening [accept First Great Awakening; accept Second Great Awakening]

parts.label: L
parts.question: Susanna, a daughter of Samuel Annesley who married into this family, covered herself with her apron  to pray for two hours daily. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: What family of that “mother of Methodism” includes Susanna's sons Charles and John, who  founded the denomination?
parts.answer: Wesley family [or Wesleys; or Susanna Wesley or Charles Wesley or John Wesley; or  Wesleyan]

parts.label: B
parts.question: Jarena Lee's preaching was endorsed by Richard Allen, who founded this offshoot of the Methodist  movement in response to segregation.
parts.answer: African Methodist Episcopal Church [or AME Church]

parts.label: C
parts.question: Women and African-Americans, such as Allen and Lee, were more involved in the second of these  periods of American religious revival than the first, led by Jonathan Edwards and George Whitefield.
parts.answer: Great Awakenings [or First Great Awakening; or Second Great Awakening]

topics.description: Kami are the spirits, deities, and sacred presences central to Shinto, including Izanagi, Izanami, and Amaterasu.

parts.label: L
parts.question: When this deity vows to kill a thousand people every day, her husband says that he will create fifteen-hundred more in response. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [H] Name this goddess who marries her twin brother in a ceremony where they both circle a pillar in opposite directions. Later, this goddess dies after giving birth to Kagutsuchi, the god of fire.
parts.answer: Izanami [do NOT accept or prompt on “Izanagi”]

parts.label: B
parts.question: [M] After the death of Izanami, many of these deities are created from the tears of her husband Izanagi. Izanami and Izanagi themselves are examples of these Shinto spirits, as are their children Amaterasu, Tsukoyomi, and Susano’o.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [E] To retrieve his dead wife, Izanagi journeys to Yomi, which is the Japanese version of this place. Because Izanami has already eaten food cooked in this place similar to hell, she is unable to return to the land of the living.

parts.label: L
parts.question: These beings are channeled by shrine maidens called miko during kagura dances. For ten points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [H] Give the original-language term for these beings central to prayer in Shintoism. These beings, examples of which are Izanagi, Izanami, and Amaterasu (AH-mah-ter-AH-soo), are worshipped in Shinto shrines.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] Shintoism is primarily practiced in this Asian country. Shinto adherents in this country go to shrines like the ones in Tokyo or Kyoto on New Year’s Day to pray to kami (kah-mee) for good luck in the coming year.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [M] During New Year’s shrine visits, called hatsumode (haat-soo-MOH-day) in Japanese, people can be seen wearing this traditional Japanese garment. These square-sleeved garments are almost always worn with a belt called an obi.

topics.description: A mortal weaver in Greek mythology who was transformed into a spider after challenging Athena to a weaving contest.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: Robert the Bruce was mythically inspired by one of these animals to keep fighting the English. In Akan (uh-KON) folklore, the trickster god and master of all stories takes the form of one of these animals and is named Anansi. A woman was punished for her skillfully woven depictions of the gods’ abuse by being turned into one of these animals by (*) Athena. Arachne was turned into, for ten points, what kind of eight-legged critter?

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: An animal of this type was believed to be the “great goddess” of Teotihuacan (TAY-oh-tee-WAH-kun).
