Two Navajo deities taking this form constantly debated over the names of their invention.  The Hopi believed in a “Grandmother” form of this animal who made humanity. All of the stories  in the world were bought from Nyame (nee-AH-may) by (*) Anansi (ah-NAN-see), who took the form  of this sort of animal. After losing a contest to Athena, Arachne (uh-RAK-nee) was turned into an animal  of this type. For 10 points, name this sort of animal, which many cultures venerate as a god of weaving.
parts.answer: spiders [or Teotihuacan Spider Woman; or Spider man; or Spider woman; or Grandmother  Spider; prompt on arachnids]

topics.description: The rebellious jinn in Islamic theology who refused to prostrate before Adam and became the chief tempter and adversary of humanity.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: Some Sufis claim that this figure was the perfect personification of love, because he chose eternal damnation over obeying anyone other than Allah. Verses named after and inspired by this figure encouraged the worship of three pagan goddesses. This figure was made from smokeless fire and refused to (*) prostrate before Adam as Adam was made from clay. During the hajj, adherents throw rocks at three pillars to symbolize the stoning of this figure. In the Bible, this figure tempts Jesus for forty days and forty nights in the desert. For 10 points each, name this evil figure who opposes Allah in Islam.
parts.answer: Iblis [or Satan or Shaitan or the Devil; accept Azazil]

parts.label: L
parts.question: The Umrah is a “lesser” form of this practice, which can be undertaken at any point in the year. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [M] Name this annual pilgrimage to Mecca, which all Muslims must complete at least once in their lifetime.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] A common ritual during the hajj is the “Stoning of [this figure].” This evil figure, called Shaitan or Iblis by Muslims, tempted Ibrahim to disobey Allah.
parts.answer: Devil [or Satan; accept Shaitan or Iblis before mentioned or The Stoning of the Devil]

parts.label: C
parts.question: [H] Another hajj ritual, running between the hills of Safa and Marwa, symbolizes Hajar’s search for this substance. The angel Jibreel provided this substance to Hajar by striking the ground with his heel.

topics.description: A Kurdish ethno-religious community whose tradition venerates Melek Tawus or Melek Taus, the Peacock Angel, and whose members have faced persecution, including by ISIS.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Belief in these beings is listed second among six articles of faith that also include belief in God's  oneness and prophets. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [10] Name these creatures made of light. One of them called Jibril revealed the Quran to Muhammad.
parts.answer: angels [or malak; or mala'ik; or mala'ikah; or archangels]

parts.label: B
parts.question: [10] Scholars debate whether the tempters Harut and Marut, mentioned in this surah, are fallen angels.  This longest chapter of the Quran contains the Throne Verse.
parts.answer: surat al-Baqarah [or The Cow; or The Heifer; or surah 2; or the second surah]

parts.label: C
parts.question: [10] Because this Kurdistani ethnic group venerates Melek Tawus (MAY-lek TAO-oos), an angel who  shares traits with Iblis, some Muslims have accused them of “devil worship.”
parts.answer: Yazidis [or Yezidis; or Ezidis; or Yazidism]

parts.label: L
parts.question: This ethnic group’s holy books are generally considered to be forgeries from the 1910s written in response to Western interest in their religion. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [H] Name this Iraqi ethno-religious group persecuted by ISIS for being “devil worshippers” due to their veneration of the Peacock God Melek Taus.
parts.answer: Yazidi [or Ezidis; or Yezidis; prompt on Kurds]

parts.label: B
parts.question: [M] Yazidis have two main religious texts, one which describes the sayings of Melek Taus. That text shares its name with this Biblical book by “John of Patmos” that opens with letters to seven churches and features events such as the opening of seven seals.
parts.answer: Book of Revelation [do NOT accept or prompt on “Revelations”]

parts.label: C
parts.question: [E] The other Yazidi holy book, the Black Book, describes the beliefs of the Yazidis, such as how they are descended from this first man, but not his wife, Eve.

topics.description: A sixth-century Italian monk who founded Western Christian monasticism and authored the Rule of Saint Benedict.

parts.label: L
parts.question: One of these locations, called Monte Cassino, was destroyed in World War II. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [E] Name these religious institutions, in which monks lived and often copied religious texts by hand.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [H] This 6th-century monk from Nursia created a namesake “rule” for monks, which included a vow of silence.
parts.answer: ANSWER: Benedict of Nursia [accept Benedictine Rule]

parts.label: C
parts.question: [M] Monks at Cluny abbey in this modern-day country attempted to reform the Benedictine Rule in the 10th century. In the 14th century, the Papacy was briefly headed in Avignon, a city in this country.
parts.answer: ANSWER: Republic of France [or Republique francaise]

parts.label: L
parts.question: Answer the following about diets and cuisine in Medieval Europe. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: Grain-based diets poor in iron and loss of iron through menstruation made medieval women more susceptible to disease, like this 14th-century epidemic that killed over one-third of Europe’s population.
parts.answer: Black Death [or Black Plague; or bubonic plague; or the Great Mortality; prompt on the plague; prompt on the pestilence]

parts.label: B
parts.question: Crop production increased as moldboard plows and horses were adopted alongside the “three-field” method of this farming technique in which different seasonal crops are grown over multiple fields to prevent overuse.

parts.label: C
parts.question: Followers of this saint would often break a rule prohibiting the consumption of “four-legged animals” in a room called the misericord [mih-ZER-ih-cord]. The adage “pray work” summarizes this saint from Nursia’s monastic rules followed by the Black Monks.
parts.answer: St. Benedict of Nursia [or Benedictus Nursiae; or Benedetto da Norcia; accept Benedictine Rules]

topics.description: A Christian denomination and millenarian religious movement known for door-to-door evangelism, rejecting the Trinity, military service, certain holidays, and blood transfusions.

parts.label: L
parts.question: This religious denomination produces tracts such as The Watchtower. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this fringe denomination of Christianity founded by Charles Taze Russell. Its members reject the Holy Trinity, refuse to celebrate holidays with supposed pagan origins like Christmas, and engage in "disfellowshipping" and shunning of members who misbehave.
parts.answer: Jehovah's Witnesses [prompt on Watch Tower Society or Bible Student movement]

parts.label: B
parts.question: Russell founded the Jehovah's Witnesses in this state's city of Pittsburgh.

parts.label: C
parts.question: Jehovah's Witnesses refuse blood transfusions based on their interpretation of this book's fifteenth chapter. Believed to have been written by the same author as the Book of Luke, it is the fifth book in the New Testament and describes the lives of the apostles after Jesus's death, including the conversion of Paul.
parts.answer: Book of Acts [or the Acts of the Apostles, or Práxeis Apostólōn]

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: This Millennialist religious denomination follows a Governing Body known as God’s “faithful and discreet slave.” This denomination celebrates Memorialization, but does not recognize Christmas, Easter, or (*) birthdays. This denomination’s Weekend Meetings use the “Study Edition” of the Watchtower magazine, and it forbids believers from engaging in military service or receiving blood transfusions. For ten points, name this Christian denomination known for preaching door-to-door.
parts.answer: Jehovah’s witnesses (prompt on “Bible Students” or “Bible Student movement”)

topics.description: The Sun is the star at the center of the Solar System and the celestial object represented or personified in various mythological traditions.

parts.label: L
parts.question: This figure accidently pulled the Hawaiian islands from the ocean floor while fishing with his magic fish hook. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [H] Name this Polynesian trickster demigod.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] Maui produced the first tree of this fruit by killing and burying an eel. A type of crab named for this fruit climbs palm trees to reach this fruit and drops it from a height to crack its hard exterior.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [M] In another story, because his mother never had enough time to finish making kapa clothes, Maui lassoed this object and bargained with it to not sink into the underworld as quickly each day.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: The three-legged crow sometimes called Yangwu (yahng-WOO) inhabits this object. Some  instances of this object are the sons of Xihe (SHEE-huh). A goddess of this object tolerates her  brother burning her rice fields but retreats away after one of her weaving maidens is killed. The  archer Hou-yi (ho-YEE) shoots (*) several examples of this object when they all appear at once, leaving  only one. Amaterasu (ah-mah-ter-AH-soo) was the Shinto god of this object and jeopardized the world  by hiding it in a cave. For 10 points, Chinese myth believed that a dragon eating what object caused total  eclipses?

topics.description: A legendary serpentine creature of Chinese mythology associated with rain, water, weather, power, and the Chinese zodiac, including the Azure Dragon tradition.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Answer some questions about Chinese traditional astrology, for 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: This Chinese practice, named from the words for "wind-water", is used to harmonize buildings with their surroundings using qi (chee).

parts.label: B
parts.question: In Chinese astrology, this cycle of animals is supposed to determine one's personality, as primarily assigned by year. Its Western counterpart assigns people to one of twelve constellations representing parts of the year.

parts.label: C
parts.question: This is the only fictitious animal in the zodiac. Chinese examples of these animals do not typically have wings, unlike Western examples.

parts.label: L
parts.question: After the construction of the Bank of China tower, which did not follow the principles of this practice, a nearby building installed cannon-like cranes on its roof to combat its negative energy. For ten points each,

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this long-standing Chinese practice of using classical elements and directional forces to create harmony between humans and their environment. Its name literally means “wind-water.”

parts.label: B
parts.question: Feng shui [fong shweh] attempts to balance these two forces. One is a cold, passive, feminine force, and the other is a warm, active, masculine force. They are represented as swirling black and white in a common symbol.
parts.answer: yin and yang (both underlined parts required; accept yin-yang)

parts.label: C
parts.question: Feng shui’s directional principles are tied to representations of four animals: a bird, a tiger, a tortoise, and one of these mythical creatures. These creatures are associated with rain in Asian cultures, but supposedly breathe fire in European stories.
parts.answer: dragon (accept long or lung; accept the Azure Dragon or Qinlong)

topics.description: Ganesha is the elephant-headed Hindu deity associated with wisdom, auspicious beginnings, and the removal of obstacles.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: A figure circled this deity and his wife to win a race with the prize of a magic mango, proposed by this god. This god is depicted with matted hair and a crescent moon on his head. After this god swallowed halahala created during the churning of the ocean, this god’s throat turned (*) blue due to the potency of the poison. For ten points, name this three-eyed destroyer deity who makes up the Trimurti with Brahma and Vishnu.

parts.label: L
parts.question: This god was created out of turmeric paste to guard his mother during a bath. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [M] Name this Hindu god, who is celebrated in a namesake “Chaturthi” festival. This elephant-headed “remover of  obstacles” defeated his brother Karthikeya in a race around the world by encircling his parents.
parts.answer: Ganesha [or Ganapati; or Vinayaka; or Pillaiyar]

parts.label: B
parts.question: [H] Ganesha was created by this goddess, his mother. This goddess’ form, Sati, is the etiology of a Hindu funerary  ritual.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [E] Ganesha and Karthikeya were both sons of this Hindu destroyer god, who makes up the Trimurti with Vishnu  and Brahma.

topics.description: A Catholic devotional object and associated prayer practice consisting of beads used to count prayers, commonly organized into decades associated with sacred Mysteries.

parts.label: L
parts.question: This object is believed to have been created by Saint Dominic during the Albigensian Heresy. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [M] Name this object from Catholicism, which is used to count Hail Marys with beads.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] In addition to beads, rosaries include a small depiction of one of these objects, one of which Jesus died on.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [H] A rosary is often used in conjunction with this Christian prayer from the Sermon on the Mount. It opens “Our Father, who art in Heaven.”

parts.label: L
parts.question: Answer the following about prayer in Abrahamic religions, for ten points each.

parts.label: A
parts.question: Members of this faith are encouraged to engage in five daily personal prayers, which should be performed facing the qibla, the direction of the Kaaba, whenever possible.

parts.label: B
parts.question: In Catholicism, prayers are often performed with the help of this beaded object, which is separated into decades representing holy Mysteries.
parts.answer: Rosary (accept Rosaries; accept Holy Rosary; accept Dominican Rosary; prompt on “prayer beads”)

parts.label: C
parts.question: This Abrahamic religion’s three Obligatory Prayers were revealed by Baha’u’llah, who founded this religion in the 1800s.

topics.description: Zeus is the Greek god of the sky and thunder, chief of the Olympian gods, and son of Cronus and Rhea.

parts.label: L
parts.question: The clashing of the Curetes (kor-AY-teez) drowned out the cries of this god as a child. For 10 points  each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this god, who overthrew his father Cronus along with brothers Hades and Poseidon to  become the chief of the Greek gods.
parts.answer: Zeus [do not accept or prompt on “Jupiter”]

parts.label: B
parts.question: Zeus fathered all three holders of this position, including Minos and Rhadamanthus (rad-aa-MAN￾thus). People holding this position decided whether souls went to the Elysian or Asphodel (ASS-fuh-del) Fields.
parts.answer: judges of the underworld [or judges of the dead; prompt on judges]

parts.label: C
parts.question: The name of Adrasteia (AD-res-TAY-uh), the nurse of Zeus, is also an epithet for this Greek goddess  of revenge.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: This deity, who was tricked into revealing his true form and killing the princess Semele, saved the infant Dionysus by sewing him into his thigh. This deity trapped the monster Typhon under Mount Etna. Rhea gave (*) Cronos a rock to swallow instead of this god, leading to his overthrow of the Titans. Lightning bolts were thrown by, for ten points, what husband of Hera and chief god of Olympus?

topics.description: The mythological king of Mycenae and Tiryns who commanded Heracles to perform his twelve labors.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Answer the following about the Labors of Heracles. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: Heracles is forced to perform his labors in service to this man, the king of Tyrins

parts.label: B
parts.question: Heracles’ first labor was to slay one of these animals from Nemea, which had impregnable skin.

parts.label: C
parts.question: The second of Heracles’ labors was to defeat this many headed-monster from Lernaea, which grew two heads  every time one was cut off. It was defeated after Iolaus burned the severed heads before they could grow back.

parts.label: L
parts.question: The parents of this animal are believed to be Orthrus and the Chimera, making it the grandson of Typhon and Echidna. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [M] Name this animal. The killer of this animal uses its own claws to skin it and return home with its thick fur.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] The Nemean (“NEE-me-in”) Lion is slain by this man as part of the first of his twelve labors, which also include cleaning the Augean stables and killing the Hydra.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [H] Heracles completes the twelve labors after being commanded to do so by this cousin of his. After Hera causes Heracles to kill his family, the Oracle at Delphi tells him to serve this king of Mycenae and Tiryns.

topics.description: Poseidon is the Greek god of the sea, earthquakes, and horses, associated with the trident and the patronage contest for Athens.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: This god granted Caenis’s wish to be turned into a man after he raped her. This god built the walls of Troy with Apollo, and delayed Odysseus’s return to Ithaca as revenge for blinding his son, the (*) cyclops Polyphemus. This creator of the first horse was the father of Pegasus, and made Pasiphae fall in love with a bull as revenge against Minos. This god lost a competition to be the patron of Athens by giving the gift of a salt spring. For ten points, name this Greek god of the sea.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: Demeter turned herself into a mare to avoid this deity’s advances, which resulted in the talking horse Arion. A son of this god gets his eye stabbed out by a hero who calls himself “Nobody”. That son of this god was the cyclops Polyphemus. Athena’s olive tree won a competition against this god’s (*) saltwater spring for patronage of Athens. For ten points, name this trident-wielding Greek god of earthquakes and the sea.

topics.description: A legendary African American railroad worker said to have defeated a mechanical drill in a contest while tunneling through rock.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: These machines were involved in a miraculous accident in Vaughan, Mississippi that killed only Casey Jones. In 1918 at Dutchman’s Curve, one hundred one people died when two of these vehicles collided because one failed to pull onto a (*) side track. John Henry legendarily beat a steel drill in a race to build a tunnel for these vehicles. Union Pacific and Central Pacific operated, for ten points, what vehicles that used the transcontinental railroad?

parts.label: L
parts.question: Wallace Saunders wrote a ballad about Casey Jones who died preventing a crash between two of these vehicles. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [E] Name these vehicles, one of which stops clocks as it recreates its travel to Springfield, Illinois with Abraham Lincoln’s body. Phantom conductors and weird tunnel lights appear in ghost sightings of these vehicles.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [M] During a contest to mine a train tunnel, this freed slave proclaims “I'll die with the hammer in my hand” while competing against a mechanical drill. This “steel-driving man” is often depicted with a sledgehammer.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [H] John Henry’s contest took place at the Big Bend Tunnel near this state’s city of Talcott. The collapse of this state’s Silver Bridge near Point Pleasant is believed to have been caused by the Mothman.

topics.description: An Ethiopian princess in Greek mythology who was chained as a sacrifice to a sea monster, rescued by Perseus, and married him.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: This figure legendarily founded the city of Mycenae, and he fulfilled a prophecy when his discus killed his grandfather Acrisius. This man's mother Danae was visited by Zeus in the form of a golden shower. This hero used Athena's (*) reflective shield to kill a Gorgon, after which Pegasus was born. Andromeda's husband was, for 10 points, what Greek hero who slew Medusa?

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: On one journey, this hero causes Libya to be infested with poisonous snakes, one of which later kills the Argonaut Mopsus. Phineus leads a riot against this hero for marrying a woman who had earlier been promised to him by Cepheus. Because he refuses to give this hero hospitality, (*) Atlas is turned into a mountain. This hero accidentally fulfills a prophecy when his discus hits Acrisius, who had earlier cast this hero and his mother into the sea in a wooden chest. This hero defeats a sea monster to rescue Andromeda. To aid this hero on a quest, Hermes and Athena give him a reflective shield and winged sandals. For 10 points, name this Greek hero who slays Medusa.

topics.description: The religious belief or process in which an individual's soul, consciousness, or life-principle is reborn in another body, forming part of a cycle of repeated birth and death.

parts.label: L
parts.question: The Chinese word chànà is derived from a Sanskrit word for a measure of this thing. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [H] Name this thing. This thing is described in the kalacakra in Jainism, where it is divided into ascending utsarpini and descending avasarpini stages.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [M] The avasarpini time cycle is divided into six periods, the current of which began three years after the death of this twenty-fourth tirthankara and founder of modern Jainism.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [E] The cyclical nature of time in Jainism is used to explain why this process continually occurs. Samsara is the cycle of death and this concept, which in Hinduism involves the transfer of the soul to another body.
parts.answer: reincarnation [or synonyms like rebirth or being born again or transmigration]

parts.label: L
parts.question: The Dalai Lama has repeatedly undergone this process, through which he has chosen a new body after death fourteen times. For ten points each,

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this cycle of birth, death, and rebirth that is common in Indian religions.
parts.answer: reincarnation (accept samsara; accept descriptions like transmigration of souls or metempsychosis; prompt on “rebirth” before it is read by asking “what process is rebirth a part of?”)

parts.label: B
parts.question: A being’s status and species following reincarnation are determined by their positive and negative actions in life, which are collectively known by this term, meaning “deeds.”

parts.label: C
parts.question: This Indian religion’s texts say that a person will be reincarnated into one of four realms of existence, called gatis. Followers of this religion practice ahimsa, or extreme non-violence.

topics.description: A raised Zoroastrian funerary structure where corpses are exposed to the elements and scavenging birds rather than buried or cremated.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Give the following about one of the world’s oldest surviving religions, Zoroastrianism, for ten points each.

parts.label: A
parts.question: Zoroastrianism was founded 2 to 3 thousand years ago by Zoroaster in this region. It corresponds to a modern-day country with capital Tehran, where converting to Zoroastrianism from Islam is illegal.

parts.label: B
parts.question: Burying human corpses would defile the soil, so Zoroastrians ritually perform sky burials in these round, raised structures, where dead bodies are exposed to the elements and scavenging birds.

parts.label: C
parts.question: In Zoroastrianism, purification can be done with either cleansing aban, water, or destructive atar, this phenomenon. In India, there are roughly 150 temples dedicated to maintaining the atar.
parts.answer: fire (accept burning and other synonyms for the act of setting something on fire)

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: Rogyapa destroy these objects and mix them with tsampa flowers after the Tibetan ritual of jhator. A plate of koliva with a candle is placed near these objects and the Trisagion is sung in Eastern Orthodox rituals. Tears [tares] called keriah are made by Jews in a white cloth covering these objects during the week-long period of (*) shiva. The demon Nasu inhabits these things when they are placed inside Towers of Silence by Zoroastrians. The Rite of Committal is administered at Christian events centered on these objects, which may be followed by a wake. For 10 points, name these objects central to religious cremations or burials.
parts.answer: corpses [or dead bodies; accept synonyms such as dead people; accept skeletons; accept bones]

topics.description: The first book of the Hebrew Bible and Old Testament, containing creation narratives, the Flood, and stories of the patriarchs.

parts.label: L
parts.question: The Talmud contains a number of tales of the wickedness and inhospitality of this city's inhabitants. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this Biblical city. God said that he would only spare this city if ten righteous people can be found there. Along with Gomorrah, this city was destroyed by fire and brimstone.

parts.label: B
parts.question: This figure's wife is turned into a pillar of salt for looking back at Sodom while fleeing the city with him and their daughters.

parts.label: C
parts.question: The tales of Sodom and Gomorrah occur in this first book of the Bible, which also tells the story of the creation of the world and Noah's Ark.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: One figure in this book is promised that his descendants will inherit land "from the river of Egypt to the great river, the river Euphrates." Isaac is born to Sarah in this book after Abram is renamed to Abraham and makes a covenant with God. In Chapter One of this book, God says (*) “Let there be light” while creating the universe in six days. Abraham and Noah feature in, for ten points, what first book of the Old Testament in the Bible?
parts.answer: Book of Genesis [prompt on Old Testament; prompt on Bible]

topics.description: The Jewish New Year observance held on the first and second days of Tishrei, marking the beginning of the High Holy Days and the Hebrew year.

parts.label: L
parts.question: In Judaism, Rosh Hashanah celebrates this event on the first and second days of the month of Tishrei. For ten points each,

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this general event that occurs when the calendar begins afresh.
parts.answer: new year (accept descriptions like “the beginning of the year”)

parts.label: B
parts.question: Rosh Hashanah begins this group of Jewish holidays, which end with the Day of Atonement on the tenth day of Tishrei.
parts.answer: High Holy Days (accept Days of Awe; accept Yamim Noraim)

parts.label: C
parts.question: The “Day of Atonement” is this last of the High Holy Days. On this day, each person’s fate for the new year is sealed in the Book of Judgement.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: In Bahai, the Nineteen Day Fast ends on one of these holidays, called Nowruz. On one of these holidays, which occurs fifteen days before the Lantern Festival, children are given red envelopes filled with money. A Jewish one of these holidays is the first of the (*) High Holy Days and takes place nine days before Yom Kippur. For 10 points, Rosh Hashanah is what type of holiday, which falls on January 1st in the Gregorian Calendar?
parts.answer: New Year’s Day [accept Nowruz until it is read, accept Chinese New Year; accept Lunar New Year; accept Rosh Hashanah until it is read]

topics.description: Domesticated bovines that appear in Irish and Greek mythological narratives, including the cattle raid in the Táin Bó Cúailnge, Geryon’s herd, and the transformations of Europa and Io.

parts.label: L
parts.question: In one story, an Ulsterian hero prevented Queen Medb (mave) from stealxing one of these animals by fighting her entire army in a series of single combats. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name these animals which included Donn Cuailnge (don cool-nuh). In Greek mythology, the three-headed Geryon owned a magnificent red herd of these livestock animals.

parts.label: B
parts.question: This hero defended Ulster during the cattle raid. Born Setanta, this hero wielded the fearsome spear Gae Bolg and received his name after killing a guard dog.

parts.label: C
parts.question: Cú Chulainn is a central figure in the mythology of this island. Fionn Mac Cumhaill (finn mac cool) consumes the Salmon of Knowledge in another myth from this Celtic island.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Answer these questions about the many times Zeus transformed himself to seduce women, for ten points each.

parts.label: A
parts.question: Zeus seduced this woman while in the form of a swan. This woman had four children with Zeus, including Helen of Troy.

parts.label: B
parts.question: Zeus took the form of gold coins falling from the sky to seduce the princess Danae. Afterwards, Danae gave birth to this hero, who freed Andromeda and killed Medusa.

parts.label: C
parts.question: Zeus seduced Europa by turning into one of these animals. Io, another woman seduced by Zeus, was turned into one of these animals by Hera.
parts.answer: cattle (accept equivalents like cows or bulls)

topics.description: A colossal land beast described in the Book of Job and later Jewish and Christian traditions, often paired with Leviathan.

parts.label: L
parts.question: The Biblioteca Ambrosiana library in Milan holds a manuscript showing these two creatures below  the Ziz, all above an illustration of the Feast of the Righteous. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [10] Name these two great beasts of the land and the sea, respectively described in chapters 40 and 41 of  the Book of Job (joab).
parts.answer: Behemoth [or Behemot] and Leviathan [or Livyatan; or Lotan; or Rahab] [all acceptable  answers may be given in either order, but do not accept or prompt if only one answer is given]

parts.label: B
parts.question: [10] The role of the Leviathan and Behemoth in the Day of Judgment is described in the apocryphal  book named for this father of Methusaleh, who directly “walked with God” into heaven without dying.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [10] The word “ziz” appears in the Hebrew text of two of the 150 songs collected in this poetic book of  the Bible.

parts.label: L
parts.question: According to the Book of Enoch, one of these creatures lives in the abyss of the ocean, while the other lives in a waste land east of Eden. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [H] Name these two creatures described to emphasize God’s might in the Book of Job.
parts.answer: Behemoth AND Leviathan [accept answers in either order]

parts.label: B
parts.question: [M] The Revised Standard Version suggests that Behemoth may be a hippo and Leviathan one of these animals. An Egyptian god of the Nile, Sobek, has the head of one of these animals.
parts.answer: crocodiles [accept crocs or Nile crocodiles or West African crocodiles]

parts.label: C
parts.question: [E] On the other hand, medieval Christian writers often considered Leviathan to be one of these beings charged with punishing envious sinners. These beings may be banished from a person with an exorcism.

topics.description: Lakshmi is the Hindu goddess of wealth, prosperity, fortune, and auspiciousness, and the consort of Vishnu.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: This holiday begins on Dhanteras and ends with Bhai Duj, which celebrates the relationship between siblings. Celebrations during this festival commemorate the defeat of the demon Narakasura and the return home of (*) Sita and Rama in the Ramayana. Offerings are given to Lakshmi during this holiday to celebrate the fiscal new year in autumn. For ten points, name this Hindu holiday celebrated with diya lamps, nicknamed the festival of lights.

parts.label: L
parts.question: This holiday typically lasts five days and celebrates the triumph of good over evil. For ten points each,

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this Hindu festival of lights that marks the day Rama defeated Ravana and returned to Ayodhya [eye-yohd-hya] with his wife, Sita.

parts.label: B
parts.question: During Diwali, a puja is performed for this goddess of wealth. This consort of Vishnu is often depicted with four arms and sitting on a lotus.
parts.answer: Lakshmi (accept Laksmi; accept Shri; accept Malakshmi)

parts.label: C
parts.question: The last day of Diwali celebrates people with this family relationship. During the celebration, women feed men who have this familial relationship to them, with whom they likely grew up.

topics.description: An imam is a Muslim religious leader, especially a leader of communal prayer and, in Twelver Shi'a Islam, one of the divinely guided successors to Muhammad.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Angels called Havaza defend mumins in this location’s section of Illiyyun. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [H] Name this location home to large-eyed beings called houris. A lote tree called the Sidrat al-Muntaha marks the upper boundary of this location, which is the opposite of Jahannam.
parts.answer: Jannah [or Jannat; accept heaven; prompt on the afterlife; prompt on paradise; prompt on the garden]

parts.label: B
parts.question: [M] Illiyyun is exclusively for messengers, prophets, martyrs, and these people. Shi’a scholars believe twelve of these people succeeded Muhammad, though more generally they are leaders of prayer in a mosque.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [E] Islamic scholars disagree on whether these beings can fully enjoy Jannah or if they are relegated to being servants. These beings made of smokeless fire can be trapped in talismans like a lamp.

parts.label: L
parts.question: One subsect of this group in Syria is called the Alawites. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this branch of Islam, whose adherents believe Ali to be the true successor to Muhammad. It is the second  largest branch of Islam, after Sunni.

parts.label: B
parts.question: The Shia Twelvers believe in twelve figures known by this title. Sunni Muslims refer to their Mosque leaders  by this title.

parts.label: C
parts.question: A hidden imam known by this name is said to appear at the end of the world and establish a final caliphate. A  man who claimed to be this figure led a series of Islamic revolts in Sudan.

topics.description: The central Christian symbol representing the cross on which Jesus was crucified.

parts.label: L
parts.question: A religious movement founded in this country holds mass wedding ceremonies so that adherents can be accepted into the lineage of God. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [H] Name this county where the Unification Church was founded by a pastor referred to as the “True Father.”
parts.answer: South Korea [or Republic of Korea or ROK; prompt on Korea; do NOT accept or prompt on “Democratic People’s Republic of Korea” or “DPRK”]

parts.label: B
parts.question: [M] The founder of the Unification Church, Sun-Myung Moon, combined Christian beliefs with the ideas of this tradition, inspired by his childhood reading of the Analects.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [E] In the early 2000s, Moon led a tour across America that sought to remove this symbol from poor churches in an attempt to unite them. This symbol represents the object on which Jesus was executed.

parts.label: L
parts.question: This object is believed to have been created by Saint Dominic during the Albigensian Heresy. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [M] Name this object from Catholicism, which is used to count Hail Marys with beads.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] In addition to beads, rosaries include a small depiction of one of these objects, one of which Jesus died on.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [H] A rosary is often used in conjunction with this Christian prayer from the Sermon on the Mount. It opens “Our Father, who art in Heaven.”

topics.description: A legendary lake creature purported to inhabit Loch Ness in the Scottish Highlands, famously associated with the debunked 1934 “surgeon’s photograph.”

parts.label: L
parts.question: The most famous photo of this creature, the so-called “surgeon’s photograph,” was revealed to be an elaborate hoax. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [M] Name this long-necked, humped cryptid that is named for and supposedly inhabits a lake in the Scottish highlands.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] The Patterson-Gimlin film supposedly shows this North American cryptid turning to face the camera as it runs away. This cryptid’s name comes from the large tracks it leaves behind.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [H] This reptilian-like cryptid, first purportedly sighted in Puerto Rico, is known for drinking the blood of goats and other livestock.

parts.label: L
parts.question: According to a text from the sixth century, this creature was stopped from attacking a monk’s follower when Saint Columba made the sign of the cross and told it to back off. For ten points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [M] Name this creature of which a “surgeon’s photograph” was taken in 1934 that has since been mostly debunked as a hoax. This large and long-necked creature supposedly inhabits a body of water in the Scottish Highlands.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] Like the Loch (lock) Ness Monster, this creature is a cryptid, since its existence is unsubstantiated. This creature is described as a hairy and ape-like humanoid creature in North American forests which leaves giant footprints.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [H] Sightings of this cryptid whose name means “goat-sucker” have mostly been in northern Mexico. This spiny creature supposedly the size of a large dog is said to attack and suck the blood from livestock.

topics.description: A Catholic religious order founded by Ignatius of Loyola, known for education, missionary work, Counter-Reformation activity, and theological scholarship.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Antonio Ruiz de Montoya wrote the first grammar of the Guaraní (gwah-rah-NEE) language while working at one of these facilities. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name these large, priest-run farms, mostly found in Paraguay, which were both missionary bases and economically self-sustaining plantations for cattle or yerba mate (YAIR-bah MAH-tay).
parts.answer: reductions [or reducción; or reducciones; or redução; or reduçoes; accept, but do not otherwise reveal, Jesuit reductions]

parts.label: B
parts.question: This Catholic order, which includes Pope Francis, was founded by Ignatius of Loyola and operated the Paraguayan reductions.

parts.label: C
parts.question: In this country, local Guaraní called Chiriguanos (sheer-ee-GWAH-nos) resisted evangelization prior to the 1892 Battle of Kuruyuki (koo-roo-YOO-kee). The coca-raising Aymara (AI-MAR-ah) people live mostly in this country.
parts.answer: Bolivia [Plurinational State of Bolivia; or Estado Plurinacional de Bolivia; or Tetã Hetãvoregua Mborivia; or Wuliwya Walja Suyunakana Marka; or Puliwya Achka Aylluska Mamallaqta]

parts.label: L
parts.question: For 10 points each, answer the following about the interpretation of Biblical prophecies during the Reformation:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [H] Martin Luther wrote that the “little horn” in this book’s vision of four beasts represented the Pope, who he identified with the Antichrist. This book also describes a giant statue made of gold, silver, bronze, iron, and clay.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [M] To refute the idea that the Antichrist was the Pope, theologians from this religious order like Francisco Ribera argued that Biblical prophecies would be fulfilled in the distant future. This order was founded by Ignatius of Loyola.
parts.answer: Jesuits [or Society of Jesus or SJ]

parts.label: C
parts.question: [E] Another Jesuit theologian, Luis del Alcázar, argued that the Antichrist had arrived far in the past in the person of this Roman emperor. This emperor is said to have fiddled during the Great Fire of Rome, which he blamed on Christians.

topics.description: The component of a contact force exerted perpendicular to the surface between two objects.

parts.label: L
parts.question: For 10 points each, answer the following about a stationary block on an inclined plane.

parts.label: A
parts.question: [10] The block does not sink through the plane thanks to this force perpendicular to a surface.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [10] The block will start moving when the static coefficient of friction is exceeded by this combination  of a trigonometric function and a physical measurement.
parts.answer: ANSWER: tangent of the angle of the incline

parts.label: C
parts.question: [10] The block is modified so that it keeps the same mass but now has a four times larger surface area.  The magnitude of the frictional force on the new block will have this relationship to the force in the  original system.
parts.answer: ANSWER: unchanged [or the same; or related by a factor of one]

parts.label: L
parts.question: The kinetic form of this force is weaker than the static form of this force because moving objects do not readily adhere to surfaces. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [E] Name this force which is characterized by a coefficient symbolized mu. This force resists motion when two objects rub up against each other.
parts.answer: friction [accept kinetic friction or static friction]

parts.label: B
parts.question: [M] The amount of kinetic friction experienced by an object moving on a plane is equal to the coefficient of friction multiplied by this force, which is orthogonal to the contact surface.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [H] The angle of repose, which gives the steepest angle at which static friction prevents an object from sliding, is equal to this trigonometric function applied to the coefficient of friction.
parts.answer: arctangent [or arctan or inverse tangent; do NOT accept or prompt on “tangent” or “cotangent”]

topics.description: An immortal human cell line derived from Henrietta Lacks's cervical cancer cells and widely used in biomedical research.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Answer the following about unethical medical experiments in the United States, for 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [H] In the 1950s and 60s, Chester M. Southam injected these cancer cells into uninformed patients. George Gey isolated this first immortal human cell line without consent from the donor.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [M] In 1955-57 over 100 Alaska Natives were given doses of radioactive iodine without being informed, to test the role of this butterfly-shaped gland in adapting to cold.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [E] As part of Project MKULTRA, the CIA administered this hallucinogenic drug to non-consenting individuals. This drug’s inventor Albert Hofmann famously rode a bicycle under its influence.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: The HER2 (“hur-two”) receptors on some cells with this condition are targeted by trastuzumab (“trass-TOO-zoo-mab”), branded as Herceptin (“hur-SEP-tin”). This condition may involve modifications to landscaper, gatekeeper or caretaker genes. The observation that cells with this condition rely on fermentation instead of aerobic respiration is called the Warburg effect. The proteins pRb and (*) p53 suppress the development of this condition. Cervical cells with this condition were non-consensually harvested to form the HeLa (“hee-lah”) cell line. Cells with this condition can metastasize to new parts of the body, requiring chemotherapy to kill. For 10 points, name this condition of uncontrolled cell replication that results in tumors.
parts.answer: cancer [or being cancerous; accept breast cancer or cervical cancer]

topics.description: A membrane-bound eukaryotic cell organelle with rough and smooth regions involved in the synthesis, folding, modification, and transport of proteins and lipids.

parts.label: L
parts.question: This organelle comes in "rough" and "smooth" forms. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this organelle which is continuous with the nuclear envelope. Both types of this organelle help with the synthesis of lipids.

parts.label: B
parts.question: The rough endoplasmic reticulum is studded with these cell structures, which have small and large subunits and are the sites of translation.

parts.label: C
parts.question: Ribosomes synthesize proteins based on codons, which are strings of this many DNA base pairs which encode a specific amino acid.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: Secretion of molecules from this organelle is inhibited by retention sequences such as KDEL . This organelle is the origin of COP1 vesicles sent to the Golgi body. A sarcoplasmic variety of this organelle releases calcium in muscle cells. Chaperonins are used in this organelle to (*) fold proteins. A part of this organelle is lined with ribosomes. For 10 points, name this organelle responsible for protein transport, with rough and smooth subunits.

topics.description: The tendency of matter to resist changes in its velocity, including remaining at rest or moving uniformly unless acted on by a net external force.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: It is not magnetism, but this property confines the plasma in a hohlraum to fuse deuterium and tritium. A balance named for this concept can measure mass in the absence of gravity. Torque is proportional to a (*) “moment” named for this concept that explains why dishes remain in place when a tablecloth is quickly pulled away. Newton’s first law concerns, for ten points, what principle that describes the tendency of objects to remain either in uniform motion or at rest?

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: The rotational analog of mass is the “moment of” this property. This word describes reference frames in which objects do not accelerate without force acting on them. Newton’s first law of motion, also known as the law of this property, states that objects (*) remain in their current state of motion unless acted on by an external force. For ten points, name this property of matter which causes objects to resist changes in velocity.

topics.description: A group of contagious respiratory viruses in the Orthomyxoviridae family, including strains such as H1N1 and those classified by hemagglutinin and neuraminidase types.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Oseltamivir prevents the cleavage of sialic acid, thus preventing this virus from traveling from cell to cell. For 10 point each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [E] Name this common virus. The H1N1 strain of this virus is known as its “swine” type.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [H] Oseltamivir is ingested in a prodrug containing one of these functional groups. The backbone of DNA is made up of sugar and this functional group.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [M] The starting material of the Hoffman–LaRoche synthesis of Tamiflu, shikimate, names a pathway for the synthesis of aromatic forms of these compounds. These compounds are the building blocks of proteins.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: This virus in the family orthomyxoviridae has hemagglutinin and neuraminidase glycoproteins on its surface, which is why strains of this virus are classified with H and N numbers. An H1N1 variant of this virus was named for its resemblance to viruses found in (*) pigs, and there are different vaccines for the new strains of this disease that emerge each year. For ten points, name this virus which has avian, swine, and Spanish varieties.
parts.answer: influenza [accept the flu or avian flu or swine flu or Spanish flu]

topics.description: The United States government agency responsible for civilian space exploration, aeronautics research, and major human and robotic spaceflight and space-science programs.

parts.label: L
parts.question: This object is half-illuminated by the Sun in a photo by William Anders titled for its “rise” published on the cover of Life magazine. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [M] Name this object. Another photograph taken in 1972 analogizes this object to a “blue marble.”

parts.label: B
parts.question: [H] Earth is seen in a band of sunlight in this later photograph, taken by the Voyager 1 probe in 1990. In a book inspired by this photograph, Carl Sagan wrote, “Look again at that dot… That’s home. That’s us.”

parts.label: C
parts.question: [E] Earthrise, The Blue Marble, and Pale Blue Dot were all taken on missions organized by this agency. This U.S. government agency built the Hubble Space Telescope along with the European Space Agency.
parts.answer: NASA [or National Aeronautics and Space Administration]

parts.label: L
parts.question: In 2020, this organization brought its “worm” logo out of retirement, though it still uses the “meatball” as its primary logo. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [E] Name this US agency, known for its research in space.
parts.answer: NASA [accept National Aeronautics and Space Administration]

parts.label: B
parts.question: [H] In 2022, the first full color photograph from this NASA telescope was released. Also known as the Next Generation Space Telescope, it was launched in December 2021.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [M] As a part of NASA’s Commercial Crew Program, this company designed the CST-100 Starliner. This corporation is best known for manufacturing airplanes, including the 737 and 747.

topics.description: Red is a visible color associated with cultural symbolism, the longest wavelengths of visible light, primary-color systems, and various scientific and branding applications.

parts.label: L
parts.question: The wirewound type of these objects can be constructed using a conductive wire around a non conductive core. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: Identify these objects whose strength is measured in ohms. Their strength is usually indicated on them with a series of lines following a standard color code.

parts.label: B
parts.question: The ohm is defined as this quantity per ampere, and is the difference in electric potential between two points. This quantity is equal to energy over charge.

parts.label: C
parts.question: This color represents the digit 2 in the resistor color code. It also has the highest wavelength of any color of visible light, appearing at the opposite end of the rainbow from violet as a result.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: Both strontium and lithium burn this color in a flame test, and litmus paper turns this color in the presence of acids. This color on the longer-wavelength end of the visible light spectrum names an allotrope of phosphorus used in matches. In the NFPA safety diamond, the number in this color’s section indicates the (*) flammability of a substance. For ten points, name this color, which is a primary color along with yellow and blue.

topics.description: A fossil fuel composed primarily of methane, commonly odorized with sulfur-containing compounds for leak detection, and used for heating, electricity generation, and industrial processes.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: Decree 172 obligates certain “unfriendly” countries to pay for this resource through the GPB bank. In  February 2022, Olaf Scholz suspended a project to transport this resource, the Nord Stream 2. Vladimir  Putin has threatened to (*) cut off Europe’s access to this resource if not paid in rubles. For 10 points, the war in  Ukraine has led to tensions between the EU and Russia on the import of what colorless, odorless fossil fuel?
parts.answer: natural gas [prompt on gas; or fossil fuels]

parts.label: L
parts.question: Many old molecular biology labs are equipped with these devices to sterilize a workspace before doing cell culture. For ten points each,

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name these devices that provide an open flame in a laboratory. They were invented by and named for a German chemist.

parts.label: B
parts.question: Bunsen burners are fed by this fossil fuel, which is mainly composed of methane but is tainted with small amounts of sulfides so that it can be smelled.

parts.label: C
parts.question: The safe way to heat a metal under a Bunsen burner is to place it in one of these round porcelain containers, which are extremely heat-resistant. A common lab demo involves measuring the weight of one after burning a magnesium ribbon.

topics.description: A butterfly-shaped endocrine gland in the neck that produces thyroid hormones, including T3 and T4, and secretes calcitonin through its parafollicular cells.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: A peroxidase in this organ is targeted by antibodies in Hashimoto’s disease, and a receptor in this organ is  targeted in Graves’ disease. This organ secretes the hormones T3 and T4. Parafollicular cells in this organ  secrete (*) calcitonin, which is opposed by PTH. This gland enlarges to form a goiter, which is caused by iodine  deficiency. For 10 points, name this butterfly-shaped gland in the neck.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Answer the following about unethical medical experiments in the United States, for 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [H] In the 1950s and 60s, Chester M. Southam injected these cancer cells into uninformed patients. George Gey isolated this first immortal human cell line without consent from the donor.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [M] In 1955-57 over 100 Alaska Natives were given doses of radioactive iodine without being informed, to test the role of this butterfly-shaped gland in adapting to cold.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [E] As part of Project MKULTRA, the CIA administered this hallucinogenic drug to non-consenting individuals. This drug’s inventor Albert Hofmann famously rode a bicycle under its influence.

topics.description: A named storage location or symbolic entity in a computer program whose value can be assigned, stored, and used during computation.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Two basic operations used to modify this structure are “push” and “pop.” For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [10] Name this “last in, first out” data structure. An “overflow” of these structures names a common  error in Java.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [10] Stack overflow can commonly occur with this type of computation. This operation involves a  function calling itself.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [10] Unlike heaps, stacks can be used to store local examples of these entities. Commonly used symbols  for these entities include the letters x and y.

parts.label: L
parts.question: You are a TA catching cheaters in a computer science class. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [E] You sigh as you see multiple assignments with identical code, but with different names given to these storage units of data. These things may have to be declared before standing in for a value.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [M] A few students use their real names as they post problems to a programming help site named for this occurrence. Infinite recursion often causes this occurrence in which memory is exceeded, leading to a crash.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [H] You easily catch cheaters using MOSS, a script compatible with this Bell Labs-created operating system. C was developed for this operating system that has a philosophy of easy-to-understand, accessible code.

topics.description: A sexually transmitted bacterial infection caused by the bacterium Treponema pallidum.

parts.label: L
parts.question: The population of the Taino people crashed in the years following contact with this man. For ten points each,

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this explorer and slaver whose first of four expeditions across the Atlantic Ocean set sail in 1492.

parts.label: B
parts.question: The genocide perpetrated by Columbus and other Spanish colonizers was documented and opposed by this Bishop of Chiapas, the first man to be appointed “Protector of the Indians.”

parts.label: C
parts.question: Some DNA studies have suggested that, after assaulting the Native Americans they encountered, Columbus’ men introduced Europe to this sexually transmitted disease, caused by pallidum bacteria.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Susan Reverby uncovered American-led experiments in which Guatemalan citizens were purposefully infected with this disease. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [H] Name this disease. The director of the Guatemalan experiments, John Charles Cutler, had earlier worked on a similar study on this disease in the United States that was initially funded by the Rosenwald Fund.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [M] That unethical study on syphilis infected hundreds of Black men and was named for this Alabama university. A group of Black airmen who trained at this university during World War II was the first Black flying group.
parts.answer: Tuskegee [or Tuskegee Institute or Tuskegee University or Tuskegee syphilis study or Tuskegee Airmen or Tuskegee experiment]

parts.label: C
parts.question: [E] In 2010, this Secretary of State formally apologized for the Guatemala syphilis experiments. Previously, a formal apology for the Tuskegee experiment had been issued by this politician’s husband, Bill.
parts.answer: Hillary Clinton [or Hillary Rodham Clinton or HRC; prompt on Clinton; prompt on Hillary]

topics.description: A red supergiant variable star in the constellation Orion, also known as Alpha Orionis.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: Rigel is a blue supergiant in this constellation. This constellation is often interpreted as fighting Taurus with its dogs Canis Major and Canis Minor. This constellation, which contains the Trapezium Cluster and the stars Bellatrix and (*) Betelgeuse, also contains a set of three stars in a line, known as its “belt.” For ten points, name this constellation that depicts a hunter from Greek mythology.
parts.answer: Orion [prompt on the Hunter before mention]

parts.label: L
parts.question: One star in this constellation experienced a drastic dimming during winter 2020, believed to have been caused by "starspots" covering over half its surface. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this constellation depicting a hunter from Greek mythology. Its most famous feature is the three stars that make up its belt.

parts.label: B
parts.question: This supergiant variable star, which experienced the aforementioned dimming, is usually the second brightest star in Orion. It forms one of Orion's "shoulders".

parts.label: C
parts.question: Astronomers believed that Betelgeuse's dimming could be a sign that it will undergo one of these events soon. In these events, a massive star collapses in on itself and explodes.

topics.description: The displacement of observed spectral lines toward longer wavelengths, commonly indicating that an astronomical object is receding from the observer.

parts.label: L
parts.question: One of these objects is at the center of astronomical object 3C 273, which is the most distant object visible through a backyard telescope because it is brighter than all stars in its surrounding galaxy combined. For ten points each,

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name these astronomical objects that are so dense that not even light can escape from their event horizons.

parts.label: B
parts.question: 3C 273 is one of these objects, the most luminous type of object in the universe. These objects are composed of an active galactic nucleus powered by a supermassive black hole.

parts.label: C
parts.question: Radio astronomer Maarten Schmidt confirmed the vast distance between quasars and Earth by measuring the high degree of this shift, an example of the Doppler effect.
parts.answer: redshift (do not accept or prompt on “blueshift”)

parts.label: L
parts.question: An image of the galaxy cluster SMACS 0723 [smacks oh-seven-two-three] released in 2022 was titled “Webb’s First [one of these images].” For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [H] Name these images taken in small regions of the sky with very long exposure times. The Hubble Space Telescope released its first of these images in 1995.
parts.answer: ANSWER: deep field images [or deep images; accept Webb’s First Deep Field or the Hubble Deep Field]

parts.label: B
parts.question: [M] Webb’s First Deep Field helped discover multiple objects whose values for this phenomenon potentially exceed the record of z = 11. This phenomenon is caused by objects getting farther from the viewer in the Doppler effect.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [E] Webb’s First Deep Field was taken using wavelengths near this region of the spectrum, which is longer than visible light but shorter than microwaves.

topics.description: The internal force per unit area in a material, associated with deformation and related to strain, especially in the context of elasticity.

parts.label: L
parts.question: The force exerted by these objects equals negative displacement times their namesake constant. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [E] Name these objects, which are subject to Hooke’s law. These elastic, coil-shaped objects store mechanical energy when compressed or stretched.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [H] As a material undergoes elastic deformation, plotting this quantity against strain produces a straight line. It’s not pressure, but this quantity has units of force per unit area.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [M] This scientist’s namesake modulus equals the ratio of stress over strain. This British scientist also conducted an early double slit experiment to confirm the wave nature of light.

parts.label: L
parts.question: To lessen human impact on the environment, this architect proposed a set of self-sustaining floating cities known as Cloud Nine. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [M] Name this architect, a proponent of geodesic [jee-uh-DESS-ik] domes, who lends his name to a 60-carbon molecule.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] Geodesic domes use triangles that can easily distribute this quantity in architecture. This quantity refers to the force on a material, while strain is the deformation of that material.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [H] Fuller’s ideas inspired the first enclosed geodesic dome called the Climatron, which was built for this city’s botanical garden. Dankmar Adler and Louis Sullivan designed a terracotta-adorned skyscraper in this city.
parts.answer: St. Louis, Missouri (The skyscraper is the Wainwright Building.)

topics.description: An analytical spectroscopic technique that uses magnetic fields and radiofrequency radiation to determine molecular structure from the chemical shifts of atomic nuclei.

parts.label: L
parts.question: This technique was first described by Isidor Rabi. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this technique, which measures a chemical shift measured in parts per million and is commonly measured relative to TMS. This technique commonly uses H-1 or C-13 isotopes.
parts.answer: NMR [or nuclear magnetic resonance; accept 1H-NMR or 13C-NMR]

parts.label: B
parts.question: TMS is composed of four methyl groups bonded to a central atom of this element, with atomic symbol Si.

parts.label: C
parts.question: Solvents in NMR often have their hydrogen atoms replaced by this isotope. This heaviest stable isotope of hydrogen has a nucleus consisting of a proton and neutron, and is found in heavy water.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Suppression of solvents in the “proton” form of this technique can be achieved by adding heavy water to reduce noise from regular H₂O molecules. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [M] Name this form of spectroscopy which measures the chemical shift of a compound upon exposure to a magnetic field.
parts.answer: NMR spectroscopy [or nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy; accept proton NMR or H-NMR]

parts.label: B
parts.question: [H] This mathematical structure can be used in tandem with the n+1 rule to determine the height of signals in H-NMR. If a signal on an H-NMR spectrum arises from a single neighboring carbon, the relative heights of the peaks created by J-coupling will align with this structure.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [E] Atoms with high levels of this quantity pull electrons away from protons, causing them to become deshielded during NMR. Fluorine has the highest value on the periodic table for this quantity, which the Pauling scale assigns a value from 0 to 4.

topics.description: A study topic covering base-two numeral representation with digits zero and one and two-valued logic with true and false. Number representation and logical truth values are related applications of two states, not identical concepts.

parts.label: L
parts.question: When using an XOR [ex-or] cipher to encrypt data, words must be encoded into strings of 8-bit numbers in this numerical base. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [E] Name this base used by computers that only includes 0’s and 1’s.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [M] In an XOR cipher, strings are encrypted using these entities. These things can be either “public” or “private” depending on how accessible they are.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [H] Cryptography algorithms commonly utilize these “one-way” functions to scramble input data. One of these functions called MD5 is now considered obsolete due to a new function that produces its “collisions.”

parts.label: L
parts.question: Hermitian examples of these things consist of complex conjugates. For ten points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [H] Name these things which are reduced into row-echelon form through Gaussian elimination. These rectangular arrays of numbers can only be multiplied if the column number of the first matches the row number of the second.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] Logical matrices only contain values of zero and this number. In Boolean logic, zero corresponds to false while this number corresponds to true.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [M] Boolean logic is this type of system, because there are only two possible values: true or false. Another system with this name uses ones and zeros to code for information in computers.

topics.description: The scientific theory explaining biological evolution, common ancestry, and the mechanisms by which populations change over generations.
aliases: Theory of evolution by natural selection

parts.label: L
parts.question: Answer some questions about the life and times of William Jennings Bryan, for 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [10] He was the lead prosecutor in the Scopes Monkey trial, which concerned John Scopes having allegedly taught this theory in school. This biological theory is opposed to creationism or intelligent design.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [10] Bryan later served as Secretary of State under this president. This president won reelection in 1916 using the slogan "He kept us out of war".

parts.label: C
parts.question: [10] Bryan is probably best known for giving a speech in which he defended bimetallism and which he ended by declaring "you shall not crucify mankind upon" one of these specific objects, for which the speech is named.
parts.answer: a cross of gold [accept Cross of Gold speech; prompt on cross]

parts.label: L
parts.question: Clarence Darrow, the defense lawyer in this trial, actually told the jury “We do not see how you could” return a verdict of not guilty, as one purpose of the trial was to bring a law to a higher court. For ten points each,

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this 1925 case, brought by the state of Tennessee against a teacher who violated the Butler Act.
parts.answer: Scopes trial (accept Scopes Monkey Trial; accept Tennessee v. John Thomas Scopes)

parts.label: B
parts.question: The Scopes Monkey Trial concerned Scopes’ illegal teaching of this scientific concept, as described by Charles Darwin and other biologists.
parts.answer: evolution of humans from other primates/apes/etc. (accept natural selection)

parts.label: C
parts.question: The prosecution’s legal team included this orator who gave the “Cross of Gold” speech, ran unsuccessfully for President three times, and was called to the stand during the Scopes trial to be questioned on the Bible.

topics.description: Blood-feeding flying insects of the family Culicidae, including species whose females transmit malaria and other diseases.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: A Timothy Winegard history of this animal describes how it annihilated Scottish settlers in the Darien Scheme. A region named for these animals was home to the Poyais Scheme and was a British-dominated area of Nicaragua. The Greeks nicknamed these animals “General Anopheles” for how well they killed Persians. Research by Ronald Ross led to nets and sleeping bags as a protectant against these animals. Sickle cell natural selection occurred among African ethnic groups because of a disease spread by these animals, which kill more people per year than any other. Malaria is carried by, for 10 points, what blood-sucking insects?

parts.label: L
parts.question: When applying the chi-squared test to this model, it’s important to remember to use only one degree of freedom,  even though the equation governing it has 3 terms. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this idealized model of a population, which assumes no migration, no genetic drift, no assortative mating,  and an infinite population size.

parts.label: B
parts.question: The 2-p-q term in the Hardy-Weinberg model gives the frequency of this kind of genotype. This kind of  genotype has two different alleles at one locus, and is usually written using a capital and a lowercase letter.

parts.label: C
parts.question: A classic example of heterozygote advantage protects against malaria, which is transmitted by Plasmodium in  these blood-sucking insects. The name of these insects means “little fly.”

topics.description: Sodium is the reactive alkali metal with atomic number 11, known for its bright-yellow flame test and compounds such as sodium chloride, sodium carbonate, sodium bicarbonate, and sodium hydroxide.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: The Downs process produces this element, which also names a “doublet” found in Fraunhofer (FROWN-hoh-fur) lines. This second-lightest alkali metal produces an intense yellow color in a flame test. This element’s carbonate is called soda ash, while its bicarbonate is known as baking soda. High concentrations of this element and (*) chlorine make ocean water undrinkable. For ten points, name this element with symbol Na, which binds with chlorine to make table salt.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Answer some questions about the flame test. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [M] The flame test commonly uses this apparatus to provide a flame. This apparatus, named for a German chemist, is also used to sterilize loops in microbiology.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] This element’s halides produce a green or blue-green frame. This metal is commonly used in wires because of its low cost and high conductivity.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [H] This alkali metal produces a bright-yellow flame. This element’s hydroxide forms a strong base called lye.

topics.description: A graph that plots stars by luminosity or absolute magnitude against surface temperature or spectral classification, revealing features such as the main sequence.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Friedrich Bessel discovered changes in the motion of this star, inferring its binary companion. For ten points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [M] Name this brightest star in the night sky. This main-sequence star found in Canis Major forms the Winter Triangle with Procyon and Betelgeuse and is often called the Dog Star.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] Sirius B, the binary companion of Sirius A, is this type of star. These stars that can come in black, brown, or white types are named for their small size.
parts.answer: dwarf star [accept white dwarf, brown dwarf, or black dwarf]

parts.label: C
parts.question: [H] While white dwarfs are located at the bottom left of this diagram, red and orange dwarfs can be found in its main sequence. This diagram plots the luminosities, stellar classifications, and temperatures of stars.
parts.answer: H-R Diagram [or Hertzsprung-Russell Diagram or HRD]

parts.label: L
parts.question: Stars at the tip of the red giant branch can serve as “standard candles” when calculating this quantity. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [E] Name this quantity that may be expressed in light-years or parsecs.
parts.answer: distance [accept answers indicating how far an object is from Earth]

parts.label: B
parts.question: [M] The tip of the red giant branch is a feature on this diagram, which plots the luminosity of stars against their temperature. A diagonal line across this diagram represents the “main sequence.”

parts.label: C
parts.question: [H] When stars leave the tip of the red giant branch, they experience a “flash” named after this element, in which it is rapidly fused into carbon.

topics.description: An idealized population-genetics model in which allele and genotype frequencies remain constant under conditions such as random mating, no migration, no selection, no mutation, no genetic drift, and a very large population.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: Random mating and no migration are two of five conditions that will prevent this process if all met, by the Hardy-Weinberg Principle. The convergent form of this process involves unrelated species developing similar traits. Studying the beaks of finches in the Galapagos prompted (*) Charles Darwin to theorize this process. For ten points, what process is characterized by changes in a species over generations ?

parts.label: L
parts.question: When applying the chi-squared test to this model, it’s important to remember to use only one degree of freedom,  even though the equation governing it has 3 terms. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this idealized model of a population, which assumes no migration, no genetic drift, no assortative mating,  and an infinite population size.

parts.label: B
parts.question: The 2-p-q term in the Hardy-Weinberg model gives the frequency of this kind of genotype. This kind of  genotype has two different alleles at one locus, and is usually written using a capital and a lowercase letter.

parts.label: C
parts.question: A classic example of heterozygote advantage protects against malaria, which is transmitted by Plasmodium in  these blood-sucking insects. The name of these insects means “little fly.”

topics.description: Random or unwanted variation that obscures meaningful information in a signal or dataset, often characterized relative to the signal through a signal-to-noise ratio.

parts.label: L
parts.question: This technique is generally slower than scan line techniques. For 10 points each,

parts.label: A
parts.question: [H] Name this technique that extrapolates light paths to generate images. It draws its name from a method in physics that models light by representing it as the namesake geometric object.
parts.answer: ray tracing [prompt on ray casting or path tracing or photon mapping]

parts.label: B
parts.question: [M] Increasing the number of rays when ray tracing can reduce this phenomenon that is the random variation of information. AM radios can create the “static” type of this phenomenon.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [E] Ray tracing can also trace the path of sound waves to create this physics phenomenon in which sound arrives after a delay. Shouting in a cave can produce this phenomenon.

parts.label: L
parts.question: The 2020 iteration of this project had a much higher rate of unanswered questions than usual. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [E] Name this project that surveys the entire U.S. population every ten years to gather demographic information and tally the country’s number of inhabitants.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [M] Controversially, the 2020 census added this statistical phenomenon to its results as part of the practice of “differential privacy.” The ratio of signal to this phenomenon is used to quantify the purity of information.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [H] As a result of differential privacy, the 2020 census “counted” a non-existent second person in Monowi, a town in this state which actually only has one resident.

topics.description: A group of RNA viruses that use reverse transcriptase to produce a DNA copy of their genome and integrate it into a host cell's DNA, including lentiviruses.

parts.label: L
parts.question: The ribonuclease H domain in these viruses degrades the U5 and R regions of one molecule. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name these viruses, which use reverse transcriptase to create complementary strands of DNA from RNA. Lentiviruses are a subtype of these viruses.

parts.label: B
parts.question: The pol gene encodes for reverse transcriptase in this bloodborne retrovirus, the causative agent of AIDS.

parts.label: C
parts.question: HIV targets these cells by attacking their CD4 surface receptor. Unlike B cells, these cells mature in the thymus.

parts.label: L
parts.question: This virus is the only one in the genus Lentivirus to infect humans, and can be treated with drugs that inhibit CD4-Positive cells. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [10] Name this sexually-transmitted virus. Patients who suffer from it often experience Kaposi's sarcoma, and it may eventually lead to AIDS.
parts.answer: HIV [or human immunodeficiency virus; accept HIV/AIDS]

parts.label: B
parts.question: [10] This bacterial disease is one of the most common causes of death for AIDS patients. This disease was historically known as consumption and infects the lungs.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [10] HIV is a member of this class of viruses. They insert a copy of their genome into the DNA of their host cells by using reverse transcriptase, an enzyme which transcribes RNA into DNA.

topics.description: A physical constant equal to the ideal gas constant divided by Avogadro's constant that relates temperature to energy per particle.

parts.label: L
parts.question: With Josef Stefan, this scientist names a law relating the power radiated from a blackbody to its temperature. For ten points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [H] Name this scientist who developed statistical mechanics and the H theorem. A constant named for this scientist is equal to the gas constant divided by Avogadro’s number, and his tombstone bears a thermodynamic equation.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [M] The equation on Boltzmann’s tombstone relates this quantity to the natural logarithm of the number of microstates. This measure of disorder of a system is always increasing in the universe.

parts.label: C
