parts.question: [E] Boltzmann’s constant, along with many other constants in physics, is represented by this letter. A subscript of this letter under the letter E is used to represent kinetic energy, and it is also used to abbreviate Kelvins.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: Dividing the ideal gas constant by this quantity results in Boltzmann’s constant. This quantity which is defined as the number of atoms in twelve grams of carbon-12 is equal to the number of particles in (*) 22.4 liters of gas at standard temperature and pressure. For 10 points, name this constant which is the number of particles in a mole, approximately equal to 6.02 times 10 to the 23rd power.
parts.answer: Avogadro’s number [accept Avogadro’s constant; prompt on variable]

topics.description: Propagating ripples or disturbances in spacetime curvature produced by accelerating massive bodies, including merging black holes or neutron stars.

parts.label: L
parts.question: These phenomena were first discovered by the LIGO observatories in Hanford, Washington and Livingston, Louisiana. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: Identify these disturbances in the curvature of spacetime. They are released as the energy from decaying orbits of two massive objects.
parts.answer: gravitational waves [or gravity waves; prompt on just waves]

parts.label: B
parts.question: Gravitational waves were predicted in this man's general theory of relativity. This man is more well known for relating mass to energy in his equation e=mc^2 ("e equals m c squared").

parts.label: C
parts.question: The L in LIGO stands for this type of light-generating device, which was used in the experiment that discovered gravitational waves. These objects may undergo population inversion and create a beam of light through stimulated emission.

parts.label: L
parts.question: The 2017 Nobel Prize in Physics was awarded for contributions to this experiment. For 10 points  each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [10] Name this experiment and group of observatories, which use mirrors four kilometers apart and laser  interferometry to detect changes that are one ten-thousandth the diameter of a proton.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [10] LIGO was designed to detect these disturbances in spacetime that are predicted by general  relativity. The setup first detected these ripples in 2016.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [10] The first gravitational waves detected by LIGO were from a merger of two of these massive objects  that light cannot escape from.

topics.description: A covalent bond in which two pairs of electrons are shared between atoms, consisting of one sigma bond and one pi bond.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Fusing two of this molecule together forms naphthalene, and adding a methyl group to this molecule yields toluene. For ten points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [H] Name this simplest aromatic hydrocarbon, whose structure was discovered by August Kekule (KEK-oo-lay) after supposedly having a vision of a snake eating its own tail. This molecule’s formula is C6H6.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [M] Benzene’s cyclic nature was confirmed by Kathleen Lonsdale, who used x-rays undergoing this process to do so. This process causes waves to bend around an encountered obstacle.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [E] In the Birch reduction of benzene, one of these structures is reduced. Benzene’s structure consists of single bonds alternating with these bonds, represented by two lines on a Lewis diagram.

parts.label: L
parts.question: The azimuthal quantum number provides quantitative information regarding the shape of these entities. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [E] Name these spaces probabilistically occupied by electrons. The letters s, p, d, and f are used to label atomic types of these entities, which consist of “shells” that can hold one spin-up and one spin-down electron each.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [H] Atomic orbitals that participate in chemical bonding exhibit this phenomenon, wherein they “mix” with each other. Carbon in an alkene exhibits the “sp2” form of this phenomenon.
parts.answer: hybridization [accept hybrid orbitals; or sp2 hybridization]

parts.label: C
parts.question: [M] Atoms that are part of these bonds often have an sp2 hybridization. These bonds, which consist of a sigma and a pi orbital, have 4 electrons.

topics.description: An electrical bridge circuit used to determine an unknown resistance by balancing the resistances in two branches.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: This is the number of resistors in a Wheatstone bridge. Superfluidity was discovered in an isotope of Helium with this number, which is also the number of Maxwell's electromagnetic equations. Along with spatial dimensions, time can be considered a (*) dimension with this number, the number of fundamental interactions in the Standard Model. For 10 points, Beryllium has what atomic number, the number of sides in a square?

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: This measure is quantized by fractions of the Von Klitzing constant in a form of the Hall effect. A Wheatstone bridge can determine this quantity that, unlike reactance, leads to Joule heating. Finding the total value for this quantity requires summing the (*) reciprocal value of each component in a parallel circuit. Conductance is the reciprocal of this quantity, which is measured in ohms. For ten points, name this quantity, equal to voltage over current, that opposes the flow of electricity.

topics.description: The process by which inherited characteristics of biological populations change across generations.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: Jean-Baptiste Lamarck stated that this phenomenon was driven by the “use,” or “disuse,” of vital organs. Charles Lyell’s Principles of Geology heavily influenced a seminal work on this phenomenon. Analogous structures develop through the “convergent” form of this phenomenon. After studying the beaks of finches, this phenomenon was termed (*) “descent with modification” in the book On the Origin of Species by Charles Darwin. For 10 points, natural selection drives what process, by which characteristics of organisms change over time?
parts.answer: evolution [accept natural selection before it is read; accept convergent evolution; accept adaptive radiation; accept speciation]

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: Random mating and no migration are two of five conditions that will prevent this process if all met, by the Hardy-Weinberg Principle. The convergent form of this process involves unrelated species developing similar traits. Studying the beaks of finches in the Galapagos prompted (*) Charles Darwin to theorize this process. For ten points, what process is characterized by changes in a species over generations ?

topics.description: A search algorithm that locates a target by repeatedly halving a sorted search space, including a sorted array or an ordered binary search tree.

parts.label: L
parts.question: This search algorithm works by recursing down a tree, choosing to go left or right at each node based on whether that node’s value is greater than or less than the value being searched for. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [M] Name this search algorithm which is much faster than linear search. In addition to its tree version, this algorithm can also operate on a sorted array by repeatedly splitting the searched area in half.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] Appropriately, given its name, binary search only works in trees with at most this many children per node. This is also the number of possible values of a single bit.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [H] Binary search has time complexity big-O of this function of the number of nodes. That’s because binary search operates on one node per tree level, and binary tree height is at most this function of the number of nodes.
parts.answer: logarithm [or base-two logarithm or log or log n or logarithm with any other base; accept big-O log n]

parts.label: L
parts.question: The node values in the left subtree of a tree used in an algorithm for this task are less than the root’s value. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this general task in computer science, which can be naively implemented by sequentially checking list elements starting from the beginning.

parts.label: B
parts.question: A search algorithm named for this word repeatedly divides subarrays in half to find a value in a sorted list. This word also refers to the base-2 number system of ones and zeroes that underpins digital computing.

parts.label: C
parts.question: The worst case space complexity of a search algorithm can be expressed with this common notation, which is also used to note the worst case runtime of an algorithm.

topics.description: Russian physiologist whose experiments on digestion and conditioned reflexes established foundational principles of classical conditioning and earned him the 1904 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: This man won the 1904 Nobel Prize in Physiology for using vivisection and fistulas to study the digestive system. The concept of “reflex at a distance” was expanded on by this man, with a test in which a (*) buzzer being sounded at the same time as an assistant provided food; both the assistant and the buzzer sound triggered the salivation response. For ten points, name this Russian scientist who studied classical conditioning by feeding dogs.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: In one experiment, these animals were grouped into yoked pairs where one of them had an effective lever and the other did not. A psychologist-slash-surgeon who was studying gastric functions in these animals also ran an experiment on them that employed whistles and tuning forks. Martin Seligman found that groups of these animals that were given inescapable shocks would later not try to escape being shocked, displaying (*) “learned helplessness.” The presence of stimuli like the ticking of a metronome caused these animals to salivate in a series of experiments on classical conditioning. For 10 points, name these animals, the subjects of experiments by Ivan Pavlov.

topics.description: A measure of a fuel’s resistance to engine knocking under compression, used to classify gasoline and other fuels.

parts.label: L
parts.question: The Betterton-Kroll process is used to extract bismuth from alloys containing this element. For ten points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [M] Name this element that was used in pipes until its toxicity was discovered. Today, it is still used in acid car batteries.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [H] Thomas Midgley used lead to decrease engine knock and to boost this gasoline rating. More premium gasoline generally has a higher value of this rating shown on gas pumps.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [E] Lead was once found in this substance, until it was discovered that it would crack and contaminate the environment. Watercolors are a type of art in which this substance is applied to canvas with brushes.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: A compound with this many carbons names the ability for fuel to withstand compression in an engine. There are this number of hydrogen atoms in a cyclobutane [sye-kloh-BYOO-tayn] molecule. An alkane [AL-kayn] with this many carbon atoms represents a fuel’s resistance to knocking with its namesake “rating.” The standard allotrope of sulfur consists of (*) rings containing this number of atoms. A beryllium isotope with this mass number is formed by combining two alpha particles. This integer value is the atomic number of oxygen. For 10 points, give this number of valence electrons in a noble gas atom, which has a full octet.
parts.answer: eight [prompt on octane rating or full octet]

topics.description: Regions of probability around an atomic nucleus, described by quantum wavefunctions, where electrons are likely to be found and classified into s, p, d, and f types.

parts.label: L
parts.question: The azimuthal quantum number provides quantitative information regarding the shape of these entities. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [E] Name these spaces probabilistically occupied by electrons. The letters s, p, d, and f are used to label atomic types of these entities, which consist of “shells” that can hold one spin-up and one spin-down electron each.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [H] Atomic orbitals that participate in chemical bonding exhibit this phenomenon, wherein they “mix” with each other. Carbon in an alkene exhibits the “sp2” form of this phenomenon.
parts.answer: hybridization [accept hybrid orbitals; or sp2 hybridization]

parts.label: C
parts.question: [M] Atoms that are part of these bonds often have an sp2 hybridization. These bonds, which consist of a sigma and a pi orbital, have 4 electrons.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: Some of these structures are non-degenerate by the presence of ligands in crystal field theory, which models their “splitting.” When these structures combine in molecules, the gap between two of them known as the HOMO and LUMO indicate the molecule’s stability. To explain the Lewis structure of methane, Linus Pauling proposed that these structures can undergo (*) hybridization. At most two particles with opposite spins can occupy these structures according to the Pauli exclusion principle. The letters s, p, d, and f each label a differently shaped type of, for 10 points, what regions in which electrons are most likely to be found?
parts.answer: (atomic) orbitals [accept subtypes such as d orbitals; accept molecular orbitals]

topics.description: The rate of change of velocity with respect to time, measured in meters per second squared and related to net force by Newton's second law.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: In uniform circular motion, this quantity always points radially inward. This quantity is the second derivative of displacement with respect to time, and it equals zero when the forces acting on an object are (*) balanced. Newton's 2nd law states that force equals mass times this quantity. For 10 points, what quantity is measured in meters per second squared and describes the change in velocity?

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: Albert Einstein deduced that experiencing a constant value of this quantity is locally indistinguishable from being in an inertial reference frame. The centripetal [sen-TRIH-pih-tul] form of this quantity equals radius times the square of angular frequency, or alternatively the square of tangential velocity over radius. This quantity’s second time derivative is called (*) snap, while its first time derivative is called jerk. This quantity’s SI unit is the meter per second squared. Force equals the product of mass and this quantity by Newton’s second law. For 10 points, what quantity is the rate of change of an object’s velocity?
parts.answer: acceleration [accept gravitational acceleration or centripetal acceleration]

topics.description: Sputnik 1 was the first artificial satellite to orbit Earth, launched by the Soviet Union in October 1957 and widely regarded as marking the beginning of the Space Race.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: This man's 1957 visit to the Turkish embassy in his country ended a summer crisis over military  influence in Syria. This leader, who launched the failed Virgin Lands Campaign, left the Four  Powers Summit after only a day due to tensions over the (*) U-2 incident. The satellite Sputnik was  launched under this leader, with whom Fidel Castro struck a deal to place nuclear missiles in Cuba. This  leader's “Secret Speech” denounced the repression of the Stalin era. For 10 points, name this Soviet  politician who bested Georgy Malenkov in a 1950s leadership struggle.

parts.label: L
parts.question: The United States claimed victory in the Space Race because we got to the Moon, so all of these other Soviet firsts don’t really count. For ten points each,

parts.label: A
parts.question: This first artificial satellite to orbit Earth was launched in October 1957. It broadcast a beeping radio signal for three weeks.

parts.label: B
parts.question: In 1957, this dog was picked up off the streets of Moscow and became the first creature to orbit the Earth, flying aboard Sputnik 2.

parts.label: C
parts.question: In 1961, Yuri Gagarin became the first human in space, flying aboard this spacecraft.

topics.description: A fluid-mechanics principle stating that, under certain steady-flow conditions, increasing fluid speed is associated with decreasing static pressure.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: The force generated by these things is density times velocity times circulation by the Kutta-Joukowski theorem. They're not wheels, but the degree of asymmetry in the shape of these objects, called camber, can allow them to function at zero angle of attack. Control surfaces like (*) flaps and ailerons may be attached to these things to prevent stalling and control roll. The Bernoulli effect explains how these things generate force, since by deflecting air downwards they create a lower pressure above them than below them. For 10 points, name these things that generate lift to keep airplanes in the air.
parts.answer: wings [accept airfoils; accept lift surfaces; prompt on airplanes or aeroplanes before mention by asking “which part of the airplane?”]

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: When these machines exceed the critical value of attack, it causes a dangerous situation called a "stall". A common and sometimes incorrect explanation for how these machines work invokes the Bernoulli principle to explain that the air above one part of them is less (*) dense than below, generating lift. For 10 points, what machines might be powered by jet engines and take off from runways?
parts.answer: airplanes [or aircraft; accept specific types of airplanes; accept airfoils or airplane wings or airplane propellors]

topics.description: A glucose-based structural polysaccharide that forms a principal component of plant cell walls.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Saprotrophic fungi are an example of this kind of organism. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [H] Name these types of organisms which absorb nutrients from decaying matter . More common examples of these organisms consist of earthworms which consume detritus.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] Some xylophagus fungi evolved with the ability to digest lignin found in this material. Termites can digest this material which is found in the bark of trees.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [M] Soft-rot fungi secrete an enzyme that can digest this glucose polymer found in plant cell walls.

parts.label: L
parts.question: The Carboniferous period may have resulted from an inability of decomposers to deal with a new molecule, lignin, being incorporated into this structure. For ten points each,

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this rigid structure that allows plant cells, but not animal cells, to withstand turgor pressure. It is found outside the cell membrane.

parts.label: B
parts.question: Unlike the walls of fungi, which are composed of chitin [KYE-tin], plant walls are made of this glucose polysaccharide.

parts.label: C
parts.question: Primary plant walls also contain varying amounts of this galactose polymer that is plentiful in apples and citrus fruits. This molecule is the gelling agent in jams and jellies.

topics.description: Highly reactive chemical species containing one or more unpaired electrons, often studied using EPR spectroscopy and involved in homolytic bond cleavage and radical reactions.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: Stable examples of these entities include Fremy's (FREH-mee's) salt and TEMPO. EPR  spectroscopy (spek-TRAH-skuh-pee) can be used to analyze these things, which are used in living  polymerization (puh-LIM-ur-iz-AY-shun) techniques such as RAFT and ARTP. Halogenation (HAA-luh-jin-AY-shun) reactions named for these things occur under light and are driven by the (*) homolytic (HOH-moh-lit-ik) cleavage of covalent bonds. Reactions involving these species use fish hook  arrows to show the movement of individual electrons. For 10 points, name these highly reactive atoms or  molecules with unpaired electrons.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Because the spin of the lone electron in these species cannot be cancelled out, they can be paramagnetic, making it possible to analyze them using EPR spectroscopy. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [M] Name these extremely reactive species whose formation can be described using fish hook arrows. These species are characterized by the presence of at least 1 unpaired electron.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [H] Free radicals are formed as a result of this form of bond cleavage. Bond-dissociation energy corresponds to the amount of energy needed for this form of cleavage to occur.
parts.answer: homolytic cleavage [accept homolytic fission; prompt on radical fission]

parts.label: C
parts.question: [E] Radicals of these elements are often used to functionalize alkanes after light-induced homolytic cleavage. This group of elements with 7 electrons in their valence shell includes bromine, chlorine, and fluorine.

topics.description: Ethanol is a volatile alcohol used in beverages, solvents, fuels, and disinfectants and produced industrially or by yeast fermentation.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: These compounds can be selectively oxidized by either pyridinium chlorochromate or sodium dichromate depending on whether the desired product is an aldehyde or a carboxylic acid. One of these compounds is toxic because a dehydrogenase oxidizes it to produce formic acid instead of the intended product acetaldehyde. It is difficult to purify one of these compounds past 96% because it forms an (*) azeotrope with water during distillation. The primary ingredient in many disinfectants is a type of these compounds named “isopropyl.” For 10 points, name these compounds which contain an -OH group and include methanol and ethanol.
parts.answer: alcohols [accept hydroxyls, accept isopropyl alcohol, prompt on methanol or ethanol by asking “what more general class of compounds is that a part of”]

parts.label: L
parts.question: Inflammation of this organ is called hepatitis. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [E] Name this largest internal organ, which is responsible for detoxifying the human body. This organ can be  damaged in cirrhosis.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [M] This substance may cause cirrhosis of the liver. This substance is produced by yeast in fermentation.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [H] In alcohol dehydrogenase overactivity, acetaldehyde is produced faster than it can be broken down into this  weak acid, with formula CH3COOH.

topics.description: A collection of interconnected web pages and related resources accessed through web browsers on the World Wide Web, typically via URLs.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: Files for these things begin with a DOCTYPE declaration and use angle brackets to denote keywords like “head” and “body.” Cascading Style Sheets are most commonly used to modify the visual elements, like color and font, of these things. The “h-ref” keyword is used to embed (*) hyperlinks in these things, which can be accessed using URLs. For 10 points, name these things that are accessed using browsers like Google Chrome.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Users of this language must start their documents with the <!DOCTYPE> tag. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question:
[H] Name this programming language whose users use “tags” such as “

” and “”. This language is often paired with CSS.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] HTML and CSS are frequently used to design these digital entities, which are accessed via URLs on the World Wide Web.
parts.answer: websites [accept web pages or other clear equivalents]

parts.label: C
parts.question: [M] HTML websites utilize this “protocol” to communicate with servers. This protocol has a four-letter abbreviation that often precedes “www.” in URLs.

topics.description: An interconnected electrical network of components and conductors that provides one or more paths for electric current.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Gustav Kirchhoff names a set of laws that can be used to solve for quantities in DC examples of these systems. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [E] Name these electronic systems which consist of electrical components, such as batteries and resistors, connected by wires.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [H] One of Kirchhoff’s laws states that the current into these parts of the circuit is equal to the current leaving them. It can be used alongside the loop rule to solve complex circuits.
parts.answer: junction [accept node or point; prompt on descriptive answers like intersections]

parts.label: C
parts.question: [M] If a circuit consists only of resistors and a battery, it can be solved by creating an equivalent resistor. Resistances can be added directly if they are in this conformation, which contrasts with parallel.

parts.label: L
parts.question: On a diagram of these systems, a resistor is indicated by a line with jagged waves, and an inductor is indicated with curls in the wire – and certainly, bad handwriting has never cause any issues with that. For ten points each, Give this term for an electrical network in which current can flow in a closed loop.

parts.label: A
parts.question: Give this term for an electrical network in which current can flow in a closed loop.

parts.label: B
parts.question: In a circuit, this device uses semiconducting material to either amplify or switch the signal. These devices allowed for the invention of small, powerful electronic gadgets - the most famous example is probably a handheld radio named for them.

parts.label: C
parts.question: This circuit element is displayed as two parallel lines causing a gap in the wire. The amount of charge that these devices can store is measured in farads.

topics.description: American theoretical physicist Richard Feynman, a principal contributor to quantum electrodynamics and a member of the Rogers Commission investigating the Challenger disaster.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: Management at Morton Thiokol decided not to stop this event, which ultimately prevented a study of Halley’s Comet. Sally Ride served on the Rogers Commission investigating this event, as did (*) Richard Feynman, who used a glass of ice water and a piece of rubber to demonstrate how the O-rings may have failed. Christa McAuliffe, a teacher, was one of the seven casualties of, for ten points, what 1986 disaster that took place 73 seconds after the launch of a Space Shuttle?
parts.answer: Space Shuttle Challenger disaster (accept descriptive answers that name the Challenger, such as “Challenger explosion”; prompt on “Space Shuttle disaster” or similar before “Space Shuttle” is read)

parts.label: L
parts.question: This man’s namesake diagrams can help visualize subatomic interactions. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [M] Name this Caltech professor, who worked on quantum electrodynamics.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] In Feynman diagrams, antiparticles are displayed as moving backwards with respect to this quantity. This quantity is measured in seconds.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [H] Feynman proposed a parton model of these particles, which are composed of two or more quarks. These particles include mesons and baryons.

topics.description: The maximum population size that an environment can sustainably support under particular resource and environmental conditions.

parts.label: L
parts.question: One of the assumptions of the Hardy-Weinberg principle is that this quantity is infinite. For 10  points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [10] Name this quantity, which is the number of individual organisms in a given area.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [10] This type of physical sampling method is used to estimate a population size without having to count  every individual.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [10] The maximum population size for an environment given the resources available is defined by this  quantity, often symbolized K.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: Pierre Verhulst introduced a logistic function to model the growth of this quantity, which Thomas Malthus theorized a geometric increase for. The value of this quantity for an environment is limited by a constant symbolized K, the (*) carrying capacity. Since the Black Death, this quantity for humans has consistently increased. For 10 points, name this quantity stating the number of organisms in a certain area.
parts.answer: population size [accept number of humans or organisms before mentioned]

topics.description: Energy derived from heat within the Earth, including its use for heating and electricity generation.

parts.label: L
parts.question: For a week in 2010, a volcanic eruption on this island disrupted air travel throughout Europe. For ten points each,

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this North Atlantic island, the site of Eyjafjallajokull [AY-yuh–f’YAT-luh–YO-kull] and numerous other volcanoes, geysers, and hot springs.

parts.label: B
parts.question: Almost all of Iceland’s energy production is renewable; it has ample sources of both hydroelectric power and this type of power, generated by its hot springs and geysers.

parts.label: C
parts.question: More than half of Iceland’s population lives in this city, the northernmost world capital.

parts.label: L
parts.question: After this country’s Supreme Court was fired and replaced by the ruling Nuevas Ideas party, the new court ruled that its current president could run for reelection to a second term. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [H] Name this Northern Triangle country, whose president Nayib Bukele has been accused of authoritarianism for actions like sending the military into the parliament building during a vote by legislators.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] In September 2021, El Salvador granted this currency the status of legal tender. This first-ever cryptocurrency, invented by a mysterious “Satoshi Nakomoto,” controversially uses energy-intensive proof-of-work.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [M] El Salvador symbolically mined bitcoin in October 2021 using power generated from a volcano, which is in this category of sustainable energy sources that includes all energy generated from the Earth’s heat.

topics.description: A capacitor is a circuit component that stores separated electric charge and energy in an electric field between conductors, with capacitance measured in farads.

parts.label: L
parts.question: For 10 points each, answer the following about the physics of neurons:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [M] The membrane of a neuron can often be represented as one of these circuit elements, because of its role in the separation of charges. Dielectrics can be used to weaken the electric field within these circuit elements.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] The myelin sheath covering the axon of most neurons is often visualized as a set of these circuit elements connected in series. These circuit elements weaken the flow of current, and their strength is measured in ohms.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [H] Myelination increases the propagation of action potentials by increasing the length constant while keeping this quantity the same. This quantity equals the product of the resistance and capacitance within an RC circuit.

parts.label: L
parts.question: On a diagram of these systems, a resistor is indicated by a line with jagged waves, and an inductor is indicated with curls in the wire – and certainly, bad handwriting has never cause any issues with that. For ten points each, Give this term for an electrical network in which current can flow in a closed loop.

parts.label: A
parts.question: Give this term for an electrical network in which current can flow in a closed loop.

parts.label: B
parts.question: In a circuit, this device uses semiconducting material to either amplify or switch the signal. These devices allowed for the invention of small, powerful electronic gadgets - the most famous example is probably a handheld radio named for them.

parts.label: C
parts.question: This circuit element is displayed as two parallel lines causing a gap in the wire. The amount of charge that these devices can store is measured in farads.

topics.description: The number of cycles or oscillations occurring per unit time, equal to the reciprocal of the period and measured in hertz.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Short bursts of these disturbances are known as “packets” or “trains,” and continuous periodic ones may be sinusoidal when acting like the graph of the sine function. For ten points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [E] Name these oscillations which can be transverse or longitudinal. Surfers usually ride these oscillations in water.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [H] This property, along with wavelength, generally describes a wave’s size. For transverse waves, this property is defined as the wave’s maximum displacement from its equilibrium point.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [M] This property of a wave is the inverse of its period, and describes the number of wavelengths that pass through a certain point over a given period of time. This value is measured in hertz.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: A heterodyne shifts between different ranges of this quantity, whose “cutoff” type marks the boundary between the stopband and passband. For a simple pendulum, this quantity is proportional to the square root of “little g” over (*) length, and it can be calculated as wave speed divided by wavelength. The reciprocal of the period is, for ten points, which quantity measured in hertz, the number of waves that pass a fixed point per unit of time?

topics.description: The energy an object possesses because of its motion, including translational and rotational forms, with translational kinetic energy given by one-half mass times velocity squared.

parts.label: L
parts.question: For a point mass, this value equals the mass multiplied by the square of distance to the axis. For 10  points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [10] Name this quantity that is the rotational analogue of mass.
parts.answer: ANSWER: moment of inertia [or rotational inertia; do not accept or prompt on “inertia”]

parts.label: B
parts.question: [10] For a rigid body with a known moment of inertia about an axis, the body's moment of inertia about  a translated axis can be calculated using this equation, also known as the Huygens (HOW-hunz)-Steiner  theorem.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [10] The moment of inertia and angular velocity are used to calculate the rotational analogue of this  quantity. This quantity is one of two added together to calculate the Hamiltonian.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: This quantity is equal to the square of momentum divided by double the mass. In addition to momentum, elastic collisions conserve this quantity. When an object falls, (*) potential energy is converted into this kind of energy. One-half mass times velocity squared is equal to, for ten points, what type of energy associated with an object's movement?

topics.description: The bending and spreading of waves around obstacles or through openings, including applications such as X-ray crystallography and electron diffraction.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Fusing two of this molecule together forms naphthalene, and adding a methyl group to this molecule yields toluene. For ten points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [H] Name this simplest aromatic hydrocarbon, whose structure was discovered by August Kekule (KEK-oo-lay) after supposedly having a vision of a snake eating its own tail. This molecule’s formula is C6H6.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [M] Benzene’s cyclic nature was confirmed by Kathleen Lonsdale, who used x-rays undergoing this process to do so. This process causes waves to bend around an encountered obstacle.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [E] In the Birch reduction of benzene, one of these structures is reduced. Benzene’s structure consists of single bonds alternating with these bonds, represented by two lines on a Lewis diagram.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: The most common application of Huygens principle is used to model this phenomenon. The equation “2d sine theta equals n times lambda” describes this phenomenon. Electrons underwent this phenomenon on a silver lattice in the Davidson-Germer experiment. This phenomenon is described by (*) Bragg’s law. A series of thin slits make up this phenomenon’s namesake grating. For 10 points, name this phenomenon, where light bends around an obstacle.

topics.description: A covalent bond in which electrons are shared unequally between bonded atoms because of a difference in electronegativity.

parts.label: L
parts.question: In the metallic form of these interactions, atoms experience attractive forces due to a cloud of free, delocalized electrons. For ten points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name these interactions which are used to join two atoms. When one of them occurs between a metal and a nonmetal, they can involve transfer of electrons in the “ionic” type.
parts.answer: bonds or bonding [accept ionic bonds or metallic bonds]

parts.label: B
parts.question: In covalent bonds, electrons are shared between the atoms, but when there is a large difference in electronegativity the bond can have this property. The covalent bonds found in water have this property.
parts.answer: polar bonds [accept polarity or strongly polar]

parts.label: C
parts.question: While covalent bonds occur between individual atoms, these interactions occur between larger molecules and are determined largely by the polarity and location of electrons around the molecules involved. These interactions include both induced dipole and hydrogen bonding interactions.
parts.answer: intermolecular forces or attractions [accept van der Waals forces or IMF’s]

parts.label: L
parts.question: The Allred-Rochow (ROH-choh) scale calculates this value using effective nuclear charge and  covalent radius. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this property that describes an atom's ability to attract electrons.

parts.label: B
parts.question: Large differences in electronegativity between two bonded atoms can result in this type of covalent  bond. This type of covalent bond occurs when electrons are shared unequally between atoms.

parts.label: C
parts.question: Fluorine has a value of 4 on the most commonly used scale for electronegativity, which is named  after this American scientist who proposed taking megadoses of Vitamin C to treat the common cold.

topics.description: A Dutch microscopist who pioneered the observation of microorganisms and cellular structures and helped establish microscopy as a biological research tool.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: Extremely powerful examples of these devices use a beam of electrons rather than light because of their lower wavelength. Specimens can be mounted on transparent glass (*) slides to be viewed using these devices. Antonie van Leeuwenhoek (lay-when-huuk) discovered cell structures and microorganisms using, for 10 points, what devices used to look at very small objects?
parts.answer: microscopes [or optical microscopes, or electron microscopes]

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: Sputter coating is used to apply a thin layer of a conducting material for samples used in one form of this  technique. This technique comes in transmission and scanning types, both of which utilize a beam of high-speed electrons. This technique was popularized by Antonie van (*) Leeuwenhoek and Robert Hooke, who used  it to discover the cell. For 10 points, name this technique, which uses optical and electron devices to magnify small  things.
parts.answer: microscopy [accept word forms; accept more specific answers, like electron microscopy]

topics.description: A phosphorus-and-oxygen functional group that can be attached to molecules during phosphorylation and forms part of structures such as prodrugs and the DNA backbone.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Pfizer’s [FAI-zur’s] drug Lufotrelvir [loo-FAH-trel-veer] is an antiviral designed to treat COVID-19 by inhibiting one of these enzymes. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [H] Name these enzymes with a “serine” subtype that break down proteins by catalyzing the hydrolysis [high-DRAH-luh-siss] of peptide bonds.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [M] Because it is a prodrug, Lufotrelvir contains one of these functional groups that is removed to form its active state. This functional group symbolized P-sub-i is attached to one molecule by a rotor-shaped synthase [SIN-thayss].
parts.answer: phosphate [FOSS-fate] group [or PO4 3- ] (ATP synthase adds a phosphate to ADP.)

parts.label: C
parts.question: [E] Unlike other Covid drugs, Lufotrelvir must be administered through an IV [I-V] rather than by this method commonly achieved with a pill. A description is acceptable.
parts.answer: oral ingestion [or swallowing; accept any underlined portion or equivalents thereof]

parts.label: L
parts.question: Oseltamivir prevents the cleavage of sialic acid, thus preventing this virus from traveling from cell to cell. For 10 point each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [E] Name this common virus. The H1N1 strain of this virus is known as its “swine” type.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [H] Oseltamivir is ingested in a prodrug containing one of these functional groups. The backbone of DNA is made up of sugar and this functional group.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [M] The starting material of the Hoffman–LaRoche synthesis of Tamiflu, shikimate, names a pathway for the synthesis of aromatic forms of these compounds. These compounds are the building blocks of proteins.

topics.description: The separation between an astronomical object and an observer or between astronomical objects, commonly expressed in parsecs or light-years and estimated using methods such as parallax, standard candles, or redshift.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: This quantity can be computed by taking the reciprocal of the apparent movement of an object in arcseconds. Recessional velocity is proportional to this quantity, according to Hubble’s law. This quantity can be measured by observing the (*) parallax of an object. The force between two astronomical bodies is proportional to the inverse square of this quantity. For 10 points, name this quantity, which is measured in parsecs or kilometers.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Stars at the tip of the red giant branch can serve as “standard candles” when calculating this quantity. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [E] Name this quantity that may be expressed in light-years or parsecs.
parts.answer: distance [accept answers indicating how far an object is from Earth]

parts.label: B
parts.question: [M] The tip of the red giant branch is a feature on this diagram, which plots the luminosity of stars against their temperature. A diagonal line across this diagram represents the “main sequence.”

parts.label: C
parts.question: [H] When stars leave the tip of the red giant branch, they experience a “flash” named after this element, in which it is rapidly fused into carbon.

topics.description: Soil is a mixture of mineral particles, organic matter, water, air, and organisms that forms the upper layer of the ground and supports plant growth.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Humus [HYOO-muss], a dark organic matter made of the decomposed remains of dead plants and animals, forms much of the top layer of this substance. For ten points each,

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this substance made of organic matter and sand, silt, or clay, in which plants can grow.
parts.answer: soil (accept topsoil; accept dirt; accept earth)

parts.label: B
parts.question: By one estimate, each gram of soil contains one million organisms from this kingdom, which does much of the work of decomposition. This kingdom includes mold and yeast.

parts.label: C
parts.question: In the tundra and taiga biomes, the most abundant animal life in the soil is worms from this phylum that includes the model organism C. elegans.

parts.label: L
parts.question: This substance’s pH is affected by its CEC, or cation-exchange capacity. For ten points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [E] Name this substance that has different textures based on how much sand, silt and clay it is composed of. This mixture of organic matter and disintegrated rock is often placed in pots to grow plants in.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [H] This fertile layer of soil, referred to as the A horizon, contains large amounts of decomposed organic matter called humus. Unless there is organic matter like plants or grass, this layer is the uppermost layer of soil.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [M] Secondary structures made of this type of rock can form through pedogenesis, the formation of soil. This type of rock is formed from accumulation of small particles.

topics.description: A Gram-negative, rod-shaped bacterium widely used in genetic research, biotechnology, and industrial protein production, with pathogenic strains that can cause foodborne illness and urinary tract infections.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: TOP10 and DH10B are strains of this organism that are utilized in cloning experiments. The  O157:H7 strain of this organism produces Shiga toxin and can cause hemolytic uremic (HEE-mohlit-ik yoo-REE-mik) syndrome. The majority of urinary tract infections are due to a (*) pathogenic  strain of this organism. This non-viral organism was used to study semi-conservative DNA replication  by Meselson (MEE-zul-sun) and Stahl. The lac operon (LAK AH-puh-ron) was first characterized in this  organism. For 10 points, name this Gram-negative, rod-shaped bacterium that can cause food poisoning.

parts.label: L
parts.question: A protein isolated from this genus called Protein A is valued in biochemistry for its ability to bind to antibodies in techniques like affinity chromatography. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [H] Name this genus of Gram-positive bacteria whose species can be differentiated depending on whether or not they produce clumping factor in the coagulase test.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] Industrial protein production often defaults to using this well-studied species of bacteria. This rod shaped model organism and frequent cause of food poisoning was used in the Hershey-Chase and Meselson-Stahl experiments.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [M] Another bacterially derived and useful protein is Cas9, which was isolated from S. pyogenes for use in this gene editing pathway. Charpentier and Doudna won the Nobel in Chemistry in 2020 for developing this procedure.
parts.answer: CRISPR/Cas9 gene-editing [or clustered regularly interspaced short palindromic repeats]

topics.description: Solid materials whose constituent atoms, ions, or molecules are arranged in a repeating, highly ordered lattice.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Answer the following about birthstones, for 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [E] This gemstone is the birthstone for the month of May. This variant of the mineral beryl is green.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [M] Because the October birthstone, opal, is amorphous [ay-MOR-fuss], it is not one of these materials and is thus considered a mineraloid rather than a mineral. Types of these materials include isometric and monoclinic.
parts.answer: crystals [or crystalline solids; accept periodic materials]

parts.label: C
parts.question: [H] Ruby, the birthstone for July, gets its characteristic red color from the presence of this element. The trioxide of this element is typically purple, but turns orange when wet.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: Vacancies in the F-centers of these materials can be described using Kröger–Vink notation and can create diversity in the color of these materials. The strength of these materials is dependent on the degree of misorientation in boundaries between microscopic examples of them called grains. The (*) cubic system of describing these materials classifies them as primitive, body-centered, or face-centered depending on their unit cells. These materials are contrasted with amorphous materials like glass, which are not ordered. For 10 points, name these solids whose molecules are arranged in a highly ordered lattice.
parts.answer: crystals [or crystalline materials, prompt on lattices before mention]

topics.description: A quantum-mechanical principle stating that identical fermions cannot occupy the same quantum state, thereby restricting electron occupancy of atomic orbitals.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: The three g-factors of the electron are the factor accounting for this property, the orbital g- factor, and the Landé (LAHN-day) g-factor. The hypothesized graviton would have a value of two  for this property. Opposite half-integer values for this property must be assigned to two electrons  in an orbital according to an (*) exclusion principle named for Pauli. The Stern-Gerlach experiment  used a beam of silver atoms to show that electrons have this property. For 10 points, name this form of  intrinsic angular momentum possessed by quantum particles.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: Some of these structures are non-degenerate by the presence of ligands in crystal field theory, which models their “splitting.” When these structures combine in molecules, the gap between two of them known as the HOMO and LUMO indicate the molecule’s stability. To explain the Lewis structure of methane, Linus Pauling proposed that these structures can undergo (*) hybridization. At most two particles with opposite spins can occupy these structures according to the Pauli exclusion principle. The letters s, p, d, and f each label a differently shaped type of, for 10 points, what regions in which electrons are most likely to be found?
parts.answer: (atomic) orbitals [accept subtypes such as d orbitals; accept molecular orbitals]

topics.description: Algorithms and computational procedures for locating a desired item, value, or solution within a collection or search space, including linear and binary search.

parts.label: L
parts.question: The node values in the left subtree of a tree used in an algorithm for this task are less than the root’s value. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this general task in computer science, which can be naively implemented by sequentially checking list elements starting from the beginning.

parts.label: B
parts.question: A search algorithm named for this word repeatedly divides subarrays in half to find a value in a sorted list. This word also refers to the base-2 number system of ones and zeroes that underpins digital computing.

parts.label: C
parts.question: The worst case space complexity of a search algorithm can be expressed with this common notation, which is also used to note the worst case runtime of an algorithm.

parts.label: L
parts.question: A* [A-star] algorithms are often used to perform this task in video games. For 10 points each,

parts.label: A
parts.question: [M] Name this task that is accomplished by Dijkstra’s [DIKE-struh’s] algorithm. The traveling salesman problem is a variation of this task.
parts.answer: pathfinding [accept equivalents like finding the shortest path]

parts.label: B
parts.question: [H] Pathfinding algorithms must be performed on these kinds of graphs, in which each edge of the graph has an associated numerical value.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [E] Pathfinding algorithms are classified as this general type of algorithm, whose types include binary and linear. Namesake “engines” use these algorithms to return results from the internet.

topics.description: The field of computer science devoted to creating systems that perform tasks associated with human intelligence, including learning, reasoning, perception, and language generation.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: Some forms of this technology use a combination of nodes and feedback algorithms known as a neural network. Processes for developing this concept include “deep learning” and “machine learning”. A model that employs this technology to produce text is known as (*) GPT-4. Tesla is attempting to use this technology to develop self-driving cars, and it is exemplified by IBM’s Watson. For 10 points, name this technology that attempts to imitate human thinking.

parts.label: L
parts.question: The results of this task can be classified by the definiteness of the Hessian matrix. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [M] Name this task, which can be performed in single-variable calculus by setting the derivative of a function to 0 to search for critical points. In multivariable calculus, this task can be performed by examining the gradient.
parts.answer: optimization [or finding minima OR maxima; accept any adjectives like local or global in front of minima OR maxima; accept finding extrema]

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] Gradient descent is a common algorithm for optimization in this field. Computer models in this field are often trained by minimizing a loss function, leading to better accuracy in tasks like imitating human behavior.
parts.answer: artificial intelligence [or AI; or machine learning; or ML; accept neural networks]

parts.label: C
parts.question: [H] A tricky situation in gradient descent is getting trapped in one of these points that have zero gradient but are not local minima, as they are concave up in some directions and concave down in others, forming a namesake shape.

topics.description: Graphene is a one-atom-thick, two-dimensional allotrope of carbon whose atoms form a hexagonal honeycomb lattice.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: This allotrope can be magnetized by contact with smoothed YIG. A “flying carpet” made of this  allotrope can be used to deliver TRAIL and DOX in cancer treatment. Andre Geim (heym) discovered this allotrope using scotch tape and mechanical exfoliation. This extremely conductive  allotrope is a lattice arranged in a (*) hexagonal shape and is another form of the same substance that  comprises buckyballs and diamonds. For 10 points, name this two-dimensional form of carbon whose  stacked layers are known as its “-ite” form and are used in pencils.
parts.answer: graphene [prompt on graphite; prompt on carbon until it is read]

parts.label: L
parts.question: For 10 points each, answer some things about MIT nanotechnologist Millie Dresselhaus [DRESS-uhl-house]:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [E] Dresselhaus was known as the “queen” of this nonmetallic element due to her extensive work on its allotropes [AL-uh-trohps], such as nanotubes and graphite.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [H] Dresselhaus pioneered the study of carbon allotropes using Raman [RAH-mun] spectroscopy, which measures this kind of molecular motion that comes in six distinct “modes.”
parts.answer: molecular vibrations [or vibrational motion or vibrating; accept vibrational modes]

parts.label: C
parts.question: [M] Dresselhaus also studied this semiconducting carbon allotrope that consists of a single flat honeycombed sheet.

topics.description: The series of 15 chemical elements from lanthanum through lutetium, associated with progressive filling of the 4f electron shell and commonly displayed in the f-block of the periodic table.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Dmitri Mendeleev is credited with creating the first version of these things. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [E] Name this display that sorts elements based on their atomic numbers, organized into groups and periods.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [H] Along with the actinides, this series of fifteen elements is usually displayed below the other elements in the periodic table. They feature elements 57–71, and all but one of them progressively fill the 4f shell.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [M] Lanthanides and actinides are also part of this group of metals, which includes those with partially filled d-shells. Most of these metals have multiple oxidation states.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Dmitri Mendeleev (men-duh-lay-ev) claimed to have developed this construct based on a vision he had in a dream. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this construct which organizes the building blocks of chemistry into rows and columns based on atomic weight and electron configuration. It currently has seven full rows comprising 118 entries.

parts.label: B
parts.question: These elements make up most of the center and left of the periodic table. They are typically grey in color, conduct electricity, and can be combined to form alloys. Examples include titanium and cobalt.

parts.label: C
parts.question: These two sections of the periodic table are not classified into any of the 18 columns; instead they are typically offset into two separate rows under the rest of the table. Name either.

topics.description: The process by which a newly synthesized polypeptide chain assumes its functional three-dimensional structure.

parts.label: L
parts.question: The Rosetta@home project aims to improve prediction of this process in part by analyzing user inputs to a video game that challenges users to simulate it as accurately as possible. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [H] Name this process which would take an impossibly long amount of time to do by chance according to Levinthal’s paradox.
parts.answer: protein folding [accept word forms] (The name of the game mentioned in the leadin is called Foldit.)

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] The deep learning algorithm AlphaFold predicts protein structure based only on the order of these subunits, which make up a protein's primary structure. In proteins, these compounds are connected by peptide bonds.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [M] Mutations in the PrP gene can cause the formation of these agents made of misfolded proteins that in turn cause other, normal proteins to take on their shape. Scrapie, kuru, and mad cow disease are all caused by these agents.

parts.label: L
parts.question: A distributed computing project called "[this process] @home" attempts to study how this process occurs. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [10] Name this process that forms the three-dimensional structure of macromolecules such as insulin and hemoglobin. In it, long chains of peptides are assembled into complex shapes.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [10] Protein folding begins with this level of protein structure which refers to its sequence of amino acids. This level precedes the secondary and tertiary structures.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [10] Mistakes in protein folding can lead to the formation of these misfolded proteins, which can cause neurodegenerative diseases such as mad cow disease or Creutzfeldt-Jakob (CROYTS-felt YAH-kub) syndrome.

topics.description: A watercraft designed for sustained operation underwater, using propulsion and ballast systems and often equipped with a periscope.

parts.label: L
parts.question: This explorer led the team that discovered wreckage from John F. Kennedy's PT-109. For 10 points  each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [10] Name this oceanographer who also discovered the wrecks of the Bismarck and Titanic.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [10] Ballard discovered the wrecked Titanic on a mission to find the Scorpion and Thresher, which were  nuclear-powered examples of these vehicles.
parts.answer: ANSWER: submarines [or subs; prompt on boats]

parts.label: C
parts.question: [10] Ballard also discovered the USS Yorktown and Hammann, which were sunk in this battle. The USS  Ballard rescued 35 sailors from the Hiryu (HEER-yoo), which sank in this battle.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: Horace Hunley developed one of these vehicles for the Confederacy, but it went down three times, the second of which killed Hunley himself. A Soviet one of these vehicles, K-129, was salvaged by the CIA after it sank. In 1915, the RMS (*) Lusitania was sunk by one of these vehicles, which the Germans called U-boats. Periscopes are used by, for 10 points, what naval vessels which can travel underwater?
parts.answer: submarines [accept U-boats until mentioned; prompt on subs; prompt on boats or watercraft; do NOT accept or prompt on "submersibles", "ships", or "warships"]

topics.description: An electronic semiconductor component that permits electric current to flow primarily in one direction.

parts.label: L
parts.question: These devices are often crystals of semiconducting material with a p-n junction. For ten points each,

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name these circuit elements that allow current to flow in just one direction.

parts.label: B
parts.question: For current to flow in one direction in a hypothetically ideal diode, this quantity for the circuit is zero in one direction and infinity in the other. This quantity is measured in ohms.

parts.label: C
parts.question: Light-emitting diodes can display different colors based on changes in the size of this region that separate occupied and empty energy levels. Semiconductors have small examples of this region, and doping can make them even smaller.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Systems with this property, like the logistic map, may undergo a period-doubling bifurcation where new trajectories emerge from existing ones at increasingly fast rates. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [M] Name this property which occurs when a deterministic system is extremely sensitive to its initial conditions, so its behavior cannot be predicted.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [H] An example of chaos in physics is one of these systems named for Chua which uses a nonlinear component to initiate period doubling. Norton and Thevenin’s theorems both describe these systems.
parts.answer: circuits [accept electronic oscillators; prompt on oscillators]

parts.label: C
parts.question: [E] Chua’s circuit contains a nonlinear, negative resistor that acts as one of these components. These circuit components allow current to flow in only one direction and have a “light-emitting” type abbreviated LED.
parts.answer: diodes [accept light emitting diodes or LEDs; accept Chua’s diode]

topics.description: The exact number of specified elementary entities per mole, defined as 6.02214076 × 10²³ mol⁻¹.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: Dividing the ideal gas constant by this quantity results in Boltzmann’s constant. This quantity which is defined as the number of atoms in twelve grams of carbon-12 is equal to the number of particles in (*) 22.4 liters of gas at standard temperature and pressure. For 10 points, name this constant which is the number of particles in a mole, approximately equal to 6.02 times 10 to the 23rd power.
parts.answer: Avogadro’s number [accept Avogadro’s constant; prompt on variable]

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: This quantity times elementary charge gives Faraday’s constant. This quantity equals the universal gas constant, divided by Boltzmann’s constant. This quantity multiplies atomic mass units to yield molar mass, since this is the number of atoms in 12 grams of (*) carbon-12. This quantity is defined as 6.022 times 10-to-the-23rd. For 10 points, identify this constant, which is equal to the number of molecules in one mole.

topics.description: A measure of the amount of a substance in a specified quantity of solution or mixture, which may be expressed in forms such as molarity or molality.

parts.label: L
parts.question: The kinetic isotope effect describes how this value for a reaction will change based on which isotopes of the atoms involved are being used. For 10 point each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [M] Name this proportionality constant. The half life of substances undergoing radioactive decay equals the natural log of 2, divided by this quantity.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [H] This approximation is commonly used to derive a rate equation for a reaction whose first step occurs much faster than its second step. This approximation assumes the rate of production and rate of consumption of an intermediate are equal.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [E] Steady-state approximations allow chemists to assume this quantity is constant for an intermediate. The reaction rate of first order reactions depends on the rate constant and this quantity, forms of which include molarity and molality.

parts.label: L
parts.question: To conduct current, a galvanic cell or battery must possess both an anode and this electrode. For ten points each,

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this positive electrode where the reduction reaction occurs. This electrode is made of copper in a zinc-copper cell.

parts.label: B
parts.question: The Nernst equation can determine the voltage of a zinc-copper cell if these quantities are known for the two ions. This quantity is usually expressed in molarity or moles per liter.

parts.label: C
parts.question: To allow flow of ions between the two electrodes, a porous cup or one of these devices may be used. A typical one of these devices is a U-shaped glass tube filled with an electrolyte solution.

topics.description: The seventh planet from the Sun, an ice giant with a pronounced axial tilt, methane-rich atmosphere, rings, and numerous moons.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: Uranus has this many outer rings. A spacecraft with this number in its name is the only one ever to visit Uranus and Neptune; that spacecraft was the last of this many (*) Voyager probes to have been launched. Mars is orbited by this many moons, and there are this many planets closer to the Sun than Earth. For 10 points, how many stars are in a binary system?

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: In 2017 a laser was used to mimic the compression of methane into diamond on these two bodies. Alexis Bouvard [boo-var] discovered that one of these two bodies had orbital perturbations caused by the other, whose position was then calculated by Urbain Le Verrier [ur-bain luh vair-yay]. Absorption of long-wavelength light by methane gas in these two bodies’ (*) atmospheres gives them their distinct color. These two planets were visited by Voyager 2, but not Voyager 1. The largest moons of these two planets are Titania and Triton. These are the seventh and eighth-farthest planets from the Sun. For 10 points, name these two “ice giants.”
parts.answer: Uranus and Neptune [accept in either order] (Diamonds are thought to fall as “rain” on these planets.)

topics.description: An aircraft operated without an onboard human pilot, either remotely controlled or capable of autonomous flight.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: On July 11, 2022, Iran announced that it will supply these devices to Russia, which is using the “Aeroscope” platform to identify communication links between these devices and their users. DJI makes commercial examples of these devices, which has been used to (*) surevil enemy positions and collect footage from safe positions by both sides of the Ukrainian conflict. Pilots remotely control, for 10 points, what unmanned aircraft?

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: This term is used for a pipe in a bagpipes whose note does not change as the pipes are played. Bees described by this word are haploid, do not have stingers, and are the only male bees. In April 2019, London Gatwick Airport was (*) shut down by one of these objects flying around it. The U.S. military has conducted "strikes" using, for 10 points, what unmanned flying vehicles?

topics.description: An ordinal scale from 1 to 10 ranking minerals by their resistance to scratching, from talc to diamond.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Despite its lack of precision, this scale is often used among geologists. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this scale used to measure the hardness of various minerals. It works on a scale of 1 to 10, with 1, the softest on the scale, being talc.

parts.label: B
parts.question: At 9 on the Mohs scale is this mineral, a crystalline form of aluminum oxide. Ruby and sapphire are varieties of this mineral.

parts.label: C
parts.question: This mineral is found at 10 on the hardness scale. Made of pure carbon, its hardness means it is often used in heavy-duty drills and other machinery.

parts.label: L
parts.question: This scale is an ordinal, not nominal, scale because its values of 1 through 10 mean essentially nothing beyond their ordered ranking. For ten points each,

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this scale that uses quartz and topaz as the references for its values of 6 and 7.
parts.answer: Mohs scale of mineral hardness (prompt on “hardness (scale)”)

parts.label: B
parts.question: The highest value on the Mohs scale, 10, is given to this valuable gemstone. This allotrope of carbon was the hardest natural material at the time of the scale’s creation.

parts.label: C
parts.question: Soapstone is made out of this easily-powdered mineral, the softest on the Mohs scale.

topics.description: A vaccine technology that delivers messenger RNA encoding an antigen so host cells produce the antigen and stimulate an adaptive immune response.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: In 2021, Glaxo-Smith-Kline released RTS,S [R-T-S-S], the first of these drugs to target malaria. Gardasil is the brand name of one of these drugs. German company BioNTech developed a way to formulate these drugs as nanoparticles that encapsulate an mRNA, rather than injecting inactivated or dead viruses. For ten points, name these drugs that are designed to provide immunity against infection, like ones produced by Pfizer and Moderna to prevent COVID-19.
parts.answer: vaccine (accept specific types of vaccines, such as mRNA vaccines, HPV vaccines, COVID vaccines, etc.)

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: These things’ effects can be enhanced through addition of compounds like the soap bark extract QS-21 or various aluminum salts. The heterologous BCG type of these things is derived from the cow-infecting Mycobacteria bovus. Dendritic cells translate globules of synthetic mRNA in vivo in a (*) recently developed form of these things, whose efficacy can be increased by adjuvants. By introducing antigens in a controlled manner, these things can generate immunity against new pathogens. For 10 points, name these medications, examples of which were produced by Pfizer and Moderna in response to COVID-19.
parts.answer: vaccines [accept mRNA vaccines or COVID-19 vaccines; prompt on antigens until mention]

topics.description: A glacier is a large, persistent body of moving land ice that forms and reshapes terrain through erosion, deposition, melting, and calving.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Alternating light and dark bands on these objects are called ogives. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: Identify these large structures which often form in polar regions and high mountain ranges. Their movement can leave moraines, eskers, and other geological formations.

parts.label: B
parts.question: Glaciers are primarily comprised of this substance. Climate change has caused some glaciers to shrink in size as this substance melts into water and flows away.

parts.label: C
parts.question: These large boulders are a common feature of the landscape in regions historically covered by glaciers. They can weigh hundreds of tons, and are deposited by retreating glaciers which picked them up during their advance.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: One feature created by these entities have “lateral” and “terminal” types. The Matterhorn was formed by the diverging erosion of these entities. These entities create U-shaped valleys and cirques and leave behind their namesake till in moraines.(*) The calving of one material forming these features creates icebergs. For 10 points, name these large bodies of moving ice.

topics.description: The H₃O⁺ ion formed when a proton associates with a water molecule, representing the strongest acid species that can persist in aqueous solution.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: These particles theoretically decay into a neutral pion (PIE-on) and a positron and are the heaviest product of beta-minus decay. This particle added to a water molecule forms the hydronium ion. The letter Z symbolizes the number of these particles in an element, known as the (*) atomic number. For ten points, name these subatomic particles which share the nucleus with neutrons and which are positively charged.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Color changes in indicators like phenolphthalein can be used to determine the concentration of an analyte in this technique. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [E] Name this analytical technique used in acid-base chemistry experiments. “Curves” produced by this technique graph pH against the volume of liquid dispensed from a burette.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [M] During titration, pH can be calculated by finding the negative log of the concentration of either H+ or this ion. No molecule can create a stronger acid in water than this ion, according to the leveling effect.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [H] The equilibrium constant for an acid-base reaction equals 10 to the power of the difference in this quantity between the conjugate acid and the acid. Finding the inflection point of a titration curve requires finding the concentration where pH equals this value.
parts.answer: pKa [or pK-sub-a; accept power of the acid dissociation constant, do not accept or prompt on “Ka” or “acid dissociation constant”]

topics.description: The chemical element lithium, the lightest alkali metal with atomic number 3, widely used in batteries.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Hard soft acid-base theory can predict the behaviors of different reactions. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [H] Due to its softness, sodium can be combusted in excess oxygen to form a salt of this polyatomic anion [AN-eye-on]. Adding two hydrogen atoms to this ion gives a compound that is degraded by catalase [CAT-uh-layss].
parts.answer: peroxide [per-OX-eyed] ion [or O2 – ; accept hydrogen peroxide; reject “superoxide (ion)”]

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] In contrast, this other metal has hard ions that form simple oxides when combusted. Ions of this alkali [AL-kuh-lie] metal are found in cell phone batteries.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [M] Lithium ions are harder than sodium ions as they form these entities less readily. London dispersion forces are caused by temporary examples of these things, which consist of a positive charge connected to a negative charge.

parts.label: L
parts.question: In the mnemonic OIL RIG, OIL represents this reaction. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [10] Name this type of reaction, one of the half reactions of redox reactions, along with reduction. In this reaction, electrons are lost, while in reduction, electrons are gained.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [10] In one of these objects, redox reactions occur in the cathode and the anode, converting chemical energy to electrical energy. Examples of these include the 9 volt, AA, and AAA varieties.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [10] Many commercial batteries use this metallic element with atomic number 3 as an anode.

topics.description: Glucose is a six-carbon monosaccharide and major biological energy source whose blood concentration is regulated by insulin and whose polymers include glycogen, cellulose, and starch.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: The three-month average of the concentration of this molecule is proxy-measured via the hemoglobin A1c test. The beta cells in the Islets of Langerhans become more active when levels of this molecule increase. An increase in the levels of this molecule stimulates the production of insulin. This substance is deficient in hypoglycemia. This molecule has formula C6H12O6, and is more abundant in individuals with diabetes. For 10 points, name this sweet molecule.
parts.answer: glucose [accept sugar; accept blood glucose level; accept blood sugar level]

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: A process synthesizing this compound uses PEP carboxykinase [pehp car-BOX-ee-KAI-nayss] in its rate-controlling step. Two subunits of this compound comprise a molecule named after germinating seeds, or malt. This compound is first acted upon by hexokinase [HEX-oh-KAI-nayss] during its breakdown within the (*) cytosol [SIGH-tuh-sawl]. The human body polymerizes this compound into glycogen [GLY-kuh-jen], while plants polymerize this compound into cellulose and starch. High blood levels of this compound are caused by impaired insulin signaling in diabetes. For 10 points, name this six-carbon sugar produced by photosynthesis.
parts.answer: glucose [accept D-glucose or dextrose or D-glucopyranose; prompt on C6H12O6]

topics.description: A quantum-mechanical principle stating that certain complementary properties, such as a particle's position and momentum, cannot both be known or measured with arbitrary precision.

parts.label: L
parts.question: This scientist’s namesake thought experiment demonstrates the idea of superposition. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [E] Name this man who names a thought experiment involving a hypothetical cat which may be simultaneously considered dead and alive.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [H] Schrödinger proposed his thought experiment to illustrate his problems with this interpretation of quantum mechanics. It is named after a European city.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [M] In 1927, a proponent of the Copenhagen interpretation introduced this principle, which limits the accuracy at which complementary variables can be measured, such as position and momentum.

parts.label: L
parts.question: If you go to the moon, your weight changes, but this quantity does not. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [10] Name this quantity measured in kilograms. Weight equals this quantity multiplied by gravitational acceleration.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [10] This vector quantity is equivalent to mass multiplied by velocity, and impulse measures the change of this quantity.
parts.answer: linear momentum [do NOT accept or prompt on "angular momentum"]

parts.label: C
parts.question: [10] This principle named for a German scientist posits that more knowledge about a particle's position means less knowledge about its momentum and vice versa.

topics.description: A fundamental interaction mediated by W and Z bosons that governs processes such as beta decay and is unified with electromagnetism in electroweak theory.

parts.label: L
parts.question: The prediction of W and Z bosons in the 1960s was a major breakthrough on the path to a “Theory of Everything.” Answer these questions about unified field theory, for ten points each.

parts.label: A
parts.question: W and Z particles mediate this fundamental force responsible for beta decay. The physicists Glashow, Weinberg, and Salam successfully unified this force with electromagnetism.

parts.label: B
parts.question: Most attempts at a unified theory fail because of this force, which Newton used to explain the motion of planets around the Sun. In relativity, this force is a distortion in spacetime around an object.

parts.label: C
