parts.question: The observed decay of these positively-charged particles would be good evidence for several unified theories, but experiments suggest it may take 1035 years [ten to the thirty-fifth years] to occur.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Lee and Yang earned the Nobel Prize in 1957 after their prediction that this force violates the conservation of parity was experimentally confirmed. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [M] Name this third-strongest of the fundamental forces. The unification of this force with electromagnetism was confirmed by the discovery of W and Z bosons.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [H] This scientist proved that the weak force violates the conservation of parity in an experiment she conducted in 1956, for which she was awarded the inaugural Wolf prize.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [E] The Wu experiment was carried out by observing the beta type of this process for a neutron in a cobalt-60 atom. This process, which is when a nucleus loses energy via radiation, has a half-life of 5,730 years for carbon-14.
parts.answer: radioactive decay [or radioactivity; accept beta decay]

topics.description: Explosive or effusive releases of magma, ash, lava, and volcanic gases from a volcano, including eruptions that can alter climate and contribute to societal disruption or mass extinctions.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: Roger Verbeek investigated one of these events that triggered the nativist Banten Peasants Revolt. David Keys argued that the Medieval era began when one of these events in 536 precipitated the collapse of societies like pre-Islamic Arabia. One of these events at Huaynaputina caused famines that precipitated Russia’s Time of Troubles. Edvard Munch’s The Scream documents how Norwegian (*) skies turned red from the jet stream after one of these events in 1883. 1815 was the “Year Without a Summer” because one of these events in Indonesia coated the world in ash. For 10 points, name these disasters caused by Mount Tambora and Krakatoa.
parts.answer: volcanic eruptions [accept word forms such as a volcano erupting; accept volcanic events; accept volcanic winter; prompt on ice ages with “What caused it?” ]

parts.label: L
parts.question: For 10 points each, answer the following about a several-million-year-long period of heavy rain called the Carnian pluvial event, or CPE:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [E] The CPE took place during this geologic period. The shift to a warmer, wetter climate helped the dinosaurs gain dominance during this period of the Mesozoic Era that occurred before the Jurassic.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [M] The climate change that caused the CPE may be linked to a series of these events in Wrangellia. An earlier series of these events created the Siberian Traps and likely caused the Permian-Triassic extinction.
parts.answer: volcanic eruptions [or equivalents that mention volcanoes; accept lava flows or flood basalts]

parts.label: C
parts.question: [H] The CPE devastated this group of now-extinct mollusks. Like nautiluses, these cephalopods (“SEH-fuh-loh-pods”) had spiral-shaped external shells that are common in the Mesozoic fossil record.

topics.description: Individual mineralized skeletal structures such as the femur and tibia that provide support, protect organs, house marrow, and participate in mineral storage.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: Secretion of parathyroid hormone decreases the density and strength of these structures, which contain Haversian (ha-VER-zee-en) canals. Vitamin D is often used to treat diseases in which these structures are weak. In addition to aiding in formation and repair of these structures, (*) osteoblasts and osteoclasts balance levels of calcium in these structures. For ten points, name these structures like the femur and tibia that make up the skeletal system.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: These structures primarily consist of mineralized collagen, and the ears contain three of these objects to conduct sound. New blood cells are produced inside these structures. These structures are weakened in (*) osteoporosis, and their interior contains marrow. The femur is the largest of, for 10 points, what hard objects which make up the skeleton?

topics.description: Enrico Fermi was an Italian-American physicist who made major contributions to quantum and nuclear physics and helped create the first controlled nuclear reactor.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Gell-Mann and Zweig proposed the existence of these particles, which Gell-Mann named after a line from James Joyce's Finnegans Wake. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [10] Name these elementary particles that come in 6 "flavors", such as the down and up types, and make up protons and neutrons.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [10] Quarks belong in a class of particles along with leptons named after this Italian scientist, who also formulated a thought experiment asking "where are the aliens?"

parts.label: C
parts.question: [10] Fermions are contrasted with this other type of subatomic particle named for an Indian physicist and whose types include W, Z, and one named for Higgs.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: A physicist from this country developed the “path integral” formulation of quantum mechanics. Photon scattering by charged particles was first detected in this country, where BCS super-conductivity theory was discovered. The (*) Michelson-Morley experiment was performed in this nation at a facility that became Case Western Reserve University. For ten points, name this country where Enrico Fermi built a nuclear reactor at the University of Chicago.
parts.answer: US (accept USA; accept either underlined portion of United States of America)

topics.description: An agricultural practice of alternating crops or fallow periods among fields and seasons to maintain soil fertility and reduce pests, diseases, and soil exhaustion.

parts.label: L
parts.question: For 10 points each, answer the following about advances in agricultural technology:

parts.label: A
parts.question: Medieval Europe saw the introduction of the three-field system of this process, in which one field was planted with oats or lentils and another left fallow. George Washington Carver advocated performing this process with legumes to increase the nitrogen content of soil.

parts.label: B
parts.question: The 20th century Green Revolution saw a dramatic spike in crop production due to the use of pesticides and this technology. This general class of substances includes any material added to soil to provide plant nutrients.

parts.label: C
parts.question: This scientist’s work in Mexico led him to breed wheat varieties resistant to rust. This “father of the Green revolution” is credited with saving over a billion people from starvation by developing semi-dwarf wheat.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Answer the following about diets and cuisine in Medieval Europe. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: Grain-based diets poor in iron and loss of iron through menstruation made medieval women more susceptible to disease, like this 14th-century epidemic that killed over one-third of Europe’s population.
parts.answer: Black Death [or Black Plague; or bubonic plague; or the Great Mortality; prompt on the plague; prompt on the pestilence]

parts.label: B
parts.question: Crop production increased as moldboard plows and horses were adopted alongside the “three-field” method of this farming technique in which different seasonal crops are grown over multiple fields to prevent overuse.

parts.label: C
parts.question: Followers of this saint would often break a rule prohibiting the consumption of “four-legged animals” in a room called the misericord [mih-ZER-ih-cord]. The adage “pray work” summarizes this saint from Nursia’s monastic rules followed by the Black Monks.
parts.answer: St. Benedict of Nursia [or Benedictus Nursiae; or Benedetto da Norcia; accept Benedictine Rules]

topics.description: A severe infectious disease caused by the bacterium Yersinia pestis, capable of producing major epidemics and multiple clinical forms.

parts.label: L
parts.question: After going to jail for shooting this author, the poet Paul Verlaine wrote a poem called “The Crime of Love.” For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [H] Name this French Symbolist poet, who wrote about his tempestuous relationship with Verlaine in A Season in Hell.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [M] In A Season in Hell, Rimbaud calls for these events to choke him with sand and blood. Thousands of rats die in the streets of Oran in a novel titled for one of these deadly events by Albert Camus.
parts.answer: Plague [or The Plague; or La Peste]

parts.label: C
parts.question: [E] Rimbaud claims to have invented the colors of these five letters in A Season in Hell. George Perec’s novel A Void only contains four of them, those being A, I, O, and U.

parts.label: L
parts.question: The Pied Piper of Hamelin might have begun as a child-friendly way to talk about the devastation left by this disease. For ten points each,

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this disease that spread across Europe in the 1300s with the help of rat fleas.
parts.answer: plague (accept Black Plague; accept bubonic plague; accept Black Death)

parts.label: B
parts.question: Giovanni Boccaccio [boh-KAH-chee-oh] wrote this short story collection, in which ten young nobles gather to tell stories while fleeing from the Black Death in Florence.

parts.label: C
parts.question: In one of the stories of the Decameron, named “The Patient Griselda,” Griselda’s husband tests her suitability as a wife by claiming he has killed two people with this relationship to her.
parts.answer: her children (accept her son and daughter)

topics.description: A Soviet space dog who became the first animal to orbit Earth aboard Sputnik 2 in 1957.

parts.label: L
parts.question: The United States claimed victory in the Space Race because we got to the Moon, so all of these other Soviet firsts don’t really count. For ten points each,

parts.label: A
parts.question: This first artificial satellite to orbit Earth was launched in October 1957. It broadcast a beeping radio signal for three weeks.

parts.label: B
parts.question: In 1957, this dog was picked up off the streets of Moscow and became the first creature to orbit the Earth, flying aboard Sputnik 2.

parts.label: C
parts.question: In 1961, Yuri Gagarin became the first human in space, flying aboard this spacecraft.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: The third object with this name contained faulty components that prevented it from mapping the Van Allen belt during the International Geophysical Year. A dog named (*) Laika became the first animal in space aboard the second of these objects and, in 1957, the first object with this name kicked off the Space Race. For ten points, name this series of Soviet spacecraft that included Earth’s first artificial satellite.
parts.answer: Sputnik program (accept Sputnik 1, 2, or 3; prompt on “satellite” before it is read)

topics.description: Deuterium is the stable isotope of hydrogen whose nucleus contains one proton and one neutron.

parts.label: L
parts.question: This technique was first described by Isidor Rabi. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this technique, which measures a chemical shift measured in parts per million and is commonly measured relative to TMS. This technique commonly uses H-1 or C-13 isotopes.
parts.answer: NMR [or nuclear magnetic resonance; accept 1H-NMR or 13C-NMR]

parts.label: B
parts.question: TMS is composed of four methyl groups bonded to a central atom of this element, with atomic symbol Si.

parts.label: C
parts.question: Solvents in NMR often have their hydrogen atoms replaced by this isotope. This heaviest stable isotope of hydrogen has a nucleus consisting of a proton and neutron, and is found in heavy water.

parts.label: L
parts.question: An effect named for these structures was used to discover proton tunneling in enzymes. For 10 points  each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [10] Name these forms of an element that have the same number of protons but a different number of  neutrons, giving them a different mass number.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [10] This isotope contains one proton, one neutron, and one electron. It is one of two stable isotopes of  hydrogen.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [10] Protein tunneling is among the processes studied using this effect, in which the rate of a reaction  changes based on which isotope of an element is present. Jacob Bigeleisen (BIG-ul-AI-zen) and Maria  Goeppert-Mayer (ger-pert-MAI-er) first explained this effect in 1947.

topics.description: The surface glycoprotein of SARS-CoV-2 that mediates host-cell entry through ACE2 binding and is a major target of COVID-19 vaccines and neutralizing antibodies.

parts.label: L
parts.question: This virus attaches to the ACE2 receptor on type II alveolar cells, causing a cytokine storm. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [M] Name this respiratory virus which can be detected through an RT-LAMP procedure obtained from a nasal swab. This virus is a strain of another one that caused an outbreak in 2002.
parts.answer: SARS-Cov-2 [accept equivalents like coronavirus 19; accept COVID-19 or COVID even though it’s the disease; prompt on coronavirus alone by asking “what specific strain of coronavirus?”]

parts.label: B
parts.question: [H] This largest glycoprotein on the SARS-Cov-2 virus is responsible for the rise of the delta and omicron variants of COVID-19. Many mRNA COVID vaccines, like Pfizer, use a modified RNA that encodes this protein.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [E] Type II alveolar cells are located in this respiratory organ which is responsible for gas exchange.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Short term regulation of this quantity is driven by the renin-angiotensin-aldosterone system. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [E] Name this quantity which, for healthy humans, is around 120 over 80 millimeters of mercury. A prolonged increase in this quantity is indicative of hypertension.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [M] Baroreceptor neurons that are sensitive to the stretching of blood vessels send signals to this region of the brain in order to maintain blood pressure. The midbrain, pons, and medulla oblongata make up this part of the brain.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [H] Receptors for ACE2, an enzyme that lowers blood pressure by hydrolyzing angiotensin II, also serves as the binding site for this protein. Regenron recently developed a mix of two monoclonal antibodies that recognize this protein.
parts.answer: SARS-CoV-2 spike protein [accept COVID spike protein or coronavirus spike protein]

topics.description: An astronomical cloud or structure of interstellar gas, plasma, and dust, including emission, dark, planetary, and supernova-remnant nebulae.

parts.label: L
parts.question: This list’s one-hundred-tenth and final object, a dwarf satellite galaxy, was added in 1967, nearly two hundred years after its first publication. For ten points each,

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this catalog of astronomical objects compiled by a French astronomer in the eighteenth century. In this catalog, M45 is the Pleiades cluster, and M31 is the Andromeda galaxy.

parts.label: B
parts.question: Messier referred to most of his objects by this term. However, we now know that only a handful are really these interstellar dust clouds. Two of these objects are M16 and M1, nicknamed the “Eagle” and the “Crab.”

parts.label: C
parts.question: M42 is the nebula named for this constellation, which contains the stars Alnitak, Alnilam, and Mintaka in its belt.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: Barnard 68 is a particularly visible "dark" version of this type of object. The Hubble Space Telescope photographed one of these objects in the photo "Pillars of Creation". "Planetary" examples of these objects are formed when stars eject their outer layers into space. The (*) "Horsehead" and "Crab" ones are famous examples of, for 10 points, what interstellar clouds of gas and dust?

topics.description: A pineal-gland hormone that regulates circadian rhythms and sleep timing.

parts.label: L
parts.question: For 10 points each,

parts.label: A
parts.question: [H] Name this amino acid coded for by the single codon UGG. The genes that code for this amino acid’s production in bacteria are a common example of a repressible operon.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [M] Tryptophan is a biological precursor to this pineal gland-secreted hormone responsible for controlling circadian rhythms.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [E] Deficiencies in serotonin, another tryptophan derivative, have been linked to this mood disorder characterized by extended feelings of sadness and emptiness.
parts.answer: clinical depression [or major depressive disorder or MDD; accept dysthymia]

parts.label: L
parts.question: One disorder associated with this phenomenon may be caused by a disruption during its deep NREM form. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this phenomenon, which is inhibited in insomnia.
parts.answer: sleep [accept word forms like sleeping; accept equivalents]

parts.label: B
parts.question: Sleep is stimulated by the secretion of this hormone from the pineal gland, which is also used to treat insomnia. Some people take supplements of this hormone to help them fall asleep.

parts.label: C
parts.question: Melatonin regulates these 24-hour cycles that control when people feel drowsy. These cycles are regulated by the suprachiasmatic nucleus.
parts.answer: circadian rhythm [or circadian cycle; accept sleep-wake cycle; prompt on sleep cycle]

topics.description: A state of matter with a definite shape and volume, in which particles are relatively fixed and the substance generally does not flow.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: This phase is depicted to the left of the triple point in phase diagrams. This phase is the starting phase of sublimation and the ending phase of deposition. The atoms in objects in this phase can be ordered in a lattice or in an irregular, “amorphous” manner. Most (*) metals are in this phase at standard temperature and pressure. For ten points, name this phase of matter whose atoms move less than those of liquids and gasses.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: The "nearly free electron" theory describes one form of this phase of matter, which is to the immediate left of the triple point. In sublimation, this phase of matter turns into a gas, and (*) precipitates formed during reactions are this phase of matter. For 10 points, identify this phase of matter which does not expand or flow, and is typically denser than liquids or gases.

topics.description: An idealized object that absorbs all incident electromagnetic radiation and emits thermal radiation with a spectrum determined solely by its temperature.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Max Planck added a correction to the Rayleigh-Jeans Law, which describes the spectral emission of these  objects. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [H] Name these objects, which perfectly absorb all wavelengths of light.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] Wien’s displacement law describes the relationship between this quantity and wavelength for a blackbody  radiation curve. This quantity can be measured by a thermometer.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [M] According to Wien’s displacement law, temperature and peak wavelength have this relationship. For a light  wave, frequency and wavelength have this relationship to each other.
parts.answer: inverse [or inversely proportional or reciprocal; accept descriptions, such as they multiply to a  constant]

parts.label: L
parts.question: When in thermal equilibrium, these objects emit their namesake radiation. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [H] Name these objects that absorb all incident electromagnetic radiation.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] Since they do not reflect light, black bodies have an albedo value of this number. Dividing by this number on a calculator typically gives an error.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [M] This man’s namesake law describes the electromagnetic radiation emitted by black bodies. This scientist’s namesake constant is symbolized h and equals 6.63 times 10 to the negative 34th.

topics.description: A tokamak is a toroidal magnetic-confinement device used to contain and heat plasma for controlled nuclear-fusion research.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: Langmuir (LANG-myoor) waves are oscillations of electron density in these substances. Tokamaks, which confine these substances using strong toroidal magnets, are used for nuclear fusion research. Touching a “globe” named for these substances will produce a strand of light to your finger. Tesla coils produce (*) arcs of these substances, which also constitute lightning. The interior of the sun consists of, for ten points, what fourth state of matter?

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: Mass movements of this kind of matter in the atmosphere can result in Birkeland currents.  Tension on magnetic field lines results in low-frequency oscillations in this matter called Alfven  waves. This matter is treated like a fluid in the field of (*) magnetohydrodynamics, and a magnetic  field is used to confine this kind of matter in the shape of a torus in a tokamak (TOW-kuh-mak). Auroras  are an example of this matter, whose partially ionized form makes up lightning. For 10 points, name this  “fourth state of matter” that comprises the Sun.

topics.description: A very soft hydrated magnesium silicate mineral rated 1 on the Mohs scale and used in products including talcum powder and soapstone.

parts.label: L
parts.question: For 10 points, answer the following about the Mohs scale:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [E] The Mohs scale measures this quantity from 1 to 10 based on which minerals can scratch each other. Diamond, which represents 10, has one of the highest known values of this quantity.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [M] A 1 on the Mohs scale corresponds to this mineral made of hydrated magnesium silicate. This soft, white, clay mineral is ground to produce baby powder.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [H] A group of minerals known by this name represent a 5 on the Mohs scale and are made of calcium phosphate. A mineral of this name prefixed “hydroxy-” (“hye-DROCK-see”) is the main component of human bones.

parts.label: L
parts.question: This scale is an ordinal, not nominal, scale because its values of 1 through 10 mean essentially nothing beyond their ordered ranking. For ten points each,

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this scale that uses quartz and topaz as the references for its values of 6 and 7.
parts.answer: Mohs scale of mineral hardness (prompt on “hardness (scale)”)

parts.label: B
parts.question: The highest value on the Mohs scale, 10, is given to this valuable gemstone. This allotrope of carbon was the hardest natural material at the time of the scale’s creation.

parts.label: C
parts.question: Soapstone is made out of this easily-powdered mineral, the softest on the Mohs scale.

topics.description: The second major layer of Earth's atmosphere, located above the troposphere and below the mesosphere, containing the ozone layer and generally warming with altitude.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: The warming of this layer is the cause of polar vortex warming and weakening. A temperature inversion causes temperature to unusually increase with altitude in this layer of the atmosphere, thanks to a high concentration of (*) ozone, which also absorbs harmful radiation. Commercial aircraft cruise in the lower part of, for 10 points, what 2nd atmospheric layer, above the troposphere?

parts.label: L
parts.question: The tropopause separates this layer from the troposphere. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [M] Name this second lowest layer of Earth’s atmosphere, above the Troposphere but lower than the Mesosphere.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] These kinds of vehicles usually fly in the lower parts of the Stratosphere to avoid turbulence in the Troposphere. The jet engines of these vehicles generate thrust, and their wings create lift.
parts.answer: planes [accept jets or airliners or aircrafts]

parts.label: C
parts.question: [H] The Ozone layer in the Earth’s stratosphere absorbs most of this type of electromagnetic radiation from the Sun. It ranges from wavelengths of 10 nanometers to 400 nanometers, shorter than the wavelength of visible light.

topics.description: Large biological molecules composed of amino acids linked by peptide bonds, performing structural, enzymatic, signaling, transport, and nutritional functions.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Answer some questions about the work of Italian biologist Camillo Golgi, for 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: Golgi discovered a large organelle which is named for him and which packages these molecules. These molecules are made up of amino acids and are a nutrient provided in food like nuts and meat.

parts.label: B
parts.question: Golgi also invented a form of this technique that allows neurons to be visualized. Hans Christian Gram names another form of this technique that can be used to classify bacteria.

parts.label: C
parts.question: Gram staining classifies organisms based on the thickness of this organelle, which surrounds the cells of some organisms. It is made of cellulose in plants and is not present in animal cells.
parts.answer: cell wall [do not accept or prompt on "cell membrane"]

parts.label: L
parts.question: A “copper-free” version of this branch of chemistry is termed “bioorthogonal” as it avoids being toxic to cells. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [H] Name this branch of chemistry that generates products through simple reactions involving a biomolecule and a reporter molecule. It is named for a sound.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [M] Researchers have discovered that triazoles can act similarly to azides in click chemistry due to the presence of this element. Amines contain a lone pair and an atom of this element.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [E] Another application of click chemistry is the effective marking of these polymers that interact with small molecules such as drugs. Amino acids are bonded together with peptide bonds in these molecules.

topics.description: Nikola Tesla was a Serbian-American inventor and electrical engineer whose work on alternating-current systems helped shape modern electrical power.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Materials with this property are used on the stripes of credit cards because of the “memory” they can retain. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [M] Name this property of materials whose electron spins are aligned, producing a permanent magnetic field.
parts.answer: ANSWER: ferromagnetism [accept word forms like ferromagnetic]

parts.label: B
parts.question: [H] Ferromagnetic materials exhibit this phenomenon, where magnetizing the material follows a different path than demagnetizing it. More generally, this phenomenon refers to the dependence of a system on its history.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [E] The SI derived unit for magnetic field strength is named for this Serbian-American inventor who pioneered alternating current during his rivalry with Thomas Edison.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: This man filmed the murder of the elephant Topsy in a Coney Island zoo. This man’s Black Maria film studio helped popularize Annie Oakley. George Westinghouse opposed this popularizer of the stock ticker in a so-called “war.” This inventor used (*) Nikola Tesla’s “alternating current” to electrocute animals to support the adoption of his “direct current.” For 10 points, name this “Wizard of Menlo Park,” the inventor of the lightbulb.
parts.answer: ANSWER: Thomas Edison [or Thomas Alva Edison]

topics.description: The functional unit of the kidney, comprising a renal corpuscle and renal tubule that filter blood and process urine.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Cancers of this organ can grow into its surrounding tissue, called Gerota’s fascia, and are treated with  nephrectomy. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [M] Name these paired organs in the abdomen, which filter the blood and excrete nitrogenous waste.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] The kidneys are responsible for secreting this liquid, which contains urea. This fluid is stored in the bladder.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [H] Within the kidney are several thousand of these functional units, which begin at the glomerulus and Bowman’s  capsule and end at the collecting duct. The loop of Henle is found in these functional units.

parts.label: L
parts.question: The capillary loops in this organ can be thickened during lupus, causing a “wire-loop” appearance.  For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [10] Name this bean-shaped organ that is responsible for the filtration of blood to produce urine.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [10] This structure formed by the renal corpuscle and renal tubule is the functional subunit of the kidney.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [10] Kidneys can reabsorb water due to insertion of this channel protein that selectively allows water to  pass through. Vasopressin promotes expression of this protein.

topics.description: A colloid is a heterogeneous mixture in which finely divided particles remain dispersed throughout a continuous phase and commonly produce the Tyndall effect by scattering light.

parts.label: L
parts.question: The term “homogenization” technically refers to any technique by which these mixtures are broken up and re-dispersed. For ten points each,

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name these mixtures in which small particles, usually solids, are suspended in a “continuous” phase, usually a liquid, without precipitating.

parts.label: B
parts.question: In practice, homogenization nearly always refers to a step in the production of this beverage, a colloid of fat globules suspended in water.

parts.label: C
parts.question: Homogenization can temporarily prevent a colloid from displaying the Tyndall effect, which occurs when the insoluble particles do this to incoming light. The Rayleigh form of this physical process also explains why the sky is blue.

parts.label: L
parts.question: These substances display the Tyndall effect when light is scattered within them. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [M] Name these cloudy substances, in which insoluble particles are suspended in another substance.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [H] Because colloids often appear as cloudy mixtures, they often have high values for this quantity . This quantity describes the relative clarity of a liquid

parts.label: C
parts.question: [E] Another type of mixture, solutions, involve a solute being dissolved in this other type of substance. Water is considered the “universal” type of this substance because of its ability to dissolve solutes.

topics.description: RNA (ribonucleic acid) is a nucleic acid involved in gene expression and gene regulation, including messenger, transfer, and small interfering forms.

parts.label: L
parts.question: The enzyme Dicer cleaves the “short hairpin” class of this molecule into its “small interfering” class. For 10  points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: This molecule’s namesake “interference” was discovered by Andrew Fire and Craig Mello. The “messenger”  variety of this molecule is single stranded.
parts.answer: RNA [or ribonucleic acid; accept RNAi; accept mRNA or RNA interference; or messenger RNA]

parts.label: B
parts.question: Fire and Mello observed RNA interference in this model organism. This nematode was the first multicellular  organism to have its whole genome sequenced.
parts.answer: C. elegans [or Caenorhabditis elegans; prompt on Caenorhabditis]

parts.label: C
parts.question: Argonaute, a RISC complex protein family that cleaves mRNA strands during RNA interference, was  discovered in Arabidopsis thaliana, a model organism in this kingdom. This kingdom includes trees.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: This molecule is theorized to have been the first sign of life on earth in its namesake “world hypothesis”. The small interfering type of this molecule is involved in post-transcriptional gene silencing. A certain type of this molecule has a cloverleaf shape and is used to (*) transfer amino acids. This molecule uses the nucleotide Uracil instead of thymine, which DNA uses. For 10 points, name this nucleic acid that is created via transcription.

topics.description: A natural history museum in Chicago, Illinois, known for its scientific collections and for housing Sue, one of the most complete Tyrannosaurus rex skeletons discovered.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Give the following about museums in Chicago, for ten points each.

parts.label: A
parts.question: A well-preserved Tyrannosaurus Rex skeleton nicknamed Sue is found in this Chicago natural history museum, found by the lakeshore in Chicago’s Museum Campus.

parts.label: B
parts.question: The Field Museum is next door to one of these facilities, named for John G. Shedd, that includes exhibits like the Caribbean Reef and the Waters of the World.

parts.label: C
parts.question: Just east of the Field Museum and Shedd Aquarium is one of these facilities, named for businessman Max Adler, that includes the Doane Observatory and an Astronomical Museum.

parts.label: L
parts.question: This creature had the strongest bite force of any terrestrial animal ever. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [M] Name this carnivorous dinosaur from the Cretaceous period, whose name translates to “King of the Tyrant Lizards.”

parts.label: B
parts.question: [H] One of the most complete T. Rex skeletons, named Sue for its discoverer, resides in this natural history museum in Chicago.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [E] Despite their depiction in films, the skin of the T. Rex and most dinosaurs were covered in these features, which cover the skin of their modern descendents, birds.

topics.description: Matter inferred from its gravitational effects on galaxies and cosmic structure despite emitting, absorbing, or reflecting little to no electromagnetic radiation.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: This substance “freezes out” and drops out of equilibrium in systems that model it as thermal relics. This substance is concentrated in clumps called subhalos. The free streaming length of this substance determines whether it is “hot,” “warm,” or “cold.” Fritz Zwicky (“TSVICK-ee”) conceptualized this substance in the Coma Cluster to explain anomalous galaxy (*) speeds. Vera Rubin’s studies of galaxy rotation curves provided evidence for this substance. This substance makes up 27 percent of the universe’s energy density and 85 percent of its mass. For 10 points, name this type of matter that does not interact with light.
parts.answer: dark matter [or dark after “matter” is read; accept cold dark matter or hot dark matter or warm dark matter or dunkle Materie or CDM or HDM or WDM; do NOT accept or prompt on “dark energy”]

parts.label: L
parts.question: Answer the following about the ultra-diffuse galaxy NGC 1052-DF2 [N-G-C one-oh-five-two D-F-two], for 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [E] Like all ultra-diffuse galaxies, DF2 has an extremely low luminosity and thus emits very little of this phenomenon, which is carried by photons.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [M] DF2 is a candidate for the first known galaxy with none of this substance. Vera Rubin found evidence for this substance from its gravitational effect on galaxy rotation curves.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [H] DF2 is also known for having an extremely luminous population of these large, spherical star clusters that are rich in Population II [two] stars.

topics.description: Torque is the rotational effect of a force, determined by the force and its lever arm, that changes an object's rotational motion about an axis.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Give the following about rotational physics, for ten points each.

parts.label: A
parts.question: An object’s rotational motion can be changed by this quantity, the rotational analog of a force. Because a lever can cause an object to move around an axis, it applies this kind of twisting force.

parts.label: B
parts.question: A moving object has this quantity, which is computed by multiplying its mass and its velocity. If the object is rotating, it has the angular type of this quantity, which is calculated similarly: moment of inertia times angular velocity.

parts.label: C
parts.question: While spinning at over 1,000 RPM, this piece of lab equipment can separate plasma from the rest of the blood. You can answer with either the name of the device or the similarly named fictitious force on which it relies.
parts.answer: centrifuge (accept word forms like centrifugation; accept centrifugal force; do not accept or prompt on “centripetal (force)”)

parts.label: L
parts.question: You watch a hexagonal pencil roll down a ramp. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: When an edge of the pencil hits the ramp, angular momentum is conserved because this quantity about the contact point equals zero. This value measured in newton-meters equals force crossed with radius.

parts.label: B
parts.question: The pencil’s total angular momentum equals the orbital angular momentum added to this other type of angular momentum. Its namesake quantum number is maximized by Hund’s rule.
parts.answer: spin angular momentum [accept spin quantum number]

parts.label: C
parts.question: If the incline exceeds a certain angle, the pencil will roll down forever, reaching a constant velocity known by this word. A falling object subject to air resistance achieves this type of constant velocity.

topics.description: The ionic compound NaCl, commonly encountered as edible salt and naturally occurring as the mineral halite, with major historical importance as a food preservative, seasoning, and traded commodity.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: Removal of this compound from water is the goal of reverse osmosis. Because an IV injection of pure water will explode your blood, dehydration is treated by a solution containing this compound. This compound is produced by evaporation ponds when they’re fed a solution of (*) brine. This compound, which is found naturally in the mineral halite, is formed along with water in the reaction of NaOH and HCl. Most of the world’s water contains, for ten points, what ionic compound, whose formula is NaCl?
parts.answer: table salt (accept sodium chloride; accept NaCl until it is read)

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: The amoleh variety of this resource is produced around Lake Afrara in northern Ethiopia. In Britain, towns whose names end in the suffix “-wich” often were large producers of this resource historically. Lithium and this resource are highly concentrated in a feature named after Uyuni in the Bolivian Altiplano. Along the coast of the Gulf of Mexico, oil is often found in (*) “domes” of this resource. A pink-colored variety of this resource found in Punjab is named for the Himalayan mountains. The Bonneville Speedway in Utah is on an exceptionally flat “pan” of this resource. For 10 points, name this mineral resource found in high concentrations in the Dead Sea.
parts.answer: salt [or rock salt or halite or sodium chloride or NaCl]

topics.description: A group of biological pigments produced by melanocytes that contributes to skin, hair, and eye coloration and helps protect against ultraviolet radiation.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: The “eu” (yoo) and “pheo” (fee-oh) varieties of this compound are both synthesized by the  catalyzation of tyrosinase (teer-AH-sin-ayz), and the latter requires the presence of cystine and a  benzothiazine (BEN-zohth-AI-uh-neen) intermediate. Like dopamine, a form of this compound  found in the brain degenerates in Parkinson's disease, and is responsible for the (*) dark color of  the substantia nigra (sub-STANT-yuh NAI-gruh). A form of skin cancer develops from the cells that  produce this compound, and UV radiation stimulates the production of this compound. For 10 points,  name this pigment that gives skin its color.

parts.label: L
parts.question: This organ contains numerous mechanoreceptors, including Pacinian (puh-SIN-ee-an) corpuscles and Merkel nerve endings. For ten points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [E] Name this largest organ of the human body, which also acts as its first line of defense against infection. The epidermis is the outermost of the layers of this organ that covers the body.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [M] This pigment in skin can protect humans from UV radiation and can prevent some of the reactions that lead to skin cancer. Dark skin is generally rich in this pigment, the primary determinant of skin color.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [H] This protein is a key structural material in the outer layers of skin in many vertebrates. The hard beta forms of this protein are found in bird beaks and claws, while the softer alpha forms are found in humans’ hair and nails.

topics.description: Metallic elements associated with the d block of the periodic table that commonly exhibit multiple oxidation states and form coordination complexes.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Dmitri Mendeleev is credited with creating the first version of these things. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [E] Name this display that sorts elements based on their atomic numbers, organized into groups and periods.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [H] Along with the actinides, this series of fifteen elements is usually displayed below the other elements in the periodic table. They feature elements 57–71, and all but one of them progressively fill the 4f shell.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [M] Lanthanides and actinides are also part of this group of metals, which includes those with partially filled d-shells. Most of these metals have multiple oxidation states.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: The transfer of functional groups between two of these elements occurs between oxidative addition and reductive elimination steps during cross-coupling reactions. The number of these elements that a substituent is bound to is its denticity. These elements are at the center of complexes whose orbital splitting behavior is described by (*) crystal field theory. Most coordination complexes are centered around one of these elements bound to ligands. The catalytic activity of these elements stems from their ability to adopt different oxidation states due to their partially filled d orbitals. For 10 points, name these metallic elements found between groups 3 and 12 on the periodic table.
parts.answer: transition metals [prompt on d-block elements or metals]

topics.description: A small, fast memory component that stores data and instructions likely to be accessed soon by the processor, commonly organized into L1, L2, and L3 levels.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Answer the following about the computer memory hierarchy, for 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [E] Towards the bottom of the hierarchy are these physical storage components, which have declined in use since  the advent of solid state drives. This component is abbreviated HDD, though it's often referred to using a two-word  term.
parts.answer: hard drive [or hard disk, or hard disk drive]

parts.label: B
parts.question: [H] These components are a smaller faster memory located close to the CPU and include L1 and L2 levels. This  term, in general, refers to any component that stores data so future requests can be served faster.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [M] The most common type of temporary memory, RAM, stands for this kind of access memory. One can use a  “seed” when generating numbers with this property.
parts.answer: random [accept random access memory; accept random numbers or random number generator;  accept pseudorandom]

parts.label: L
parts.question: Types of this resource are often categorized into a “hierarchy” whose levels correspond to different points on the tradeoff between speed and size. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [E] Name this resource whose capacity might be measured in megabytes or gigabytes. RAM is the random-access kind of this resource, which in general stores data for computers.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [M] This level of memory is faster but smaller than RAM, and is used to temporarily store data the CPU expects to soon use. In web browsers, an analogous structure stores previously-visited pages.
parts.answer: cache [accept L1 cache or L2 cache; accept word forms like caching]

parts.label: C
parts.question: [H] These computer components fill the relatively large, slow role of secondary memory. These components usually use NAND flash cells, and might connect to a motherboard through NVMe.

topics.description: A chemical bonding principle stating that atoms tend to achieve a stable valence shell containing eight electrons, typically through bonding or electron gain or loss.

parts.label: L
parts.question: This element is an important component of Pyrex glass. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [10] Name this group 13 element that has atomic number 5, the lightest metalloid.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [10] Boron only needs 6 electrons in its valence shell to be stable, violating this law, which says that an element is stable when its valence shell is filled with 8 electrons.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [10] The octet rule can be tracked using dot diagrams named for this chemist. This man also names a definition of acids as electron pair acceptors.
parts.answer: Gilbert [Newton] Lewis [accept Lewis dot diagram[s] or Lewis structure[s]]

parts.label: L
parts.question: This rule is violated by phosphorous pentachloride, which has five bonds around the central atom. For 10 points  each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [M] Name this oft-violated rule in chemistry, which states that atoms seek to have eight valence electrons.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [H] Phosphorus pentachloride has 10 valence electrons forming 5 bonds and no lone pairs, giving it this geometry.  Equatorial and axial substituents in this geometry can be exchanged via the Berry pseudorotation.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [E] The fluorides of one member of this group, xenon, also violate the octet rule. These elements occupy the  rightmost column of the periodic table and are very unreactive.

topics.description: Ferromagnetism is the property of certain materials in which aligned electron spins produce persistent or permanent magnetization.

parts.label: L
parts.question: This field is present when electrical charges move, and can be visualized by the orientation of iron filings. For ten points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [M] Name this field denoted by the letter B, whose strength is measured in Teslas. The Earth’s field of this kind protects it from the solar wind and cosmic rays.
parts.answer: magnetic field [or the Earth’s geomagnetic field]

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] These navigational devices use a magnetic needle and the earth’s magnetic field to point to magnetic north, which is slightly different from geographic north.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [H] Compasses and bar magnets can point north because they have this strongest type of magnetism, which allows iron, cobalt, or nickel to form permanent magnets.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Materials with this property are used on the stripes of credit cards because of the “memory” they can retain. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [M] Name this property of materials whose electron spins are aligned, producing a permanent magnetic field.
parts.answer: ANSWER: ferromagnetism [accept word forms like ferromagnetic]

parts.label: B
parts.question: [H] Ferromagnetic materials exhibit this phenomenon, where magnetizing the material follows a different path than demagnetizing it. More generally, this phenomenon refers to the dependence of a system on its history.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [E] The SI derived unit for magnetic field strength is named for this Serbian-American inventor who pioneered alternating current during his rivalry with Thomas Edison.

topics.description: Sharks are a diverse group of marine cartilaginous fishes, including the great white shark, that use sensory organs such as the ampullae of Lorenzini to detect electric fields.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: A painting of one of these animals depicts attempts to rescue a young boy and is by John Singleton Copley. These animals caused problems for early underwater telegraph cables, since their ampullae of Lorenzini allow them to sense electric fields. These animals which must (*) swim constantly to stay afloat have bodies made primarily of cartilage. For ten points, name these scary kinds of fish, an example of which is the great white.

parts.label: L
parts.question: The Bahamian story of McCabe’s curse inspired this painting while its artist was vacationing in the Caribbean after his father's death. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [M] Name this Winslow Homer painting of a Black man stranded on a small boat in the middle of the ocean.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] Homer’s painting The Gulf Stream depicts several of these animals. A painting by John Singleton Copley depicts one of these animals attacking Brook Watson off of the coast of Havana Harbor.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [H] The sharks in Homer’s The Gulf Stream inspired damned souls biting the title ship in this artist’s The Barque of Dante. During his Orientalist phase, this artist painted three women sitting in an ornate room around a hookah pipe.

topics.description: A class of solar-system bodies that orbit the Sun, are massive enough to be nearly round, and have not cleared their orbital neighborhoods.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: Eris is the most massive of the five recognized ones of these objects, of which Ceres is the only one closer to the sun than Uranus. Unlike a class of larger related objects, these things have not cleared their orbits. In 2006, the IAU officially reclassified (*) Pluto as one of these objects. For 10 points, identify these solar system objects named for the fact that they are smaller than planets.
parts.answer: dwarf planets [prompt on planets until mentioned; prompt on Kuiper belt objects]

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: The first asteroid to be discovered is now classified as one of these objects, because it does not clear its neighboring region. Haumea and Makemake (MAH-kay-MAH-kay) are two of these objects found in the Kuiper (KYE-per) Belt, and Eris is the second-largest known one of these objects. One of these objects discovered by Clyde Tombaugh was (*) reclassified in 2006. For ten points, name these astronomical objects, like Pluto, which are smaller than planets.

topics.description: The fundamental units of ordinary matter, consisting of a central nucleus surrounded by electrons and characterized by their number of protons.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: Moseley’s law disproved a theory arguing that these things have randomly distributed corpuscles. John Dalton coined the name of these things and used them to explain his law of definite proportions. The Greek philosopher (*) Democritus is credited as the inventor of the “theory” of these things, whose name means “indivisible” in Greek. Niels Bohr and Ernest Rutherford theorized that a nucleus is at the center of, for ten points, what small building blocks of matter?

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: The motion of two parts of these entities can be considered separately, according to the Born-Oppenheimer approximation. Arnold Sommerfeld introduced the azimuthal quantum number and elliptical paths to a model of these entities created by Ernest Rutherford. Niels (*) Bohr formulated the planetary model of these entities, which can undergo alpha and beta decay. For 10 points, name these entities that consist of electrons that follow clearly defined circular shells, which surround a central nucleus.
parts.answer: atoms [accept nucleus before it is read; prompt on element]

topics.description: The fundamental interaction described by quantum chromodynamics, mediated by gluons, that binds quarks into hadrons and contributes through its residual force to binding atomic nuclei.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: This force is described by a gauge theory with symmetry group SU(3). Asymptotic freedom and color  confinement are properties of this force, which is described by quantum chromodynamics. This fundamental  force is mediated by the (*) gluon, and holds together protons and neutrons in a nucleus. As its name suggests, this  force has a higher strength than the gravitational, electromagnetic, and weak forces. For 10 points, name this most  powerful fundamental force.
parts.answer: strong force [accept strong interaction; accept strong nuclear force]

parts.label: L
parts.question: These particles share the atomic nucleus with, and are slightly more massive than, protons. For ten points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [E] Name these neutrally charged particles, whose number determines the isotope of an atom.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [H] This force holds atomic nuclei together despite the electrical repulsion of neutrons and protons. This force has an extremely small range, the shortest of the four fundamental forces.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [M] Since neutrons and protons are both hadrons, they are made up of these smaller particles held together with gluons. These particles have three colors and six flavors: up, down, top, bottom, strange, and charm.

topics.description: ʻAʻā is a type of basaltic lava flow with a rough, jagged surface made of broken, hardened lava fragments or clinkers.

parts.label: L
parts.question: “Pillow” examples of this substance are extruded at mid-ocean ridges. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [E] Give this term for molten rock on the Earth’s surface. It is contrasted with magma.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [M] This volcanic rock names a type of fast-flowing lava with a low proportion of silica [SILL-ih-kuh]. The solidification of this rock creates shield volcanoes in places like Hawaii.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [H] This Hawaiian term refers to lava flows with a rough, jagged surface that is difficult to walk across. It is contrasted with a smoother type of lava known by a different name.

parts.label: L
parts.question: The Wikipedia article for this substance compares its viscosity to ketchup, but geologists probably haven’t tested that by pouring it out of a glass bottle. For ten points each,

parts.label: A
parts.question: Give this term for molten rock that has emerged onto or above the surface of the crust.

parts.label: B
parts.question: Among the types of lava are pahoehoe [pa-ho-ay-ho-ay], whose surface is billowing and smooth, and this type, with a craggly surface of “clinkers”. This name also has a Hawaiian derivation.

parts.label: C
parts.question: Lava that cools very rapidly without growing crystals may form this rock, often described as volcanic glass because it can break apart into sheets with sharp edges.

topics.description: A group of fat-soluble vitamins that regulate calcium absorption and can be synthesized in the skin through sunlight exposure.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Milk contains a number of essential nutrients. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [10] Cow's milk is a good source of calcium, which helps to prevent this disease characterized by the  weakening of bones.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [10] Milk is a good source of this B vitamin that must be derived from animal products, and has a central  cobalt ion.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [10] This vitamin that regulates calcium absorption was originally added to milk in the US in an effort to  eradicate rickets. It is produced in the skin after exposure to sunlight.

parts.label: L
parts.question: You are reading the Nutrition Facts label of a carton of whole milk. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [M] You see that the milk contains five grams of these fully hydrogenated [high-DRAH-juh-nay-tud] compounds, which have linear chains and no double bonds.
parts.answer: saturated fats [accept saturated fatty acids; prompt on partial answers]

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] You notice the milk is fortified with this vitamin that the body requires to absorb calcium. This vitamin can be synthesized by human skin.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [H] You also notice the milk is fortified with DHA, one of these unsaturated fatty acids that have a double bond three atoms away from the terminal methyl group.

topics.description: Electromagnetic radiation with wavelengths shorter than visible light and longer than X-rays, including solar radiation associated with sunburn and absorbed in large part by Earth’s ozone layer.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: In the Lyman series, this form of radiation is emitted when an electron jumps to a higher energy  level in a hydrogen atom. The prediction that a black body would emit an unbounded amount of  energy at this radiation's wavelength is known as its “catastrophe.” A type of spectroscopy (spekTRAH-skuh-pee) measures absorption in both the (*) visible region and this region of the spectrum.  Blacklights emit this form of radiation, which lies just above X-rays on the EM spectrum. For 10 points,  name this harmful type of radiation from the sun that sunscreen protects against.

parts.label: L
parts.question: The tropopause separates this layer from the troposphere. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [M] Name this second lowest layer of Earth’s atmosphere, above the Troposphere but lower than the Mesosphere.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] These kinds of vehicles usually fly in the lower parts of the Stratosphere to avoid turbulence in the Troposphere. The jet engines of these vehicles generate thrust, and their wings create lift.
parts.answer: planes [accept jets or airliners or aircrafts]

parts.label: C
parts.question: [H] The Ozone layer in the Earth’s stratosphere absorbs most of this type of electromagnetic radiation from the Sun. It ranges from wavelengths of 10 nanometers to 400 nanometers, shorter than the wavelength of visible light.

topics.description: Ants are eusocial insects in the family Formicidae, including diverse species organized into complex colonies with workers, soldiers, and reproductive queens.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: The Attini subgroup of this family can create food by intentionally promoting fungal growth. Certain species of acacias grow hollow spicules to provide homes for animals in this family as a mutualistic defense mechanism. E. O. Wilson’s extensive research on animals in this family led to the founding of sociobiology. Studies using these members of order (*) Hymenoptera led to the first isolation of formic acid. A red-colored invasive species in this family of insects can form rafts and defend colonies using pincers. For 10 points, name this family of eusocial insects whose varieties include “fire,” “army,” and “leafcutter” species.
parts.answer: ants [or Formicidae; prompt on insects or Hymenopterans before mention]

parts.label: L
parts.question: Some groups of these insects have evolved to “farm” various fungi. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [E] Name these colonial insects of the family Formicidae. They come in several forms including “workers,” “soldiers,” and “queens.”

parts.label: B
parts.question: [M] This group of ants practice highly sophisticated fungal agriculture using three different types of workers. These ants get their common name from slicing apart a certain food source.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [H] Other groups of ants perform “dairy farming” by protecting these sap-sucking insects and harvesting their nutrient-rich honeydew secretion.
parts.answer: aphids [or greenflies or blackflies or Aphidoidea]

topics.description: The SI unit of amount of substance, defined as exactly 6.02214076 × 10^23 specified elementary entities.
aliases: SI unit of amount of substance

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: Dividing the ideal gas constant by this quantity results in Boltzmann’s constant. This quantity which is defined as the number of atoms in twelve grams of carbon-12 is equal to the number of particles in (*) 22.4 liters of gas at standard temperature and pressure. For 10 points, name this constant which is the number of particles in a mole, approximately equal to 6.02 times 10 to the 23rd power.
parts.answer: Avogadro’s number [accept Avogadro’s constant; prompt on variable]

parts.label: L
parts.question: Answer some questions about carbon-12's role in chemical measurement, for 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: This unit of quantity is equal to the number of particles in 12 grams of carbon-12. The mass of one of these units for a specific element is that element's molecular weight.

parts.label: B
parts.question: One mole is equal to 6.02 x 10 23 , a number named for this Italian scientist.
parts.answer: Amedeo Avogadro [or Lorenzo Romano Amedeo Carlo Avogadro; accept Avogadro's number]

parts.label: C
parts.question: One mole of the "ideal" form of this state of matter will occupy a volume of 22.4 liters at standard temperature and pressure. This state of matter expands to fill its containers and is the least dense of the three primary phases.

topics.description: A membrane-based water-treatment process that uses pressure to force water through a semipermeable membrane while retaining dissolved salts and other impurities.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: Removal of this compound from water is the goal of reverse osmosis. Because an IV injection of pure water will explode your blood, dehydration is treated by a solution containing this compound. This compound is produced by evaporation ponds when they’re fed a solution of (*) brine. This compound, which is found naturally in the mineral halite, is formed along with water in the reaction of NaOH and HCl. Most of the world’s water contains, for ten points, what ionic compound, whose formula is NaCl?
parts.answer: table salt (accept sodium chloride; accept NaCl until it is read)

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: Description acceptable. Food production and this process were the goals of Egypt’s IBTS Greenhouse project. Graphene oxide membranes are the newest technology for this process, which uses ion channel traps in its electro-dialysis form. A solar (*) still achieves this process slowly, and Key West is supplied by a plant that does this by reverse osmosis. Brine is a waste product of, for ten points, what process that creates potable drinking water from seawater?
parts.answer: desalination (accept desalinization or desalting; accept any description of removing salt from water)

topics.description: A circuit law stating that the algebraic sum of voltage changes or potential differences around any closed loop is zero.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: The sum of this quantity around a closed loop equals zero, according to Kirchhoff's second law. For a  parallel-plate capacitor, this quantity equals its electric field times plate separation. Power is equal to (*) current times this quantity. This quantity is equal to current times resistance, according to Ohm’s Law. Batteries  generate a difference in, for 10 points, what quantity, which is symbolized V?
parts.answer: voltage [or electric potential or scalar potential; accept electromotive force or EMF; prompt on V;  reject answers that contain “energy,” such as “potential energy” or “electric potential energy”]

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: A Weston cell is used to calibrate devices that measure this quantity; those devices usually have  a high resistance. A difference in this quantity is produced when a magnetic field is applied  perpendicular to the current in the Hall effect. The sum of this quantity around a loop equals zero  according to (*) Kirchoff's (KEER-kahf's) law for this quantity. This quantity is equal to current times  resistance according to Ohm's law. For 10 points, name this quantity that is stored in batteries and  measured in volts.
parts.answer: voltage [or electric potential; or electromotive force; or EMF]

topics.description: Seismic events caused by the sudden release of energy through fault rupture or tectonic movement, producing seismic waves and potentially causing ground shaking, structural damage, and tsunamis.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: The release of energy in these events is described by elastic-rebound theory. These events are detected by triangulation of P and S waves. The modified Mercalli scale measures the (*) intensity of these events, unlike a logarithmic scale for their magnitude, which is named for Charles Richter. These events begin at an epicenter and can cause tsunamis. For ten points, name these natural disasters that are caused by rupturing faults in the crust.

parts.label: L
parts.question: One of these occurred on Good Friday in 1964 in Alaska, and a devastating one of these in 1906 caused days of fires in San Francisco. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [10] Name these events in which tectonic plates interact, causing the release of seismic waves. They often cause the ground to shake and destroy buildings.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [10] Earthquakes' intensity is measured by this logarithmic scale, which has largely been replaced by the moment magnitude scale. Earthquakes with a value of above 7.0 on this scale are considered "major".

parts.label: C
parts.question: [10] This term is used to describe the point on the Earth's surface directly above where an earthquake started. It is contrasted with the hypocenter.

topics.description: The empirical relation that a galaxy's recessional velocity is approximately proportional to its distance, providing evidence that the universe is expanding.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: The Planck (plonk) epoch immediately followed this event. Evidence for this event includes the CMBR and Hubble’s law, which shows that galaxies are moving apart. Following this event, protons and neutrons (*) fused to form atoms like deuterium and helium. For ten points, name this event around 14 billion years ago in which the universe expanded from a single point.
parts.answer: the Big Bang [prompt on creation of the universe or the beginning of time or logical equivalents]

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: This quantity can be computed by taking the reciprocal of the apparent movement of an object in arcseconds. Recessional velocity is proportional to this quantity, according to Hubble’s law. This quantity can be measured by observing the (*) parallax of an object. The force between two astronomical bodies is proportional to the inverse square of this quantity. For 10 points, name this quantity, which is measured in parsecs or kilometers.

topics.description: A caldera is a large volcanic depression formed when an eruption empties or substantially drains a magma chamber, causing the overlying volcanic structure to collapse.

parts.label: L
parts.question: The center of Yellowstone National Park sits within one of these geologic structures, the remains of an eruption from six hundred forty thousand years ago. For ten points each,

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this hollow depression that forms when an eruption causes a volcano to collapse. Mount Mazama’s eruption created one of these structures that filled with water and became Crater Lake.

parts.label: B
parts.question: A caldera can result from the release of this hot, molten rock during an eruption. Before this substance reaches the surface, it is called magma.

parts.label: C
parts.question: The Hawaiian islands contain few calderas because they were formed over one of these regions where mantle plumes push magma up towards the crust, creating fairly constant lava flows.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Two types of this substance are distinguished by surface texture and are called a’a (AH-ah) and pahoehoe (PUH-hoy-ay-ho-ay). For ten points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [E] Name this kind of molten rock that can erupt from volcanoes. When this substance is below the Earth’s surface, it is called magma instead.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [M] This kind of volcano is formed by basaltic lava, which flows relatively quickly and thus gives them shallow sides. These volcanoes are contrasted with cinder cone and stratovolcanoes.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [H] When their magma chambers are emptied, which often occurs during explosive eruptions, volcanoes can collapse into these structures. Crater Lake is found in one of these depressions at the top of volcanoes.

topics.description: A prion is a misfolded infectious protein that can induce abnormal folding in other proteins and cause transmissible neurodegenerative diseases.

parts.label: L
parts.question: The Rosetta@home project aims to improve prediction of this process in part by analyzing user inputs to a video game that challenges users to simulate it as accurately as possible. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [H] Name this process which would take an impossibly long amount of time to do by chance according to Levinthal’s paradox.
parts.answer: protein folding [accept word forms] (The name of the game mentioned in the leadin is called Foldit.)

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] The deep learning algorithm AlphaFold predicts protein structure based only on the order of these subunits, which make up a protein's primary structure. In proteins, these compounds are connected by peptide bonds.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [M] Mutations in the PrP gene can cause the formation of these agents made of misfolded proteins that in turn cause other, normal proteins to take on their shape. Scrapie, kuru, and mad cow disease are all caused by these agents.

parts.label: L
parts.question: A distributed computing project called "[this process] @home" attempts to study how this process occurs. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [10] Name this process that forms the three-dimensional structure of macromolecules such as insulin and hemoglobin. In it, long chains of peptides are assembled into complex shapes.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [10] Protein folding begins with this level of protein structure which refers to its sequence of amino acids. This level precedes the secondary and tertiary structures.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [10] Mistakes in protein folding can lead to the formation of these misfolded proteins, which can cause neurodegenerative diseases such as mad cow disease or Creutzfeldt-Jakob (CROYTS-felt YAH-kub) syndrome.

topics.description: A highly corrosive strong diprotic mineral acid with the formula H2SO4, produced industrially by the contact process and used in applications including lead-acid batteries.

parts.label: L
parts.question: This compound was historically known as “oil of vitriol”. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [10] Name this caustic compound used in a variety of industrial applications, with chemical formula H2SO4. It can be produced through the contact process.
parts.answer: sulfuric acid [do NOT accept or prompt on “sulfurous acid”]

parts.label: B
parts.question: [10] In the contact process, vanadium pentoxide is used as one of these things, and in ammonia production, iron is used as one of these as well. These things lower the activation energy in reactions.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [10] Sulfuric acid can also be produced in this element's namesake chamber process. This element symbolized Pb is used for protection from X-rays, and many old houses have this element as an ingredient in their paint.

parts.label: L
parts.question: These substances can be classified into monoprotic and polyprotic types. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [E] Name these substances with a low pH value, often contrasted with bases.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [M] This scientist defined acids as electron acceptors. His namesake dot diagrams can help visualize bonding between two atoms.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [H] This acid was created in high concentrations through the Lead chamber process before it was replaced with the contact process. This acid is the only diprotic strong acid, and it often acts as the electrolyte in lead-acid batteries.

topics.description: A gas-powered laboratory burner that produces a controllable open flame for heating, sterilization, and related laboratory work.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Many old molecular biology labs are equipped with these devices to sterilize a workspace before doing cell culture. For ten points each,

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name these devices that provide an open flame in a laboratory. They were invented by and named for a German chemist.

parts.label: B
parts.question: Bunsen burners are fed by this fossil fuel, which is mainly composed of methane but is tainted with small amounts of sulfides so that it can be smelled.

parts.label: C
parts.question: The safe way to heat a metal under a Bunsen burner is to place it in one of these round porcelain containers, which are extremely heat-resistant. A common lab demo involves measuring the weight of one after burning a magnesium ribbon.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Answer some questions about the flame test. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [M] The flame test commonly uses this apparatus to provide a flame. This apparatus, named for a German chemist, is also used to sterilize loops in microbiology.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] This element’s halides produce a green or blue-green frame. This metal is commonly used in wires because of its low cost and high conductivity.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [H] This alkali metal produces a bright-yellow flame. This element’s hydroxide forms a strong base called lye.

topics.description: An interpretation of quantum mechanics associated with Niels Bohr and Werner Heisenberg that emphasizes probabilistic measurement and the absence of definite classical properties before observation.

parts.label: L
parts.question: This scientist’s namesake thought experiment demonstrates the idea of superposition. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [E] Name this man who names a thought experiment involving a hypothetical cat which may be simultaneously considered dead and alive.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [H] Schrödinger proposed his thought experiment to illustrate his problems with this interpretation of quantum mechanics. It is named after a European city.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [M] In 1927, a proponent of the Copenhagen interpretation introduced this principle, which limits the accuracy at which complementary variables can be measured, such as position and momentum.

parts.label: L
parts.question: The squared magnitude of this function gives the probability density function. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [10] Name this quantity, symbolized psi, that represents the quantum state of a particle.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [10] The wavefunction can be described by an equation named after this physicist, who formulated a  thought experiment in which a cat is locked in a box with poison.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [10] Schrodinger's cat is meant to illustrate the absurdity of this interpretation of quantum mechanics,  named for a Danish city, which states that physical systems do not have defined properties until  observed.

topics.description: A dynamically typed, high-level programming language used for interactive web behavior and backend applications.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Node is used to run this language on backend webservers, while frameworks like React can be used to augment it on the front-end browser side. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [M] Name this high-level language, which TypeScript compiles to. While HTML and CSS are used to display and style web content, this language handles dynamic behavior.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [H] JavaScript scripts can be run by event handlers attached to entries in this hierarchical model of a web page, which correspond to HTML elements. This model is often referred to by a three-letter abbreviation.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [E] The DOM takes the form of this data structure, which is hierarchical because elements may have children. The top-most node of this structure is called the root, while the terminating nodes are called leaves.
parts.answer: tree [accept specific types of tree like binary trees]

parts.label: L
parts.question: Objects in this language are managed by the Document Object Model. For ten points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [M] Name this language, created by Tim Berners-Lee, which uses tags and attributes to construct web pages.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [H] HTML and CSS work with this language, standardized by ES6, to make websites interactive. Working with this dynamically-typed language, one might use a library called jQuery or a framework like React.
parts.answer: Javascript [Do not accept of prompt on “Java”]

parts.label: C
parts.question: [E] Web pages can be viewed in browsers like this most widely used browser on the planet. Google distributes this browser, which has an easter egg of a secret dinosaur game, visible when this browser can’t access the Internet.

topics.description: A specialized form of cell division that produces haploid gametes from diploid precursor cells and contributes to genetic variation.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Cyclin-dependent forms of these molecules help to regulate the phases of the cell cycle. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name these enzymes that catalyze the transfer of phosphate groups.

parts.label: B
parts.question: Aurora kinases are involved in this stage of mitosis, in which chromatin (KROH-muh-tin) condenses into chromosomes and crossing over occurs.

parts.label: C
parts.question: While mitosis produces most human cells, gametes (GAA-meets) such as egg cells are produced by this other type of cell division.

parts.label: L
parts.question: The synaptonemal complex forms in one stage of this process. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [M] Name this process that results in the formation of gametes. This process results in a haploid cell, unlike a similarly named process in somatic cells that creates new diploid cells.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] The anaphase stage of both mitosis and meiosis pulls apart these X shaped structures in the cells that contain genes, normally found in the nucleus.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [H] One aspect of meiosis is the “crossing over” of genes, which adds genetic variability. This phenomenon is when a pair of genes are close together and are usually inherited together, explaining why people with freckles often have red hair.

topics.description: Thomas Edison was an American inventor and entrepreneur associated with electric lighting, direct-current electrical systems, sound recording, and early motion-picture technology, including the Black Maria studio.

parts.label: L
