parts.question: During World War I, this woman offered to organize a unit of volunteer female sharpshooters, but was rejected. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [M] Name this sharpshooter who promoted armed self-defense for women and toured with Buffalo Bill’s Wild West Show.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [H] In 1903, this person libelled Oakley, claiming that she had stolen money to feed a cocaine addiction. Frederic Remington, who had briefly travelled with the Wild West Show, worked in Cuba after being hired by this man.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [E] Annie Oakley and her husband Frank E. Butler were the subject of a film produced by this inventor’s Black Maria film studio. This “Wizard of Menlo Park” is often inaccurately credited with inventing the lightbulb.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: This man filmed the murder of the elephant Topsy in a Coney Island zoo. This man’s Black Maria film studio helped popularize Annie Oakley. George Westinghouse opposed this popularizer of the stock ticker in a so-called “war.” This inventor used (*) Nikola Tesla’s “alternating current” to electrocute animals to support the adoption of his “direct current.” For 10 points, name this “Wizard of Menlo Park,” the inventor of the lightbulb.
parts.answer: ANSWER: Thomas Edison [or Thomas Alva Edison]

topics.description: A long-lived woody plant typically characterized by a trunk or multiple stems supporting a crown of branches and leaves.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: A “Witness” one of these objects titles a Pulitzer-winning poetry collection by Robert Frost. In the poem “Mending Wall,” Frost argues that objects of this type cannot “get across and eat the (*) cones” under another type of these plants. In a poem titled for a type of these plants, Frost describes boys “swinging” in these things after “climbing carefully to the top branches.” For ten points, name these tall plants in the poem “Birches.”
parts.answer: trees (accept A Witness Tree; accept apple trees or pine trees; accept Birches; prompt on “apple” after “get across” is read)

parts.label: L
parts.question: This philosopher believed that objects exist continuously only because God perceives everything. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [M] Name this Irish philosopher who coined the phrase “to be is to be perceived” in his Treatise Concerning the Principles of Human Knowledge. This man also wrote Three Dialogues Between Hylas and Philonous.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] Berkeley’s master argument demonstrates the impossibility of conceiving an unconceived one of these objects. A thought experiment asks if one of these objects that falls in the forest makes a sound if no one is around to hear it.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [H] Berkeley’s immaterialism is sometimes described as the subjective form of this philosophical position. This position holds that reality is dependent on the mind.

topics.description: A rapid, widespread loss of biodiversity in which an unusually large proportion of species disappear during a relatively short geological interval.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: The largest of these events is blamed on the eruption of carbon dioxide from Siberian traps. The ongoing “Holocene” one of these events is being caused by humans. A gigantic (*) crater on the Yucatan Peninsula lends credence to a theory that one of these events was caused by an asteroid. The ends of the Permian and Cretaceous eras were marked by, for ten points, what destructive events that killed off many species at once?
parts.answer: mass extinctions (accept any specific extinction event; accept Great Dying; accept extinction of the dinosaurs)

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: These events were defined using a compendium of marine animals written by Jack Sepkoski. A  “gun” hypothesis describes how the breakup of methane clathrates may have contributed to one of  these events. One of these events described by the Alvarez hypothesis made way for a large  amount of (*) adaptive radiation in mammal species. The sixth one of these events, dubbed the  Holocene, is currently ongoing, and the last one happened 65 million years ago. For 10 points, name  these events, such as the K-T and the “Great Dying” in which many species end.

topics.description: A wave in which particles of the medium oscillate parallel to the direction of propagation, producing alternating compressions and rarefactions.

parts.label: L
parts.question: This type of wave is audible if its frequency is between 20 and 20,000 Hertz. For ten points each,

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this phenomenon whose vibrations travel through room temperature air at roughly 3443 meters per second.

parts.label: B
parts.question: The intensity of a sound wave is measured in this logarithmic unit, which also has several applications in electronics. A jet engine’s noise commonly registers 140 of these units.
parts.answer: decibel (accept dB; accept bel or B)

parts.label: C
parts.question: While moving through air, sound waves are classified as this type of wave, because the medium moves perpendicular to the motion of the wave. In the main alternative, a transverse wave, the medium moves in parallel.

parts.label: L
parts.question: The SOFAR channel is the location in the ocean that minimizes this quantity, which is typically  standardized at 343 meters per second at 20 degrees Celsius. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [10] Name this rate at which acoustic waves travel through an elastic medium such as air.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [10] This dimensionless quantity is the ratio of an object's velocity to the local speed of sound.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [10] Sound waves are an example of this type of wave that contains compressions and rarefactions,  which is also exemplified by the p-waves produced in an earthquake.

topics.description: The Hall effect is the production of a transverse voltage across a current-carrying conductor or semiconductor placed in a magnetic field perpendicular to the current.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: A Weston cell is used to calibrate devices that measure this quantity; those devices usually have  a high resistance. A difference in this quantity is produced when a magnetic field is applied  perpendicular to the current in the Hall effect. The sum of this quantity around a loop equals zero  according to (*) Kirchoff's (KEER-kahf's) law for this quantity. This quantity is equal to current times  resistance according to Ohm's law. For 10 points, name this quantity that is stored in batteries and  measured in volts.
parts.answer: voltage [or electric potential; or electromotive force; or EMF]

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: Removing these entities from certain objects can leave behind a phenomenon called “remanence.” In the Zeeman [ZAY-mun] effect, these entities split apart spectral lines. Applying these entities perpendicular to a conductor results in the Hall effect. These entities are constant within an ideal (*) solenoid [SAHL-uh-noyd] far from the edges. The Biot-Savart [bee-oh suh-var] law describes the strength of these entities when they are induced by an electric current. The magnitudes of these entities can be calculated using Ampère’s [am-peer’s] law. For 10 points, name these vector fields symbolized B, which are measured in teslas.
parts.answer: magnetic fields [accept magnetic after “fields”; accept B-fields before “B”; accept H-fields before “(These entities are) constant”; prompt on vector fields before “fields”]

topics.description: A chemical substance that accepts protons or otherwise neutralizes acids, often producing hydroxide ions and a pH above 7 in aqueous solution.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Many toilet bowl cleaners carry a warning not to mix them with bleach because deadly chloroform gas will result. Answer these questions about the chemistry of other household cleaning products, for ten points each.

parts.label: A
parts.question: Oven cleaners and drain cleaners that contain lye are examples of the “strong” type of these compounds, which have a pH greater than seven.

parts.label: B
parts.question: This term labels soaps like Dawn and Tide, which use surfactants to make grease and fats more soluble in water, and therefore easier to wash away.

parts.label: C
parts.question: Though more common in cooking, this compound, also known as baking soda, can be used to remove odors from laundry and coffee stains from cups.
parts.answer: sodium bicarbonate (accept sodium hydrogen carbonate and bicarbonate of soda; prompt on “bicarbonate”)

parts.label: L
parts.question: The Hammett function replaces this quantity when the molecule in question is more acidic than sulfuric acid. For  10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [M] Name this quantity, the most common measure of acidity. This quantity is equal to the negative log of the  hydrogen ion concentration.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [H] This equation, which gives the pH of a buffer system, equals the pKa of the buffer component, plus the log of a  conjugate pair.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [E] These compounds have a pH above 7. These compounds are the opposite of acids.

topics.description: A proportionality constant in a chemical rate law that quantifies reaction speed under specified conditions and is also used in first-order radioactive-decay kinetics.

parts.label: L
parts.question: The kinetic isotope effect describes how this value for a reaction will change based on which isotopes of the atoms involved are being used. For 10 point each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [M] Name this proportionality constant. The half life of substances undergoing radioactive decay equals the natural log of 2, divided by this quantity.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [H] This approximation is commonly used to derive a rate equation for a reaction whose first step occurs much faster than its second step. This approximation assumes the rate of production and rate of consumption of an intermediate are equal.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [E] Steady-state approximations allow chemists to assume this quantity is constant for an intermediate. The reaction rate of first order reactions depends on the rate constant and this quantity, forms of which include molarity and molality.

parts.label: L
parts.question: This quantity is symbolized “E sub a” and is measured in joules per mole. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this quantity, the minimum amount of energy required for a reaction to occur.

parts.label: B
parts.question: This related quantity has a namesake constant symbolized k. It is the speed at which a chemical reaction occurs.

parts.label: C
parts.question: The rate constant is related to the activation energy in this equation named for a Swedish chemist. This equation also contains a pre-exponential factor.

topics.description: A material composed of at least two elements, including at least one metal, whose properties may differ from those of its constituent elements.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Electrum is one of these materials composed of gold and silver. For ten points each,

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this solid mixtures, usually comprised of two metals, which also include useful materials like bronze and brass.

parts.label: B
parts.question: Nonmetals can form alloys too. For example, this element is alloyed to iron in steel.

parts.label: C
parts.question: Metallurgists often alloy aluminum with this other nonmetal to make them easier to melt. Extremely pure forms of this element are often doped with aluminum, boron, or phosphorus, to increase the number of charge carriers.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: These materials' substitutional type is created by switching one atom for a similar sized atom. When these materials involve mercury, they are called amalgams. Corrosion resistance in one of these materials is achieved by introducing chromium, which makes it “stainless. (*) Examples of these materials that contain copper include bronze and brass. For 10 points, name these materials, which are composed of at least two different metals.

topics.description: An atmospheric condition in which temperature increases with altitude through a layer, reversing the usual decrease and often suppressing convection and trapping pollutants.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Above eight thousand meters, this layer is called the “death zone” because its effective oxygen percentage is just eight percent, compared to twenty-one percent at sea level. For ten points each,

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this lowest region of Earth’s atmosphere, where all weather occurs.

parts.label: B
parts.question: The troposphere over large urban areas like Los Angeles and Mexico City tends to trap this visible, toxic form of air pollution that consists of nitrogen and sulfur oxides.

parts.label: C
parts.question: Urban air tends to trap smog close to the ground because of an inversion of this quantity, which normally decreases with altitude toward the top of the troposphere, where it can drop below negative fifty Celsius.

parts.label: L
parts.question: The 1987 Montreal Protocol banned this general class of chemical compounds. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name these compounds utilized as refrigerants, propellants, and solvents, that react in the  atmosphere to create radicals.

parts.label: B
parts.question: CFCs were the chief contributor to the depletion of this triatomic oxygen molecule.

parts.label: C
parts.question: The absorption of ultraviolet light by the ozone layer causes this phenomenon in the stratosphere, in  which the usual relationship between altitude and another property changes direction.

topics.description: Boron is the group 13 chemical element with atomic number 5 and the lightest metalloid.

parts.label: L
parts.question: This element is an important component of Pyrex glass. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [10] Name this group 13 element that has atomic number 5, the lightest metalloid.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [10] Boron only needs 6 electrons in its valence shell to be stable, violating this law, which says that an element is stable when its valence shell is filled with 8 electrons.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [10] The octet rule can be tracked using dot diagrams named for this chemist. This man also names a definition of acids as electron pair acceptors.
parts.answer: Gilbert [Newton] Lewis [accept Lewis dot diagram[s] or Lewis structure[s]]

parts.label: L
parts.question: Wade’s rules describe hydrides of this element. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [H] Name this lightest metalloid. This element often violates the octet rule by having just six electrons around it.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] Hydrides, by definition, contain at least one atom of this element. This is the lightest element.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [M] In hydrides, Hydrogen usually acts as one of these chemical species. These species have negative charge and form ionic bonds with cations.

topics.description: A group of closely related Galápagos songbird species whose varied beaks exemplify adaptive radiation and provided evidence relevant to natural selection and evolution.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: This scientist noted differently-shaped beaks adapted to different island environments in a group of finches named for him. This man discovered those birds on a journey aboard the HMS (*) Beagle that inspired his treatise On the Origin of Species. The Galapagos Islands' ecology was studied by, for 10 points, what naturalist who formulated the theory of natural selection?

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: Random mating and no migration are two of five conditions that will prevent this process if all met, by the Hardy-Weinberg Principle. The convergent form of this process involves unrelated species developing similar traits. Studying the beaks of finches in the Galapagos prompted (*) Charles Darwin to theorize this process. For ten points, what process is characterized by changes in a species over generations ?

topics.description: A neutral subatomic particle found in atomic nuclei, composed of one up quark and two down quarks, whose number varies among isotopes of an element.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: These particles are emitted in namesake “generators” by the limited fusion of deuterium [doo-TEER-ee-um] and tritium. Roughly 80 percent of ITER’s [EYE-tur’s] energy will be transferred to these particles. In fission reactors, graphite and water have high cross-sections for these particles and are called their namesake (*) “moderators.” These particles are composed of two down quarks and one up quark. In beta-minus decay, one of these particles turns into a neutrino, an electron, and a proton. Different numbers of these particles are found in each isotope of an element. For 10 points, what particles with zero net charge are found in atomic nuclei?
parts.answer: neutrons [accept neutron generators or neutron moderators; reject “neutrinos”]

parts.label: L
parts.question: These particles share the atomic nucleus with, and are slightly more massive than, protons. For ten points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [E] Name these neutrally charged particles, whose number determines the isotope of an atom.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [H] This force holds atomic nuclei together despite the electrical repulsion of neutrons and protons. This force has an extremely small range, the shortest of the four fundamental forces.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [M] Since neutrons and protons are both hadrons, they are made up of these smaller particles held together with gluons. These particles have three colors and six flavors: up, down, top, bottom, strange, and charm.

topics.description: A technique for determining the age of rocks, fossils, and other materials by measuring the predictable radioactive decay of isotopes.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: Drugs are encapsulated inside of delivery vehicles to increase their bioavailability, and therefore, this quantity, which exactly equals “the natural logarithm of 2, divided by a first-order rate constant.” This quantity is estimated to exceed three years for “forever chemicals” known as PFAS. Radiometric dating relies on the fact that this value is exactly 5730 years for carbon-13. For ten points, name this amount of time required for fifty percent of a sample to decay.
parts.answer: half-life (prompt on “time” until it is read)

parts.label: L
parts.question: Willard Libby developed numerous forms of this technique. For ten points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [E] Name this technique that analyzes the decay of radioactive materials to determine the age of geologic substances. The most commonly used form of this technique uses the carbon-14 isotope.
parts.answer: dating [accept radiometric dating or radiocarbon dating or radioactive dating or radioisotope dating or absolute dating or carbon dating]

parts.label: B
parts.question: [M] Due to its presence in many rock formations, the decay of this element into argon is also commonly used to date rocks. This alkali metal commonly found in fertilizers with nitrogen and phosphorus has atomic symbol K.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [H] This isotope’s oxidation into HTO can be used to date water. This radioactive isotope of hydrogen has two neutrons.

topics.description: Marine ecosystems formed primarily by colonies of reef-building corals and other cnidarians that support high biodiversity.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: These ecosystems are threatened by acidification of their surroundings, which can cause them to undergo bleaching. Ring-shaped examples of these ecosystems which enclose a lagoon are called (*) atolls. These ecosystems' namesake animals consist of colonies of thousands of polyps. For 10 points, name these marine biodiversity hotspots which include a "Great Barrier" one off the coast of Australia.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: These locations are the home of a group of organisms whose species include the “staghorn” and “elkhorn." The Great Blue Hole can be found within one of these locations, named after the country of Belize. The largest of the (*) “barrier” type of these locations is located off the coast of Queensland, Australia. For 10 points, name these complex marine ecosystems, which primarily consist of the namesake cnidarians.
parts.answer: coral reefs [prompt on partial answers; or a barrier coral reef]

topics.description: LIGO is a network of laser interferometric observatories that detects gravitational waves by measuring extraordinarily small changes in the lengths of its arms.

parts.label: L
parts.question: The 2017 Nobel Prize in Physics was awarded for contributions to this experiment. For 10 points  each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [10] Name this experiment and group of observatories, which use mirrors four kilometers apart and laser  interferometry to detect changes that are one ten-thousandth the diameter of a proton.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [10] LIGO was designed to detect these disturbances in spacetime that are predicted by general  relativity. The setup first detected these ripples in 2016.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [10] The first gravitational waves detected by LIGO were from a merger of two of these massive objects  that light cannot escape from.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: The currently unsolved hierarchy problem describes the discrepancies in aspects of this force and the weak force . Unlike special relativity, general relativity accounts for this force, the weakest of the fundamental forces. (*) Waves created by this force are detected by LIGO, and this force is most intense in the singularity of a black hole. Weight can be attributed to, for 10 points, what attractive force between two objects?

topics.description: A fibrous structural protein found in vertebrate skin and in structures such as hair, nails, feathers, beaks, and claws.

parts.label: L
parts.question: This human organ has the largest surface area. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this organ, the major component of the integumentary system. The epidermis is the outermost layer of this organ.

parts.label: B
parts.question: The skin contains follicles for these thin protein filaments, which are found most abundantly on the head and can be brushed with a comb.

parts.label: C
parts.question: Hair and fingernails are both abundant in this tough protein. 95% of the epidermis consists of cells that make this protein.

parts.label: L
parts.question: This organ contains numerous mechanoreceptors, including Pacinian (puh-SIN-ee-an) corpuscles and Merkel nerve endings. For ten points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [E] Name this largest organ of the human body, which also acts as its first line of defense against infection. The epidermis is the outermost of the layers of this organ that covers the body.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [M] This pigment in skin can protect humans from UV radiation and can prevent some of the reactions that lead to skin cancer. Dark skin is generally rich in this pigment, the primary determinant of skin color.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [H] This protein is a key structural material in the outer layers of skin in many vertebrates. The hard beta forms of this protein are found in bird beaks and claws, while the softer alpha forms are found in humans’ hair and nails.

topics.description: The amount of three-dimensional space occupied by an object, substance, or thermodynamic system, commonly measured in cubic meters or liters.

parts.label: L
parts.question: The molar form of this quantity is equal to 3R for most solids according to the Dulong Petit law. For 10 points each,

parts.label: A
parts.question: [M] Name this quantity defined as the amount of energy that needs to be added for an object’s temperature to increase by one degree.
parts.answer: ANSWER: heat capacity [accept specific heat capacity]

parts.label: B
parts.question: [H] The ratio of the heat capacity at constant pressure and heat capacity at constant volume gives an “index” described by this term. In this type of thermodynamic process, there is zero heat exchanged.
parts.answer: ANSWER: adiabatic [AY-dee-uh-BAT-ick] [accept adiabatic process or adiabatic index]

parts.label: C
parts.question: [E] An adiabatic process has a constant value for pressure times this quantity to the power of the adiabatic index. This quantity can be expressed in meters cubed or liters.

parts.label: L
parts.question: This law can be derived by substituting Z equals 1 into the virial equation of state. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this law, which states that PV equals nRT.

parts.label: B
parts.question: This generalization of the ideal gas law adds the constants a and b to account for intermolecular forces and  particle size, respectively. It’s named for a Dutch physicist.

parts.label: C
parts.question: Both the V in the ideal gas law and the b in the Van Der Waals equation represent this quantity, measured in  cubic meters. For a rectangular prism, this quantity equals the product of the three side lengths.

topics.description: An optics experiment in which light passes through two slits to produce an interference pattern, demonstrating the wave nature of light.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: This phenomenon disappears with “which-path” information in the delayed-choice quantum eraser experiment. Concentric rings caused by this phenomenon are named after Issac Newton. A device named after this phenomenon used a beam splitter to disprove the existence of luminiferous aether. Along with diffraction, a pattern caused by this phenomenon is visible in Young's double-slit experiment. The constructive and destructive types of this phenomenon result from coherent and correlated waves. For 10 points, name this phenomenon in which two waves combine.

parts.label: L
parts.question: While the wave-particle duality of light is now accepted, this experiment’s namesake believed the wave theory of light to be true. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [H] Name this experiment where light was shone through its namesake openings. It helped disprove the corpuscular theory of light.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [M] A pattern due to this phenomenon appears in Young’s double-slit experiment. It has constructive and destructive types.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [E] While Young’s double-slit experiment was typically reproduced using beams of light, Claus Jönsson used a beam of these negatively charged particles which orbit the atomic nucleus.

topics.description: A substance added to soil or plants to supply essential nutrients and support plant growth and crop production.

parts.label: L
parts.question: For 10 points each, answer the following about advances in agricultural technology:

parts.label: A
parts.question: Medieval Europe saw the introduction of the three-field system of this process, in which one field was planted with oats or lentils and another left fallow. George Washington Carver advocated performing this process with legumes to increase the nitrogen content of soil.

parts.label: B
parts.question: The 20th century Green Revolution saw a dramatic spike in crop production due to the use of pesticides and this technology. This general class of substances includes any material added to soil to provide plant nutrients.

parts.label: C
parts.question: This scientist’s work in Mexico led him to breed wheat varieties resistant to rust. This “father of the Green revolution” is credited with saving over a billion people from starvation by developing semi-dwarf wheat.

parts.label: L
parts.question: To supplement your college fund, you’ve decided to become an organic tomato farmer. Answer these horticultural questions, for ten points each.

parts.label: A
parts.question: You can use compost or manure as an organic one of these nutrient supplements for your crop. These substances should contain sufficient levels of nitrogen, phosphorus, and potassium.

parts.label: B
parts.question: If your leaves turn yellow, it’s a good bet that the soil is deficient in magnesium, a necessary component of this plant pigment.

parts.label: C
parts.question: Fortunately, you no longer have to worry about convincing customers that tomatoes are edible, unlike their relatives henbane and belladonna in this plant family.

topics.description: The number of individual organisms belonging to a population within a specified area or environment.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: Pierre Verhulst introduced a logistic function to model the growth of this quantity, which Thomas Malthus theorized a geometric increase for. The value of this quantity for an environment is limited by a constant symbolized K, the (*) carrying capacity. Since the Black Death, this quantity for humans has consistently increased. For 10 points, name this quantity stating the number of organisms in a certain area.
parts.answer: population size [accept number of humans or organisms before mentioned]

parts.label: L
parts.question: One of the assumptions of the Hardy-Weinberg principle is that this quantity is infinite. For 10  points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [10] Name this quantity, which is the number of individual organisms in a given area.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [10] This type of physical sampling method is used to estimate a population size without having to count  every individual.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [10] The maximum population size for an environment given the resources available is defined by this  quantity, often symbolized K.

topics.description: A gas law stating that the pressure and volume of a fixed amount of gas are inversely proportional at constant temperature.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: One improvement of a statement which describes these substances uses an a and b term to represent intermolecular forces and volume. These substances are described by the Van der Waals equation. Boyle’s law states that pressure and volume are inversely related in these substances. Kinetic molecular (*) theory assumes that these substances exist at high temperatures and low pressures. For 10 points, name this theoretical substance whose namesake law states that PV = nRT.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Bernoulli’s principle states that when fluid speed increases, either potential energy or this quantity must decrease. For ten points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this quantity that is directly proportional to temperature according to Gay-Lussac’s Law. This force per unit area’s atmospheric type can be measured with a barometer and is commonly expressed in torrs, pascals, and psi.

parts.label: B
parts.question: Pressure is multiplied by volume on one side of an equation that describes the “ideal” form of this phase of matter, PV=nRT. This phase of matter has no fixed shape and higher kinetic energy than solids and liquids.

parts.label: C
parts.question: The ideal gas law is a combination of Avogadro’s Law, Gay-Lussac’s Law, Charles’s Law, and this law. This law relates pressure and volume and is typically expressed as P-one V-one equals P-two V-two

topics.description: A chronic immune-mediated neurological disease involving damage to myelin in the central nervous system, with progressive or relapsing-remitting symptoms.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Electrical signals are passed between these cells, axon-to-dendrite, through small gaps called synapses. For ten points each,

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name these cells that transmit signals throughout the nervous system.

parts.label: B
parts.question: To avoid unwanted electrical signals from popping off, neural axons are sheathed in an insulating layer of this fatty material. Small gaps in it are present at nodes of Ranvier.

parts.label: C
parts.question: Loss of myelin leads to nervous system collapse in this debilitating disease, which scars white matter and often occurs in relapsing-remitting courses in patients. Its cause is still unknown.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Answer some questions about the myelin sheath, for 10 points each: For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: The myelin sheath covers some cells in this body system which includes the brain, spinal cord, and its namesake structures, which transmit electrical impulses throughout the body to communicate with the brain.

parts.label: B
parts.question: The myelin sheath covers this part of a nerve cell. Each nerve cell has one of these long protrusions which carry electrical impulses, along with many dendrites.

parts.label: C
parts.question: In this medical condition, the myelin sheath is degraded, inhibiting neurological function. It is typically divided into "progressive" and "relapsing-remitting" types.

topics.description: American geneticist whose Drosophila experiments established that genes are carried on chromosomes and helped explain genetic linkage and inheritance.

parts.label: L
parts.question: This biologist “invented” the “auto-sexing chicken,” which apparently make it easier for breeders to classify them as male or female. For ten points each,

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this British scientist whose important work on industrial agriculture is mostly dwarfed by his frankly self-explanatory “square” diagram that predicts the probability of how Mendelian genes are inherited.

parts.label: B
parts.question: Punnett squares are pretty useless in practice due to gene linkage, an effect first described by this American scientist. He is reviled by biologists today for his efforts in making the pesky fruit fly a model organism.

parts.label: C
parts.question: Fly-hating biologists would probably prefer to work with Punnett squares and these plants, Gregor Mendel’s favorite vegetables to study, because they are easy to see and don’t move.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Inheritance named for this man can be visualized through Punnett Squares. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this Austrian monk who published his results on pea plant hybridization. He introduced the laws of Segregation, Dominance, and Independent Assortment.

parts.label: B
parts.question: Mendel coined this term to describe alleles that are often masked by their dominant counterparts. Two copies of these alleles are required to express their trait.

parts.label: C
parts.question: This scientist’s work related to the ideas of Mendelian inheritance showed that genes are carried on chromosomes. He studied Drosophila melanogaster, the fruit fly.

topics.description: A region or state containing little or no matter and therefore having very low pressure, with idealized cases used in classical and quantum physics.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: A McLeod gauge is attached to equipment operating under this condition, which minimizes heat conduction within a Dewar flask. This phenomenon exists between Magdeburg hemispheres, and is found above the mercury (*) column in a Torricelli barometer. Robert Boyle designed an air pump to prove that sound cannot travel through this medium. Aristotle said that “nature abhors,” for ten points, what condition in which a space is entirely devoid of matter?

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: “False” examples of these things exist at local instead of global energy minima, and can spontaneously collapse through bubble nucleation. Quantum fluctuations generating virtual electron-positron pairs cause these things to become polarized. Uncharged plates separated by one of these things feel an attractive force in the Casimir effect. (*) Epsilon-naught represents the electric permittivity of this medium. In introductory physics, most mechanics problems take place in a frictionless example of this medium, since it lacks any drag forces or pressure. For 10 points, name these regions devoid of matter.
parts.answer: vacuums [accept perfect vacuum or frictionless vacuum; accept free space]

topics.description: The domesticated equid descended from the African wild ass, also known as an ass or burro.

parts.label: L
parts.question: God allowed this figure to regain his super strength one last time so he could collapse the Temple of Dagon, killing the people gathered within. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [M] Name this Biblical judge who originally loses his super strength when his lover Delilah cuts his hair.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] Samson was constantly at odds with the Philistines, who were later defeated when David killed this giant with a slingshot.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [H] Samson once destroyed an entire Philistine army with the jawbone of one of these animals. Balaam owned a talking one of these animals.

parts.label: L
parts.question: This novel’s title character reads too many romantic novels, convinces himself that he’s a knight, and rides around on his elderly horse, Rocinante, getting into trouble. For ten points each,

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this Spanish novel by Miguel de Cervantes [ser-VON-tays] about a man who attacks windmills because he imagines they’re giants.
parts.answer: Don Quijote [kee-HOH-tay] (accept The Ingenious Gentleman Don Quijote of La Mancha; accept El Ingenioso hidalgo Don Quixote de la Mancha)

parts.label: B
parts.question: Don Quijote [don kee-HOH-tay] is accompanied on his misguided adventures by this man, his long-suffering servant.

parts.label: C
parts.question: While traveling with Don Quijote, Sancho Panza rides Dapple, a gray-brown one of these long-eared, horse-like animals.

topics.description: A small rodent commonly represented in literature and zoological contexts, including Robert Burns’s “To a Mouse,” Despereaux, and Stuart Little.

parts.label: L
parts.question: In a poem about this insect, the speaker wishes for the gift “to see ourselves as others see us” and calls this bug a “crowlan ferlie.” For ten points each,

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this parasitic insect, the subject of a poem by Robert Burns that discusses “Seeing One on a Lady’s Bonnet at Church.”
parts.answer: louse (accept lice; accept To a Louse, On Seeing One on a Lady’s Bonnet at Church)

parts.label: B
parts.question: In another poem by Burns, this small rodent is called a “wee, sleeket, cowran, tim’rous beastie.” The poem reflects that “the best laid plans of” these animals “and men / oft go awry.”
parts.answer: mouse (accept mice; accept To a Mouse, On Turning her up in her Nest, with the Plough, November 1785)

parts.label: C
parts.question: Robert Burns called the louse a “crowlan ferlie” and the mouse a “tim’rous beastie” because he often wrote in the common dialect of this country, his home nation, which merged with England in 1707 to form Great Britain.
parts.answer: Scotland (accept Scottish; do not accept or prompt on “United Kingdom” or “UK”)

parts.label: L
parts.question: In this book, a librarian describes the Littmus Lozenge candies that were mixed with melancholy. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: Opal Buloni moves to Naomi, Florida, to live with her preacher father in this children's book, named after the dog she finds there.

parts.label: B
parts.question: Because of Winn-Dixie was written by this American author of The Tale of Despereaux.

parts.label: C
parts.question: The title character of The Tale of Despereaux is one of these cheese-loving rodents, as is E. B. White's Stuart Little.

topics.description: A specialized processor with many parallel computing units that accelerates image rendering and other highly parallel computations.

parts.label: L
parts.question: For ten points each, name some pieces of computer hardware.

parts.label: A
parts.question: [E] The QWERTY layout is the most widely used in these pieces of hardware because it is deliberately inefficient to reduce jamming. These devices are used to type numbers and letters into computers.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [M] These devices contain components like the ALU and registers, and their clock rate is typically measured in gigahertz. These devices execute instructions and do most of the computations for computers.
parts.answer: CPU or central processing unit [accept central processor or main processor or just processor]

parts.label: C
parts.question: [H] These devices with a similar name to CPUs are specialized circuits that use numerous computing units to operate on pixels. These devices accelerate the creation of images for output to a display device.
parts.answer: GPU or graphics processing unit [accept VPU or visual processing unit; prompt on integrated graphics or video card or graphics card or display card or graphics adaptor or display adaptor]

parts.label: L
parts.question: Answer some questions about computer components. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: These components were the focus of the race to 5 gigahertz, and can have one or multiple cores. Manufacturers of these components include Intel.
parts.answer: processors [accept central processing units or CPUs]

parts.label: B
parts.question: Primary manufacturers of these components include NVidia and AMD, and later iterations of these components have included hardware-accelerated ray tracing.
parts.answer: graphics cards [accept graphics processing units or GPUs]

parts.label: C
parts.question: Computers use these devices to display things to users. In laptop computers, these screens are typically attached to the rest of the computer, while desktop computers often have separate versions.

topics.description: A specialized nervous-system cell that transmits electrical and chemical signals, with structures such as axons and dendrites.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Electrical signals are passed between these cells, axon-to-dendrite, through small gaps called synapses. For ten points each,

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name these cells that transmit signals throughout the nervous system.

parts.label: B
parts.question: To avoid unwanted electrical signals from popping off, neural axons are sheathed in an insulating layer of this fatty material. Small gaps in it are present at nodes of Ranvier.

parts.label: C
parts.question: Loss of myelin leads to nervous system collapse in this debilitating disease, which scars white matter and often occurs in relapsing-remitting courses in patients. Its cause is still unknown.

parts.label: L
parts.question: This scientist names a sensory receptor that senses changes in muscle tension. For ten points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [H] Name this Italian scientist who names a cell organelle that modifies and packages proteins into vesicles to be sent to their final destination.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [M] Golgi also names a staining method that is used to visualize tissue made of these cells. These cells primarily found in the brain consist of axons and dendrites and are separated by synapses.
parts.answer: neuron or neurone or nerve cell

parts.label: C
parts.question: [E] The Golgi reaction was initially named after the fact that it stains neurons this color. This color is produced by the absence or complete absorption of light.

topics.description: A transparent optical device with refracting surfaces that focuses, diverges, or otherwise shapes light.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Diopters (DYE-op-terz) measure the strength of mirrors and these other devices. For ten points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name these devices, typically made of glass or plastic, that focus or disperse light. Common examples of these devices are found in cameras and in glasses.

parts.label: B
parts.question: Lenses work by means of this process, in which waves traveling between media change direction. This process is the reason why objects seem to bend when placed partly in water, and is contrasted with reflection.

parts.label: C
parts.question: This optical law relates the angles of incidence to indices of refraction and so can be used to determine how bent objects placed in water appear.

parts.label: L
parts.question: A convex example of these devices on top of a planar surface can result in Newton's rings. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name these devices, typically made from glass, that are used to focus light.

parts.label: B
parts.question: The thin lens equation states that the reciprocal of the object distance plus the reciprocal of the image distance equals the reciprocal of this quantity.

parts.label: C
parts.question: The reciprocal of focal length gives the optical power, which is typically measured in this SI unit equivalent to an inverse meter.

topics.description: The vertebral column, a series of vertebrae extending from the neck to the coccyx that supports the body and encloses the spinal cord.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: Hypertrophy of this structure’s ligamenta flava can led to stenosis. Parts of this structure have pedicles that attach to transverse and superior articular processes. VCFS and burst fractures in this structure cause damage to tissue within it responsible for motor function. In Scheuermann’s (*) Kyphosis, parts of this structure become wedged together in its thoracic or lumbar region. This structure takes an S or C shape in scoliosis. Herniated discs lay between 33 vertically stacked bones that make up this structure that ends at the coccyx. For 10 points, name this long series of bones that runs down the back.
parts.answer: spine [or spinal column or vertebral column or backbone; reject “spinal cord”]

parts.label: L
parts.question: After this god was murdered by his brother, Set, his body was dismembered and scattered across Egypt. For ten points each,

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this green-skinned Egyptian ruler of the underworld.
parts.answer: Osiris (accept Usiris; accept Aser; accept Usire)

parts.label: B
parts.question: This sister-wife of Osiris collected his body parts and put him back together after Set’s attack. After temporarily reviving Osiris, this goddess gives birth to Horus.
parts.answer: Isis (accept Aset; accept Iset; accept Ase)

parts.label: C
parts.question: In some tellings of the myth, the body parts of Osiris had symbolic meaning; this part is associated with the djed column or pillar, which symbolizes stability. Egyptian mummies often had djed amulets kept near this body part.

topics.description: An object or device that produces a magnetic field, with north and south poles, capable of attracting or repelling magnetic materials and deflecting compass needles.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: Extremely strong types of these objects can be made out of rare earth metals such as neodymium. These objects generate a field which is measured in Teslas, and iron filings will (*) align themselves in arcs around these objects. Holding one of these objects near a compass needle will deflect it. For 10 points, what objects have North and South poles which attract each other?

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: At low temperatures, molecules with unpaired electrons act like these devices. Neodymium is mixed with iron and boron in a particularly strong class of these devices. Passing an (*) electric current through a coil of wire turns it into one of these things called a solenoid. These devices cause iron fillings to line up between their north and south poles. For ten points, name these devices used in compasses and to attract metals.
parts.answer: magnets (accept specific types of magnets, including bar magnets and electromagnets)

topics.description: The diverse clade of extinct reptiles that dominated terrestrial ecosystems during the Mesozoic Era and includes groups such as velociraptors, triceratops, Tyrannosaurus rex, and Stegosaurus.

parts.label: L
parts.question: The extinction of these organisms may have been caused by the eruption of the Deccan Traps. For ten points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [E] Name these organisms wiped out by a mass extinction event that ended the Cretaceous period. Examples of these organisms include velociraptors and triceratops.
parts.answer: dinosaurs [accept dinosauria; prompt on animals or animalia, prompt on chordates or chordata or vertebrates]

parts.label: B
parts.question: [H] The Alvarez hypothesis posits that the mass extinction of dinosaurs was caused by an impact event, based on the presence of the “shocked” form of this mineral. This mineral’s formula is silicon dioxide.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [M] The Alvarez hypothesis was theorized based on the Chicxulub (CHICK-suh-loob) crater located in this country. Many examples of fossil evidence for an instantaneous extinction event can be found in this country’s Yucatan peninsula.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: In one novel, a drawing of one of these animals in Maple White’s sketchbook helps convince Daily Gazette reporter E. D. Malone to join an expedition. Eckels steps on a butterfly after paying ten thousand dollars to shoot one of these animals in “A Sound of Thunder.” Professor Challenger discovers a South-American plateau inhabited by these animals in Sir Arthur Conan Doyle’s novel (*) The Lost World. InGen discovers how to clone these animals from the blood of mosquitoes trapped in amber in a Michael Crichton novel in which they escape their enclosures on Isla Nublar. For 10 points, name these animals that are brought back from extinction in Jurassic Park.
parts.answer: dinosaurs [accept specific dinosaurs like Stegosaurus or Tyrannosaurus rex or Velociraptor]

topics.description: The chemical element helium, a colorless noble gas with atomic number 2 that is involved in stellar helium fusion and has applications including balloons, cryogenics, and lasers.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Stars at the tip of the red giant branch can serve as “standard candles” when calculating this quantity. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [E] Name this quantity that may be expressed in light-years or parsecs.
parts.answer: distance [accept answers indicating how far an object is from Earth]

parts.label: B
parts.question: [M] The tip of the red giant branch is a feature on this diagram, which plots the luminosity of stars against their temperature. A diagonal line across this diagram represents the “main sequence.”

parts.label: C
parts.question: [H] When stars leave the tip of the red giant branch, they experience a “flash” named after this element, in which it is rapidly fused into carbon.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: This element is used with neon in the gain medium of a common type of laser used in barcode scanners. The nucleus of the most common isotope of this element is identical to an alpha particle, and this gas can be inhaled to make the pitch of one’s voice (*) higher than normal due to its low density. This gas is often put into party balloons to make them lighter than air. For ten points, name this lightest noble gas, which has chemical symbol He.

topics.description: A potentially fatal syndrome caused by advanced infection with human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) that severely damages the immune system.

parts.label: L
parts.question: A mural in Barcelona shows numerous dancing red figures to the left of Spanish words translating to “Together We Can Stop [this disease].” For ten points each,

parts.label: A
parts.question: [M] Name this disease which took the life of Keith Haring before he was able to complete a purposefully unfinished self-portrait.
parts.answer: AIDS [accept Todos Juntos Podemos Parar el SIDA; prompt on HIV]

parts.label: B
parts.question: [H] The largest piece of folk art ever created was one of these artworks to recognize AIDS victims in 1985. Faith Ringgold creates “story” examples of these artworks.
parts.answer: quilts [accept story quilts; accept the AIDS quilt]

parts.label: C
parts.question: [E] Haring created artworks in this artistic medium, in which images are spray painted onto urban walls.

parts.label: L
parts.question: One member of this profession is a drag queen who takes care of Prior Walter. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [E] Name this profession of Belize in Angels in America. It’s not a doctor, but, in Ken Kesey’s One Flew Over the Cuckoo’s Nest, Ratched has this profession, whose members take care of patients in hospitals.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [H] Angels in America is by this playwright, who also wrote A Bright Room Called Day.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [M] An epidemic regarding this disease is central to Angels in America. Roy Cohn hoards AZT to treat this disease.

topics.description: A human-infecting lentivirus that progressively damages the immune system and can cause acquired immunodeficiency syndrome (AIDS).

parts.label: L
parts.question: This virus is the only one in the genus Lentivirus to infect humans, and can be treated with drugs that inhibit CD4-Positive cells. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [10] Name this sexually-transmitted virus. Patients who suffer from it often experience Kaposi's sarcoma, and it may eventually lead to AIDS.
parts.answer: HIV [or human immunodeficiency virus; accept HIV/AIDS]

parts.label: B
parts.question: [10] This bacterial disease is one of the most common causes of death for AIDS patients. This disease was historically known as consumption and infects the lungs.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [10] HIV is a member of this class of viruses. They insert a copy of their genome into the DNA of their host cells by using reverse transcriptase, an enzyme which transcribes RNA into DNA.

parts.label: L
parts.question: The ribonuclease H domain in these viruses degrades the U5 and R regions of one molecule. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name these viruses, which use reverse transcriptase to create complementary strands of DNA from RNA. Lentiviruses are a subtype of these viruses.

parts.label: B
parts.question: The pol gene encodes for reverse transcriptase in this bloodborne retrovirus, the causative agent of AIDS.

parts.label: C
parts.question: HIV targets these cells by attacking their CD4 surface receptor. Unlike B cells, these cells mature in the thymus.

topics.description: A broad class of synthetic, moldable materials composed primarily of polymers and used to make products such as bags, bottles, and straws.

parts.label: L
parts.question: The polydispersity index characterizes the mass distribution of these molecules. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name these large molecules, which are composed of repeating units of monomers.

parts.label: B
parts.question: The glass transition temperature of polymers can be measured using the differential scanning type of these devices. A constant-pressure type of these devices, used for combustion, puts the sample in a “bomb.”
parts.answer: calorimeter [accept differential scanning calorimeter; accept bomb calorimeter]

parts.label: C
parts.question: This general class of materials consists of hydrocarbon polymers. The LDPE type of this material is used in bags.

parts.label: L
parts.question: These compounds can be produced through step-growth and chain-growth reactions. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [M] Name these compounds made of repeating units called monomers. Nylon and PVC are examples of these macromolecules.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] PVC is a “thermo” one of these materials that can be molded easily. These materials, which are made up of polymers, are used to produce objects like water bottles and straws.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [H] This compound, which is also a thermoplastic, is a polymer composed of tetrafluoroethylene monomers. This compound is often used in non-stick cookware

topics.description: An infectious bacterial disease caused primarily by Mycobacterium tuberculosis, commonly affecting the lungs and historically known as consumption.

parts.label: L
parts.question: This virus is the only one in the genus Lentivirus to infect humans, and can be treated with drugs that inhibit CD4-Positive cells. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [10] Name this sexually-transmitted virus. Patients who suffer from it often experience Kaposi's sarcoma, and it may eventually lead to AIDS.
parts.answer: HIV [or human immunodeficiency virus; accept HIV/AIDS]

parts.label: B
parts.question: [10] This bacterial disease is one of the most common causes of death for AIDS patients. This disease was historically known as consumption and infects the lungs.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [10] HIV is a member of this class of viruses. They insert a copy of their genome into the DNA of their host cells by using reverse transcriptase, an enzyme which transcribes RNA into DNA.

parts.label: L
parts.question: The transgender scientist Alan Hart discovered that x-rays could be used to detect this disease. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this “White Death” which spread rapidly from horse carcasses and human waste on American city streets in the late 1800s. This lung disease was once called consumption.

parts.label: B
parts.question: The belief in an “open air” cure for TB led American builders to add windows and these features to structures. William McKinley rarely traveled outside of Ohio during an 1896 campaign strategy named for these features.
parts.answer: porches [or front porches; accept front porch campaigns]

parts.label: C
parts.question: This modern-day state was nicknamed the “World’s Sanitarium” since one-third of its residents were tuberculosis victims. The Fifty-Niners settled this state where the Ludlow Massacre of coal miners occured.

topics.description: The gradual reduction of an oscillator’s amplitude or motion due to energy loss from resistive forces such as friction.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Answer some questions about the motion of pendulums, for 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [E] This quantity equals the amount of time it takes for the pendulum to return to its original position and complete one full  cycle. Frequency equals one over this quantity.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [M] The “simple harmonic” type of this type of motion is exemplified by the motion of pendulums. This term is used to refer  to motion that is periodic.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [H] In this process, an external force, such as friction, slows down the oscillation of a pendulum, eventually causing it to stop.  Taipei 101 contains an enormous steel ball that is tuned to the tower’s resonant frequency to perform this process.

parts.label: L
parts.question: A harmonic oscillator is an object that, when it moves away from its natural position, experiences a force that acts to restore it to that position. For ten points each,

parts.label: A
parts.question: Grandfather clocks feature these harmonic oscillators, which naturally hang straight down and swing from left to right.

parts.label: B
parts.question: When the harmonic oscillator is this type of compressible coil, then the formula for the restoring force is called Hooke’s Law.

parts.label: C
parts.question: A harmonic oscillator may be simple, in which the only force acting on it is the restoring force, or it may have this feature, in which another force counters the restoring force and reduces the oscillation.
parts.answer: damping (accept word forms and additional information, like damped oscillator)

topics.description: The light-sensitive tissue layer at the back of the eye that contains photoreceptors and transmits visual signals toward the optic nerve.

parts.label: L
parts.question: VEGF inhibitors can be used to lessen the effects of the “wet” form of this disease. For 10 points:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [H] Name this eye disease that results in a loss of central vision. Drusen buildups cause the “dry” form of this disease.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [M] Drusen builds up behind the pigmented layer of this part of the eye. This layer of tissue is home to photoreceptor cells like rods and cones.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [E] Another common cause of vision loss is cataracts, which occur when this structure is cloudy. This transparent structure focuses light onto the retina.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Macular degeneration causes blurred vision by damaging a section of this part of the eye. For 10  points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this structure at the back of the eye that processes light and transmits signals to the optic  nerve.

parts.label: B
parts.question: The retina contains cones and this other photoreceptor cell mainly responsible for peripheral vision.

parts.label: C
parts.question: Rods are also responsible for night vision, which is accomplished through this G-protein coupled  receptor that is also known as “visual purple.”

topics.description: The phase change in which a liquid, especially water, becomes vapor at or near its surface and enters the gas phase.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: This process is responsible for the formation of minerals such as borax and halite, and it also  names that class of minerals. The rate of this process can be calculated by how much the level in a  Class A pan drops over twenty-four hours. Wet-bulb temperature is lower than dry-bulb  temperature in (*) unsaturated air due to this process's cooling effect. This process is one of the three  steps in the water cycle along with condensation and precipitation. For 10 points, name this process in  which water becomes a gas and enters the atmosphere.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: Distillation separates substances in a mixture by using this process and then condensing the products. During transpiration, plants cool themselves via this process, which also cools human skin when it occurs to sweat. This process occurs just before (*) condensation in the water cycle. For 10 points, name this phase change that occurs to water when heated, the transition of a liquid to a gas.

topics.description: Hairlike cellular structures that can propel cells or move material across a cell surface, with primary cilia also serving signaling functions.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: These structures make up the iridescent “combs” of comb jellies. Vorticella [vor-tih-SELL-uh] and Stentor belong to a phylum named for these structures in which cells have two differently sized nuclei. The “primary” type of these structures is involved in cell signaling rather than movement and contains a “nine plus zero” arrangement of (*) microtubules [micro-TUBE-yoolz]. Other examples of these structures push dirt and mucus out of the human respiratory tract through a continuous beating motion, which is contrasted with the whip- or corkscrew-like motion of flagella [fluh-JEL-uh]. For 10 points, name these cellular structures that resemble hairs.
parts.answer: cilia [SIL-ee-uh] or cilium [accept primary cilia or motile cilia; accept ciliates or Ciliophora]

parts.label: L
parts.question: Stentor, Euglena, and Spirogyra are among the organisms that can be seen in a drop of pond water examined under one of these devices. For ten points each,

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this optical device with a stage and eyepiece, whose compound type may have maximum magnification of one thousand times.

parts.label: B
parts.question: Careful examination of a pond water slide is needed to find this type of slow, amorphous protozoan that moves by pseudopods and engulfs its prey by phago-cytosis.
parts.answer: amoeba (accept amoebae or amoebas; accept ameboids)

parts.label: C
parts.question: In contrast to an amoeba, Paramecia appear to move quickly under the microscope because they are covered in these stiff, hair-like structures that beat back and forth.

topics.description: A photosynthetic organelle found in plant and algal cells that converts light energy into chemical energy.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Name some quirks of plant cells, for ten points each.

parts.label: A
parts.question: Perhaps the most meaningful quirk, compared to animal cells, is that plant cells have these organelles where photosynthesis occurs.

parts.label: B
parts.question: Plant cells have a rigid wall made of cellulose, which maintains turgidity. By contrast, animal cells just have this flexible and semipermeable lipid bilayer, which lets water freely in and out.
parts.answer: cell membrane (accept plasma membrane or PM)

parts.label: C
parts.question: Although plants use cellulose in their cell walls, animals can’t make it. The closest structural polysaccharide made by animals is this polymer of N-acetyl-glucosamine, which comprises the cell walls of many fungi as well as the exoskeletons of insects.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: It's not the mitochondrion, but this organelle is believed to have originated through endosymbiosis. "Light" and "dark" reactions are part of a process that takes place in this organelle and converts carbon dioxide and water into (*) glucose. The presence of a pigment in these organelles is responsible for plant leaves' green color. For 10 points, in what plant organelles does photosynthesis occur?

topics.description: The hard, highly mineralized outer tissue covering the crowns of teeth, composed primarily of hydroxyapatite and subject to demineralization by acids and bacterial activity.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Deposits from the GCF onto these structures cause the buildup of hardened plaque called tartar. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [M] Name these anatomical structures, which have canine,molar and incisor types.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [H] This mineralized substance on the teeth is composed primarily of hydroxyapatite and can be degraded by dental caries.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [E] Dental cavities can be prevented by using toothpaste enriched with an anion of this most electronegative element, with symbol F.

parts.label: L
parts.question: This organ’s eight muscles include ones originating from the styloid process and the hyoid bone. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [H] Name this papilla-studded muscular organ. An abnormality in the shape of the frenulum that anchors this organ causes ankyloglossia.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] The tongue and mouth are lubricated by this substance, secreted by the parotid and submandibular glands. This substance is used to wet the mouth and conduct chemicals to taste receptors, and it contains digestive and antimicrobial enzymes such as amylase.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [M] Saliva carries the calcium, fluoride and phosphate ions deposited in this outer layer of the teeth in the process of remineralization. This hard white tissue covering the crowns requires daily repair because of damage from acidic foods and bacteria.

topics.description: A measure of an organism’s relative evolutionary and reproductive success, including its ability to survive, reproduce, and pass genes to the next generation.

parts.label: L
parts.question: A multidimensional “landscape” named for this quantity plots genotype against it, and generally assumes that successful organisms fall into local minima. For ten points each,

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this quantity that broadly translates to “evolutionary success,” since individuals with the greatest amount of it survive to reproduce.
parts.answer: biological fitness (accept word forms like fittest)

parts.label: B
parts.question: The concept of survival of the fittest drives this mechanism of evolution, which was postulated by Charles Darwin in The Origin of Species.

parts.label: C
parts.question: The notion that natural selection slowly explores rugged fitness landscapes, in which successful adaptations are very shallow local ditches, is challenged by this more radical theory of rapid-bursts of successful trait evolution, proposed by Stephen Jay Gould.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: The rate of increase in this quantity is equal to genetic variance according to Fisher's  fundamental theorem. The frequency of a particular genotype in a population will decrease if it  has a low value for this quantity. The “inclusive” form of this quantity is increased in (*) kin  selection, and parental investment is a strategy to increase this quantity. Inbreeding decreases this  quantity, which in sterile animals is zero. For 10 points, name this measure of an organism's ability to  pass its genes on to the next generation.

topics.description: Bosons are particles with integer spin that are not subject to the Pauli exclusion principle and can occupy the same quantum state, including particles such as photons, W and Z bosons, and the Higgs boson.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Gell-Mann and Zweig proposed the existence of these particles, which Gell-Mann named after a line from James Joyce's Finnegans Wake. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [10] Name these elementary particles that come in 6 "flavors", such as the down and up types, and make up protons and neutrons.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [10] Quarks belong in a class of particles along with leptons named after this Italian scientist, who also formulated a thought experiment asking "where are the aliens?"

parts.label: C
parts.question: [10] Fermions are contrasted with this other type of subatomic particle named for an Indian physicist and whose types include W, Z, and one named for Higgs.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Lithium niobate is a crystal employed in circuits that use these particles instead of electrons. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [E] Name these massless particles that carry the electromagnetic force. These particles are the quanta of light.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [M] The high error rate of the photonic circuits used in these devices has led critics to claim that these devices cannot attain “supremacy.” These devices use bits that are capable of superimposing into more than two states.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [H] Photonic circuits are used to implement a quantum computation model that “samples” from particles of this type. These particles are not affected by the exclusion principle and can thus exist in the same quantum state.

topics.description: The light-independent cycle of photosynthetic reactions in the chloroplast stroma that fixes carbon dioxide and produces carbohydrate.

parts.label: L
parts.question: The light-dependent reactions of photosynthesis take place on the membrane of these components of  chloroplasts. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [10] Name these disk-shaped components that are arranged in stacks known as grana.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [10] Just outside of the thylakoid membrane is the site of this process of carbon fixation, reduction, and  regeneration, named for an American chemist.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [10] The first stage of the Calvin cycle uses up two molecules of this compound, which is known as the  energy currency of the cell.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: The Z-scheme is a part of this process in which the oxygen evolution reaction produces electrons that are donated to P680. The Calvin cycle in this process uses RuBP (r-u-b-p) and RuBisCO to convert carbon dioxide and other compounds into (*) glucose, and is called the light-independent phase of this process. For ten points, name this process which occurs in chloroplasts where light is converted into energy for plants.

topics.description: Corn is the cereal grass crop Zea mays, domesticated from teosinte and cultivated for food, feed, and industrial products.

parts.label: L
parts.question: This crop’s wild ancestor, teosinte [tee-oh-SIN-tee], has only 5 to 10 seeds in each pod. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [M] Name this staple crop in the genus Zea [ZEE-uh], a member of the Three Sisters. Types of it include “field” and “sweet.”

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] In the U.S., corn is often processed into a type of syrup “high” in this sugar that is sweeter than glucose. As its name suggests, it is common in fruits.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [H] While studying inheritance in corn, Barbara McClintock discovered these genetic elements that include LINEs [lines] and SINEs [sines]. They make up about 50 percent of the human genome.
parts.answer: transposons [or transposable elements or jumping genes]

parts.label: L
parts.question: Tofu and edamame are both made from this plant. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [10] Name this nitrogen-fixing legume which is the most valuable U.S. agricultural export. A "textured vegetable product" made from this crop is a common meat substitute.
parts.answer: soybeans [or the soy plant or soya]

parts.label: B
parts.question: [10] This company, which has been acquired by Bayer, made a genetically modified soybean that was immune to its Roundup pesticide and the first commercial potato plants that produced the insecticide Bt.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [10] Soybeans are primarily grown in the U.S. in the Midwest, a region which is also noted for its production of this crop. This food can be eaten "on the cob" or processed into a namesake "high fructose syrup".

topics.description: Visual organs containing light-sensitive structures that detect light and support vision.

parts.label: L
parts.question: The Aye-Aye species of this primate is the largest nocturnal primate in the world. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [H] Name these primates whose most widely recognized species is the “ring-tailed” one. This primate is endemic to an island also home to most species of the baobab tree and the Malagasy people.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [M] Lemurs are endemic to this extremely biodiverse island nation, separated from mainland Africa by the Mozambique Channel.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [E] Lemurs are the only primates other than humans to possess blue features in these organs. Lemurs possess large examples of these organs, allowing them to see well at night.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: Diabetics are particularly susceptible to a disease in which this body part’s drainage angle remains open, leading to a buildup of aqueous humor. Conjunctivitis inflames part of this organ, which is also affected by (*) astigmatisms. Other parts of this organ are affected by macular degeneration and cataracts in the lenses. For ten points, name this sensory organ in which glaucoma is a leading cause of blindness.
parts.answer: eye (accept lens; accept cornea; accept retina)

topics.description: Regions of high-energy charged particles trapped by Earth's magnetic field in the magnetosphere.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: The third object with this name contained faulty components that prevented it from mapping the Van Allen belt during the International Geophysical Year. A dog named (*) Laika became the first animal in space aboard the second of these objects and, in 1957, the first object with this name kicked off the Space Race. For ten points, name this series of Soviet spacecraft that included Earth’s first artificial satellite.
parts.answer: Sputnik program (accept Sputnik 1, 2, or 3; prompt on “satellite” before it is read)

parts.label: L
parts.question: For 10 points each, answer the following about challenges to space exploration posed by ionizing radiation:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [E] Without the protection of earth’s atmosphere and magnetic field, spacecraft are exposed to the “wind” of charged particles emitted by this body at the center of the Solar System.
parts.answer: the Sun [or Sol; accept solar wind]

parts.label: B
parts.question: [H] Some particles from the solar wind can become trapped by Earth’s magnetosphere, forming these regions of high-energy protons and electrons. These regions named for an American physicist pose a serious hazard to electronics passing through them.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [M] In addition to the solar wind, the Van Allen belts can trap these rays that originate outside the Solar System. These rays made of protons and atomic nuclei can flip bits in satellite circuits.

topics.description: A wave is a propagating oscillation or disturbance that transfers energy through space or a medium and may be transverse or longitudinal.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Short bursts of these disturbances are known as “packets” or “trains,” and continuous periodic ones may be sinusoidal when acting like the graph of the sine function. For ten points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [E] Name these oscillations which can be transverse or longitudinal. Surfers usually ride these oscillations in water.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [H] This property, along with wavelength, generally describes a wave’s size. For transverse waves, this property is defined as the wave’s maximum displacement from its equilibrium point.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [M] This property of a wave is the inverse of its period, and describes the number of wavelengths that pass through a certain point over a given period of time. This value is measured in hertz.

parts.label: L
parts.question: These phenomena's frequency is the inverse of their period. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [10] Name these phenomena, examples of which include those carrying light and sound. These phenomena also occur on bodies of water, where they can hurt ships if they are sufficiently large.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [10] This quantity is the magnitude of the maximum displacement from the equilibrium position during an oscillation and is always positive. It effectively measures the height of waves.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [10] When two waves collide, this phenomenon occurs. It has both "constructive" and "destructive" types and involves the waves affecting each other.

topics.description: Aluminum is the chemical element Al, a lightweight metal produced industrially from alumina and widely used in products such as foil.

parts.label: L
parts.question: The Hall-Héroult (ay-roo) process involves dissolving this element's oxide in molten cryolite. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this metal, whose oxide is commonly isolated from bauxite through the Bayer process.

parts.label: B
parts.question: A step in the Hall-Héroult process utilizes this technique of introducing a current to move a chemical reaction forward.

parts.label: C
parts.question: Aluminum possesses this property, which is similar to malleability, of being able to be stretched into a thin wire without breaking.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Anorthosite is a rock comprised almost entirely of this mineral. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: What mineral which forms the continuous branch of Bowen's reaction series is the most common mineral in the Earth's crust?

parts.label: B
parts.question: Feldspar's molecular structure includes eight atoms of this element, which comprises almost half of the Earth's crust. The primary component of sand is a compound of silicon and this element called silica.

parts.label: C
parts.question: Feldspar typically contains silicon, oxygen, an alkali metal, and this element, the most common metal in the Earth's crust. It is symbolized Al, and is commonly used to make foil.
parts.answer: aluminum [or aluminium; prompt on Al] <Sethi, Science>

topics.description: An eight-legged arachnid of the order Araneae, many species of which produce silk and construct webs.

parts.label: tossup
