parts.label: tossup
parts.question: An argument against this process dubs it irrational because belief in a “uniformity principle”  is neither demonstrative nor moral. A later objection to this process involves the time-dependent  colors “grue” and “bleen.” That “new (*) riddle of” this process builds on an Enlightenment-era  objection to this process stating “that the sun will not rise tomorrow” is a valid belief. Nelson Goodman  and David Hume questioned the reliability of, for 10 points, what process in which general rules or  future events are believed in based on past examples?

parts.label: L
parts.question: In a 1931 work, Herbert Butterfield criticized an “interpretation of history” described by this adjective. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this adjective used to describe portrayals of history that lead to a “glorious present.” This is also the name of the party that opposed the Tories.
parts.answer: Whigs [or The Whig Interpretation of History]

parts.label: B
parts.question: The term “Whig” was used to describe histories of this European country, where the Whigs rivaled the Tories in its Parliament.
parts.answer: England [accept Great Britain or the United Kingdom]

parts.label: C
parts.question: Whig historians attacked this man’s History of England, which spanned from Julius Caesar’s invasion to the Glorious Revolution. Immanuel Kant credited this man with awakening him from his “dogmatic slumber.”

topics.description: German philosopher whose works developed concepts including the will to power, the Übermensch, and the death of God, while criticizing traditional morality and religion.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: This writer’s literary theories include the duality of Apollonian and Dionysian forces in tragedy. This thinker described the self-determining force of each person as the “will to power” in books like (*) Thus Spake Zarathustra, which were edited after his death by his sister Elizabeth into a pro-Nazi ideology. The Antichrist and Beyond Good and Evil were written by, for ten points, what German philosopher who proclaimed “God is dead”?

parts.label: L
parts.question: This thinker dedicated “Schopenhauer as Educator,” one of his Untimely Meditations, to Arthur Schopenhauer since he was one of the only philosophers that this thinker respected. For ten points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [M] Name this German philosopher, the author of works like Thus Spake Zarathustra and Beyond Good and Evil. The master-slave morality is a central theme of this thinker’s On the Genealogy of Morality.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] In his The Gay Science, Nietzsche wrote that humanity has “still to overcome his shadow!” after declaring the death of this omniscient figure. In another of his works, Zarathustra famously declares that “[this figure] is dead.”

parts.label: C
parts.question: [H] In Thus Spake Zarathustra, Zarathustra also proposes this concept as an ultimate form of existence for humankind. This German-language term is usually translated “Superman.”

topics.description: Swiss psychiatrist and psychologist who founded analytical psychology and developed theories of the collective unconscious, archetypes, and synchronicity.

parts.label: L
parts.question: This color’s association with hunger has resulted in heavy use by fast food companies like McDonald’s and KFC. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [E] Athletes wearing clothes of what color have been cited as winning more due to its association with aggressiveness and dominance?

parts.label: B
parts.question: [H] In contrast, this color has been associated with calmness and reduced aggressiveness. The Baker-Miller shade of this color has been cited as potentially reducing violence in prisons.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [M] This psychologist promoted the role of color in psychology. This psychologist also referred to “meaningful coincidences” as “synchronicity”, and analyzed archetypes like the shadow, anima, and animus.

parts.label: L
parts.question: This man suffered from indigestion, lust-driven insomnia, and a general distaste for how downright informal Americans were during this 1909 trip to the United States. For ten points each,

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this Austrian thinker whose theories of psychoanalysis became decidedly more popular in the US than in Europe.

parts.label: B
parts.question: Freud was one of several thinkers invited by Clark University to speak in America; another was this colleague, who coined the theory of the “collective unconscious” and recommended that Freud cheat on his wife in order to get some sound sleep. Freud declined.

parts.label: C
parts.question: Freud’s lectures in America were largely based on his 1899 work on The Interpretation of these unconscious events, which mainly occur during REM sleep. Freud complained of having awful examples of these events during his American trip.
parts.answer: dreams (accept The Interpretation of Dreams; accept Die Traumdeutung)

topics.description: The percentage of the labor force that is unemployed and actively seeking work, used as a key labor-market indicator.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: A one percent change in this quantity causes a two percent change in GDP, according to Okun’s Law. An inverse relationship between inflation and this quantity is depicted in the Phillips Curve. The “frictional” and “structural” types of this concept add up to its (*) “natural rate.” Discouraged and retired workers are not included in the calculation of this quantity. For 10 points, what quantity describes the number of people who cannot find jobs.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: The Beveridge curve plots the vacancy rate against this economic quantity. This quantity is called “structural” when it is caused by a gap in the skills demanded by firms and supplied by the market. The 2021 Great (*) Resignation is actually having a low impact on this because of a high retirement rate. Automation threatens to cause an increase in this quantity as certain jobs become obsolete. For ten points, name this measurement of the number of people out of work.

topics.description: An international financial institution that promotes monetary cooperation and provides policy advice, loans, and financial assistance to member countries.

parts.label: L
parts.question: This leader resigned in 2022 amidst a sexual misconduct scandal of one of his colleagues, Chris Pincher, and a major cost of living crisis. For ten points each,

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this former mayor of London who stepped down as British Prime Minister in September 2022.
parts.answer: Boris Johnson (accept Alexander Boris de Pfeffel Johnson)

parts.label: B
parts.question: Johnson was succeeded as British Prime Minister by this woman. Two days before Queen Elizabeth II died, she appointed this woman as Prime Minister at Balmoral Castle.

parts.label: C
parts.question: Almost immediately after taking power, Truss’s government announced a tax cut that was so controversial, this international organization told the UK to reconsider. The World Bank and this arm of the United Nations are largely considered the two most important international financial institutions.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Protestors in this country took over the President and Prime Ministers residences in Colombo. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [M] Name this island nation off the tip of India, where protests over economic mismanagement toppled the government of Gotabaya Rajapaksa in July 2022.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] Rajapaksa’s government blamed COVID-19’s effects on this industry, Sri Lanka’s main economic driver, for the poor economy. This industry involved foreigners going to a country to view its landmarks and attractions.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [H] This financial institution is working on a 3 billion dollar bailout package for Sri Lanka. This financial institution was founded, along with the World Bank, at the Bretton Woods Conference.

topics.description: German socialist philosopher, political theorist, and revolutionary who collaborated with Karl Marx and co-authored The Communist Manifesto.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: This thinker wrote that philosophy was meant to change the world in his Theses on Feuerbach (FOY-uhr-bock) and called religion the "opium of the people" in a critique of Hegel. In another work, this thinker claimed all history was a "history of (*) class struggles" and commanded the proletarians of the world to "unite!". For 10 points, name this collaborator of Friedrich Engels who wrote The Communist Manifesto.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: A Jacques Derrida book titled in reference to this work’s first sentence coined the term “hauntology” to refer to the recurrence of historical themes in the present. This work’s author pleads guilty to “wanting to stop the exploitation of children by their parents” in a section that calls for an end to both family and religion. This work summarizes its thesis as “abolition of (*) private property.” According to this text, a revolution led by the proletariat should overthrow capitalism and replace it with the title ideology. For 10 points, class struggle is described in what radical left-wing pamphlet by Friedrich Engels and Karl Marx?
parts.answer: The Communist Manifesto [or Manifesto of the Communist Party; or Manifest der Kommunistischen Partei] (The Derrida book is titled Specters of Marx.)

topics.description: The Confucian virtue and ethical duty of honoring, respecting, and caring for one's parents and elders, often extending to ancestors.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: A painting of this philosopher grimacing while tasting vinegar represents his negative views on the goodness of life. According to this thinker, an ethical ruler should radiate moral goodness in a way similar to the north star. A work by this non-Aristotle philosopher may contain the first occurrence of the golden rule. This thinker’s Four Books includes a work by the (*) “second sage” that succeeded this philosopher, Mencius. This philosopher’s belief that children should respect their elders is known as filial piety [PIE-uh-dee]. For 10 points, the Analects is a compilation of the sayings of what ancient Chinese philosopher?
parts.answer: Confucius [or Kongzi or Kong Fuzi or Kong Qiu or Master Kong or Zhongni]

parts.label: L
parts.question: One thinker argued that social harmony arises when behavior matches what is entailed by these words, a concept called the “rectification of [these words]. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [E] What words are used to identify people? In China, the most common “family” type of these words is Wang.
parts.answer: name [or last name or surname or first name; prompt on title]

parts.label: B
parts.question: [H] The rectification of the names was promoted by this ancient Chinese philosopher, whose sayings are compiled in the Analects.
parts.answer: Confucius [or Kong Fuzi or Master Kong]

parts.label: C
parts.question: [M] Confucius argued that one should respect these people, a virtue called filial piety. Examples of filial piety include bringing honor to these people and taking care of them in their later years.
parts.answer: parents [or elders or ancestors or older people; prompt on family]

topics.description: A Chinese ethical, philosophical, and religious tradition associated with Confucius that emphasizes social roles, ritual, filial piety, learning, virtue, and harmonious conduct.

parts.label: L
parts.question: The term “daojiao” (dao-JEE-ao) first appeared in a text of this philosophical school, during a critique  of a rival concept of fate. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this Chinese philosophy that promoted “impartial care.” Its founder may be named for being  a tattooed ex-convict.
parts.answer: Mohism [or Moism; or Mojia; or the School of Master Mo]

parts.label: B
parts.question: The Mozi (MO-zee) denounces this rival school that emphasized “five relationships.” The Analects are attributed to the scholar who names this school.
parts.answer: Confucianism [or Ruism; or Ru Classicism; or Kongjiao]

parts.label: C
parts.question: Mohists and Confucians used this Chinese term to mean “morality,” and Daoists used it to mean  “inner power.” It is sometimes translated as “virtue,” as in the second word of a core Daoist text's title.
parts.answer: de (day) [or te (tay)] [As in Dao de jing.]

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: The founder of this school of thought believed that the “rectification of names” would solve social disorder. The Classic of Poetry and the Book of Changes are two of this school’s Five Classics. In this school, the virtue of respect for one’s parents, ancestors, and societal hierarchies is called (*) filial piety. For ten points, name this school of thought named for its founder, a philosopher from ancient China.

topics.description: A philosophical dialogue by Plato presenting Socrates' defense at his trial for impiety and corrupting the youth of Athens.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: This philosopher describes a slave doubling the area of a square in Meno. This philosopher, who claimed “I know that I know nothing,” is referred to as “the gadfly of the state” in one work. Crito attempts to convince this man to escape prison after he is tried for (*) “corrupting the youth of Athens” in the Apology. For 10 points, name this philosopher who was sentenced to death by drinking hemlock, a teacher of Plato.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: In a work about him, this philosopher compares himself to a gadfly because he stings people “in the service of truth,” and defends himself against the charge of corrupting the youth of (*) Athens in the book Apology. This philosopher was convicted of those charges and sentenced to die by drinking hemlock. For ten points, name this ancient Greek philosopher whose thoughts are recorded in dialogues written by his student, Plato.

topics.description: An interdisciplinary legal and social framework examining how law and institutions can reproduce systemic racial inequality.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Answer the following about the teaching of black history in the United States. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [E] In February 2023, this organization announced that it would add an African American Studies class to the list of  its Advanced Placement course offerings. This organization also administers the SAT.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [H] This initiative, developed by Nikole Hannah-Jones, aims to frame American history through the focus of  slavery. A curriculum was developed for this initiative, named for the year when African slaves first landed in  Jamestown.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [M] Critics of the 1619 Project note its basis in this theory, which holds that many American legal systems are  inherently racist. Florida passed the W.O.K.E. act to prevent the teaching of this theory.

parts.label: L
parts.question: As of 2022, seven states used this specific phrase in legislation banning it from public K-12 schools.  For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [10] Conservative activist Christopher Rufo often campaigns against what three-word phrase, which  originally referred to an idea put forth in law schools by Kimberlé Crenshaw and Derrick Bell?

parts.label: B
parts.question: [10] In 2017, Rufo sued this city for instituting a new income tax. Amazon is headquartered in this city  in Washington.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [10] Business groups, the ACLU, and FIRE all joined a 2022 lawsuit against a law signed by this  governor, alleging that the wide-ranging “Stop WOKE Act” he signed infringes free speech.

topics.description: American philosopher and psychologist who helped establish pragmatism and wrote The Varieties of Religious Experience and The Will to Believe.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: Christopher Hookway described this school’s epistemology as fallibilist in a book that compared a thinker from it to Josiah Royce. One philosopher from this school stated that our conception of an object consists of the effects that object has, which is known as this school’s maxim. A work that refers to this school as “a (*) new name for some old ways of thinking” illustrates its method using the example of a man who chases a squirrel around a tree. A thinker from this school defended religious faith in the lecture “The Will to Believe.” For 10 points, William James popularized what American philosophical school that emphasized practicality?
parts.answer: ANSWER: pragmatism [accept pragmatic maxim or pragmatic method]

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: One thinker from this country used the example of a man chasing a squirrel in a book subtitled “a new  name for some old ways of thinking.” A philosophical school originating in this country emphasized the  importance of (*) practicality in assessing value. For 10 points, what country is home to Charles Sanders Peirce and  William James, the founders of Pragmatism?
parts.answer: United States of America [or the United States; accept USA]

topics.description: An Indo-Iranian language spoken primarily in Iran, Afghanistan, and Tajikistan and used in major Persian literary works by authors including Omar Khayyam, Rumi, Attar, and Ferdowsi.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: In a poem in this language, a group of thirty birds realizes that the great bird they are looking for is actually themselves. Another poem in this language begins, “Listen to this reed how it complains: / it is telling a tale of separations.” A poem based on a poem in this language declares, “Oh, Wilderness were Paradise enow!” That poem was adapted from this language by (*) Edward FitzGerald and also describes “A Jug of Wine, a Loaf of Bread— and Thou.” Another poet used this language to write the Masnavi, which was inspired by Sufism. For 10 points, Omar Khayyam and Rumi wrote in what language spoken in Iran?
parts.answer: Persian [or Farsi] (The first poem is The Conference of the Birds by Farid ud-Din Attar.)

parts.label: L
parts.question: This work describes “the Winter garment of Repentance fling” in the poem “Come, fill the Cup, and in the Fire of Spring.” For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [M] Name this collection of quatrains, where the speaker asks for “a jug of wine, a loaf of bread—and thou," written by Omar Khayyam.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] The Rubaiyat was written in this language. This language was also used by Ferdowsi to write the Shahnameh, the national epic of Iran.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [H] Another Persian poet was Rumi, who wrote thousands of poems in this form in his Divan-e Shams. This Arabic poetic form, also used in Indian classical music, often expresses unattainable love.

topics.description: An economic system characterized by predominantly private ownership of the means of production and production for markets and profit.

parts.label: L
parts.question: For 10 points each, answer the following about the work of economist Adam Smith:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [10] In The Wealth of Nations, Smith argued that division of this term makes workers more efficient. This term, a synonym for "work", is the total human activity required to produce a good.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [10] To illustrate the division of labor, Smith began The Wealth of Nations with an anecdote about visiting a factory for these objects, where every worker had a different job.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [10] Smith's ideas are foundational to this economic system, in which the means of production are privately owned and operated for a profit by corporations. It is often contrasted with communism, in which the means of production are public.
parts.answer: capitalism [accept word forms like capitalist; accept specific types of capitalism, such as free-market capitalism]

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: One work titled for this concept discusses “commodity fetishism” and the labor theory of value. This concept names an economic system in which the means of production are privately owned. Along with (*) land, labor, and entrepreneurship, this concept makes up the four factors of production. For 10 points, Karl Marx wrote a treatise on what concept, assets which can be used to produce more assets.

topics.description: A philosophical movement concerned with human existence, freedom, responsibility, choice, and the creation or search for meaning.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Give the following about 20th century philosophy Martin Heidegger, for ten points each.

parts.label: A
parts.question: Through works like 1927’s Being and Time, Heidegger was a major influence on this philosophical movement, later championed by Jean-Paul Sartre [sart] and Albert Camus [ca-moo], that studies how a human can “be.”

parts.label: B
parts.question: Beyond philosophy, Heidegger is best known for his membership in this German political party from 1933 to 1945. Heidegger later distanced himself from this party, but his posthumously-published notebooks include several examples of anti-semitism.
parts.answer: Nazi Party (accept National Socialist German Workers’ Party; accept Nationalsozialistische Deutsche Arbeiterpartei; accept NSDAP)

parts.label: C
parts.question: Heidegger’s less controversial post-war work includes The Question Concerning this concept, an essay that eventually defines it as including the “equipment, tools, and machines, the manufactured and used things themselves.” Stone tools and computers are commonly cited on opposite ends of humanity’s history of this concept.

parts.label: L
parts.question: This essay defines the absurd as “sin without God” and rejects Kierkegaardian leaps of faith as “philosophical suicide.” For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [H] Name this 1942 essay that examines man’s place in a meaningless universe. It ends by claiming that “One must imagine [the title figure] happy.”
parts.answer: The Myth of Sisyphus [or Le Mythe de Sisyphe]

parts.label: B
parts.question: [M] The author of The Myth of Sisyphus, Albert Camus, is often considered a member of this philosophical movement. Another member of this movement, Jean-Paul Sartre, stated that this movement “is a humanism.”
parts.answer: existentialism [accept word forms like existentialist or existential]

parts.label: C
parts.question: [E] Unlike the Christian existentialist Søren Kierkegaard, both Sartre and Camus ascribed to this philosophical and theological position, which holds that there is no God.
parts.answer: atheism [accept word forms like atheist; do NOT accept or prompt on agnosticism]

topics.description: Subjective mental experiences involving images, thoughts, and emotions that occur during sleep and may be interpreted psychologically or represented in film.

parts.label: L
parts.question: In Mulholland Drive, a man brings his friend to visit Winkie’s Diner because he saw a terrifying thing behind it during one of these events. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [E] Name these events that may be represented in film through “sequences” that depict a distorted reality. Much of Mulholland Drive takes place during one of these events that ends when the Cowboy says, “time to wake up.”

parts.label: B
parts.question: [M] In a film by this director, the screen flashes red throughout a dream sequence in which Jimmy Stewart’s character recalls failing to save Madeleine Elster from jumping out of a tower. That film by this director uses the dolly zoom to represent Scottie Ferguson’s fear of heights.
parts.answer: ANSWER: Alfred Hitchcock (The film is Vertigo.)

parts.label: C
parts.question: [H] This director showed a man struggling to get out of a locked car before floating up into the sky in a dream sequence that opens his film 8½ (“eight and a half”). This Italian also directed La Dolce (“DOLE-chay”) Vita.

parts.label: L
parts.question: This man suffered from indigestion, lust-driven insomnia, and a general distaste for how downright informal Americans were during this 1909 trip to the United States. For ten points each,

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this Austrian thinker whose theories of psychoanalysis became decidedly more popular in the US than in Europe.

parts.label: B
parts.question: Freud was one of several thinkers invited by Clark University to speak in America; another was this colleague, who coined the theory of the “collective unconscious” and recommended that Freud cheat on his wife in order to get some sound sleep. Freud declined.

parts.label: C
parts.question: Freud’s lectures in America were largely based on his 1899 work on The Interpretation of these unconscious events, which mainly occur during REM sleep. Freud complained of having awful examples of these events during his American trip.
parts.answer: dreams (accept The Interpretation of Dreams; accept Die Traumdeutung)

topics.description: A social movement and body of thought advocating gender equality and analyzing and opposing systems of women's oppression.

parts.label: L
parts.question: The title character of this novel “had not the option” to be romantically involved with Sally Seton. For ten points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [H] Give this novel named after a character whose first name is Clarissa. In this novel, Septimus Smith is seen in the park before he jumps out of a hospital window to commit suicide.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [M] This English author of Mrs. Dalloway wrote the stream-of-consciousness novel To The Lighthouse. She also created Judith, a fictional sister of William Shakespeare, in her essay “A Room of One’s Own.”

parts.label: C
parts.question: [E] "A Room of One's Own" argues that women need money and physical space to establish a metaphorical space in the literary world. It's seen as an important text in this movement that advocates equality of the sexes.

parts.label: L
parts.question: This writer collaborated with Cornel West on the discussion of Black academics Breaking Bread. For  10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [10] Name this writer of All About Love and a theoretical text subtitled From Margin to Center, who  adopted an all-lowercase pen name in 1978.
parts.answer: ANSWER: bell hooks [or Gloria Jean Watkins]

parts.label: B
parts.question: [10] hooks, who is considered a major part of the “third wave” of this movement, critiqued “second  wave” writers in this movement such as Betty Friedan (free-DAN).

parts.label: C
parts.question: [10] Hooks's most widely read book on the intersection of Black and feminist concerns is a 1981 volume  titled after this speech repeatedly given by Sojourner Truth.

topics.description: A word board game in which players form words from letter tiles on a game board, typically a 15-by-15 grid, and score points based on tile values and board bonuses.

parts.label: L
parts.question: The Serbian writer Milorad Pavić (pah-veech) wrote a mostly-plotless "lexicon novel" titled for one of these works "of the Khazars". For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name these works, a satirical "Devil's" one of which was written by Ambrose Bierce. The “Petit Larousse” is a famous French one of these works.
parts.answer: dictionaries [accept The Devil’s Dictionary; accept Dictionary of the Khazars or Hazarski rečnik]

parts.label: B
parts.question: Henry Black wrote the first two editions of an authoritative dictionary used by people with this profession. In order to become part of this profession, prospective members must pass the "bar exam", for which each state has a different version.
parts.answer: lawyers [or attorneys; accept anything relating to practicing law]

parts.label: C
parts.question: This board game also maintains its own dictionary, which lists all the words which may be played in it. Players in this board game take turns playing tiles on a 15-by-15 board to form words, scoring more points for using rarer letters like the Q and Z.

parts.label: L
parts.question: One of these figures named Ofglen hangs herself to avoid being tortured by the Eyes of God. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [H] Name this group, which includes the Commander’s concubine Offred. These figures are considered essential to the survival of the human race in Gilead.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [M] The handmaid Offred is the protagonist of The Handmaid’s Tale, a novel by this author. This author also wrote The Testaments and Oryx and Crake.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [E] In The Handmaid’s Tale, Offred plays this forbidden game with the Commander. Players of this board game form words using lettered tiles.

topics.description: A word puzzle in which solvers fill answers into intersecting Across and Down entries on a grid based on written clues.

parts.label: L
parts.question: For ten points each, answer some questions about Will Shortz.

parts.label: A
parts.question: [H] Shortz is the creator and editor for the section of the New York Times that publishes these puzzles. In a tribute to Shortz, artist Ken Knowlton created a portrait of Shortz using the black and white squares of these puzzles.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] Shortz’s favorite crossword was published on Election Day 1996 and had two possible solutions stating either that Bob Dole or this candidate won. This candidate did win, before a scandal in which he cheated on his wife Hillary.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [M] In addition to creating puzzles for NPR’s Weekend Edition, Shortz created the puzzle clues for the movie named for [this superhero] Forever. Those clues were left by The Riddler for Val Kilmer’s portrayal of this “Caped Crusader”.

parts.label: L
parts.question: People who construct these puzzles are sometimes referred to as "cruciverbalists". For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name these word puzzles which contain "Across" and "Down" clues, and consist of a grid in which words must be filled in all the empty squares.

parts.label: B
parts.question: This other kind of crossword more popular in Britain uses clues that contain complex puzzles like anagrams and other wordplay, and typically contains many more black squares than standard crosswords.

parts.label: C
parts.question: A well-known crossword is published every week in the Sunday edition of this newspaper. Its slogan is "All the News that's Fit to Print".
parts.answer: The New York Times [or the NYT; prompt on The Times] <McAvoy-Bickford, Miscellaneous>

topics.description: A winter sport and recreational practice involving travel over snow using skis.

parts.label: L
parts.question: This mountain overlooks the resort town of Zermatt. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this notoriously dangerous “Peak of the Meadows,” which lies on the border of Switzerland and Italy. This mountain is partly named for its unique shape, which is a result of the collision of four cirques.
parts.answer: Matterhorn [or Mont Cervin; or Monte Cervino]

parts.label: B
parts.question: The Matterhorn is one of this mountain range’s namesake “four-thousanders.” This largest mountain range in Europe runs from France to Slovenia.

parts.label: C
parts.question: Zermatt is popular for mountaineering and this other winter sport prevalent in Switzerland. Cities in the United States, such as Telluride and Aspen, are popular resorts for snowboarding and this other activity.

parts.label: L
parts.question: This state’s five national parks include Arches, Zion, and Bryce Canyon, which are all in desert canyonland. For ten points each,

parts.label: A
parts.question: [E] Name this Western state with great geographical diversity whose capital is Salt Lake City.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [H] A prehistoric lake of this name left exceptionally flat salt flats in Northwestern Utah which share the same name. Those salt flats of this name are the site of many land-speed records.
parts.answer: Bonneville [or Lake Bonneville or the Bonneville Salt Flats]

parts.label: C
parts.question: [M] Park City and Deer Valley are sites in northeastern Utah for this sport. Utah’s suitability for this sport is part of the reason Salt Lake City was awarded the 2002 Olympics.

topics.description: The practice and sport of propelling arrows with a bow, including traditional, legendary, and competitive forms.

parts.label: L
parts.question: This character wins his wife in a contest with Krishna. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this character who was born to Kunti (koon-TEE) and Pandu due to the miraculous  intervention of Indra. He engages in a theological dialogue with his charioteer before battle in the  Kurukshetra (koo-rook-SHET-ruh) War.

parts.label: B
